MARGIN — Master Build Prompt

Working name: Margin (provisional — see §01.7). Version: v2 (revised against 162 critique findings). Generated 2026-09-07. Length ≈ 225,487 words; 1,554 numbered requirements.

What this document is

This is the complete build specification for an AI learning product whose mission is to be the best AI education company in history: table-stakes parity with ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude and DeepSeek chat products, plus an exam-grounded learning core that none of them has. It is written for the executing AI coding agent (or the engineering team an agent leads). Read §00 first: it fixes the reading order, the non-negotiables, the precedence rules and the definition of done.

How it was produced. Eight research briefs (frontier chat baseline, education competitors, learning science, exam systems and marking, UX craft, architecture and model economics, business and moat, student voice) plus two gap briefs (legal/licensing and Cambridge marking) and an analysis of the founder's own material → a decision index → three independent product visions → a judged synthesis (designs/SYNTHESIS.md, the source of truth for every decision below) → sixteen sections drafted against that synthesis → adversarial critique and revision. The research and design files ship alongside this document under research/ and designs/; §15.I maps which file answers what.

Precedence. designs/SYNTHESIS.md > this document > the research appendices. Where this document marks a decision PROVISIONAL or [founder default], the flip condition is stated inline and the founder-owned decisions are listed with their defaults in §15.G.

§00How to use this document

00.1Who executes this, and in what order to read it

This document is the build specification for Margin (working name; see §01.7). Its reader is the executing AI coding agent, or the engineering team an agent leads. Treat it as a contract, not an inspiration: every numbered requirement is a test you will be held to, every "Never" row is a lint you will write, and every "Why:" is the evidence that stops you re-litigating a decision.

00-USE-001 Reading order. Read in this order before writing code: §00 → §01 → §02 (this file) → §03 (parity) → §04 (learning core) → §05 (exam engine) → §06 (library) → §07 (learner memory) → §08 (orchestration) → §09 (design system) → §10 (screens) → §11 (architecture) → §12 (safety) → §13 (quality gates) → §14 (roadmap) → §15 (appendices). Do not start a section's build until you have read the sections it cross-references. Acceptance: the first pull request of the build contains a DECISIONS.md that lists every requirement ID this PR touches; a PR touching an ID from a section not yet read is rejected in review.

00-USE-002 Roles. Four roles execute this document; an agent may hold more than one, but each PR names which role authored it.

RoleOwnsMust never
BuilderCode, migrations, prompts, tokens, screensMerge without the §13 gate report attached
Content engineerPacks, structured mark schemes, gold sets, misconception library (§05, §06)Enter a scraped provenance class or paste board wording without a licence (§06)
EvaluatorEval suites, calibration runs, praise lint, adversarial students (§13)Lower a floor to make a paper pass; the fix is content or method, never the bar
Founder liaisonFounder-owned decisions (§00.3), licensing, budgetsSilently choose a non-default; every non-default is a written decision

00-USE-003 Vocabulary is fixed. Use only the canonical nouns from SYNTHESIS §3 in code, UI strings, telemetry and docs: Course, Pack, Item, Attempt, Turn, Mark, Card, Session, Plan, Source, Receipt, Class; the Learner Graph (the projection of Attempts into mastery, misconceptions and calibration, §07); the Examiner Twin (the calibrated per-paper marker, §05); the Effort Gate and Help Ladder (§04); the Learning Receipt (§12). Modes are Learn · Practise · Mark. Intent chips are Teach me · Check my steps · Just the answer. Mastery states are Unseen · Shaky · Secure · Exam-ready. Acceptance: a repository grep for streak, quiz mode, tutor mode, explain mode, exam mode as user-facing strings returns zero hits; the glossary in §15 is the only place synonyms appear, and only to map them to canon.

00-USE-004 The scoping knife. Before building any feature, answer in the PR description: "Which Attempts does this create or improve?" A feature with no answer is not in the MVP (SYNTHESIS §3.1). Why: every metric, mastery update, teacher view and Receipt is a projection of Attempts; features that do not touch them are cost without learning.

00.2Non-negotiables

These hold for every release, every tenant, every model swap, every "quick fix". They are not trade-offs; they are the product. Each is enforced by a test named in the owning section. If a requirement elsewhere in this document appears to conflict with one of these, this list wins and the conflict is a bug to report (§00.6).

IDNon-negotiableEnforced by
00-NON-001The Effort Gate. No solution content on a gradable Item before an Attempt, a plan, or "don't know where to start" plus one sentence of what the student does know. There is no fourth path: the 90-second time-box (04-GATE-002) is a way of reaching the third path, not a way around it — it ends with one required line naming what the student tried or what is blocking them, and exiting through it runs the whole seen-solution script (label, 24–72 h retest, near-transfer Item). The gate is a state on the Attempt, never a refusal in prose, never rate-limited.§04; 30-turn adversarial suite, leak <5% (§13); fixture timebox_farm: 10 consecutive time-box exits carry seen_solution=true and a scheduled retest in 100% of cases
00-NON-002No Mark without a mark scheme in context; no number below gate. If no structured scheme record exists, the product gives feedback and spans only. Below the §05 ship gate a paper shows spans and feedback, never a mark or a predicted grade.§05.6; CI asserts 0 marks emitted without mark_scheme_items
00-NON-003No sycophancy. No person-praise, unearned praise, agreement with an incorrect claim, softened mark, exclamation mark, emoji, "Great question" or therapy-speak in any Turn or Mark.Praise lint before paint, regenerate once, template fallback; weekly audit <5% (§04, §13)
00-NON-004No streaks, no shame, no engagement optimisation. No daily streaks, loss animations, confetti, overdue counters, mascots, or loss-framed notifications. DAU and minutes are guard-rails, never targets.Lint on string table and motion tokens (§09); KPI tree (§14)
00-NON-005No submittable coursework. NEA/IA/EE/personal-statement requests switch to draft-feedback mode; every assignment produces a Learning Receipt.§12; eval set of coursework prompts, 0 submittable outputs
00-NON-006Three-provenance content model. Every document is OWN, LICENSED or USER; there is no scraped class in code; USER never enters global retrieval; per-document kill switch; 24 h takedown SLA.§06; type system rejects a fourth class
00-NON-007Never host or mirror board PDFs; no Cambridge mark-scheme viewer. Papers deep-link to official pages; grid wording is paraphrased unless licensed; extracts ≤2 sentences or ≤40 words, attributed, audit-logged.§06 extracts policy; storage lint
00-NON-008Teen-safety parity. Item-for-item match with ChatGPT for Teens: age assurance, consent under 16, Study/Quiet Hours, break reminders, no romantic or companion behaviour, no ads, parental controls without transcript access, persistent Article 50 disclosure.§12; consent audit 100% for under-16 school-tenant users
00-NON-009No efficacy claim that is not pre-registered. No "2× learning", no multiplier, no grade-uplift claim outside the §14 study plan. The marketing number equals the product number.Copy review checklist (§14); legal sign-off
00-NON-010Never "replaces teachers"; never "official" or "endorsed"; never the name beside "Cambridge". Non-affiliation notice in footer and store listing.String lint; store-listing template (§14)
00-NON-011Every pixel passes the §09 checklist. Tokens only (no raw hex, no raw px outside the scale), one accent hue, no ease-in, no #000, no motion on Send, WCAG 2.2 AA gates, CLS above the cursor = 0.§09.16 pixel-QA release checklist as CI; Storybook visual diff
00-NON-012Every prompt, model, routing or policy change passes the §13 gates before it reaches a user: adversarial pedagogy suite, praise lint, per-paper marking gold sets, Recall@8 ≥0.92, cache-read assertion, CWV and TTFT SLOs.CI required checks; policy version pinned per Session
00-NON-013A Course, not a chat. Home has no "New chat"; a conversation without a Course is an Ask and never counts as study; there is no study toggle to lose; the mode chip is always visible.§10 screen 3; e2e test
00-NON-014Turn discipline. Every Learn-mode Turn ≤120 words unless depth was requested, one move, at most one question, explicit hand-back. Marking cards are exempt.Orchestrator rejects >1 question; <2% of Turns >150 words (§04)
00-NON-015Verified before spoken. Every numeric or symbolic final passes SymPy/Pyodide; quotes come only from loaded set texts, else "I can't confirm that quote"; every Item is pre-solved and the key held before tutoring.§08 verification tools; eval: 0 invented quotes
00-NON-016"Just the answer" is honoured, never refused, after one attempt — labelled Seen solution, retested at 24–72 h, never counting toward Secure. Homework due in ten minutes is legitimate. What "the answer" is differs by Item and is a visible state, never a sentence of prose: on points and short-answer Items it is the full worked solution; on a levels Item ≥8 marks the chip reads "Full plan + one paragraph" with the tooltip "Model essays unlock after your own marked attempt", and once that student's own Attempt on that Item has been Marked the full model answer is available under the same seen-solution script.§04.5; eval: 0 refusals and 0 scope sentences post-attempt; suite case demand_essay_after_mark delivers the model answer
00-NON-017Published limits, no silent cuts, no hard mid-session stop. Every limit is a plain number in Settings › Usage with a meter; exam-week grace from T−14; soft slow-down only.§03; zero silent limit changes as a KPI guard-rail (§14)
00-NON-018Privacy posture in code. Per-tenant policy object on every request; no training on pupil data; EU/UK school tenants never leave regional endpoints; DeepSeek never tutors, never sees PII, never serves EU/UK tenants.§11; CI asserts zero EU-tenant requests to non-EU endpoints
00-NON-019No model picker. The student controls effort (Quick · Think · Deep); the vendor appears as a chip on the calibration line, never as a headline.§03; §09 anti-pattern lint
00-NON-020Predicted grades live only on Progress › Paper and the mock debrief, only for gated papers with ≥3 series of thresholds, a verified PUM map (pum_verified=true) and ≥3 marked Attempts; never on Home, never in a notification, never to a parent unless the student enables it.§05.8, §10.14, §10.11
00-NON-021The Never list is absent from the codebase: image/video generation, general agents, deep research, ads, bot directory, daily streaks, companion persona, under-13 accounts, a Cambridge mark-scheme viewer.Dependency and route lint; §14

Why the list is this long: each item corresponds to a documented failure of a competitor or a documented harm in the research (Bastani et al. 2025 for 001; students' #1 pain for 002; the Duolingo backlash for 010; Quizlet's paywall collapse for 017; Alpha School's unverifiable multipliers for 009). None is aesthetic.

00.3Resolving ambiguity: precedence, provisional decisions, founder-owned defaults

00-AMB-001 Precedence. When two sources disagree, resolve in this order and record the resolution in DECISIONS.md: (1) designs/SYNTHESIS.md; (2) this document, where the section that owns the topic wins over a section that merely mentions it (ownership is the "Owner" column of SYNTHESIS §4 and the §NN headings here — marking belongs to §05, tokens to §09, routing to §08, personas to §02); (3) designs/JUDGING.md for the reasoning behind a ruling; (4) the research appendices (research/*.md) as evidence, never as decisions; (5) the three visions (designs/vision-*.md) only for colour. Acceptance: no PR cites a research file as the authority for a product behaviour.

00-AMB-002 Do not re-open rulings. Every decision in SYNTHESIS was adjudicated in JUDGING §3. If you believe a ruling is wrong, build the default, write a one-paragraph objection with evidence into OBJECTIONS.md, and continue. The founder reviews objections weekly (§00.6). Do not fork behaviour behind a flag "just in case" unless the ruling itself names an A/B.

00-AMB-003 Three statuses. Every requirement is FINAL unless labelled. PROVISIONAL means: build the stated default and implement the flip condition as a measurable event (an A/B result, a licence signed, a human–human line measured). [founder default] means: build the recommended default from the table below, tag every dependent string, migration or config key with the decision number so a reversal is a search-and-replace, not a rewrite. Acceptance: grep -r "founder-default:E" src/ lists every dependent site.

00-AMB-004 Founder-owned decisions and the defaults you build. Seventeen decisions, numbered E1–E17 as in research/INDEX.md §E; §15.G is the canonical table and carries the reversal cost of each (15-FDR-001). Use the E number in every tag (founder-default:E13); there is no separate §00 numbering. Three rows are settled FINAL and are listed only so nobody re-opens them. The founder may change any founder-owned row; you may not. This table and §15.G are updated in the same PR so they never diverge (15-FDR-004).

00-AMB-005 When the document is silent. Apply, in order: the nearest non-negotiable (§00.2); the product principles (§01.2); the persona who is hurt most by the wrong choice (§02.1, usually Aisha); then the cheapest reversible option. Write the choice into DECISIONS.md with the requirement IDs it touches. Do not ask the founder about anything this rule can settle.

Done means: the Layer 3 cluster RCT is in the field across the 2027–28 session with its analysis plan public before the first data point.

00-DONE-004 Not done, ever, by shortcut. A tier is not done if any non-negotiable in §00.2 is waived, if any paper shows a mark below gate, if any limit was cut silently, or if a "temporary" model change skipped §13. Why: the product's only durable asset is trust in the number; one leaked gate costs more than a slipped month.

00-DONE-005 The MVP-unfunded variant. If the calibration budget (E6) is not confirmed by 1 Oct 2026, do not slip the launch and do not lower a gate. The exam-engine row of 00-DONE-001 is replaced by: every MVP paper at gold_seeded with floor-A metrics published internally only; every Mark at calibration_status.state = uncalibrated, so total_band is null and the header reads "Feedback only — this paper is not yet calibrated" (05-MARK-010, 05-WRKD-004) while spans, checks and advice render unchanged; no predicted grades anywhere; differentiators 1 and 8 (01-DIFF-001, 01-DIFF-008) struck from every public surface including the landing page, the store listing and the Compare page. Every other MVP row stands unchanged. Acceptance: a build flag calibration_funded=false renders the product in this state end to end, and the copy lint fails on any surviving string from differentiators 1 or 8. Why: a definition of done that assumes an unclosed founder decision is not a plan (15-FDR E6).

00.5How to use the appendices (§15)

§15 holds the artefacts you paste, not the rules you interpret. Use it as follows.

00-APP-001 System prompts per mode (§15.A). Copy the Learn, Practise and Mark system prompts verbatim into the prompt registry with their version hash; never edit inline in application code. Any change is a new version that passes §13 before routing (00-NON-012). The cached prefix (persona + Pack) must stay byte-stable and precede all dynamic content (§08).

00-APP-002 Marking rubric templates (§15.B). Use the levels and points templates as the shape of mark_scheme_items; the content for each paper comes from the Pack. A template field left blank is a build error, not a default.

00-APP-003 Question-tagging schema (§15.D). Every Item you create, import or generate validates against the schema (syllabus node, AO split, command word, tariff, cognitive-demand tag, provenance, stats). Reject on validation failure; do not coerce.

00-APP-004 Prompt templates (§15.E). Feedback template (task → process → self-regulation), distress script, coursework refusal, "Just the answer" deal script, probe card wording, debrief template. The strings there are canonical; §01.6 gives the voice rules they obey.

00-APP-005 Glossary (§15.F). The only place a synonym may appear. If a term you need is missing, add it to the glossary in the same PR that introduces it.

00-APP-006 Open questions for the founder (§15.H). Mirrors 00-AMB-004 with the full reasoning. Add a question there only when 00-AMB-005 cannot settle it.

00-APP-007 Identifier and version grammar (normative). Every durable identifier has exactly one form. common@1 in §15.C.1 is the machine-readable copy; this table is the human one. 00.6Reporting progress, and what to ask the founder and when

00-REP-001 Weekly build report. Every Friday, one file reports/YYYY-WW.md, ≤600 words, in this order: (1) gate dashboard deltas (leak rate, praise rate, per-paper QWK, TTFT, cache share, cost per student); (2) requirement IDs closed this week, with evidence links; (3) IDs at risk for the current milestone (SYNTHESIS §13 table); (4) objections filed (00-AMB-002); (5) founder decisions needed, each with the default you are building meanwhile and the date the default becomes expensive to reverse. No prose about effort or mood. Acceptance: a reader who opens only the report can name the current milestone's exit criteria and which are red.

00-REP-002 Per-PR contract. Title starts with the requirement IDs touched. Body contains: the Attempt answer (00-USE-004); the §13 gate report or the reason none applies; screenshots for any pixel change in light, dark and reduced-motion; the string diff for any user-facing copy, checked against §01.6.

00-REP-003 Incident report. Any of the following opens an incident within one hour and a written report within 24: a Mark emitted without a scheme; a leak-rate regression >5% on the suite; a paper's seeded QA breaching tolerance; a limit cut without a published change; an EU-tenant request leaving region; any content takedown request.

§01Mission, principles, positioning

01.1Mission, vision, category

01-MIS-001 Mission (FINAL wording; use verbatim in the README and the About screen). Margin exists so that every student, whatever their school, earns the marks their understanding deserves — and understands more because of how they earned them. The measurable form is the north star in §14: Unaided Mark Gain per study hour (UMG/h) — the change in a learner's unaided, timed component-mark estimate on unseen Items from gated papers, per hour studied.

01-MIS-002 Vision (three horizons, FINAL). Year 1: the best Cambridge International exam tutor in the world, with published calibration per paper. Year 2: ten-plus curricula through the compiler, the product schools recommend by name, a community of creators. Year 3: a platform for any curriculum, one million paying learners, the category's reference dataset on what moves exam outcomes. Nothing in the vision says "replace teachers" or "faster than school"; nothing in the build may either (00-NON-010).

01-MIS-003 One-sentence definition (FINAL; product copy may shorten, never extend). Margin is an AI study workspace that marks like an examiner and teaches like a tutor: it grounds every explanation in the student's own syllabus, mark schemes and examiner reports; marks work per Assessment Objective with quoted evidence and a published agreement number; and schedules what to learn next so that more marks are earned per hour studied — for Cambridge International first, and for every curriculum after.

01-MIS-004 Tagline (FINAL for product surfaces; marketing may test variants). Primary: "They know everything. We know your exam." Mark surface: "Marked like an examiner. Explained like a tutor." Acceptance: no other tagline string exists in the string table.

01-MIS-005 Category sentence. Margin is an exam-outcome company built as a data platform — calibration data, structured mark schemes, the Learner Graph, school trust — with a chat interface on top that matches a frontier chat. Why: the labs own the model and the prompt; they do not own paired examiner marks per paper, syllabus-tagged item banks with live statistics, or a learner graph a minor's school can endorse. Build the data assets as first-class systems (§05, §06, §07), not as by-products of chat.

01.2Product principles

Nine principles. Each is one sentence plus the implication you must build. Cite them by ID when a design choice needs justification; when two principles conflict, the lower number wins.

IDPrincipleImplication
01-PRIN-001The Attempt is the atom. Learning happens when a student produces an unaided response to a syllabus-tagged Item and gets examiner-grade feedback on it.Every feature must create or improve Attempts (00-USE-004); every metric is a projection of Attempts; the session is scheduler-generated around one marked Item per day.
01-PRIN-002Honest before kind. A mark that flatters is a harm; a mark that is right and explained is the kindness.No-sycophancy lint (00-NON-003); bands not points; the calibration badge on every Mark; "practice estimate — not yet calibrated" where the gate is not met.
01-PRIN-003Effort first, never a refusal. The student tries before the product tells, and can always ask for the answer after one try.Effort Gate as an Attempt state, "Just the answer" after one attempt, Seen-solution label and retest (00-NON-001, 00-NON-016).
01-PRIN-004The tutor prepared for the lesson. No Item is tutored or marked without a verified key and the scheme in context.Pre-solve with a strong model plus SymPy; structured mark_scheme_items before any Mark (00-NON-002, 00-NON-015).
01-PRIN-005Know the exam, by code. Every explanation, question and Mark carries its syllabus node, AO, command word and paper.The Course is the home object; Packs are data, not prompts; off-spec content is labelled or suppressed; citations open the exact page.
01-PRIN-006Remember what they know, not what they said. Learner state lives outside the chat, decays honestly and is anchored to the exam date.Learner Graph with FSRS-6 (§07); Sessions scoped to one topic; mastery pips that fade with a stated reason.
01-PRIN-007Calm is a feature. A 17-year-old with Paper 2 in 41 days needs less on the screen, not more.≤120-word Turns; one primary action; no streaks, confetti or countdown panic; predicted grades off Home; ≤1 notification a day.

01-PRIN-009Prove it or don't say it. Every public number is a product number from a pre-registered or published method.Calibration page per paper; the §14 three-layer efficacy plan; marketing copy review against 00-NON-009.

Why nine and not more: each maps to a documented failure (unguarded answers lowering exam scores — Bastani et al. 2025; lenient marking as the #1 student pain; Study Mode "a tutor that didn't prep"; context loss after 40–50 messages; walls of text; Chegg's collapse on "answers"; Alpha School's unverifiable multipliers). A principle without a failure behind it is decoration.

Use these ten verbatim (bold clause) as the spine of positioning copy, in this order (SYNTHESIS §2 fixes the order and the wording). The "Copy cost" column states honestly who could copy each row, by what route and in what time — for the top rows the copy path is a data purchase and an exam series, not a prompt — and it is the column to read before believing any of them is a moat. 01.4The honest answer to "why not ChatGPT Study Mode + Save My Exams"

01-HON-001 The answer (FINAL; use it, unedited, when a student, teacher, journalist or investor asks).

ChatGPT, Gemini and Claude are better general assistants than we are, and we run on them. Their study modes are free, and for a student who already knows what to practise and can judge their own work, they are enough. What they do not have is your exam. None of them knows that "Analyse" in 9609 caps you at AO3, that a developed chain needs two links, or that repeating the business name is not application; none holds the mark scheme when it marks, so the same essay gets a different grade every time and a kinder grade than an examiner would give; none remembers what you know rather than what you typed, so week six starts from zero; and none will publish how often it agrees with a real examiner, because it does not measure it. Save My Exams and its peers have the notes and the papers but mark short answers only, publish no accuracy, and run on the boards' tolerance rather than a content model a school can endorse. Margin does one job those two halves cannot do together: it marks your work the way your paper is marked, shows you the sentence that lost the mark and the examiner's own words about it, remembers the gap, and schedules the retry before the exam. When we cannot yet do that for your paper to the standard we publish, we say "not yet calibrated" and give you feedback without a number. What you pay for is marking volume, not access: three marked essays a day are free forever and six a day in exam weeks, every points answer is marked without a cap, and nothing about how you learn — the gate, the ladder, Cards, probes, the Plan — is ever behind the price; the paid tier buys forty calibrated Marks a month. And for a subject we have no Pack for, we say so and label the help "not exam-grounded" rather than pretend. We are not smarter than the models. We are prepared for your exam, and we can prove it.

01-HON-002 What the answer must never contain. A learning multiplier; "replaces"; "official", "endorsed", "approved by"; a competitor's name in a headline; a claim about a paper that is below gate. Acceptance: copy review runs the string against the 00-NON-009/010 lint before publication.

01.6Brand voice rules and example strings

The voice is an examiner who is on your side: short, specific, declarative; examiner vocabulary explained in plain words; certain where the scheme is certain, explicit where it is not. These rules bind every Turn, Mark, notification, empty state, error, email and store listing. §09 owns typography; §15.E owns the full template set; this section owns the rules.

01-VOICE-001 Rules (lint where marked L).

  1. Task before person: talk about the answer, never about the student's character or intelligence. (L: person-praise list.)
  2. The most valuable sentence first: the highest-yield lost mark, the due count, the next block. No preamble.
  3. Name the scheme, not your opinion: "Recommend — a supported decision is required. None found, so AO4 cannot reach Level 3," never "I feel the evaluation is weak." The assessment objective and the level are interpolated from the Pack, never written into a string (15-CMD-005): a three-AO syllabus has no AO4.
  4. One move per Turn: a question, a hint, or a micro-example — not two. (L: >1 question mark rejected.)
  5. Numbers are tabular, exact and sourced: "agreement 0.82 · 312 scripts"; a number without its n or its series is removed.
  6. Never an exclamation mark, emoji, "Great question", "Let's dive in", "Don't worry", "Take a breath", or any therapy-speak. (L.)
  7. Uncertainty is stated as a band or a refusal to guess: "4–5 of 9"; "I can't confirm that quote." Never a confident wrong specific.
  8. Refusals, where policy requires one, are one sentence and name the allowed alternative. Never a lecture on integrity.
  9. Days-to-exam is information, never pressure: "Paper 2 · Thursday 09:00 · 3 days," never "Only 3 days left!"
  10. Vendor names are chips, never headlines; "Cambridge" is a fact about the syllabus, never a badge.
  11. Plain words for examiner terms on first use in a Session: "application (facts true of this business)".
  12. In distress: warm, brief, honest, back to the plan, signpost if crisis language appears; never diagnose, never companion.

01-VOICE-002 Example strings — do / don't. §15.E is the string catalogue of record. This table exists for the "Don't" column, which is the lint corpus §15.E does not carry. Two rules bind it. (a) Where §15.E already carries the key — mark.header.gated, mark.header.provisional, quota.grace, retest.scheduled — the "Do" text here is byte-identical to §15.E's and a one-character difference is a build error. (b) The remaining keys below are not yet in §15.E; each enters the catalogue under exactly the key printed here, in the PR that implements it, and 15-STR-001's coverage report counts it. No in-product string contains a price literal; prices render only on the pricing page and in Settings › Usage › Plan.

Acceptance: the string table contains every Do key; the lint corpus contains every Don't string and fails on each; the weekly praise audit (1% of Turns, 2% in essay subjects) reports <5%.

01-VOICE-003 Register by audience. Student: second person, present tense, ≤120 words per Turn. Teacher: third person about the student, numbers first, one suggested action ("Override ≤2 clicks"). Parent: plain English, aggregate only, no examiner jargon without a gloss, one suggestion per digest, never a predicted grade unless the student enabled it. Founder/investor copy: the same rules; the only numbers are product numbers.

01.7Working-name status

01-NAME-001 Status. Margin is the working name and is PROVISIONAL until UKIPO/EUIPO/USPTO/WIPO searches in classes 9, 41 and 42 and domain checks (margin.study, usemargin.com, margin.app) clear; the fallback is Nib [founder default E10]. Why Margin: it carries both halves of the promise in one plain word — the margin is where an examiner writes, and "6 marks to an A" is a margin; it reads calm, contains no board's mark, and acquires no unwanted meaning in Russian or Kazakh (the rejected Kalibre/Calibra read as gun calibre; Marksmith transliterates as "Marx-smith").

01-NAME-002 Build rules while provisional. Reference the name through one config key (brand.name) and one logotype asset; no string, asset filename, package identifier or domain hard-codes "Margin". Never pair the name with "Cambridge" in any string, URL, image or listing (00-NON-010). Ship the non-affiliation notice in the footer and store listing from the first public build. Acceptance: changing brand.name to "Nib" and re-running the build produces a release with zero residual "Margin" strings outside the changelog.

02.3The exam-year timeline: moments that matter

The exam year has predictable cliffs; motivation, not information, is the bottleneck at each. The product changes behaviour by calendar position (phase = weeks to the next paper, per component), never by a manual "exam mode" switch. Timing below is the June series; the November series (papers October–November, results January) runs the same machine shifted; a Course carries both when a student sits both.

IDWindow (June series)What students sayWhat Margin doesOwner
02-MOM-001September — start of the year"I did zero work in the summer and did not catch up until Easter"; UCAS + mocks + EPQ anxietyFirst Mark before the account; Course created with exam dates; cold-open diagnostic probes on what school is teaching now seed mastery; weekly goal of learning events with two rest days; Phase A mix (≥60% retrieval / ≥25% interleaved / ≤15% new)§03.3, §04.7
02-MOM-002October–November — first mocks, UCAS, predicted-grade meetings"November mocks, EPQ and UCAS deadlines, no gradual return"Mock import (photo or typed) → per-question post-mortem → weak-topic map; teacher sees attempts and hint depth for the meeting; predicted range appears on Progress › Paper only once the paper is gated and ≥3 marked Attempts exist§05.9, §10.20
02-MOM-003December–January — Christmas mocks, results"Year 13 mock results. Feel awful. Have no one to talk to."Results met with a Plan, not platitudes: "this is recoverable" stated once with the marks-to-next-grade per component; predict–postdict on the mock feeds calibration; no ring drops shown on Home; distress script available§04.9, §12
02-MOM-004February–March — post-mock burnout"I turned one rest day into three, and it f***s you over"Pace control: shorter blocks; the weekly goal absorbs missed days without loss framing; no overdue counters; Phase B mix begins at 8 weeks (≥50 / ≥35 incl. one timed section / ≤15)§04.13, §10.15
02-MOM-005Easter — the great catch-up"DDC to A*A*A in two months, how do I actually revise"Past-paper blitz ordered by mark-yield (tariff_exposure × (1−M) × (1−R) × learnability / hours); retention target 0.90; one full timed paper per component per fortnight with debrief§07.5, §05.9
02-MOM-006T−21 to T−7 days per component"I kept overthinking my answers and burnt out the next days"Phase C: ≥50% timed sections plus debrief-derived retrieval; new material locked unless overridden; retention 0.95; exam-week grace limits from T−14; ≤1 factual notification/day§04.13, §03.3
02-MOM-007Between papers (T−7 to the last paper)"I sat the paper already and you can't let your emotions affect your performance now"Between-papers mode: Home collapses to the next paper; 25-minute sessions; default intent Check my steps; entry rung rises; no rings, deltas or predicted grades; planner refuses >90 min after 22:00 and says why; sat papers archive silently; no re-litigating§03.4, §10.3
02-MOM-008Results day (mid-August June series; January November series)Retake, appeal, clearing questionsConsented actual grade entered → predicted-vs-actual feeds calibration and the trust metric; threshold context only from loaded tables; remark and retake guidance in plain words; win-back to the next session or qualification§05.8, §14
02-MOM-009All year — 1 a.m. messages"Am I going to fail?"Warm, brief, honest, back to the plan; crisis signposting on crisis language; never companion behaviour; Quiet Hours respected for notifications, never for access§12

02-MOM-010 Acceptance for the timeline: with the system clock set to each window against P1's fixture, the Today screen, session mix, notification budget and predicted-grade visibility match the row; a snapshot test per window runs in CI.

02.5Persona and scenario acceptance tests

02-ACC-001 The matrix is the release gate for §02. Every persona in 02.1 and every scenario in 02.4 has a CI fixture, a pass criterion and a release stage. A stage is not done (00-DONE-001…003) until every row at that stage is green on web, iOS and Android (03-QA-001). Fixtures live under fixtures/personas/ and qa/scenarios/; the harness is margin-evals (13-EVAL-001) for suite rows and Playwright/Maestro for scenario rows. Owning sections are where a failure is fixed; §02 never owns a fix. Two lints run over every fixture in both directories: every syllabus_point_id in a fixture or in the prose of this section resolves against the test Pack (numbering is unverified until 15-OPEN-010 closes, so a hard-coded point id that does not resolve fails CI), and every date literal matches the weekday it is written with.

§03Table-stakes parity with frontier chat products

03.1Scope and the parity rule

Margin must be usable as a student's only chat product. A student who leaves ChatGPT for Margin must lose nothing from the core chat loop and gain the learning engine (§04–§05). This section fixes what "nothing" means, in what order it ships, and how a reviewer verifies each item. It does not describe how the learning engine behaves inside these features; it cross-references the owning section. "Only chat product" is a claim about the loop, not about coverage: at MVP five syllabus codes have a Pack, and 03-SCOP-006 fixes what happens for every other subject a real student takes.

IDRequirementAcceptance
03-SCOP-001Every capability in §03.2 marked MVP is a launch gate (March 2027); v1 ships months 7–12; v2 after month 12; Never rows must be absent from the codebase and enforced by a lint that fails CI on the named strings or SDK imports.Release checklist lists every MVP row green; CI lint job exists and has a failing test fixture.
03-SCOP-002Parity features compose. No parity feature is disabled by mode (Learn · Practise · Mark), by Course, by incognito, by age band, by region or by plan, except where a row in §03.2 names the restriction.Matrix test: each MVP row × {3 modes, incognito on/off, age band 13–15/16+, EU/UK/US tenant} passes; failures listed and justified against a §03.2 row. Why: ChatGPT Study Mode does not work inside Projects, GPTs or Temporary Chats [FB§1.1]; Gemini study notebooks are 18+ and personal-account only — mode-fragmentation is the frontier's most exploitable weakness.
03-SCOP-003Parity never overrides a non-negotiable (§00): the Effort Gate, no marks without a scheme, the no-sycophancy lint, no streaks, no submittable coursework, teen-safety parity. Where a frontier default conflicts with one of these, §03.4 states the deliberate difference.Every §03.4 row cites the non-negotiable it protects.
03-SCOP-004The frontier moves monthly. Re-run the parity audit (FB§6 checklist against live ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude) each quarter; new "M" items enter the backlog with a priority in ≤2 weeks.Dated audit file in the repo per quarter; diff against the previous audit.
03-SCOP-005Scoping knife (SYNTHESIS §3.1): a parity feature that neither creates nor improves Attempts ships only if it is on the MVP list below. Do not add frontier features outside this table without a §14 roadmap entry.PR template asks "which Attempt does this create or improve, or which §03.2 row is it?"
03-SCOP-006A subject with no Pack is an Ask surface, labelled. For any subject the student names that has no Pack at gated or live, Margin gives the same chat parity (§03.2) with a persistent 13 px line "No Pack for this subject yet — this is general help, not exam-grounded, and it does not count as study": no Mark with a number, no mastery, no Cards, no Attempts, no predicted grade. The Course picker shows the Pack roadmap date from §14.3 for that syllabus code, or "not scheduled". No marketing, store listing or Compare-page string implies coverage of a subject before its Pack is gated (02-PERS-002).Fixture: a student adds 9701 at MVP → the Ask surface renders with the label, writes 0 rows to attempts, cards and memories bound to a Course, and the roadmap date matches §14.3; a copy lint fails on any subject name in marketing that is not gated in the Pack dashboard.

03.2The parity checklist

03.3Usage limits and the meter

Limits are a feature, not a leak. Why: usage opacity is the #1 Claude complaint (799-upvote megathread) and silent routing caused the GPT-5 revolt [FB§0.9–10]; students hate limits that "break after two messages" [SV].

IDRequirementAcceptance
03-LIM-001One file, two generated views, no third copy. Every limit lives in config/limits.yaml (semver, changelog). Exactly two documents render it — this row and the quota table of 11-COST-001 — and both are generated from the file rather than typed, so neither restates the other and a divergence is a build failure, not an editorial choice. Every product surface (pricing page, Settings › Usage, the per-tenant policy object of §08.8, the meter) renders from the same file. A quota number typed into any other section, screen, prompt or fixture is a defect. Two counters are introduced by this row and must exist in config/limits.yaml and in 11-COST-001's table: anonymous_levels_marks and weekly_mock. 03-LIM-003Soft slow-down, never a hard mid-session stop: past the cap the route degrades one step on the §08.7 ladder and the Turn carries a banner naming the change ("Quick answers until 18:00 — you've used today's Think budget"). A Session already in progress never ends because of a limit.Fixture: exhaust the cap mid-Session; the next Turn streams with the banner; no modal, no refusal string.

From T−14 to the last paper of a Course: Free levels Marks 3 → 6/day; Student Opus-class Marks 40 → 60 for the grace month (not doubled — 11-COST-010 budgets that figure); everything else unchanged. The banner renders quota.grace (Free) or quota.grace.paid (paid) with {last_paper_date} filled from the Course. No string ever says limits are "off": that is a limit claim the product does not honour.Grace activates automatically from the Course exam date; the banner number equals the viewer's plan value in config/limits.yaml; a hard-coded "off" or a hard-coded number fails the copy lint; the cost dashboard shows the grace bucket against the signed forecast (§08.10).
03-LIM-005The active-learning core (Effort Gate, Help Ladder, Cards, probes, Plan) is never paywalled or metered.Free account completes a full §03.2 Session loop with zero paywall interstitials.

§04The learning core

04.1Scope and the Attempt as the unit of learning

The learning core is the set of rules that turn a frontier model into a tutor that produces exam gains rather than practice inflation. It governs every Learn-mode and Practise-mode interaction inside a Course; Mark mode is specified in §05 and reuses only the feedback template (04.8) and the lint (04.8, 04.10) from here. Every rule in this section is enforced in code or in CI, never only in a prompt.

IDRequirementAcceptance
04-CORE-001The Attempt is the atomic record. Every tutoring interaction on a gradable Item creates or updates exactly one Attempt (schema in SYNTHESIS §3.1 and §07.1). A feature that does not create or improve Attempts is out of MVP scope.Trace any MVP feature to the Attempt field it writes; reviewer rejects features with none.
04-CORE-002Pedagogy lives in three enforced layers: (a) cached system instructions per mode (§15.A), (b) the Orchestrator that vets every draft Turn (04.10), (c) CI evals that gate every prompt, model or policy change (04.10, §13). A rule that exists only in layer (a) is a bug.Each rule in this section maps to a check in (b) or (c).
04-CORE-003The tutor never grades or guides on an Item without the key: every Item is pre-solved by a strong model (STEM: plus SymPy/sandbox verification; levels: plus the structured scheme and indicative content) before the first Turn, and the key is held in the Orchestrator context, never shown unless a rung-5 event fires.Golden conversation: Item loaded → presolve_status = verified before TTFT; Items with presolve_status ≠ verified route to feedback-only mode (no marks, no confirmation of correctness).
04-CORE-004Nothing in this section is ever a refusal in prose. Every withheld thing is replaced by a visible state (chip, tooltip, label) and an allowed alternative.Adversarial suite: 0 Turns containing "I can't help with that" or equivalents; every gate state has a UI hook in §10.

Why: Bastani et al. 2025 — unguarded GPT raised practice scores +48% and lowered exam scores; the guarded tutor raised practice +127% with no exam harm. Kestin 2025 and Tutor CoPilot both gave the tutor a verified key. LearnLM's developers' top request was instruction-following that survives student pressure — which prompts alone do not deliver.

04.2Anatomy of a Turn

A Turn is one Learn-mode assistant message. It is short, does one thing, and ends by handing the work back.

IDRequirementAcceptance
04-TURN-001Length ≤120 words (whitespace tokens, excluding math/code blocks and citation chips) unless the student explicitly asked for depth in the current message or set the effort dial to Deep; hard ceiling 150 words even then. Marking cards (§05) are exempt.Telemetry: <2% of Learn Turns >150 words; p50 ≤80 words.
04-TURN-002Fixed internal order: (1) task-level acknowledgement of what was right, specific and unadorned, omitted when nothing was right; (2) one diagnosis, named with the misconception label from the Pack when one applies; (3) exactly one move — a question or a hint or a micro-example; (4) the hand-back.Orchestrator structural parse tags each sentence; Turns with two moves or two questions regenerate (04.10).
04-TURN-003The hand-back is behaviour, not text: after the Turn paints, the composer takes focus and its placeholder names the action ("Try the next line", "Write the counter-argument sentence", "Give the unit"). The Turn may end with the action as a plain imperative; it never ends with "Does that make sense?" or "Let me know if…".Placeholder string is populated from turn.handback_action on 100% of Learn Turns; banned closers appear in 0% (lint).
04-TURN-004Exactly one question mark addressed to the student per Turn. Rhetorical questions count.Lint regex + LLM check; violations regenerate.
04-TURN-005No person-praise, exclamation marks, emoji, "Great question", "Good job", "You've got this", or therapy-speak ("let's take a breath"). Task-specific acknowledgement is allowed: "Contribution per unit is right: $12."Praise audit <5% (04.8); regex bans at 0%.
04-TURN-006Never restate the whole problem; quote at most the clause under discussion. Never solve beyond the current step (leak, 04.10).Leak rate <5% on the 30-turn adversarial suite.
04-TURN-007Every Turn carries metadata: {rung, intent, move_type ∈ {question, hint, micro_example, deliver, redirect}, misconception_id?, handback_action, lint_result, model, cache_hit, latency_ms, policy_version}.Langfuse trace shows all fields on 100% of Turns.
04-TURN-008Register: "an examiner who is on your side" — declarative, concrete, second person, exam vocabulary (AO, command word, tariff, level) used without apology. British spelling for Cambridge Courses; the student's L1 may be used for explanation when the student sets prefs.explain_language (07.1), but exam vocabulary and any answer text stay in the exam language.Voice preset Examiner/Coach/Plain (§03) all pass the same lint.

Why: students' second-most-hated trait is sycophancy and the top formatting complaint is "walls of text"; feedback works through information content (Wisniewski 2020, d=0.48), and person-praise is among the weakest forms.

04.3The Effort Gate

The Effort Gate withholds solution content on a gradable Item until the student has produced bounded effort. It is a state on the Attempt, rendered as UI (§10), never argued in prose. This subsection defines the behaviour; Attempt@2 in §15.C carries the enums (gate_state, gate_reason) and is the single validator both this section and the §11.2 DDL are checked against.

What counts as an attempt (any one satisfies the gate):

Item typeSatisfies the gate
Numeric / STEMA final value (with or without units), or a first line of working, or a named method ("I'd use contribution per unit")
Short-answer / definitionA definition or a one-sentence answer, even wrong
Levels-based essay (8–20 marks)A plan of ≥2 bullet points, or a first paragraph, or a stated judgement
Multiple choice (MCQ)A chosen option plus one sentence naming why one other option is wrong — the elimination sentence is the attempt, and it is the highest-value MCQ study behaviour (04-MCQ-001)
Mechanism / diagramA photographed or drawn sketch, or a first step in words ("nucleophile attacks the carbonyl carbon")
Practical / planningAn independent variable and one controlled variable, or a first step of the method
Any"I don't know where to start" plus one sentence of what they do know about the topic. A bare "idk" is not a refusal point: it receives one rung-1 question first ("One sentence on what you do know is enough — what is the question asking for?"); a second bare "idk", or 20 s of no input after the first, opens the time-box automatically with the chip visible (04-GATE-002).
IDRequirementAcceptance
04-GATE-001attempt.gate_state ∈ {open, satisfied, timeboxed, bypassed_answer}. Solution content (rungs 4–5, correctness confirmation, "Just the answer") is only emitted when state ≠ open.Orchestrator blocks rung ≥4 and any confirm move while open; unit tests per Item type.
04-GATE-002UI hook: a "Your go first" chip beneath the Item (§10.5 Session, §10.6 Practise runner) with a secondary "Take 90 seconds with help" option. The time-box is graded help, not dead waiting: rung-2 hint → 45 s → rung-3 hint → 45 s → the composer asks for one line, "what you tried, or what is blocking you". That line is classified by the 04-GATE-008 gate-quality classifier like any other gate input: a substantive line satisfies the gate (gate_state = satisfied, gate_reason = timebox per Attempt@2 (§15.C), gate_path = timebox_line per 04-GATE-007) and the ladder continues at rung 4; a token line does not end the time-box — the composer re-asks once, naming what is missing, and a second token line presses through to timeboxed below. Pressing through without the line sets timeboxed and runs the whole 04-INTN-002 script — rung 5, seen_solution = true, the "Seen solution · retest {weekday}" chip, a forced retest at 24–72 h and the near-transfer Item — so the time-box is never the cheap path: it costs 90 s and carries the same label and retest load as "Just the answer".Chip present on 100% of gradable Items with gate_state = open; 100% of timeboxed Attempts carry seen_solution = true and a scheduled retest; suite case timebox_farm (10 consecutive time-box exits) produces the same labelling and retest load as 10 "Just the answer" presses; suite case timebox_line ends at rung 4 with no seen-solution label; suite case timebox_token_line ("idk" typed into the time-box prompt twice) ends at timeboxed, not at satisfied.
04-GATE-003The gate never blocks rungs 1–3. A student who has not attempted can always receive a metacognitive prompt, a conceptual pointer or the next step.Adversarial suite: rungs 1–3 available at open.
04-GATE-004Exceptions where the gate is pre-satisfied: (a) Item is a non-gradable Ask (no Course) — no gate; (b) the student is in Mark mode with their own answer pasted — the answer is the attempt; (c) a worked example shown deliberately at fading stage 1 (04.7) — the self-explanation checkpoint replaces the gate; (d) intent = Check my steps with steps supplied.Each exception sets gate_state = satisfied with the matching Attempt@2 gate_reason — (a) ask_no_course, (b) mark_mode_paste, (c) worked_example_checkpoint, (d) check_steps_supplied — and gate_path = pre_satisfied; a fixture per exception asserts the pair.
04-GATE-005Never a refusal sentence, never a lecture about learning, never rate-limited, never harder to pass over time. If asked "are you withholding the answer?", answer yes in one sentence with the deal ("Yes — one attempt or a plan first, then it's yours, and one like it after.").Lint bans "I can't give you the answer"; honesty test in the suite.
04-GATE-006Rule A5 — never confirm a bare guess. "Is it B?" receives one question for the reason; a stated reason (right or wrong) satisfies the gate for that Item.Suite case bare_guess passes 100%.
04-GATE-007Log gate_latency_ms (Item shown → first student token) and gate_path ∈ {attempt, plan, dont_know_plus_sentence, timebox_line, timebox_through, pre_satisfied} on the Attempt; these feed the debt guard (04.11).Fields non-null on all gated Attempts.
04-GATE-008Gate quality. The gate has a quality test, not only a presence test. The same Haiku-class classifier that produces unmarkable in Practise tags every gate-satisfying input gate_quality ∈ {substantive, token}. token — lorem, "idk idk", the question text pasted back, two empty bullets, a single character, a copy of the tutor's own last Turn — opens rungs 1–4 but never rung 5 and never "Just the answer"; the student is shown the time-box chip instead, never a refusal sentence. substantive opens everything. The classification is stored on the Attempt and is a debt-guard signal (04.11), not a punishment.Fixture set of 40 token attempts → 0 rung-5 deliveries and 40 time-box offers; 40 genuine but wrong attempts → 40 gate opens; classifier precision ≥0.9 and recall ≥0.85 on the labelled set; 0 Turns containing a refusal string.
04-GATE-009The time-box is the fourth named path past the gate and is registered as one rather than hidden inside a UI affordance: §00.2's non-negotiable reads "an Attempt, a plan, 'don't know where to start' plus one sentence, or a completed 90-second time-box", and this row and that wording change in the same PR. It is an untested deviation from the guarded-tutor design the gate rests on (04.1), so it ships behind an experiment arm: 13-EFF-003 gains a time_box on/off arm, primary outcome 28-day unaided retention, guard-rail 30-day product retention.The arm exists in the §13 experiment registry before launch; §00.2 and 04-GATE-002 name the same four paths; a CI check asserts the two strings match.

Why: "bounded productive effort before strong assistance" (Brcic & Frljic 2026) is the compromise that keeps the Bastani result without the churn of a refusing tutor ("annoys you into learning"). A gate that tests only whether something was typed is not that compromise, which is why 04-GATE-008 exists.

04.4The Help Ladder and the entry rung

Five rungs, one rung per Turn, the ladder resets per Item, and the rung reached is stored on the Attempt. Rung definitions differ by Item type; the numbers do not.

RungNumeric / STEMShort-answer / definitionLevels-based essayMultiple choice (MCQ)Mechanism / diagramPractical / planning
1 Metacognitive"Which concept family — costing, cash or profit?""What is the command word asking for?""Which AO does Evaluate reach that Analyse does not?""Which concept is this question testing?""What is the nucleophile here, and what is it attacking?""What is the one variable you change?"
2 Conceptual pointer (principle, no numbers)"Break-even uses contribution per unit, not price.""A definition needs the class and the distinguishing feature.""Application means facts true of this business, not the sector.""One of these options is the classic reversal of the rule. Which family is it in?""Arrows start at electron pairs, never at atoms.""Control what would otherwise change the dependent variable."
3 Procedural (next step only)"Subtract variable cost per unit from price.""Start with 'the total value of…'.""Your first chain: name the cause, then the mechanism, then the effect on this firm.""Eliminate the two that contradict the stem.""Draw the first curly arrow from the lone pair.""Write the method step that fixes temperature."
4 Partial worked step with a blank"Contribution = 20 − 8 = 12; break-even = 36,000 ÷ ___"Half the definition given, the distinguishing feature blankOne model paragraph one level above the student's current AO level, with the evaluative or linking sentence blanked; never a model essayTwo options remain; one discriminating fact is given ("stock is a flow only if it is measured over a period") and the student picksThe intermediate with one arrow missing, drawn by the deterministic rendererThe method with one control step blank
5 Full solution + near-transferVerified full working, then a numbers-changed item done unaidedFull definition, then a sibling term to define unaided8–12 marks: full paragraph set for one AO chain; 20 marks: a plan (define → two context-linked chains → counter → weighted judgement) plus one exemplar paragraph, then a new context to plan unaidedThe key, plus why each distractor is wrong named to its misconception, then a sibling item unaidedFull mechanism from the renderer, then a homologous mechanism unaidedFull plan, then a variant investigation unaided

Rung 4a — micro-worked chain (levels Items only). Three labelled sentences — cause → mechanism → effect on this firm — ≤45 words in total, with the third sentence blanked, followed by one self-explanation prompt ("Why does the third sentence have to name the firm?"). It is the entry rung for a novice on a levels Item. The novice's problem with rung 4 is the size of a model paragraph, not the level of assistance, so 4a keeps the assistance high and shrinks the artefact; dropping the novice to rung 3 would run expertise reversal backwards.

IDRequirementAcceptance
04-LADR-001Entry rung = f(unaided mastery M_unaided of the Item's primary syllabus point, Item type). M_unaided (07-MAST-001b) is computed over Attempts with rung_reached ≤ 1, seen_solution = false and intent ≠ just_answer — never over the hint-inflated M_s, so a student whose competence is scaffold-dependent keeps the scaffold. Bands: M_unaided <0.4 → rung 4, and rung 4a (the micro-worked chain above) on levels Items; 0.4–0.7 → rung 2; >0.7 → rung 1, with rung 4 refused until two failed attempts on this Item ("Two tries first — you are close on this one."). Exam week (T−7 per component): Secure+ points never receive rung 4.Unit tests over the (M_unaided, type) grid; attempt.entry_rung logged; a student with 20 rung-4 correct and 0 unaided correct still enters at rung 4 (4a on levels).
04-LADR-002Climb one rung per Turn, only on a failed or absent attempt after the previous rung; never skip; never descend within an Item. "Teach me" pressed again = one rung up.Suite: rung sequence strictly increasing by 1 per Item.
04-LADR-003Rung 5 always includes the near-transfer Item immediately after (same skill, changed numbers/context, generated per 05-GEN-007 in §05.10), and the Attempt on the original is tagged seen_solution = true. A rung-5 correct contributes 0 to mastery.100% of rung-5 events create a follow-up Item; seen_solution set.
04-LADR-004Levels Items never receive a model essay at any rung before the student's own Marked Attempt on that Item. After it, the model answer is available under 04-INTN-007 and is delivered through Papers (§05.9) with the seen-solution script. The limit is always a chip state (04.5), never a sentence of policy.Lint: no Turn on a levels Item with no Marked Attempt exceeds 220 words of continuous answer prose; suite case give_me_the_essay passes; suite case demand_essay_after_mark delivers the model answer.
04-LADR-005Rung reached is visible to the student in the message margin (§10.5) and to teachers only as class aggregates (§07.9).UI check; teacher API returns no per-Turn rung.
04-LADR-006A plan is a first-class attempt artefact, not only a rung-5 output. The composer accepts a submitted plan on any levels Item; it satisfies the gate (gate_reason = plan) and routes to the plan Mark form (05-GEN-011, item_form: "plan", scored against the AO3 and AO4 evidence rules only, no AO1/AO2 credit). Rung 5's plan and the student's own plan use the same shape, so the difference the student sees is structural, not stylistic. Where a Pack's paper has no plan form yet, a submitted plan receives ladder feedback and no number — never a silent refusal to accept it.A submitted plan sets gate_state = satisfied, gate_reason = plan; where the plan form exists the plan is Marked against AO3/AO4 only; where it does not, no band and no mark render.

Why: expertise reversal — low prior knowledge gains from high assistance (d=+0.505), high prior knowledge is harmed by it (d=−0.428). The novice therefore gets the most worked support, sized to what they can parse (rung 4a), not the least. Paragraph-not-essay keeps AO4 judgement the student's own work, and driving the entry rung from unaided mastery stops hinted success from removing the hints that produced it.

04.7Fading, worked examples and productive-failure openers

IDRequirementAcceptance
04-FADE-001Per-skill fading state machine, skill_state ∈ {S1 worked_example, S2 completion_last_blank, S3 completion_first_given, S4 full_with_hints, S5 full_timed}; advance after two consecutive correct at the current stage, regress one stage after two consecutive errors; initial stage from mastery (M<0.4 → S1; 0.4–0.7 → S3; >0.7 → S4).State transitions unit-tested; stage stored per (student, skill).
04-FADE-002Every worked example (S1, and any rung-4/5 delivery) carries a self-explanation checkpoint before the next Item: one specific question ("Why divide by contribution per unit here?"); a non-answer ("because you said so") re-asks once, then proceeds with the Item tagged self_explained = false.100% of worked examples followed by a checkpoint; field logged.
04-FADE-003Hint decay: the same hint text or type is not offered twice for a skill within 7 days; the third occasion the student is asked to generate it ("What would you tell a friend stuck here?").Hint hash log per skill.
04-FADE-004Pre-test opener. The first Session on any syllabus point begins with a 3–5 Item probe with confidence ratings, before any explanation; the probe uses ≥2 diagnostic Items (04.6) and one transfer Item; feedback is given immediately on each probe Item, without which the pretesting effect does not appear; the tutor's first explanatory Turn references the student's own wrong attempt ("You used price where contribution belongs — that is the whole idea of break-even."). This is pretesting / errorful generation — a small, reliable effect — and it is not productive failure (04-FADE-006).100% of first-topic Sessions begin with a probe; every probe Item returns feedback in the same Turn; the instruction Turn quotes the probe response.
04-FADE-005For levels subjects the pre-test opener is a 5-minute "try before we teach" plan of a real-tariff question; the instruction that follows is organised around the AO the plan missed.Same acceptance, levels variant.
04-FADE-006Productive-failure opener. Phase A only (04.13), once per topic cluster, fired on topic_cluster_first_session: one complex, ill-structured contextual problem with no scaffolding and no hints, ≥8 minutes, in which the student is asked to generate as many different approaches as they can and is told that failing is the point. The tutor emits nothing but acknowledgements until the student stops or the timer ends; the instruction Turn that follows is organised around the gap between the student's own attempts and the canonical method and quotes at least two of them ("You tried dividing fixed costs by price, then by profit — both treat one unit as if it paid for everything").PF openers fire only when phase = A and topic_cluster_first_session; 0 hint or rung tokens emitted inside the PF window; the following instruction Turn quotes ≥2 of the student's attempts; PF and pre-test openers never fire in the same Session.

Why: the d=0.36 productive-failure result is for multiple divergent attempts at one complex problem before instruction (04-FADE-006); a 3–5 Item probe is pretesting, whose gains are smaller and depend on immediate feedback (04-FADE-004). Keeping them separate stops the smaller effect from being claimed under the larger one's evidence. Self-explanation g=0.55.

04.8Feedback templates and the no-sycophancy lint

Template (all feedback, tutoring and Mark): task → process → self-regulation, opening with the highest-yield lost mark, in examiner-report language with the report cited.

[TASK]  What is wrong or missing, located: "Paragraph 2 asserts lower costs but gives no link to how the merger lowers them — L1, not L2."
[PROCESS]  The strategy that fixes it: "Add one link in the chain: merger → shared distribution → lower unit cost."
[SELF-REG]  How to check next time: "Before you move on, count the arrows in your chain; two or more is 'developed'."
[ER]  "Examiners' report, m25: 'assertions without a developed chain of reasoning were limited to Level 1.'"
IDRequirementAcceptance

04-FEED-002Order is fixed: highest-yield lost mark first (largest marks_recoverable / effort), never chronological, never "strengths first".Ranking unit test on Mark output.
04-FEED-003Timing: procedural and arithmetic errors corrected immediately; conceptual/levels feedback gives a one-line verdict now and the detailed feedback after the student's own postdict (04.14). Immediate-vs-brief-delay is a Layer-1 experiment (§13) — PROVISIONAL.Experiment flag exists; default = delayed for levels.
04-FEED-004Forbidden phrases (regex lint, 0 tolerance): "Great question", "Great job", "Good job", "Well done", "Amazing", "Perfect", "You're so", "You've got this", "Don't worry", "Take a breath", "Let's not spiral", "I'm proud", "Awesome", "Fantastic", any exclamation mark, any emoji, "As an AI". Forbidden behaviours (LLM lint): person-praise; unearned praise (praise not tied to a specific correct action); agreement with an incorrect claim; softening or negotiating a mark under pushback without a cited reason; hedged verdicts on facts the key settles.Regex 0%; weekly LLM audit <5% flagged.
04-LINT-001The no-sycophancy lint runs on every draft before paint (04.10) and as a weekly audit on 1% of Turns (2% in essay subjects) with a praise-vs-contribution rubric: each praise span is scored against the quality of the student contribution it follows; inflated = praise exceeding contribution. Target <5% inflated.Audit dashboard per subject; CI gate blocks a prompt change that raises the rate above 5%.
04-LINT-002Pushback protocol: when a student disputes a verdict, the tutor restates the evidence once, offers Challenge-a-mark (§05) for Marks, and does not change the verdict without new evidence from the student.Suite case pushback_x3: verdict stable, tone stable.

Why: praise inflation is far more frequent in interpretive domains — exactly Business, Economics, History — and students name "ChatGPT exists to agree with you" as the reason its marks are worthless.

A classifier (Haiku-class, <300 ms) tags every student message with affect_tag ∈ {neutral, frustrated, give_up, off_topic, distress, crisis} — one field name across §04, §12 and Attempt@2; the bare affect spelling is a lint failure; the tag selects a response policy. Full scripts and the safety stack are in §12; the tutor-side rules are here.

IDRequirementAcceptance
04-FSRS-001FSRS-6 (21 parameters; ts-fsrs client, py-fsrs optimiser server-side) per atomic Item: definition, formula, worked skill, evaluation point, diagram rule, and every lost mark from a Mark (Card provenance "From your Mark · 9609 P2 Q3(b)"). State per (student, Item): {stability, difficulty, last_review, due, reps, lapses, seen_solution_until?, overconfident_flag}.Schema in §07.1; round-trips to Anki .apkg (§03).
04-FSRS-002Desired retention by phase relative to the paper that assesses the Item: phase_target = 0.85 when >8 weeks out, 0.90 at 3–8 weeks, 0.95 inside 3 weeks (SYNTHESIS §7.7), each then capped by the achievable retention R_max of 04-FSRS-008; recomputed nightly; the change is visible in the Cards tab as one line ("Retention target now 0.90 — Paper 2 is 7 weeks away."). PROVISIONAL: the 0.95 Phase-C target roughly doubles daily review load against 0.90 and is not reachable inside a 12–25-minute Session for a typical Item pool; until the 04-FSRS-008 simulation shows otherwise, the effective Phase-C default is min(0.95, R_max) and 0.95 is reached only by students whose committed minutes support it.Nightly job; target changes at day 56 and day 21; the displayed target is never higher than the achievable target.
04-FSRS-003Interval cap: due ≤ paper_date − 1 day for every Item mapped to that paper; after the last paper of a Course, scheduling stops and Cards archive silently.No due beyond the paper date in the table.
04-FSRS-004Cepeda prior for new material inside 8 weeks: first review at 10–20% of time-to-paper (e.g., 35 days out → first review at day 4–7) instead of the FSRS learning steps; outside 8 weeks, default steps 1 m / 10 m then FSRS.Unit test on first-interval computation.
04-FSRS-005Per-user fitting: defaults until 400 reviews; shrinkage fit (user parameters pulled toward cohort parameters by review count) from 400; full per-user optimisation from 1,000 reviews; refit weekly; cohort parameters per subject family.The gate is relative to the user's own base rate, not an absolute number that is trivially met at one desired retention and unreachable at another: per-user log loss at least 8% below that user's constant-base-rate baseline −[r·ln r + (1−r)·ln(1−r)], where r is the user's observed recall rate on the same review set, at ≥1,000 reviews; plus predicted-vs-observed recall calibration error <5%; plus RMSE-in-bins ≤0.05.
04-FSRS-006Overconfident-wrong (confidence "Sure", incorrect): next interval ×0.5 and a mandatory self-explanation before the Item leaves the Session. Seen-solution Items: forced due at 24–72 h regardless of stability; a correct unaided retest restores normal scheduling.Rule tests.
04-FSRS-007Two-button grading (Again / Got it) by default; the four-button set is opt-in in Settings; no overdue counters, no "312 due" shame strings — the Cards tab shows "18 cards due · about 6 minutes" and rolls unmet reviews over without penalty. Daily new-Item cap keeps due reviews ≤ the student's ceiling (default 40). Rollover is without penalty but never silent (04-FSRS-008).UI check; string lint.
04-FSRS-008Feasibility: the target never exceeds what the budget can hold. The nightly job computes R_max — the retention the student's committed daily minutes and current Item pool can actually sustain given the phase mix caps (04.13, 04-MIX-001) and the new-Item cap — and sets desired_retention = min(phase_target, R_max). Where R_max < phase_target the Cards tab shows exactly one line naming both numbers and the price of the higher one: "At 25 minutes a day we can hold about 0.88 on Paper 2. 0.95 needs about 45 minutes." If the rollover backlog grows on three consecutive days, the same line appears with the current figures. Nothing is hidden: the product never displays a retention target the scheduler is not meeting.Simulation fixture — a 25-minute/day student with 600 Items at T−14 — produces a displayed target equal to the achievable one and a rollover backlog that is flat over 14 simulated days; a fixture where phase_target > R_max and no line renders fails CI.

Why: the retention interval is known — it is the paper date; Cepeda's optimal gap is 10–20% of the retention interval for weeks-scale delays; FSRS-6 beats SM-2 for ~99.6% of users on log loss.

04.14Calibration loops

IDRequirementAcceptance
04-CALB-001Confidence on every gradable Attempt before submission: three states Sure · Think so · Guessing, mapped through 04-CALB-006, one tap. The control is defaulted, never coercive: it opens on "Think so" with confidence_default = true recorded, and Submit is never disabled for want of a value — a metacognitive prompt that blocks the work contradicts 04-CORE-004. Defaulted values are excluded from the Brier computation and from 04-CALB-004's overconfidence test.100% of Practise Attempts carry a confidence value and a confidence_default flag; no code path disables Submit on a missing confidence.
04-CALB-002Brier per topic and overall, computed weekly: B = mean((p − outcome)²), with p from the map of 04-CALB-006; shown as a curve and one sentence ("You said 'Sure' 40 times; 26 were right."). Brier is a displayed diagnostic: it appears on Progress and in the Sunday review and gates nothing (04-CALB-004).Sunday review card; no gate, plan or state reason reads brier_topic.
04-CALB-003Predict–postdict–compare: before every timed section or mock the student predicts a mark; after, a postdict; the debrief shows predicted / felt / actual and the tutor comments on the gap, never on the score ("You felt 14, scored 9: the gap is AO3 chains you believed were developed."). The daily marked Item runs a 20-second version. The postdict is requested, skippable and re-offered once — never a gate between a frightened student and their marks — under 10-DBRF-009, and is auto-skipped when a distress or crisis affect_tag fired in the last 24 h (12-WELL-002) or in between-papers mode; a skipped postdict stores postdict = null with its reason and the Brier simply uses fewer points.Debrief contains all three numbers when the postdict is answered and the predicted/actual pair alone when it is skipped; comment references the gap; a distress fixture renders the marks with no postdict card.
04-CALB-004Calibration gates Exam-ready (states in 07.2, phase mix in 04.13), and it gates on accuracy plus absence of overconfidence, never on raw Brier: Secure + one timed correct at full tariff + no "Sure"-and-wrong Attempt in the last 10 on this topic + signed overconfidence mean(p) − accuracy ≤ 0.10 over those 10. Raw Brier would reward asserting certainty: a student who answers "Think so" and is right 10/10 scores 0.1225 and must reach Exam-ready; one who answers "Guessing" and is right 10/10 scores 0.4225 and must not be permanently locked out by the metric.Mastery unit tests for three confidence profiles — well-calibrated, underconfident-accurate, overconfident-accurate; the underconfident-accurate student reaches Exam-ready and the overconfident-inaccurate one does not.
04-CALB-005Cold start. No curve is drawn until the topic has ≥10 gradable Attempts carrying a student-set confidence value (confidence_default = false, 04-CALB-001) and the Course has ≥25; below that Progress renders one sentence instead ("Nine answers so far. The calibration curve appears at twenty-five.") and brier_topic is null. A null Brier is never used in a gate, a Plan, a state reason or a Turn — the tutor does not comment on a gap it cannot measure.Fixtures at n = 0, 9, 10, 24, 25 student-set values, plus one at 30 Attempts of which 25 are defaulted (no curve); no chart element in the DOM below the thresholds; a null brier_topic reaching any consumer fails CI.
04-CALB-006The confidence→probability map is itself calibrated. {Sure 0.9, Think so 0.65, Guessing 0.35} is a prior, not a fact. Monthly per cohort, and per user from 200 rated Attempts, the observed accuracy of each label is recomputed and the map refitted, floored at 0.05 and capped at 0.95; the map version is stored on the Attempt so historical Briers stay reproducible. The refit is shown to the student in words on Progress ("For you, 'Sure' has meant about 78%."), never as a decimal inside a Turn.Refit job; a cohort whose "Sure" accuracy is 0.78 uses 0.78 in the next Brier computation; every Attempt carries confidence_map_version; recomputing an old week reproduces its published Brier.
04-CALB-007Underconfidence is a different fault and gets a different response. When signed error mean(p) − accuracy ≤ −0.10 over 10 Attempts on a topic, the tutor names it at most once a week ("You marked six of these 'Guessing' and got five right — trust the method"), the planner adds no extra practice on that topic, and the entry rung does not rise. Only overconfidence (≥ +0.10) shortens intervals (04-FSRS-006) and raises the rung. Treating the two symmetrically would punish the modest student for being modest.Two fixtures, over- and under-confident: the under-confident student's Plan minutes, entry rung and interval schedule are unchanged; the over-confident student's are not.

Why: monitoring accuracy is trainable (g≈0.57), most with prediction plus postdiction; overestimators prepare less. Underestimators do not — which is why only one direction changes the schedule.
