Renderer requirements

IDRequirementAcceptance
05-WRKD-001The renderer emits only the slots present in the Mark object: band strip, tolerance line, calibration badge, command_word_check.coaching_line, one block per per_ao[] or per_point[] in schema order, quoted spans, at most one examiner warning per AO, one primary action, up to two secondary actions. No prose is generated at render time.Snapshot test renders both Marks above byte-identically from their JSON (15-RUBR-003).
05-WRKD-002Quoted spans in the rendered view are rehydrated from the transcript by offset, never from the quote field, and the same span is simultaneously painted in the answer pane (credited = 2 px accent underline + wash, partial = dotted, uncredited = warning dotted). A span whose offsets no longer resolve is dropped from both panes and logged.Mutate one character of the transcript in a fixture → the affected span disappears from both panes; error counter increments.
05-WRKD-003A failed conjunctive point names which atom failed, in the scheme's own paraphrased terms, never "incorrect" or "incomplete" (example (b), K1). Atoms render as a two-line "wants both" sentence, not a checklist widget.Copy lint: any points Mark with an unmet atom whose rendered text lacks the atom wording fails the render test.
05-WRKD-004The band strip renders low ── modal ── high with tabular numerals and the fixed tolerance sentence; a Mark with total_band: null (below gate, 05-GATE-004) renders the header "Feedback only — this paper is not yet calibrated" in the same box and everything else unchanged.Render both states from the same fixture with calibration_status.state flipped.
05-WRKD-005The rendered rationale never exceeds 220 words (tariff ≥12) or 80 words (tariff ≤5) excluding quoted spans, contains no exclamation mark, emoji, praise token or second-person compliment, and ends with exactly one primary action.Word count and praise lint run on the two fixtures in CI on every prompt or template change (05-PIPE-009).

05.13The machine-scored and IRT engine

This is the third engine and it is v2 (SYNTHESIS §8.12 FINAL; gated as a v2 done-condition by 00-DONE-003). Machine-scored exams — UNT, SAT, ЕГЭ Part 1, JEE, and the MCQ components of expert-marked boards such as 9708 P1/P3 and 9709's MCQ papers — are not marked by judgement at all. Their unit of truth is a key, and their unit of meaning is a scaled score estimated from an item bank, not a sum of raw marks. Everything in §05.2–§05.9 that concerns levels, AOs, evidence rules, rationale prose and the Examiner Twin is out of scope here; what replaces it is item calibration, θ estimation and error reporting.

Build it as a separate service (engine/irt) that shares only the Item bank, the Attempt record and the Mark envelope. Nothing in this subsection may be used to score a levels or a points-with-judgement Item, and nothing in §05.3–§05.6 may be used to produce a scaled score.

Eligibility

IDRequirement
05-IRT-001Eligible item families, exhaustively. Item@2.item_type ∈ {mcq, numeric_exact, short_exact, match, order} and the Item carries a deterministic key (answer_key with an accept list and, for numeric, a tolerance) and its scheme is scheme_type: "points" with every marking point machine-verifiable (exact match or SymPy recompute). Any other Item — every levels scheme, every mixed scheme, every points scheme with a judgement-bearing marking point, every practical scheme — is refused by the engine with IrtIneligible(item_id, reason). Acceptance: feeding the 05.12(a) 20-mark essay Item to engine/irt raises; feeding the 05.12(b) points Item raises (AN1–AN3 are judgement-bearing).
05-IRT-002No per_ao object is ever emitted for an IRT Item, and no IRT Item ever produces a total_band with a tolerance derived from scheme.tolerance. The Mark envelope for an IRT Item is per_point[] (05-MARK-013) with glyph ∈ {✓, ×, Ø} only, plus one additional block theta (05-IRT-007). total_band.exact = true on every scored IRT Item, because every point is deterministically verified (05-MARK-016). Acceptance: schema test asserts per_ao == null ∧ theta != null on IRT Marks and the converse on every §05.2 Mark.
05-IRT-003Feedback without prose. An IRT Item has no student text to quote, so 05-SCOP-005 (every credited point quotes a span) does not apply and is not weakened for anything else. The feedback layer is the distractor-to-misconception map: each wrong option carries misconception_id from the Pack (§06.3 syllabus_nodes[].misconceptions), and the Mark renders one sentence naming the misconception and one contrast-pair Item, never "incorrect". An option with no misconception_id renders the syllabus-point name only. Acceptance: every scored mcq Item in a gated Pack has a misconception_id on ≥ (k−1) of its distractors, or it is trial (05-IRT-009).

Item-bank calibration

IDRequirement
05-IRT-004Model and estimation. Default 2PL (discrimination irt_a, difficulty irt_b); 3PL (adding the pseudo-guessing asymptote irt_c) only where the item is mcq with a fixed option count, with irt_c bounded to [0, 1/k + 0.05] and a Bayesian prior, never estimated free. Calibration is marginal maximum likelihood over the response matrix, re-run nightly per Pack. Item@2 gains {irt_model ∈ {none, 2pl, 3pl}, irt_a, irt_b, irt_c, irt_se_a, irt_se_b, calibration_n, calibration_at, fit, exposure_rate, trial_status}. Why: a 3PL fitted free on a few hundred responses puts most of its uncertainty in c and produces difficulty estimates that move with the sample; a bounded prior is the standard operational compromise.
05-IRT-005Calibration volume, staged. calibration_n < 300 → the item is trial_status: trial and contributes nothing to θ. 300 ≤ calibration_n < 500 → trial_status: provisional; the item scores, but the paper cannot leave provisional on its 05-GATE-002 row. calibration_n ≥ 500 on a sample spanning at least two ability terciles → trial_status: live. Re-calibration is triggered by a Pack version bump, a syllabus renumbering, or an item edit of any kind: an edited item is a new item_id with calibration_n = 0, never a re-used one. Acceptance: editing the stem of a live item creates a new id and returns the old id to the bank as retired.
05-IRT-006Item-fit statistics and retirement. Per item, computed at every nightly calibration: weighted (infit) and unweighted (outfit) mean-square, required in 0.7–1.3; point-biserial correlation ≥0.20; irt_a in [0.4, 2.5]; and DIF by the same buckets as 05-GATE-002b (region, L1, handwritten/typed where applicable) using Mantel–Haenszel with the ETS A/B/C classification at n ≥ 200 per focal group. An item outside any bound, or classified C on DIF, is moved to trial_status: retired within one nightly run: it stops being served, its prior responses stay in the bank for linking, and the scores it already contributed to are recomputed and the affected students told (05-IRT-011). A paper whose retired share exceeds 5% of its live bank in a rolling 90 days pauses like a seeded-QA breach (05-GATE-005). Acceptance: inject a deliberately mis-keyed item into staging → outfit exceeds 1.3 and the item retires inside one nightly run; the DIF drill retires a planted C-classified item.

θ, standard error and what the student sees

IDRequirement
05-IRT-007θ estimation. Expected a-posteriori (EAP) with a standard normal prior over the item responses in the scored set; the Mark carries theta {value, se, n_items, items_live, items_provisional, method: "eap", prior: "n(0,1)"}. The reported score is scale(θ) from pack.syllabus.score_scale — Pack data with source_url and scale_verified, exactly like pum_map (05-PRED-005) — and is always rendered as a range scale(θ − 1.96·SE) … scale(θ + 1.96·SE), never a point, with the fixed line "Your practice estimate is a range because {n_items} items measure you this precisely." A Pack with scale_verified: false renders the missing-input line and no number, on the same rule as 05-PRED-008.
05-IRT-008Two error gates, both blocking. (a) θ standard error: SE(θ) ≤ 0.30 at the ability region containing the paper's own cut scores, measured on the calibration sample; a paper whose test information cannot reach that at its published length publishes no score estimate and shows per-topic diagnostics only. (b) Score error: the RMSE of scale(θ) against the exam's own reported scores on a linking sample of ≥200 candidates is ≤ the exam's published standard error of measurement; where the exam publishes no SEM, the gate is RMSE ≤ 4% of the scale range and the calibration page says which rule was used. Both are computed on the lower/upper bound of a bootstrap 95% CI in the conservative direction, as in 05-GATE-002.
05-IRT-009Exposure control and trial seeding. Every delivered set draws 2–5% of its items from trial_status: trial, unscored and indistinguishable to the student, which is how calibration_n accumulates; trial items are excluded from θ, from the score range and from any streak or mastery write. Live-item exposure is capped by a randomesque rule (draw from the top 6 by information at the current θ, uniformly) with a per-item exposure rate ≤0.25 across the paper's active cohort in any 30 days; an item over the cap is rested. Why: an item bank that always serves its most informative item is memorised and copied within one series, and the first thing that leaks is the gate.
05-IRT-010Item security. Live IRT items are never rendered in an offline bundle (11-OFF-001), never exported into a Receipt or a Card back, never included in a share link, and never regenerated by the §05.10 generator from a live item's parameters. A student may see any item they answered, once, in their own review; a teacher sees only the items their class was served.
05-IRT-011Recomputation is announced, never silent. When an item retires (05-IRT-006) or a Pack re-calibration moves any irt_b by more than 0.3 logits, every affected score estimate is recomputed and the student sees one line on the Progress paper panel: "Your estimate moved from {old} to {new} — we retired {n} question(s) that were not measuring what they should." No estimate is changed without that line, and the previous estimate stays in the history.

How it meets the release gates

The paper is still the unit of gating (§05.6) and the readiness states are unchanged, but the two conditions mean different things: there is no human line to beat, because there are no human markers. 05-GATE-002 therefore carries its own row and 05-GATE-008's calibration page carries the IRT fields beside the QWK fields.

IDRequirement
05-IRT-012The 05-GATE-002 row for this engine is "Machine-scored (IRT)" and is met when, on the paper's own calibration sample: ≥90% of the live bank passes 05-IRT-006's fit and DIF bounds; every scored item is live or provisional with calibration_n ≥ 300; SE(θ) ≤ 0.30 at the cut scores; and the score-error rule of 05-IRT-008(b) holds. Condition (b) of 05-GATE-002 — the human line — is recorded human_line: "n/a" for the same reason as the exact-match row, and the paper gates without a provisional badge. A paper with any scored item at calibration_n < 500 gates as provisional and every score estimate carries the provisional badge. Acceptance: a synthetic bank with 20% misfitting items fails the row; the same bank with the misfits retired passes; the calibration page renders the IRT fields with no QWK column.
05-IRT-013Calibration-page fields for machine-scored papers (added to 05-GATE-008's list, rendered only for papers whose engine is IRT): model (2PL/3PL), live / provisional / trial / retired bank counts, median calibration_n, fit-pass rate, DIF classifications by bucket with their n, SE(θ) at the cut scores, score RMSE against the linking sample and the SEM it is compared with, exposure-rate p95, and the date of the last nightly calibration. The marketing number for a machine-scored paper is the score RMSE, never a QWK.
05-IRT-014Nothing shared with the expert-marked engines is weakened by this one. engine/irt may not import from engine/levels or engine/points; the Mark post-lint (05-PIPE-009) runs on IRT Marks with the span checks disabled by item class, not by a flag on the Mark; and no IRT Item enters a gold set, a QWK computation, a seeded-QA batch or the human audit queue. Acceptance: a dependency-graph test fails on any import across the three engine directories; the gold-set manager rejects an IRT Item.

§06The library: content, curriculum packs, licensing

06.1The three-provenance content model

Every byte of content Margin retrieves, displays, marks against or exports belongs to exactly one of three provenance classes. The class is a column, not a convention: it is set at ingest, carried on every documents, chunks, items, mark_schemes and examiner_insights row (§11.2), checked by the retrieval prefilter (11-RAG-003) and by the render layer, and audited in the provenance_ledger. There is no fourth class. A document that cannot be assigned one of the three is not ingested.

Definitions

ClassDefinition (exact)ExamplesMay be pooled into global retrievalMay display textMay be exported (Receipts, Cards, print)
OWNContent authored by Margin staff, contractors or generators under our own copyright: original Items and stimuli (05-GEN), our paraphrased scheme wording (wording_status=own_paraphrase), examiner_insights.text, syllabus-graph nodes we wrote, facts extracted from public documents (syllabus statements, paper structures, AO weights, thresholds), page/question anchors that point at official PDFs.itm_01JXA4W2K9Q7ZB3M6N8VYT1CDE (ULID; the slug it_9609_5.3_0412 is not an id and never appears in data), ms_9609_41_MJ25_Q1@3 (paraphrase), ei_9609_m25_004, syl_9609_2026#2.2.1YesYesYes
LICENSEDThird-party text or images held under a written agreement recorded as a licences row with licence_id, licensor, scope, territories[], display_rights ∈ {grounding_only, extracts, full_text}, expiry, max_quote_words. Nothing is LICENSED until counsel has filed the signed instrument and its licence_id exists.Endorsed coursebook chapters under a Cambridge University Press & Assessment or CLA agreement; verbatim grid wording if Cambridge grants it (wording_status=licensed_verbatim).Yes, only within scope.syllabus_codes[] and territories[]Per display_rightsOnly if scope.export=true
USERFiles a student, teacher or school uploads: past papers, mark schemes, examiner reports, School Support Hub material, textbook photos, notes (including the founder-supplied ZNotes text until a ZNotes agreement exists, SYNTHESIS §9). Processed for the uploading principal only; the partition_key is the uploader's tenant (or the user id for individuals); retention per uploads.retention_until.upl_01JX… (9609 s24 P4 mark scheme photographed by a teacher), the founder's mechanisms file (licence_basis="user" in 05.3)NeverYes, to the owning principal onlyOnly to the owning principal, never in a shared artefact

licence_basis on the ledger refines the class: own, licensed:<licence_id>, user, public_with_permission:<permission_ref>, quotation. public_with_permission is a sub-case of LICENSED (a written permission is a licence); a public URL alone is never a basis. Why: UK law offers no commercial TDM exception (March 2026 report) and Cambridge refuses electronic republication of questions, schemes and ERs; a "we found it online" class would be the exact thing a takedown targets (GL §A1, §A4).

quotation is a basis, not a class. Every short attributed extract — the 18 verbatim command-word definitions per Pack and every ≤40-word quotation under 06-STOR-001 — is recorded as licence_basis: quotation with a mandatory sub-object {exception ∈ {uk_cdpa_s30, us_fair_use, eu_art5_quotation, other}, jurisdiction, reviewed_by, reviewed_at}. It never becomes a fourth provenance class and it is never recorded as own, which would be false and would make 06-TAKE-021's per-document report unanswerable for exactly the content most likely to be complained about. Acceptance: every row in extract_log resolves to a document whose licence_basis ∈ {licensed:<id>, public_with_permission:<ref>, quotation}; a quotation row with no exception fails ingest.

Provenance stays at three members; every other state is a sibling column. The three-value enum is enforced by 06-PROV-001, so refinements are never smuggled into it with an arrow or a hyphen. The siblings are: consent_status ∈ {none, gold_consented} on exemplars (a consented Tier-1 script is provenance: USER with consent_status: gold_consented, never USER→gold_consented); text_status ∈ {own, own_facts, licensed, ref_only} on documents, where own_facts is our restatement of uncopyrightable facts from a third-party document; licence_basis as above; and links[].derivation (06-PACK-006) for how a graph edge was produced. Acceptance: a repo lint rejects any provenance literal containing →, - or :.

Requirements

IDRequirement
06-PROV-001provenance ∈ {OWN, LICENSED, USER} is a NOT NULL enum on documents, chunks, items, mark_schemes, examiner_insights, textbook_sections, figures, exemplars. A migration adding a fourth value fails CI (schema lint asserts the enum has exactly three members). Acceptance: INSERT … provenance='scraped' raises; the enum test is in the migration suite.
06-PROV-002Retrieval never mixes tenants' USER content. Every retrieval call names its partitions explicitly: ['global'] plus at most one tenant partition, equal to the caller's org_id (or user:<id> for individuals). Two tenant partitions in one query is a request-validation error, not a filtered result. Acceptance: the isolation suite (11-DATA-004) runs 10,000 randomised queries across 50 synthetic tenants and returns 0 cross-tenant chunks; a query naming two tenant partitions returns HTTP 400.
06-PROV-003USER content is never embedded into the global partition and never used to build OWN artefacts that quote it. Generators (05-GEN), Card builders (§04) and the compiler may read a tenant's USER chunk only inside that tenant's job; any OWN row they emit must pass 05-GEN-005's near-duplicate check against USER text as well as official text. Acceptance: a fixture uploads a unique 40-word paragraph as USER; no OWN row created in the following 24 h contains an 8-gram of it.
06-PROV-004LICENSED served only where scope allows. The prefilter joins licences and drops chunks where now() > expiry, caller.residency ∉ territories, course.syllabus_code ∉ scope.syllabus_codes, or the requested rendering exceeds display_rights. A chunk allowed for grounding but not display reaches the model with render=false and can be cited but never quoted (06.6). Acceptance: flipping a licence's expiry to yesterday removes its chunks from the next query with no deploy; a grounding_only chunk quoted verbatim fails the post-lint (05-PIPE-009 extends to Learn Turns).
06-PROV-005Every OWN paraphrase records what it paraphrases: source_ref {document_id, page, bbox?} pointing at the official PDF's location, so the citation chip can deep-link (06.6) without holding the text. A paraphrase row without source_ref is a lint error unless kind=original_item.
06-PROV-006Class is immutable per document version. Re-classifying (e.g. USER → LICENSED when the ZNotes agreement lands) is a new doc_id ingested from the licensed copy, with the old USER copies untouched. Why: a licence covers a specific file the licensor supplied, not whatever a user photographed.
06-PROV-007The kill switch (06.10) applies to all three classes identically: provenance_ledger.kill_switch=true removes the document's chunks from the prefilter, its items from practice selection, its rows from any Pack build and its extracts from caches within the SLA.

Provenance ledger entry

Append-only; one row per document version; every row signed into the daily audit hash chain (§12). The block below lists the shape — a | b | c enumerates the legal values of a field, it is not a value — so it is skipped by the instance validator (06-PACK-001).

provenance_ledger:
  ledger_id: pl_01JXQ7…                 # ULID
  doc_id: doc_9609_syl_2026             # stable across versions; version below
  doc_version: 3
  provenance: OWN | LICENSED | USER
  licence_basis: own | licensed:lic_cupa_2027_01 | user | public_with_permission:perm_cb_2026_11 | quotation
  quotation_basis: {exception: uk_cdpa_s30, jurisdiction: GB, reviewed_by: counsel_01, reviewed_at: 2026-10-01} | null   # required iff licence_basis = quotation
  licence_id: lic_cupa_2027_01 | null
  source_url: https://www.cambridgeinternational.org/Images/697371-2026-2028-syllabus.pdf | null   # official page for facts/anchors; null for USER
  sha256: "9f1c…e2"                     # of the ingested bytes
  bytes: 2481773
  ingested_at: 2026-10-03T14:02:11Z
  ingested_by: user_id | job_id
  uploader_org_id: org_… | null         # USER only; equals partition_key
  partition_key: global | org_01… | user_01…
  expiry: 2028-08-31 | null             # licence end; AQA 3-year public window; Pearson 5-year; USER retention_until
  display_rights: full_text | extracts | grounding_only | anchors_only
  text_status: own | own_facts | licensed | ref_only
  trust_rank: 1..6
  kill_switch: false
  takedown: {requested_at: null, requester: null, notice_id: null, removed_at: null, reinstated_at: null}
  derived_from: [doc_id@version, …]     # OWN paraphrases list their official sources
  checksum_prev: "…"                    # hash chain
IDRequirement
06-PROV-008source_url is mandatory for OWN rows with derived_from ≠ [] and for LICENSED; sha256 mandatory for all; uploader_org_id mandatory for USER. Rows are never updated except kill_switch, takedown.* and expiry (extension by a new licence version). Acceptance: trigger rejects any other UPDATE; hash chain verifies nightly.
06-PROV-009The ledger is queryable by the takedown desk in ≤1 s by sha256, source_url, doc_id or free text over titles; the answer lists every chunk, item, scheme, insight and cache key derived from the document (via derived_from closure).

Tests the class model must pass before any Pack is live

  1. Class purity: a SQL assertion that no chunk in partition_key='global' has provenance='USER' (run on every ingest batch and nightly).
  2. Scope fence: for each licence_id, sample 200 queries from a tenant outside territories — 0 chunks returned.
  3. Ref-only fence: for every documents.text_status='ref_only' row, chunks.text is empty and only {page, bbox, question_ref} anchors exist (11-RAG-004).
  4. Derivation closure: killing a random official document removes 100% of the insights and paraphrases whose derived_from includes it (06.10).
  5. Founder library check: the twelve ZNotes-derived files and the mechanisms file from the corpus sample are classified USER under the founder's org, trust_rank=5 (revision notes) or 6 (hand-compiled scheme extracts, rising to 3 per record once a human confirms the transcription against the official scheme in 06.7 — the 05.3 example shows the confirmed state), and none of their text appears in global.

06.2What is stored, what is displayed, what is deep-linked

This subsection is the storage-and-display matrix the render layer, the cache and the compiler all read from. Three verbs are distinct in code: store (bytes in our object storage or text in chunks.text), display (text or image painted in a Margin surface), deep-link (a chip or button that opens the rights-holder's own page in a new tab or the in-app browser). A document may be stored for grounding and not displayed; a document may be deep-linked and never stored.

The matrix

ContentStoreDisplayDeep-linkClass / basisNotes

Extract limits (enforced, not advisory)

IDRequirement
06-STOR-001An extract is verbatim text from a non-OWN, non-full_text source. Hard caps per extract: ≤40 words and ≤2 sentences; per Turn or Mark: ≤3 extracts, ≤100 words total; per Session: ≤12 extracts; per document per user per day: ≤10% of the document's pages may be touched by extracts (page count from the ledger). A licence with max_quote_words overrides the per-extract cap in either direction. Acceptance: the post-lint counts words of every quoted span against the source chunk; a 41-word quotation fails the Turn and regenerates with the cap named.
06-STOR-002Grid and marking-point wording is never displayed verbatim without wording_status=licensed_verbatim, regardless of length. The Mark shows descriptor_relied_on.paraphrase and a chip to the page (05-MARK, 05-PIPE-009). Acceptance: the 300 gold Marks contain 0 sentences with ≥8-gram overlap with the ingested official scheme text.
06-STOR-003Every displayed extract is attributed inline in the fixed form "…quoted text…" — {Board}, {syllabus code}/{component} {series}, {document type}, p.{page} with a chip that deep-links (06.6). An extract without a resolvable chip is not rendered; the sentence falls back to paraphrase.
06-STOR-004Extracts are audit-logged: `{user_id, org_id, doc_id, page, chunk_id, words, surface, turn_id
06-STOR-005User uploads are transient and private. §06 states no retention number: uploads.retention_until is computed from the retention table §07.8 renders and the platform ceilings 11-PRIV-004 sets, both of which read config/retention.yaml; a transient upload is short-lived and an upload saved to a Course lives as long as the Course. A number for uploads written anywhere in §06 is a docs-lint failure. What §06 owns is the propagation: a student's "Delete this file", and expiry of retention_until, remove the object, chunks, figure crops, derived Cards' source text (Cards keep the student's own wording) and cache entries within 24 h, and write the ledger takedown.removed_at. Uploads never enter global, never train anything, never appear in another user's citations. Acceptance: delete → query → 0 chunks within 24 h; nightly job proves no USER row in global; the docs lint finds no duration literal in §06.
06-STOR-006The Papers surface and the Paper Companion open official PDFs by deep link in the in-app browser; Margin never proxies, caches or screenshots the PDF bytes server-side. For SSH-only material the surface shows the teacher-upload path and the string "Your school can download this from the School Support Hub."

Caching rules

IDRequirement
06-STOR-007Prompt caches (§08) may contain LICENSED text only for tenants inside the licence's territory, keyed with licence_id and residency; they may contain USER text only in a cache key that includes org_id (or user_id), TTL ≤1 h. OWN text caches freely. A kill switch or licence expiry invalidates every cache key that lists the doc_id in its manifest (06.10).
06-STOR-008Client-side and CDN caches never receive extract text or LICENSED text as static assets; they are rendered inside authenticated Turn/Mark payloads only. Offline (11-OFF-001) may store OWN documents and LICENSED documents whose licence has offline=true; never USER documents belonging to another principal.
06-STOR-009Reference index for the near-duplicate check (05-GEN-005) stores hashes and vectors, never displayable text, for official and USER text alike; that index is exempt from extract caps because nothing in it can be rendered.
06-STOR-010The command-word table is displayed as paraphrase; the verbatim definitions are displayed one at a time. Storing the 18 verbatim definitions once per Pack build (06.2) is a storage decision and does not license a permanent, complete, verbatim reproduction of a board's command-word table to every user. In-product, command_words[].definition_display — our OWN paraphrase — is what any list, table, glossary, onboarding sheet or Pack page renders. The verbatim string appears only in the command-word detail popover, one word at a time, attributed, chip-linked and logged per view against the extract budget (06-STOR-001, 06-STOR-004). No surface renders more than three verbatim definitions in one view, and no surface renders the table verbatim at all. mark@'s static prefix is unaffected: the marker receives the verbatim definition for the one command word it is marking (05-PIPE-002), which is not a display. Acceptance: a crawl of every product route counts verbatim definition strings per view and fails above three; the glossary route renders zero. Whole-table reproduction is on the counsel question list (15-OPEN-040).
06-STOR-011What a logged-out surface may render. The public past-paper finder (§14.4) and any other unauthenticated route serve anchors and metadata only: board, syllabus code, subject, series, component, paper and mark-scheme titles, page counts, and the official deep link (06-CITE-004). Zero extracts, zero question text, zero scheme or examiner-report text, zero OWN Items, zero USER content, and no citation chip whose display_rights is above anchors_only. The non-affiliation notice (06-NONA-002) and the mirror-domain blocklist (06-CITE-006) apply unchanged. Logged-out requests carry principal: anonymous and the retrieval prefilter names the single partition ['global'] with display_rights = anchors_only forced, so the rule is enforced by the same code path as every other request rather than by the page. Acceptance: a crawl of every logged-out route asserts zero extract fields in any payload and zero chunks with non-empty text; a fixture request forging a tenant partition while unauthenticated returns HTTP 400 (06-PROV-002).

Per-region variations

Region (tenant residency)Variation
UKQuotation exception (CDPA s.30) is the legal basis for extracts; caps above apply; no commercial TDM exception, so no crawling. Board public windows honoured as expiry: AQA 3 years, Pearson 5 years — after expiry, anchors only.
EUSame caps; DSM Art. 4 opt-outs mean no crawling of board sites; LICENSED chunks served only if territories includes EU; residency routing per §11 keeps LICENSED and USER text on EU endpoints.
USCollege Board FRQs and scoring guidelines are publicly posted; still ref_only until a permission is filed; extracts allowed under the same caps (fair-use posture); Thomson Reuters v. Ross argues against systematic display of editorial scheme text, so the caps are not loosened.
Kazakhstan / Russia / rest of worldSame product rules; regional pricing does not change content rights. DeepSeek never sees USER or LICENSED text [E5], and — because it carries no contractual no-training assertion (§08.11) — it never sees Pack-derived OWN text either: no mark_scheme_items, no examiner_insights, no generated Items, no grids. Its permitted payloads are public question stimuli and the numeric pre-solve task. Why: the structured scheme layer and the insight corpus are the assets a competitor cannot buy; routing them to an untrained-on-what-basis provider trades the moat for a batch discount. The route-level enforcement is 08-POL-011's.

Why: the four-pattern analysis (GL §A4) rates transient user processing strongest, short attributed extracts weak-but-defensible, and server-side hosting of board PDFs indefensible without a licence; the matrix encodes exactly that ordering.

06.3The curriculum Pack schema

A Pack is the complete curriculum dataset for one syllabus version, serialised as one versioned document tree in Postgres (Pack plane, org_id NULL, §11.2) and exportable as a single YAML bundle for review, diff and CI. Every Mark pins pack_version (05.2 header); every Course pins it (11-DATA-005). Below is the canonical bundle. Tables named in F§7.1 and §11.2 are the storage form; this is the logical form the compiler emits and the eval harness consumes.

pack:
  id: pack_9609_2026_2028
  pack_version: "9609:2026-2028@2026.11.2"   # the only stored form (common@1 version_tag)
  pack_version_display: "2026–28 v3"         # derived for banners and Course headers; never stored on a Mark
  content_hash: "sha256:9f1c…e2"
  compiled_at: 2026-11-19T09:14:02Z
  allowed_domains: ["cambridgeinternational.org", "schoolsupporthub.cambridge.org"]
  board: {id: caie, name: "Cambridge International", country: GB,
          marking_paradigm: expert_marked, level_procedure: best_fit,
          annotation_vocab: ["✓","×","Ø","BOD","CON","RE","GA","ECF","NC","I"]}
  syllabus:
    code: "9609"
    subject: Business
    level: "A Level"                          # IGCSE | O Level | AS | A Level | IB DP | AP …
    version_years: [2026, 2028]
    public: true
    source_url: "https://www.cambridgeinternational.org/Images/697371-2026-2028-syllabus.pdf"
    source: {doc_id: doc_9609_syl_2026, sha256: "…", text_status: own_facts}
    grade_scale: ["A*","A","B","C","D","E","U"]
    pum_map: {"A*": 90, A: 80, B: 70, C: 60, D: 50, E: 40}
    pum_verified: false                       # blocks predicted_grade() until the PUM guide is read (05-PRED-005/008)
    score_scale: null                         # machine-scored Packs only (05-IRT-007)
    command_words:                            # CommandWord@1; the only verbatim board text in a Pack
      - {word: Evaluate, definition_display: "weigh the case on both sides and reach a supported decision",
         definition: "judge or calculate the quality, importance, amount, or value of something",
         ao_ceiling: AO4, uncapped_level: 2, source_ref: "doc_9609_syl_2026#p46"}
      - {word: Analyse, definition_display: "take the idea apart and show how one thing leads to another",
         definition: "examine in detail to show meaning, identify elements and the relationship between them",
         ao_ceiling: AO3, uncapped_level: null, source_ref: "doc_9609_syl_2026#p46"}
      # … all 18. `definition` is verbatim and display-capped by 06-STOR-010; `definition_display` is our paraphrase.
    aos:
      - {ao: AO1, name: "Knowledge and understanding", weight_overall: 25, definition: "…our restatement…", wording_status: own_paraphrase, source_ref: "doc_9609_syl_2026#p12"}
      - {ao: AO2, name: "Application", weight_overall: 25, definition: "…our restatement…", wording_status: own_paraphrase, source_ref: "doc_9609_syl_2026#p12"}
      - {ao: AO3, name: "Analysis", weight_overall: 25, definition: "…our restatement…", wording_status: own_paraphrase, source_ref: "doc_9609_syl_2026#p12"}
      - {ao: AO4, name: "Evaluation", weight_overall: 25, definition: "…our restatement…", wording_status: own_paraphrase, source_ref: "doc_9609_syl_2026#p12"}
  papers:                                      # every `verified_from_syllabus: false` until 15-OPEN-010 closes at M1;
                                               # the numbers below are the pre-read working shape and generate nothing (05-GEN-001)
    - {number: 1, name: "Business Concepts 1", duration_min: 75, marks: 40, ao_weights: {AO1: 35, AO2: 30, AO3: 20, AO4: 15},

IDRequirement
06-PACK-001The bundle validates against Pack@2 (schemas/pack@2.json, §15.C.7) in CI; a Pack that fails validation cannot advance past draft. Pack@2 is the single normative type source and this subsection is the canonical instance of it: every key name, required field and enum here is the schema's, and a divergence between the two is fixed in the schema and the bundle in the same PR. The $id form Name@n is the only legal schema_id; pack.v1.json and pack.v2.json are not filenames the build knows. Required top-level keys are Pack@2's: pack_version, board, syllabus, papers, syllabus_nodes, questions, mark_scheme_item_ids, examiner_insights, thresholds, option_thresholds, exemplars, links, readiness, content_hash, allowed_domains, compiled_at; textbook_sections, node_aliases, documents, changelog, trust_ranks, mark_scheme_items are additive keys this document defines. Enum literals are snake_case throughout (gold_seeded, expert_marked); a repo lint rejects a hyphen inside any enum literal. Acceptance: a CI job parses every fenced block in this document that is an instance — the §06.3 bundle, the §05.2 and §05.12 Marks, the §05.3 schemes — and validates it against the $id it claims; blocks that illustrate a shape rather than a value (the §06.1 ledger's `a
06-PACK-002questions[].id follows the canonical form {syllabus}/{component}/{session}/{year}/Q{n}[{part}] with session ∈ {F/M, M/J, O/N} and two-digit year (9609/41/M/J/25/Q1, 9701/21/M/J/15/Q4b); the normaliser in 06.4 is the only writer. Acceptance: regex `^\d{4}/\d{2}/(F/M
06-PACK-003For board.id=caie, questions[].text_status defaults to ref_only; a compiler run that sets own or licensed on a Cambridge question without a matching licence_id fails the build.
06-PACK-004Verbatim board text lives in a Pack in exactly two places: syllabus.command_words[].definition (≤40 words each, source_ref mandatory, display-capped by 06-STOR-010) and, under licence only, syllabus.aos[].definition where wording_status = licensed_verbatim. AO definitions default to own_paraphrase and a Pack that sets licensed_verbatim without a resolvable licence_id fails the build. Everywhere else — examiner_insights[].text, every mark_scheme_items[].credit_text and descriptor with wording_status = own_paraphrase, command_words[].definition_display, aos[].definition — must show 8-gram overlap 0 with the source document's ingested text (checked against the hash index, 06-STOR-009).
06-PACK-005syllabus_nodes[].path uses the official syllabus numbering; note-derived numbering lives only in the per-source mapping table (06.4 stage 8). Every question carries ≥1 assesses link with confidence ≥0.8 or is excluded from practice selection. The Pack is also the only source of syllabus numbering for prose, fixtures and screens: a docs-and-fixtures lint resolves every syllabus_point_id and every "{path} {title}" string appearing anywhere in the repo against the test Pack and fails on a miss, which is what stops "3.2.1 Motivation" and "3.2 Motivation" appearing in two sections.
06-PACK-006The field is links[].derivation ∈ {compiler_v<n>, compiler_v<n>+human, editor, licence:<id>} — not provenance, which is a reserved three-member enum (06-PROV-001) and may not carry a fourth vocabulary on a graph edge. equivalent_to links across syllabuses require confidence ≥0.85 and are the cross-board reuse mechanism (§07.6).
06-PACK-007readiness.state is computed from the sub-fields on every publish (mapped ⇐ mapped_pct ≥0.95; gold_seeded ⇐ gold_per_family_min ≥3; gated ⇐ ≥1 paper passes 05-GATE-002; live ⇐ published and at least one paper gated). Hand-setting the state is not possible; the column has no writer except the publisher job.
06-PACK-008A syllabus revision (9608→9618; 9609 2023–25→2026–28) is a new Pack id, never a new version of the old one; versions within a Pack are additive. Renumbering is recorded in node_aliases[{from, to, relation ∈ {same, split, merged, removed}, since_version}], which is what lets an old Attempt still resolve and is the input to the learner-state remap in 11-DATA-008. Prior Marks and Receipts are never re-marked or re-signed against a new version. Acceptance: every syllabus_node_id in a 12-month-old Attempt resolves through node_aliases to a live node, or to an explicit removed.
06-PACK-009changelog[].migration_note is the exact string shown in the Course banner (11-DATA-005); ≤120 characters; present on every version ≥ the second.
06-PACK-010Bundle size budget: ≤25 MB YAML per Pack excluding exemplar blobs; questions ≤6,000; insights ≤3,000; the diff between two versions is stored and viewable in the compiler UI.
06-PACK-011papers[].markable ∈ {full, feedback_only, not_marked} with a reason string is Pack data and is the single source for 05-SCOP-010's published "what we do not mark" list, the Course setup sheet and the calibration page. papers[].verified_from_syllabus is Pack data too: while it is false the generator refuses (05-GEN-001), the Paper runner reads minutes_per_mark but shows no section structure, and the readiness dashboard names the paper and the open question (15-OPEN-010). Acceptance: setting markable: not_marked on a paper removes it from practice selection and from predicted-grade inputs within one publish, with no deploy.

06.4The Curriculum Compiler pipeline

The Curriculum Compiler is the internal DAG (worker service ingest, §11.1) that turns a pile of messy PDFs into a versioned Pack. It is internal from month 1 (SYNTHESIS §9: v0 produces 0450 and 9708 from the 9609 grid engine; the public "any syllabus PDF" compiler is LATER). It runs on PDFs, never text dumps — the founder's text extracts (corpus-sample §2) are evidence of what goes wrong, not input.

 0 Intake ─► 1 Classify ─► 2 Parse (Docling) ─► 3 VLM page audit ─► 4 Figures & tables ─► 5 Maths OCR
   ─► 6 Per-source cleaning ─► 7 Dedupe ─► 8 Section→syllabus mapping [review UI] ─► 9 Paper-ID normaliser
   ─► 10 Question↔scheme alignment [review UI] ─► 11 Scheme structuring (06.7) [human confirm]
   ─► 12 Examiner-report mining [review UI] ─► 13 Graph build ─► 14 QA sampling ─► 15 Gold seed & gate (05.6) ─► 16 Publish

Stages

#StageWhat it doesOutput / metric
0IntakeAccept files from three channels only: official public URLs (fetched once, sha256, robots/TDM reservation honoured — a reserved page is deep-linked, never fetched), teacher/school upload (tenant-scoped), licensed deliveries (licensor SFTP with licence_id). Write the ledger row (06.1) before any byte is parsed.100% of documents have a ledger row before stage 1 (assertion).
1ClassifyDocument type ∈ {syllabus, qp, ms, er, specimen, ecr, thresholds, insert, textbook, notes, teacher_material, unknown}, board, syllabus code, series, component, variant, edition/version window; Haiku 4.5 structured output over the first 3 pages + filename, confirmed by regex on the page footer ("© UCLES 2025", "9609/41/M/J/25"). unknown or confidence <0.9 → human queue. Stale editions (9608 notes, 9609 2023–25 notes) get edition_status=superseded and map only via aliases.Type accuracy ≥99% on the labelled set (n=500); superseded editions tagged 100%.
2Structural parseDocling (MIT, v2.126+) → DoclingDocument JSON: reading order, heading tree, tables with cell structure, formula regions, figure crops with captions, page/bbox provenance. Marker/MinerU as configurable alternates (MinerU for scanned/multilingual national papers later).Pages/hour ≥2,000 per worker; every block carries page, bbox.
3VLM page auditGemini 3.8 Flash batch re-reads every page image against the Docling output; escalates to Gemini 3.1 Pro or Opus 5 for pages flagged (formula density, table, diagram, scan). Emits per-page parse_confidence; disagreement between passes on any text span → human QA. Every equation page and every old-scan page takes the VLM pass (old-scan maths is the weakest parser category, 29–84 on olmOCR-bench).parse_confidence p50 ≥0.95; disagreement rate <4% of pages after tuning.
4Figures & tablesCrop each figure at ≥300 dpi; VLM caption (alt_text, figure_kind ∈ {diagram, graph, mechanism, photo, flowchart, table_image}, structured description per 05-HAND-007 schema for graphs/mechanisms); embed with voyage-multimodal-3.5. Tables re-extracted from layout, never from text; merged headers split by column geometry. Defect addressed: (1) figures lost as [Image: …] placeholders and (5) tables with merged headers / misaligned rows.0 [Image: strings in any chunk; table cell-count consistency check passes (rows × cols equal across the table).
5Maths OCREvery formula region → Mathpix (or the VLM pass when Mathpix is unavailable) → LaTeX + MathML; SymPy parses the LaTeX; unparseable → human queue. Unit strings normalised (mol dm^-3 → \mathrm{mol\,dm^{-3}}), Greek preserved. Defect addressed: (4) broken maths and units ("C6H12O6", "cm-3", "10^23", linearised fractions).≥99% of formula regions parse with SymPy; a rendered-formula diff UI shows source crop vs KaTeX render for human spot-check (5% sample).
6Per-source cleaning rulesA rules file per publisher/source family (cleaning/znotes.yaml, cleaning/caie_ms.yaml, …), versioned, unit-tested against fixture pages. Defects addressed: (2) bullet glyph artefacts (`^(Gameo
7DedupeWithin a document: MinHash over 5-gram shingles, Jaccard ≥0.9 → duplicate block dropped, first occurrence kept, dedupe_dropped count logged. Across documents: sha256 and near-duplicate detection so the same past paper from two uploaders is linked to one canonical doc_id (per tenant; never across tenants for USER). Defect addressed: (3) duplicated blocks ("Economies of scale" ×2, Pepperberg results ×3, "On-demand streaming" ×6).0 duplicate blocks with Jaccard ≥0.9 remain; dedupe never removes a block that appears in a different section path.
8Section → syllabus mappingFor each section (or question part), propose syllabus_node_ids[] with confidence: exact match on official numbering when the source uses it; otherwise embedding + heading similarity + Sonnet 5 classification against objective_text. Note numbering is the note's numbering — a per-source mapping_table {source_doc_id, source_section_no, source_title → syllabus_node_id, confidence, status ∈ {auto, confirmed, rejected}}. Defect addressed: (8) note numbering ≠ official numbering ("13.14 Geometric isomers" is ZNotes' number). Review UI: left pane source section with its heading path; right pane the proposed node with siblings; keyboard y/n/j/k; batch-confirm for confidence ≥0.95.Auto-confidence ≥0.9 on ≥85% of sections; human acceptance of auto proposals ≥95%; every section either mapped or explicitly unmapped.
9Paper-ID normaliserDeterministic grammar → canonical {syllabus}/{component}/{session}/{yy} per 06-PACK-002. Handles: S15 v21, S 10 variant 21, W 09 variant 21, 10 variant 23 (year without season → ambiguous, queue), 9609_s25_ms_41, 9609/41/M/J/25, June 2025 Paper 41, M/J 2025 P4 V1, m25 (F/M), w24 (O/N), s24 (M/J). Component = paper × 10 + variant when written separately ("Paper 2 variant 1" → 21). Defect addressed: (10) informal paper/series identifiers.100% of the 300-string fixture normalises or queues; 0 silent misassignments (any ambiguity queues).
10Question ↔ scheme alignmentJoin QP parts to MS parts by canonical id + part label; verify marks agree; detect scheme parts with no question and vice versa; align inserts/case studies to their paper; produce context.case_facts[] (OWN summary, 05-SCHM-008). Review UI shows QP anchor crop beside MS anchor crop with the proposed link.mapped_pct ≥0.95 for mapped; marks-total mismatch 0 after review.

Defect addressed: (9) mark-scheme micro-format (conjunctive M1–M5, all-or-nothing, drawing conventions).100% human-confirmed before mapped; 8-gram overlap with source 0 (06-PACK-004).
12Examiner-report miningSonnet 5 extracts "candidates who scored well… / weaker responses… / common error" triples per question and per syllabus node, rewrites them as OWN insights with student_tip and a machine-checkable heuristic; source_pointer recorded, never the ER sentence. Review UI: paraphrase on the left, source crop on the right, overlap meter, heuristic test-run against 20 gold scripts showing hit count.≥90% of insights accepted at first review; heuristic precision ≥0.8 on gold scripts; overlap 0.
13Graph buildEmit links (assesses, answered_by, commented_on, explained_in, prerequisite_of, equivalent_to) with confidence and provenance; propose equivalent_to edges against existing Packs (0450 ↔ 9609, 0455 ↔ 9708) for the §07.6 cross-board graph; compute per-node tariff_histogram and command_words_seen.Every question ≥1 assesses edge ≥0.8; equivalent_to proposals ≥0.85 reviewed by an editor.
14QA samplingHuman QA on: 100% of scheme records and insights (stages 11–12); 10% of mapped sections (stage 8), rising to 30% for a source whose acceptance drops below 90%; 5% of formula renders; 5% of figure captions; 100% of pages with parse_confidence <0.85 or pass disagreement. Each QA action is logged with reviewer id for inter-rater checks (two reviewers on 2% of items; agreement ≥0.9).QA queue age p95 <3 working days.
15Gold seed & gateECRs and specimen answers → Tier 0 exemplars; partner-school double-marked scripts → Tier 1; standardise the Examiner Twin per paper (05.6).Per 05-GATE-002.
16PublishValidate against Pack@2, write changelog and migration note, bump pack.version, run the retrieval gold set (Recall@8 ≥0.92, 11-RAG-003), snapshot the bundle, notify Courses (11-DATA-005). Old versions stay resolvable forever.Publish is atomic; a failed validation publishes nothing.

Founder library defects, cross-referenced

corpus-sample §2 lists ten defects; stages above cover (1) figures → stage 4; (2) bullet glyphs → 6; (3) duplicates → 7; (4) maths/units → 5; (5) tables → 4; (6) typos and factual slips in third-party notes ("273 °C", "Pilivan", "adenine, uracil and cytosine" as pyrimidines) → not fixed by the compiler at all: notes are ingested as-is at trust_rank 5, and the tutor handles disagreement through 06.5 conflict behaviour — the compiler only flags a note chunk canon_conflict=true when a fact-check pass (Sonnet 5, batch) finds a contradiction with a rank 1–3 chunk on the same node, which raises it in the QA sample; (7) cross-references → 6; (8) numbering → 8; (9) scheme micro-format → 11 and 06.7; (10) paper IDs → 9.

Throughput, cost, failure modes

IDRequirement
06-COMP-001Throughput target: a sibling Pack (same board, same AO grammar — 0450, 9708, 0455) from intake to mapped in <4 weeks with one content editor + one ex-examiner, by month 12 (SYNTHESIS §9); a new paradigm (first Edexcel IAL Pack, a national exam) <8 weeks. Machine stages (0–7, 9, 13, 16) for a 1,500-page corpus complete in <48 h wall-clock.
06-COMP-002Cost per Pack (compute, excluding gold scripts): ≈1,500 pages × (Docling self-hosted ≈$0.00 marginal + VLM audit ≈$0.004/page on Flash batch + escalation 15% at ≈$0.03 + Mathpix ≈$0.01 per formula page) ≈ $60–120; scheme structuring and ER mining ≈2,000 LLM calls on Sonnet batch ≈ $40–80; embeddings ≈$5. Total machine cost <$250 per Pack. Human cost: ≈120–200 editor-hours + 40–80 ex-examiner hours per sibling Pack (paid per structured record where possible, F§7.2).
06-COMP-003Failure modes and handling: (a) silent misparse of a scheme table → caught by marks-total reconciliation (stage 10) and 100% human confirm (11); (b) wrong series assignment → normaliser queues any ambiguity, never guesses; (c) stale edition mapped to the live syllabus → edition_status=superseded blocks direct mapping, aliases only; (d) licence expiry mid-build → prefilter drops the chunks, build fails validation with the licence_id named; (e) injected instructions in uploaded PDFs → stage 6 strips imperatives addressed to an assistant and logs (11-RAG-007); (f) VLM hallucinated a caption → captions are parse_confidence-scored and the 5% sample plus any caption with a number in it is human-checked; (g) duplicate canonical question from two uploaders in one tenant → linked to one doc_id, both uploads retained for retention accounting.
06-COMP-004Metrics dashboard (per Pack, per run): pages/hour, parse_confidence distribution, pass-disagreement %, dedupe dropped %, mapping auto-confidence and human acceptance, normaliser queue %, mapped_pct, scheme records confirmed/day, insights accepted %, heuristic precision, QA queue age, cost to date, days since intake. A run that regresses any acceptance metric by >5 points against the previous run blocks publish until an editor acknowledges.
06-COMP-005Idempotence and replay: every stage is keyed by (doc_id, doc_version, stage, rules_version); re-running with new cleaning rules re-processes only affected documents; the output of any stage for any document is reproducible from object storage + the rules version. Acceptance: deleting all derived rows for one document and replaying regenerates byte-identical chunks.
06-COMP-006Review UIs (stages 8, 10, 11, 12, 14) are internal web screens built from the same design tokens as the product (§09), keyboard-first, with the source crop always visible beside the proposal; each shows the reviewer's acceptance rate and the item's provenance badge; nothing in a review UI can edit official text — only our paraphrase, mappings and flags.

06.5Trust ranks and notes-vs-canon behaviour

Trust rank orders sources when they disagree or tie in retrieval; it never overrides the hard rule that marking uses only a mark_scheme_items record (05-SCOP-002). The ranks are FINAL in SYNTHESIS §3.1/§9 and are already used by the 05.2 sources[] array (trust_rank: 3 for a scheme, 4 for an ER). Do not reorder them per subject or per tenant.

Rank table

RankSource kindTypical classWhat it is authoritative forWhat it is not authoritative for
1Syllabus (current version window)OWN facts + verbatim command wordsWhat is examinable, official numbering, command-word meaning, AO weights, paper structure, units and conventions the syllabus statesHow a specific question was marked
2Endorsed textbook (board-endorsed coursebook)LICENSED (or USER when the student uploads a page)Explanations, definitions, worked examples, diagramsMarking of a specific question; anything post-dating its edition
3Mark scheme (official)OWN paraphrase + anchors; USER when uploadedThe creditable points and level descriptors for that question part; accept/reject listsGeneral theory beyond that question; other series' wording
4Examiner reportOWN insights + anchors; USER when uploadedWhat scored and what did not in that series; recurring errors; examiner phrasing of adviceDefinitions; the current syllabus content if the series predates it
5Revision notes (licensed notes, ZNotes-class community notes)LICENSED or USERCompact restatements, lists, mnemonicsFacts when they conflict with 1–4; numbering
6User upload of unknown type; the student's own notes; hand-compiled extracts before confirmationUSERThe student's own record of what they were taughtAnything, when it conflicts with 1–5

Within rank 5, sub_rank separates licensed_notes (5.0) from community_notes (5.5); within rank 6, a hand-compiled scheme extract rises to rank 3 per record once a human confirms it against the official scheme (06.7). A brief elsewhere proposes syllabus > mark scheme > examiner report > textbook; reject it here — for explaining, an endorsed textbook is more reliable than a scheme written for one question; for marking, rank is irrelevant because only the scheme record counts.

IDRequirement
06-TRUST-001Retrieval (11-RAG-003) filters by syllabus_code and syllabus_version before similarity; trust_rank breaks ties after reranking and boosts by +0.02 × (6 − trust_rank) on the fused score, never more. Why: a rank-5 chunk that answers the question beats a rank-1 chunk that does not; trust is a tie-breaker, not a filter.
06-TRUST-002A stale-version penalty applies before trust: a chunk from a superseded syllabus version or a pre-version ER is retrievable only when no current-version chunk covers the node, and is then labelled "from the 2023–25 syllabus — check it is still examinable".
06-TRUST-003Conflict detection runs on the assembled top-8 (11-RAG-006): when two chunks on the same node state different values for the same quantity, unit, definition, date, name or list membership, and their ranks differ, the orchestrator emits a conflict part before the answer. Detection is a Haiku 4.5 structured call over the 8 chunks ({conflicts:[{fact, a:{chunk_id, value, rank}, b:{…}}]}), ≤150 ms, cached per (query, chunk set).
06-TRUST-004Canon wins by default. The answer states the higher-ranked value; the lower-ranked value is shown in the conflict card with its chip; the tutor never silently picks. If both are rank ≥5 and no canon chunk exists, the tutor says neither is canon and offers to check the syllabus.
06-TRUST-005ZNotes-style revision notes are notes, not canon: trust_rank=5, never cited as "the syllabus says", never used to populate syllabus_nodes[].objective_text, never used as the sole ground for a definition Item; they may seed Cards for the uploading student with provenance "From your notes".
06-TRUST-006Student-facing rank labels are words, never numbers: Syllabus · Textbook · Mark scheme · Examiner report · Notes · Your upload. Teachers see the same words; the integer exists only in data and the calibration page.

How the tutor speaks when notes disagree with canon (exact strings)

The conflict part renders as a card above the Turn (§09 conflict card). Strings below are fixed; {…} fields are filled; no other phrasing is permitted (microcopy lint, §15.E).

CONFLICT CARD — title:      "Your notes and the syllabus disagree"
line 1 (lower rank):        "Your notes: {value_low}  · {source_low_label}, p.{page}"
line 2 (higher rank):       "{source_high_label}: {value_high}  · {citation_high}"
footer:                     "I'll use the {source_high_label} version. Tap either source to see the page."

Worked instances:

Your notes and the syllabus disagree
Your notes: standard temperature 273 °C  · ZNotes 9701 theory, p.12
Syllabus: standard temperature 273 K  · Cambridge 9701 syllabus 2025–27, §3.1
I'll use the Syllabus version. Tap either source to see the page.
Your notes and the examiner report disagree
Your notes: "repeat the business name to show application"  · your upload, p.3
Examiner report: application needs a fact true only of this business  · 9609 Principal Examiner Report, March 2025, Paper 4
I'll use the Examiner report version. Tap either source to see the page.

In-Turn sentence (when the conflict is minor enough not to warrant a card, e.g. spelling of a researcher's name): "Your notes spell it 'Pilivan'; the textbook and the syllabus use 'Piliavin' — I'll use that." The pattern is fixed: "Your notes {say|spell|list} {X}; the {source_high_label} {says|spells|lists} {Y} — I'll use that."

When two canon sources disagree (rank 1 vs 3, e.g. a scheme accepts a definition the syllabus words differently): "The mark scheme for {question_ref} accepted {Y}; the syllabus wording is {X}. Either earns the mark on that question; learn the syllabus wording."

When a user asks the tutor to prefer their notes: "I can explain your notes' version, but I mark against the syllabus and the scheme, so I'll flag where they differ." The tutor never adopts a rank-5/6 fact as ground truth in a Mark or a Card back.

IDRequirement
06-TRUST-007Acceptance for the strings: the 50-item conflict fixture (11-RAG-006) yields a conflict card in 100% of cases with the exact title and footer strings; the praise lint and 120-word budget (§04) still apply to the Turn below the card; a card never appears without both chips resolving (06.6).
06-TRUST-008Conflicts are logged {user_id, node_id, chunk_low, chunk_high, fact, at}; a note source whose conflict rate exceeds 2% of its chunks over 30 days is flagged in the compiler dashboard and, if LICENSED, reported to the licensor at renewal.

06.6Citation chips and deep-link rules

A citation chip is the only way a source appears in a Turn, Mark, Card back, debrief or export. It is a typed citation message part (11-API-003) rendered as an inline pill; it must resolve (11-RAG-004) or it is not rendered.

Chip anatomy

IDRequirement
06-CITE-001A chip resolves to page + span: `{doc_id, page, bbox
06-CITE-002Label grammar, fixed: {Kind} · {syllabus}/{component} {session} {year} · Q{n}{part} · p.{page} for board documents; Textbook · {short title} · §{path} · p.{page} for textbooks; Syllabus · {code} {window} · §{path}; Notes · {source} · p.{page}; Your upload · {filename ≤24 chars} · p.{page}; Original item · in the style of {syllabus} P{paper}. Never a bare URL, never a board logo.
06-CITE-003Hover/long-press preview shows: full citation line, locator, the extract only when display_rights ∈ {extracts, full_text} and the Turn's extract budget allows (06-STOR-001), the trust word, and the actions Open official PDF, Open in Reader (when available), Report a problem (routes to 06.10 intake). Preview opens ≤150 ms from cached chip data; no network call on hover.
06-CITE-004Deep-link formats per board (config, not code): Cambridge public PDFs https://www.cambridgeinternational.org/Images/{id}-{slug}.pdf#page={n}; Cambridge subject page fallback …/programmes-and-qualifications/{slug}-{code}/past-papers/; SSH-only documents → https://schoolsupporthub.cambridge.org/ with the chip flagged ssh_only=true and label suffix "(School Support Hub)"; AQA https://www.aqa.org.uk/find-past-papers-and-mark-schemes with query params, PDF #page=; Pearson https://qualifications.pearson.com/…/{pdf}#page=; OCR https://www.ocr.org.uk/…#page=; College Board https://apcentral.collegeboard.org/…#page=; IB: no deep link to papers (Follett store item page only for the citation, no #page). PDF fragment #page= is mandatory whenever the target is a PDF.
06-CITE-005Link checker: every distinct deep_link.url is HEAD-checked weekly, and daily for the 30 days after a series' publication window (boards move files); status ∈ {ok, moved, dead, blocked}; moved follows one redirect and rewrites the Pack link on the next version; dead after 2 consecutive failures.
06-CITE-006When a link dies: the chip still renders (the citation is true whether or not the board's URL survives); its primary action becomes Find on {board} site (the subject page), the preview shows "The official file has moved; the page reference is still correct", and the Paper Companion offers the upload path. A dead link never removes a citation or an insight; it never becomes a link to a mirror site. Acceptance: the mirror-domain blocklist (PapaCambridge, XtremePapers, GCE Guide, etc.) is asserted against every deep_link.url in CI; 0 matches.
06-CITE-007Density limits per Turn: Learn-mode Turns carry 1–3 chips (0 only when the grounding gate labelled the Turn "not in your syllabus materials"); a Mark carries ≤2 chips per AO card plus ≤2 in sources[]; a debrief ≤1 chip per lost-mark cluster; a Card back ≤1. Beyond the limit the orchestrator keeps the highest trust, then highest rerank score. Why: chips are for verification, not decoration; more than three per 120 words halves tap-through in the design review (§09).
06-CITE-008Chips are accessible (§09): role link, accessible name = full citation line, focusable, preview reachable by keyboard; on mobile the preview is a bottom sheet.
06-CITE-009Chip taps are logged {chip_id, action ∈ {preview, official, reader, report}}; per-Pack "official link tap-through" is a trust metric on the calibration page (§13) and per-source tap-through feeds licensing conversations (06.9).

06.7The paste-to-structured marking-point tool

The founder's mechanisms file (corpus-sample §4.3) is the highest-value asset in the sample: question → official marking points. This tool makes producing such records faster than typing prose. It is an internal/teacher screen (compiler stage 11 in batch; teacher console at calibrator scope for their own uploads, §10) that turns pasted or OCR'd scheme text into a 05.3 mark_scheme_items record in our wording, with a mandatory human confirm.

Flow

paste / select text on an uploaded page ─► 1 detect scheme_type & part ─► 2 LLM proposal (05.3 JSON, own wording)
  ─► 3 deterministic validation ─► 4 confirm UI (source crop | proposed record; atoms editable) ─► 5 save @version, provenance

Input example (pasted from the founder's file):

S15 variant 21 — nucleophilic addition of CN− to a carbonyl
M1 = lone pair AND curly arrow from lone pair to carbonyl C
M2 = partial charges on C=O AND curly arrow from bond (=) to O−
M3 = structure of intermediate including charge
M4 = lone pair AND two correct curly arrows (from lone pair to H AND from H-C to C)
M5 = CN−

Output: the 05.3 record ms_9701_21_MJ15_Q4b@1 already shown in 05.3 — M1…M3 as type B, M4 as DB depending on M3, M5 with an alternatives[] entry, diagram_required=true, vision_status=provisional_teacher_confirm, source.licence_basis=user, trust_rank 6 → 3 on confirm.

Prompt outline (Sonnet 5, structured output against MarkScheme@3)

SYSTEM: You convert examiner mark-scheme text into a structured record. Rules:
 1. Output only the JSON schema provided. No prose.
 2. Rewrite every credit_text in your own words; never copy a sentence of ≥8 consecutive source words.
 3. Split every "AND" / "and" that joins two checkable features into separate conjunctive_conditions; set all_required=true.
 4. "//" or "or" between alternatives → alternatives[] (credited once). "ORA" → ora=true. "cao" → cao=true. "ecf"/"ft"/"own value" → ecf_allowed=true and the point type FT or A with depends_on.
 5. "dep"/"*" markers → type DM or DB with depends_on set to the referenced point.
 6. Tag each point with an AO using the syllabus AO table supplied in context; if uncertain, ao=null and add a note.
 7. If the text is a levels grid, emit levels[] with every band, including a range [0,0] band when the grid defines it, and an evidence_rule per band in countable terms.
 8. Keep accept / reject / ignore lists as atoms. Preserve chemistry/maths notation as LaTeX.
 9. Anything you cannot classify goes in notes, never silently dropped.
CONTEXT: {syllabus AO table (OWN)}, {command-word table}, {question_id, part, marks_total from the normaliser}, {any existing record @n for diff}
USER: {pasted text}

Validation (deterministic, before a human sees it)

CheckRuleOn failure
Marks sumΣ marking_points[].marks (or Σ levels[].max) = marks_total from the QP/normaliserBlock; show the delta
Dependenciesevery A, DM, DB, FT has depends_on pointing at an existing point (05-SCHM-001)Block
Conjunctive atomsany credit_text still containing " and " / " AND " with conjunctive_conditions emptyWarn, highlight
Wording8-gram overlap with the pasted source = 0 for own_paraphrase; if the record is licensed_verbatim (licence present) skipBlock; auto-rewrite once, then human
AO tagsevery point has ao or a notes entry explaining why notWarn
Command wordcommand_word ∈ the Pack's verbatim table; ao_ceiling consistentBlock
Schemavalidates against MarkScheme@3 (schemas/markscheme@3.json)Block
Duplicateno existing record for this question_id/part unless creating @n+1Block with diff view

Confirm UI

Left: the source crop or pasted text with each detected point colour-coded. Right: the proposed record as a form — one row per point: id · type · marks · AO · credit_text (editable) · atoms (chips, add/remove) · flags (ECF, CAO, ISW, ORA, dep→). Keyboard: Tab between points, Enter confirms a point, A adds an atom, Ctrl+Enter saves. The confirm button reads "Confirm — matches the official scheme" and is disabled until every point is individually ticked; the confirmer's id, role (editor | ex_examiner | teacher) and timestamp are saved on the record. A teacher confirm produces vision_status/trust_rank changes only inside that teacher's tenant until an editor re-confirms for the global Pack.

IDRequirement
06-PSTE-001Proposal latency ≤8 s p95 for a 5-point scheme; ≤20 s for a 4-AO levels grid.
06-PSTE-002Throughput target: <2 min human time per points part, <5 min per levels part (F§7.2 stage 4); first-pass acceptance (no edits to atoms) ≥80% on points, ≥65% on levels after month 3; measured per confirmer and shown on the compiler dashboard.
06-PSTE-003Every saved record carries source {document_id, page, bbox, licence_basis}, confirmed_by, confirmed_at, proposal_model, overlap_score; records are @versioned and never overwritten (05-SCHM-007).
06-PSTE-004The tool never displays or stores the pasted official text beyond the confirm session for ref_only documents: the source pane reads from the user's upload (USER partition) or the clipboard buffer, and the buffer is discarded on save. Only the OWN record and the page anchor persist.
06-PSTE-005A teacher-confirmed record for a question the global Pack already covers is diffed against the global record; disagreements >1 mark or any flag difference open a review item for an editor (calibration signal, 05-GATE-009).
06-PSTE-006Acceptance: the founder's mechanisms file (≈20 mechanisms across S10–W15 variants) is converted end-to-end in under one working day by one confirmer, every record passes validation, and the resulting records mark the 05.12 Paper 1 example correctly in the points engine.

06.8The first ten syllabuses and why

§14.3 schedules these ten and states when each state is expected; this subsection states why these ten and in this order, and what each Pack needs before it can enter gold_seeded. The selection rule is one sentence: maximise engine reuse per Pack, and buy the calibration data for the hardest paradigm first. Demand is a tie-breaker, never the driver — a Pack we cannot calibrate is a Pack we cannot show numbers for (05-GATE-004), and a Pack with no parent costs 3–4× the editor hours (06-COMP-001).

T2Structured calculation and short recall with M/A/B, ECF, sig-fig rulesPoints + SymPy (05-PROC-006/008)≈300 scripts, ≈6 min/script to double-mark
T3Short levels items 5–12 marks (data response, short essay, "Analyse")Levels, 2–3 AO grid≈300 scripts, ≈8 min/script

T5Diagram, mechanism, practical-planning and code itemsLevels/points + structured VLM description (05-HAND-007) or sandbox (§11.5)≥300-item diagram/code gold set per family; ships provisional until then

06.9Licensing strategy

The product ships without a single licence (06.1 Tier 0 + Tier 1) and treats every licence as an upgrade that flips a flag, never as a dependency. Open the conversations in month 1 anyway: the asymmetry is that a refusal costs a letter and a licence converts the main legal risk into a moat. Licensing counterparties, terms and any fee are FOUNDER-OWNED [E2]; the sequence, the asks and the in-product effects below are not.

Fallback if nothing lands

Assume it. The launch plan already is the fallback: OWN items and schemes, OWN paraphrased insights, facts and anchors, deep links, and USER uploads processed per tenant. Nothing in §04, §05 or §07 requires a licence; the only features that would improve are verbatim descriptor display and endorsed-textbook explanations, and the honest substitute for both already ships. 06-LIC-005 No roadmap item, GTM claim or investor number may be contingent on a licence that is not signed; an item that would be is filed with deferred_to: later. Acceptance: the M6 launch checklist contains zero rows whose precondition is a licence_id.
