08-POL-001training_opt_in is a constant false, not a setting: the schema declares {"const": false} and every adapter asserts the provider's no-training / zero-retention flag where the API offers one. Where the API offers none, the field is not the control — 08-POL-011 is, and it restricts what that provider may be sent at all. Each adapter declares capabilities.no_training_assertion ∈ {contractual, api_flag, none}, and none binds 08-POL-011.Schema fixture with true fails validation; adapter unit tests per provider (§08.11 conformance); an adapter with no_training_assertion: none and no permitted_content_classes list fails to register in routing.yaml.
08-POL-002deepseek_allowed defaults to false for every tenant type. A request reaches a DeepSeek route only when all four hold on the LlmRequest itself (§08.11): job_class ∈ {pre_solve_second_solver, bulk_corpus} ∧ pii_class = none ∧ content_classes ⊆ {public_stimulus, numeric_presolve} ∧ content_residency ∈ {us, global} (08-RT-019, 08-POL-011) [founder default E5 — §15.G]. There is deliberately no age_band clause: both permitted job classes are batch work with no student attached, so an age test there is either vacuous or silently skipped — the protection that actually holds is pii_class = none.Router test matrix: 16 combinations; only the two permitted job classes with pii_class=none and permitted content classes reach DeepSeek; audit query provider='deepseek' AND (pii_class != 'none' OR job_class NOT IN ('pre_solve_second_solver','bulk_corpus')) returns 0.
08-POL-003zdr_required: true adds every model with provider-side retention beyond the ZDR window to excluded_models; Fable 5.1 (30-day retention) is excluded, so 08-RT-006 appeals route to GPT-5.6 Sol and 08-ENS-002 third opinions to Gemini 3.1 Pro.Fixture ZDR tenant: appeal completes on Sol; model='claude-fable-5-1' count = 0 for ZDR tenants in a 24 h audit.
08-POL-004A null endpoint means "this provider is unavailable for this tenant": the route falls to the next rung of the §08.7 ladder, never to a non-regional host (11-PRIV-002). Regional uplift is added to the route's cost budget (§08.10) at resolution time, not at invoice time.Chaos test: EU tenant with anthropic regional outage lands on google/europe-west4, never on a first-party US host; cost_usd on the Turn includes the uplift.
08-POL-005logging_level ∈ {none, redacted, full} controls trace content only, never metrics: none = metadata rows only, redacted = prompts/completions with the pii_rules scrubber applied, full = verbatim, permitted only for 18plus consumers who opted in and for synthetic tenants. Teen bands (13_15, 16_17) are pinned to none (UK AADC defaults, 11-PRIV-001).A 16_17 tenant with logging_level: full in config fails policy validation at boot.
08-POL-006Quotas resolve per Course, not per user: a Course owned by a school tenant uses the school's quotas and budget; a personal Course on a paid plan keeps the plan's quotas even for a student who is also in a school tenant. Budgets (tenant_budget_usd_*) are always the owning tenant's.Dual-membership fixture: school Course capped at 3 levels Marks/day while the student's personal Course serves 40/month.

Resolution and precedence

08-POL-007 Resolution path. At session establishment (POST /v1/sessions) and on every request that carries no session, policy.resolve(user_id, course_id) = merge(defaults, tenant_policies…, user_prefs) where tenant policies are ordered school | tutor_centre → family → individual. The result is cached in Redis under (user_id, course_id, tenant_set_hash, policy_config_version) with a 60 s TTL, pinned to the Session as policy_version for its lifetime (13-GATE-004), and its hash is written on every Turn, Mark and log line. A request that reaches the orchestrator without a resolved policy fails closed with a logged 500 (11-API-006) — never a permissive default.

08-POL-008 Merge rules per field class. Precedence is "school > parent > student" in the sense that the more accountable party sets the ceiling and the stricter value always wins; a student can only make their own settings stricter.

Field classFieldsMerge rule
Enum latticeresidency, consent_mode, logging_level, age_bandMost protective on a fixed lattice: residency eu > uk > us > global (never widened by a lower tenant); logging_level none > redacted > full; age_band the youngest asserted band
Permission booleansdeepseek_allowed, features.*, training_opt_in, research_pseudonymisedLogical AND (any tenant that forbids, forbids). Exception: features.incognito — a school may not disable a student's incognito Session, only exclude it from assignment work
Restriction booleanszdr_required, school_safe, pii_rules.redactionLogical OR (any tenant that requires, requires)
Setsallowed_providers, consent_scopesIntersection
Retention numbersretention_days.*Minimum, floored by legal minima (receipts, audit_log are fixed by 11-PRIV-004 and never reduced)
Quotas and budgetsquotas.*Owning tenant of the Course (08-POL-006); the platform ceiling in config/limits.yaml always applies

08-POL-009 Enforcement points. Each is an independent gate; none trusts the others.

#PointEnforcesFailure mode
1API gatewaypolicy attached, age_band route allow-list, quota counters500 fail-closed, alarm
2Router (§08.2)allowed_providers, excluded_models, deepseek_allowed, ladder rung skipping (08-DEGR-002)rung skipped; if no rung remains, the route refuses with the factual §08.7 string
3Adapter (§08.11)endpoints host/region, no-training flag, ZDR header, max_tokensadapter throws PolicyViolation before the socket opens
4Redaction filterpii_rules on every outbound payload and every trace writerequest blocked, security event
5Retrievalper-tenant vector partition, trust_rank, school_safe corpus filterempty result, logged
6Storage / RLSorg_id isolation, retention_days on write (TTL columns)RLS denial paged (11-OBS-005)

08-POL-010 Tests (all in the stage-2 and nightly suites, 11-CICD-001). (a) Merge unit tests: ≥40 cases covering every field class and every tenant combination, including the dual-membership case and the "student cannot loosen" case. (b) Residency: nightly SELECT count(*) FROM audit_log WHERE residency IN ('eu','uk') AND provider_region NOT LIKE 'europe-%' = 0 (11-PRIV-002); a synthetic EU tenant runs one Turn, one Mark, one upload, one voice attempt and one appeal per hour for 24 h. (c) DeepSeek: 08-POL-002 matrix plus a payload lint asserting no free text, Course id or transcript in any DeepSeek request. (d) ZDR: 08-POL-003 fixture. (e) Fail-closed: a request with the policy header stripped returns 500 and writes policy_missing — a permissive default is a CI failure. (f) Boot validation: the whole tenant table is validated against the schema on deploy; one invalid tenant blocks the release.

08-POL-011 A provider without a contractual no-training assertion may not receive the data assets. mark_scheme_items, examiner_insights, generated Items, Pack-derived OWN prose, any LICENSED text and any USER text are refused for such a provider at the adapter (enforcement point 3 above), before the socket opens. Today that provider is DeepSeek, whose permitted payloads are exactly two: public_stimulus (the published question text of a past-paper Item) and numeric_presolve (the numeric task and its candidate answer). Why: the bulk work DeepSeek is cheap at is precisely the structured mark-scheme layer and the examiner-insight paraphrases that SYNTHESIS §12 names the company's primary data asset, and a 50% batch discount is not a price worth paying for it; the same rule is enforced on the storage side by 11-SEC-003. The exposure is a row in compliance/risk-register.yaml, re-reviewed each time a provider is added. Acceptance: a payload-class lint on every adapter whose capabilities.no_training_assertion = false fails on any content_class outside that adapter's permitted set; a planted mark_scheme_items payload on the DeepSeek adapter raises PolicyViolation in the adapter unit test; the risk register carries the row and names its owner.

08.9Eval gates per model or prompt change

A prompt change, a model swap, an effort remap, a route-table edit and a Pack pin change are all the same kind of change: a new policy_version. They ship through the pipeline of 11.16 and are gated by the suites of §13. This subsection fixes what runs, what promotes, what rolls back, and what the student can see about which version marked their script.

What a version is

08-EVG-001 The pinned bundle. policy_version is a semver-dated label (2026.09.2) over a manifest that pins everything that can change an answer. Nothing else is allowed to vary between two calls with the same policy_version.

policy_version: 2026.09.2
prompts:            # Langfuse (name, version), immutable once labelled
  learn.system: v31        practise.system: v18      mark.levels.system: v27
  mark.points.system: v14  orchestrator.vet: v9      classifier.intent: v7
routes: routing.yaml@rev 412        # models, effort, fallbacks, budgets, ladders
schemas: Mark@3, Item@2, Card@1, Plan@1        # the only legal spelling (00-APP-007)
packs:  {9609: "9609:2026-2028@2026.11.2", 0450: "0450:2026-2027@2026.09.1",
         9709: "9709:2026-2028@2026.10.2"}     # version_tag form only (00-APP-007)
retriever: {embed: voyage-4@int8-1024, rerank: rerank-2.5-lite, ingest_v: 19}
lints: {turn: v6, praise: v4, copy: v11}
graders: {judge.pedagogy: v5, judge.praise: v3}
labels: {prod: 2026.09.2, canary: 2026.09.3-rc1, previous: 2026.09.1}
IDRequirementAcceptance
08-EVG-002A Session, a Paper runner and a Mark are pinned to the policy_version current when they started; a promotion never changes a Session in flight (13-GATE-004). Marks store the version in provenance.Fixture: promote mid-Session; the Session's remaining Turns report the old version; the next Session reports the new one.
08-EVG-003Rollback is a label flip (prod → previous manifest), ≤60 s to 100%, with no code deploy and no cache rebuild beyond the prefix re-warm (11-CICD-006).Timed drill each release: flip and back, measured.
08-EVG-004An AI coding agent may open a version PR but may not change a gate threshold, a gold set, a grader prompt or a §15.A system prompt without a named human reviewer from the owning role (13-EVAL-006, 13-GATE-005).CODEOWNERS enforced; attempted agent merge blocked in a test PR.

Any PR touching prompts/, orchestrator/, marking/, retrieval/, config/routes* or config/policy* runs the subset below against the candidate manifest; all thresholds are hard fails.

08-EVG-005 A model swap additionally runs: the full per-paper marking gates for every gated paper the model marks, the trivial/classifier gold set, the tokeniser-baseline job (Claude 4.7+ tokenisers are ~30% heavier, so max_tokens and context budgets are re-derived per model, 08-PRIN-005), and a fresh cache-minimum check (08-CACH-003). Acceptance: a swap PR without a tokeniser-baseline artefact fails stage 2.

Canary and promotion

08-EVG-006 Canary. 5% of traffic by sticky user_id hash for ≥2 h, ≥6 h during exam weeks, excluding school tenants that opted out and any tenant with a timed paper in progress (11-CICD-002). Marking versions canary at 5% of Marks but with 100% cross-family second marking during the window regardless of the sampling rate in force, so every canary Mark has an independent comparison.

08-EVG-007 Promotion criteria — all must hold over the canary window with n ≥ the stated minimum; otherwise the label does not flip.

MetricThresholdMin n

Canary vs prod QWK per touched papernot worse by >0.0240 Marks/paper
Second-family disagreement >1 level≤ baseline + 1 pp40 Marks
Production leak sample (§13.2 grader on live Turns)<5%200 Turns
Praise lint on live Turns<5%200 Turns
TTFT p95<1.5 s500 Turns
5xx<0.5%—
Challenge rate (§08.6)not up >1 pp vs the 7-day baseline100 Marks

08-EVG-008 Automatic rollback triggers (evaluated every 5 minutes on the canary cohort; any one flips the label back and pages the owner): any promotion metric breached; seeded-QA auto-pause on any question family (05-GATE-005); schema validation failure rate >1%; repair rate >6%; a safety-classifier regression (distress recall below the fixture floor); provider stop_reason: refusal rate >0.5%; or a route_expected != route_actual rate >5% (08-PRIN-001). Rollback is automatic and unattended; the incident is opened afterwards (RB-05, 08-DEGR-007).

08-EVG-009 Post-promotion. After 100%, the previous manifest stays warm for 7 days; the nightly full suites (13-GATE-002) run on the new version; the calibration report (§05) is re-published if any per-paper number moved, and a per-paper number may not move without the content lead's signature.

What the student sees

08-EVG-010 Model provenance on the Mark. Every Mark carries a provenance chip resolving to {model_family, model, second_marker, policy_version, pack_version, calibration_state, marked_at} (§12.9 transparency; §05.2 contract). Tapping it opens "How this was marked", which names the marker in plain words ("Marked by Claude Opus 5, second-checked by GPT-5.6 Sol · scheme version 9609 P2 2026.3 · marking version 2026.09.2"). Re-marks after a version change never silently overwrite: the original Mark is kept and the new one is labelled "Re-marked on the new marking version — your earlier mark is below".

08-EVG-011 Change log. release_notes (11-CICD-007) exposes, in Settings › What changed and on the calibration page, every version that altered marking, limits or Packs, with the suite results attached. A change to a paper's calibration state or to a published limit that does not appear in the log is a release-blocking defect (02-INV: zero silent limit cuts).

08-EVG-012 Dated hazards gate the config, not just the calendar. CI fails if any route references a model whose valid_to has passed, or whose hazard effective date (11-COST-008: Gemini Flash price doubling 1 Jan 2027; Haiku 4.5 retirement from 15 Oct 2026; Sonnet 5 / Opus 5 / Fable 5.1 commitment floors) is <30 days away without an ack_by field naming the reviewer and a linked successor-eval run. Acceptance: clock-advanced test fails the build 29 days before a hazard without an ack, passes with one.

08.10Cost model

This is the arithmetic the business plan (§14.6) and the quota table (11-COST-001) both rest on. Every number is a unit cost from §08.2 multiplied by a volume; every volume is a counter that exists in telemetry (§08.12), so the model is reconciled against invoices monthly, not guessed.

08-COST-001 Regional uplift is applied at policy resolution, not at reporting: cost_usd = list_cost × (1 + endpoints[provider].cost_uplift) — +10% Vertex regional, +8% Azure EU (§08.8). EU/UK school seats are budgeted at the uplifted rate. Acceptance: a EU-tenant Turn and a US-tenant Turn on the same route differ by exactly the uplift in the cost dashboard.

08-COST-002 Cache assumptions are a commitment, not a hope. The blended figures above assume ≥60% of input tokens billed as cache reads on chat routes and ≥80% on Mark routes (08-CACH-005). Model the downside: at 0% cache the median student costs ×1.6 and the heavy student ×1.7. The alarm at <50% for 30 minutes (11-OBS-002) exists because a prompt-layout regression is a cost incident, not a quality one.

Blended cost per MAU by persona

Volumes are per active month, off-season, and come from config/personas.yaml — the one volume file §14.6 also computes from, so no cost figure in this document is derived twice. Two totals are given because 08-ENS-001 mandates 100% cross-family second marking for a paper's first two exam series: the FY1 row is what finance carries at MVP and through v1, the steady-state row is what the model converges to once every MVP paper is past its second series. 11-COST-003's tenant budgets and §14.6's margin table are computed on the steady-state figure and re-checked against the FY1 figure at each monthly cost review; the gap is the number that must be signed before each series, not discovered after it (08-COST-004).

08-COST-003 Envelope to defend (SYNTHESIS §11/§12): median paid student $1.6–2.6/month, heavy $8–13/month, free $0.5–1/MAU in season [founder default E8]. The free in-season figure above ($1.53) sits above the accepted band because it assumes every free MAU uses the doubled exam-week marking grace; the blended free-tier month across the whole free cohort must come in at ≤$1.00 because ~55% of free MAUs make no Mark at all. Acceptance: the monthly report shows blended free-tier cost per MAU ≤$1.00 in season and ≤$0.60 off-season; two consecutive months above triggers a quota review (11-COST-009), not a silent degradation. Gross margin at $8/month on the median student is 72% at the steady-state marking rate and 70% at the FY1 rate; below 65% for two months is a pricing decision, not an engineering one (§14.6).

08-COST-004 Exam-season multiplier. From T−14 of a Course's first paper to the day after its last, per-learner volumes rise: chat ×1.5, levels Marks ×2.4 (grace doubles the free cap, 03-LIM-004), timed papers ×4, vision ×2. The platform month multiplier in May–June and October–November is ×1.8 on blended cost per MAU with a peak-day multiplier of ×3.0 on marking. Finance signs the grace budget before each series and the 120%-of-forecast platform alarm refers to that signed number (11-COST-010). Acceptance: the forecast for the June 2027 series is written before 1 April 2027 and the realised cost lands within ±20%; the 3× load test (§13.6) is run against the peak-day figure, not the mean.

08.11Vendor abstraction layer

Every model call in the product goes through one interface. The Vercel AI SDK 7 carries transport and UI streaming; provider-specific capabilities that the differentiators depend on — Anthropic cache_control, effort and citations, Gemini thinking level and context caches, OpenAI reasoning effort, Bedrock/Vertex regional hosts — are exposed through our adapter contract using the native SDKs underneath. Why: an abstraction that flattens to the lowest common denominator throws away exactly the features §08.3 and §08.4 are built on [AR§19, AR§21].

The interface

// packages/llm/src/contract.ts — the only surface product code may import
export interface ModelAdapter {
  readonly id: ProviderId;                     // 'anthropic' | 'google' | 'openai' | 'deepseek' | ...
  readonly capabilities: Capabilities;         // static, asserted by conformance tests

  complete(req: LlmRequest): Promise<LlmResult>;                 // non-streamed
  stream(req: LlmRequest): AsyncIterable<StreamPart>;            // typed parts (§09.8)
  structured<T>(req: LlmRequest, schema: SchemaRef): Promise<Validated<T>>;  // §08.4
  tools(req: LlmRequest, tools: ToolDef[]): AsyncIterable<StreamPart>;       // allow-listed, §08.5
  vision(req: LlmRequest, images: ImageRef[]): Promise<LlmResult>;
  cache: { plan(blocks: PromptBlock[]): CachePlan; minPrefixTokens(model: string): number };
  batch: { submit(jobs: LlmRequest[]): Promise<BatchHandle>;
           poll(h: BatchHandle): Promise<BatchStatus>; results(h: BatchHandle): AsyncIterable<LlmResult> };
  embed?(texts: string[], opts: EmbedOpts): Promise<Float32Array[]>;
  rerank?(query: string, docs: string[], k: number): Promise<Ranked[]>;
  countTokens(req: LlmRequest): Promise<number>;                 // per-model tokeniser
  health(): Promise<{ ok: boolean; region: string; latencyMs: number }>;
}

export interface LlmRequest {
  route: RouteId;               // 08-RT-0NN — the adapter never infers the route
  policy: PolicyObject;         // §08.8; adapter refuses if host/region/model not permitted
  blocks: PromptBlock[];        // ordered per 08-CACH-001, each {role, content, cacheable}
  effort: 'none' | 'low' | 'medium' | 'high';   // mapped per provider by the adapter
  maxTokens: number; stopReasonsExpected?: string[];
  schema?: SchemaRef; tools?: ToolDef[]; images?: ImageRef[];

  // Payload classification — set by the caller, asserted by the adapter (08-POL-002, 08-POL-011).
  // These four fields are what the DeepSeek guard and the redaction filter actually read;
  // an LlmRequest without them fails type-checking, so the guard cannot be skipped by omission.
  jobClass: 'interactive' | 'pre_solve_second_solver' | 'bulk_corpus' | 'eval';
  piiClass: 'none' | 'pseudonymous' | 'direct';
  contentClasses: ContentClass[];   // 'public_stimulus' | 'numeric_presolve' | 'own_pack'
                                    // | 'licensed' | 'user_upload' | 'learner_text'
  contentResidency: 'eu' | 'uk' | 'us' | 'global';

  idempotencyKey: string; traceparent: string;
}

export interface LlmResult {
  text?: string; object?: unknown; toolCalls?: ToolCall[];
  usage: { inTokens: number; outTokens: number; cacheReadTokens: number; cacheWriteTokens: number;
           reasoningTokens?: number };
  costUsd: number;              // computed from config/pricing.yaml + policy uplift (08-COST-001)
  model: string; host: string; region: string; stopReason: string;
  ttftMs: number; totalMs: number; raw: unknown;   // raw kept per 08-SCH-007
}
IDRequirementAcceptance
08-VND-001Product code (orchestrator, marking, retrieval, jobs, UI) imports only packages/llm. A direct import of @anthropic-ai/sdk, @google/genai, openai or an HTTP client to a provider host outside packages/llm/adapters/* fails the lint.ESLint no-restricted-imports rule + a CI grep over the monorepo; a planted violation fails the build.
08-VND-002No vendor-specific prompt text in product code or prompts. Prompts contain no provider names, no "as Claude", no model-specific formatting hacks, no XML-vs-Markdown branching by vendor; provider-shaped wrapping (Anthropic XML block tags, Gemini systemInstruction placement, OpenAI developer-message conventions) is applied by the adapter from the neutral PromptBlock[].Prompt lint: regex over prompts/ for provider names and model ids = 0 hits; the same golden Turn rendered through three adapters produces the same visible content and passes the same Turn lint.
08-VND-003Capability gaps are declared, never emulated silently. If a route asks for a capability the adapter lacks, it throws CapabilityUnsupported and the router moves to the next rung (§08.7) with the visible chip — an adapter never quietly drops caching, thinking or a schema.Fault-injection: force structured on an adapter with strictJson: false; assert the rung move and the route.failover chip, not a degraded answer.
08-VND-004Cost, tokens and cache accounting are computed in the adapter from provider usage fields and config/pricing.yaml; no caller computes cost.Adapter unit tests compare against recorded invoices for 100 sampled calls; delta ≤1%.
08-VND-005Idempotency: retries reuse idempotencyKey; a stream that has emitted a token is never retried (08-DEGR-006).Replay test: forced 529 after first token yields one partial, no duplicate charge.

Conformance and onboarding

08-VND-007 Adapter conformance suite (pnpm test:adapters, run per PR against record/replay fixtures and nightly against live providers with a $5/day cap): 60 cases per adapter — a plain completion; a stream with mid-stream cancellation; a stream that is cut and resumed; typed part ordering; a 4-block cached prompt asserting cacheReadTokens > 0 on the second call; a below-minimum prefix asserting no cache write is attempted; a strict-schema call with a valid and an invalid response plus one repair; three tool calls including one typed error; a vision call with a 2,000 px downsample; a batch of 20 with poll and partial failure; token counting within ±2% of the provider's own counter; cost within ±1% of the price table; a 429 with retry-after; a 529; a refusal stop_reason; a policy violation (forbidden host) refused before the socket opens; and a redaction assertion (no pii_fields in the outbound payload). Acceptance: every adapter passes all 60 or is not registered in routing.yaml.

08-VND-008 Feature flags. Each adapter is behind provider.<id>.enabled and each capability behind provider.<id>.cap.<name> (11-CICD-003), so a provider incident is a flag flip, not a deploy, and a newly onboarded provider ships dark. Flags carry an owner and a 30-day expiry for release-class flags.

08-VND-009 Onboarding a new provider in <1 week — the checklist is the definition of done: day 1 adapter skeleton + capabilities.json + pricing rows with valid_from; day 2 conformance suite green on record/replay; day 3 live-key conformance in staging, region and residency mapping added to endpoints (§08.8) and to /legal/subprocessors with the 30-day tenant objection window opened (11-PRIV-007); day 4 route table entry as a ladder rung only, behind a dark flag; day 5 §08.9 gates on the routes it can serve; day 6–7 canary at 5%. Promotion to a primary route always requires the full per-paper marking gates or the full pedagogy suite for the class it would serve. Acceptance: a rehearsal in M4 onboards one unused provider end-to-end inside five working days, evidenced by the PR trail; no product-code file changes in that PR other than config.

08.12Logging and observability per call

One row per model call, one span per model call, the same field names everywhere. §11.11 owns the infrastructure (Langfuse 4 self-hosted, OpenTelemetry, Sentry, ClickHouse roll-ups) and the SLO paging policy; this subsection fixes the payload so that cost (§08.10), routing (§08.2), degradation (§08.7), evals (§08.9) and the learner-facing provenance chip (§12.9) all read the same fields.

The per-call record

Emitted by the adapter (§08.11) on every completion, stream close, batch item and tool call. class marks how the field is treated by the redaction filter: M metadata (always kept), P pseudonymous, C content (governed by logging_level, §08.8).

08-LOG-001 Every field above is present on every call (nullable where the route makes it meaningless); a call missing policy_version, route_actual, cost_usd or user_hash is a CI failure and, in production, an alert. Acceptance: a schema check on the trace exporter rejects incomplete spans; a synthetic incomplete span pages in staging.

Trace linkage

08-LOG-002 One trace per user action. Span hierarchy: request → policy.resolve → classifier (parallel) → retrieval (embed, search, rerank) → llm.call (one per model call, including each failover rung and each self-consistency run) → tool.* → validate → lint → persist (Attempt/Turn/Mark write). Background work joins by link, not by parent: a batch job carries links[] to the Attempt trace that caused it (Card generation, pre-solve, second mark), so a Mark shown to a student resolves to every call that produced it. The mark_id and turn_id are queryable keys in Langfuse, so "show me every call behind this Mark" is one lookup — the same lookup the support tool and the appeal reviewer use. Acceptance: pick 20 random Marks; each resolves to a complete call set including the second marker and any repair call, with no orphan spans.

08-LOG-003 Client to server: the web and Expo clients propagate traceparent on the stream request and report first_paint_ms, stream_resumes, abandon_before_first_token back onto the same trace, so a latency complaint is answerable end to end (§11.14 budgets).

Redaction and retention

08-LOG-004 The redaction filter runs before the trace leaves the process, not in the pipeline: logging_level: none drops all C fields at source; redacted applies the pii_rules scrubber (names, contacts, school names, faces blurred on images, free-text scrub) and stores a content hash for eval replay; full is permitted only for consenting 18plus consumers and synthetic tenants (08-POL-005). Teen bands are pinned to none. Retrieved chunk text is stored as ids only unless full. Acceptance: a provider-payload and trace-payload lint in CI fails on any pii_fields name; a teen-tenant soak produces zero C fields across 24 h.

08-LOG-005 Retention follows 11-PRIV-004: traces none metadata 90 days, redacted 30 days, full 14 days; raw_output for schema routes 90 days (08-SCH-007) subject to the tenant's retention_days; account deletion purges traces keyed by user_hash within 7 days, which is why user_hash — not a raw id — is the join key everywhere. Metrics roll-ups are aggregate-only and survive deletion (they contain no user_hash beyond k ≥ 20 buckets). Acceptance: the deletion-SLA test asserts zero trace rows for the deleted user_hash at hour 168, and that the cost dashboard totals are unchanged by the deletion.

Dashboards and alerts

08-LOG-006 Build these on the §11.11 infrastructure; do not duplicate its paging policy. Dashboards: Routing (route_expected == route_actual rate, rung distribution, failover reasons by provider/region); Cost (§08.10 report inputs live, per route/model/tenant, cache-read share, batch share); Latency (TTFT p50/p95 by route and region, first-AO-card, tool time, queue time); Quality (lint pass rate, leak and praise sample rates, repair rate, schema failures, verified share on STEM finals, per-paper QWK and challenge rate); Safety (affect tags, refusals, classifier fail-closed events); Policy (EU/UK calls by provider_region, DeepSeek calls by job class, ZDR excluded-model attempts). Alerts that page (11-OBS-005 owns the routing): any EU/UK call to a non-European provider_region; any DeepSeek call with pii_class != none, a non-permitted job_class, or a content_classes entry outside {public_stimulus, numeric_presolve} (08-POL-011); route_expected != route_actual >5% for 10 min; cache-read share <50% for 30 min; seeded-QA auto-pause; TTFT p95 >1.5 s for 10 min; unverified numeric final observed in production; a Turn rendered with lint_result.leak = true. Acceptance: each alert has a staging fixture that fires it, and each has a runbook (08-DEGR-007 or 11.11) linked from the alert text.

§09Design system and UX specification ("every pixel")

09.1Design principles

The interface is a pedagogical instrument. Calm removes extraneous load; speed keeps feedback inside the window where the Attempt is still in working memory; one visible next action is the visual form of "one move per Turn". Every token and component below serves one of those three. Each principle is a rule plus the test a reviewer runs; a PR that fails the test does not merge.

IDPrincipleRuleTest
09-PRIN-001Calm by default, expressive by exceptionMotion, colour and celebration budgets are spent only on rare moments; the product has exactly one celebratory animation (a paper first reaching Exam-ready).grep the animation registry: one entry tagged celebrate; no confetti/particle code in the bundle.
09-PRIN-002The source is one gesture awayEvery claim about a syllabus, mark scheme, examiner report or textbook carries a citation chip that opens the exact page.Sample 50 assistant paragraphs with syllabus claims: 50 chips; chip → highlighted page ≤400 ms p95 from cache.
09-PRIN-003Reading is the primary activityBody text 17 px/1.55 at ≤68 ch in chat; 18/1.6 at ≤66 ch in the reader; nothing anywhere wider than 75 ch.Playwright measures the widest paragraph on every screen at 1280, 1600 and 2560 px.

Why: the praised 2025–26 redesigns (Linear, Gemini's larger type) reduced noise and raised hierarchy; the criticised ones (pulsing "thinking" backgrounds, flat recency sidebars) added motion or clutter with no task benefit (research/ux-design §0). Students' top interface complaints are walls of text and busy screens (student-voice §0.8, §9).

09.3Spacing, radii, sizes and elevation

09-SPCE-001 Spacing is a 4 px base; only these tokens: --space-1..16 = 4 8 12 16 20 24 32 40 48 64. Component internals may use 2 px only for hairline offsets (focus ring offset, chip padding-inline 6 px counts as 4+2). Stylelint rejects any margin/padding/gap not expressed as a token.

09-SPCE-002 Radii: --radius-xs 4 (keycaps, code inline) · -sm 6 (rows, chips, citation chips) · -md 8 (buttons, inputs) · -lg 12 (composer, cards) · -xl 16 (user message block, sheets top corners) · -2xl 20 (large panels) · -pill 9999 (mode chip, intent chips, tags). Nested radii: inner = outer − padding, never larger than outer.

09-SPCE-004 Elevation is border-first. --ring-hairline: 0 0 0 1px oklch(0% 0 0 / .08) (dark: oklch(100% 0 0 / .08)). --shadow-1 = hairline (cards, inputs). --shadow-2 = 0 1px 1px /.02, 0 2px 2px /.04 + hairline (popovers, hover cards, dropdown). --shadow-3 = 0 2px 2px /.04, 0 8px 16px −4px /.04 + hairline (sheets, drawers). --shadow-4 = 0 1px 1px /.02, 0 8px 16px −4px /.04, 0 24px 32px −8px /.06 + hairline (the rare modal). No single heavy drop; no shadow above 12% alpha; no shadows on cards inside lists or on the Turn canvas. Dark mode conveys elevation by surface step, not shadow strength.

09-SPCE-005 Grid. Desktop ≥1280: grid-template-columns: var(--sidebar-w) 1fr var(--panel-w); between 1280 and 1600 the panel shrinks first to its minimum; above 1600 surplus goes to centre margins, never to the measure. Tablet 900–1279: 1fr 420px, sidebar overlay. Mobile <900: one column. wide variant: at ≥1600 two screens — Mark view (10.7) and the Reader (10.16) — may instead render var(--sidebar-w) 1fr var(--panel-w-2) var(--panel-w), showing two right panes side by side and dropping their tab strip; no other screen may use it, and the centre measure is unchanged by the variant. Acceptance: resize 1280→2560 on every route; centre paragraph width stays ≤68 ch throughout; at 1600 and 2560 the Mark view shows two panes of 440 and 480 px and every other route shows one.

09.4Colour roles (OKLCH, light and dark)

09-COLR-001 All colour is OKLCH, expressed as semantic roles with Radix 12-step meaning (1–2 backgrounds · 3–5 component fills · 6–8 borders · 9–10 solids · 11–12 text). No raw colour literal outside tokens.css; stylelint enforces. One accent hue (250) in the whole product. AO cards, modes, trust badges and subjects are distinguished by label and shape, never by hue.

09-COLR-002 Mastery pip colours. State is carried by shape (empty ring · ¼ · ¾ · full disc) and colour reinforces: Unseen ring --border-control; Shaky ¼ --warning-fill inside a 1 px --warning-line outline (a 10 px graphic carries meaning, so its outline is gated at 3:1); Secure ¾ --success; Exam-ready full --success with a 1 px --text outline. A decaying Secure pip (retrievability <0.7) renders Shaky by shape and colour together. Acceptance: pips remain distinguishable in a greyscale screenshot.

09-COLR-003 Heatmap: five tones of one hue — oklch(93% .03 250), 86% .07, 76% .11, 64% .14, 52% .16 (dark: 24% .03 250 → 72% .13) — mapped to learning events per day; empty day = --bg-el. Never red; never a streak count.

09-COLR-004 Span marking colours: credited = 2 px underline --accent + --accent-subtle wash; partial = 2 px dotted --accent; uncredited attempt = 2 px dotted --warning-line; ECF = --accent underline with ecf mono badge. Hover/focus on any span raises the wash one step and shows the reason.

09-COLR-005 Contrast+ variant: text 12 → 10% / 98%, borders +1 step, --text-muted → 36% / 80%, all alphas ×1.3, hairlines 1.5 px. Ships with both themes at launch.

09-COLR-006 CI runs an APCA/WCAG matrix over every text-role × surface-role pair in light, dark and Contrast+; any pair below 4.5:1 (3:1 for ≥24 px/19 px bold and for UI borders/focus rings) fails the build. The same job enforces the role split: a token that measures below 3:1 on --bg-app may not be referenced by a border-*, outline-*, text-decoration-color or color declaration anywhere in the stylesheet — which is what confines --border-subtle, --border and --warning-fill to decorative separators and surfaces (WCAG 1.4.11 exempts purely decorative boundaries).

09.5Motion

09-MOTN-001 Durations and easings are tokens; a lint forbids any transition/animation that does not use them.

--dur-press: 120ms;   /* :active scale .97, chip select */
--dur-tooltip: 150ms; /* tooltips, selection popover, hover card (120ms allowed for cite card) */
--dur-fast: 180ms;    /* dropdown, popover, toast in */
--dur-base: 220ms;    /* delta fade-in, card expand, tab switch */
--dur-page: 260ms;    /* route transitions (mobile push) */
--dur-drawer: 320ms;  /* sheets, sidebar overlay, right pane open */
--dur-celebrate: 400ms; /* the one two-tone ring fade */
--dur-shimmer: 1600ms;  /* skeleton shimmer loop; off under reduced motion */
--stagger: 40ms;      /* max 6 items staggered */
--ease-out: cubic-bezier(.23,1,.32,1);
--ease-in-out: cubic-bezier(.77,0,.175,1);
--ease-drawer: cubic-bezier(.32,.72,0,1);

Springs are not CSS. motion.ts exports exactly one, springGesture = { type: 'spring', duration: 0.5, bounce: 0.15 }, used only by the drag-to-dismiss handler; the animation-registry lint of 09-QA-023 reads tokens.css and motion.ts together, and any spring outside that export fails it.

09-MOTN-002 Rules: animate only transform, opacity and clip-path; entrances start at scale .96 (never 0) from transform-origin at the trigger; exits run ~20% faster than entrances; elements that move together share duration and easing; hover effects only under (hover:hover) and (pointer:fine); no transition exceeds 320 ms except the single 400 ms celebration.

09-MOTN-003 Zero-animation actions (an animation here is a defect): Send/Stop swap, message append, command palette open/close, any keyboard-initiated action, tab switch in the right pane, mode-chip change, pip state change, flashcard button press, timer ticks, sidebar row selection.

09-MOTN-004 Forbidden: ease-in on UI, scale(0), bounce or overshoot outside drag-to-dismiss, pulsing or gradient "thinking" backgrounds, typing-cursor blink faster than 1 Hz, any shimmer loop not driven by --dur-shimmer, parallax, auto-playing loops, confetti, particles, mascots, loss animations, layout-affecting animations (height/width/margin).

09-MOTN-005 Reduced motion (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, or forced in Settings): all transforms removed; opacity/colour fades only at ≤160 ms; skeleton shimmer off; sheets appear in place; flashcard flip becomes a 150 ms crossfade; the celebration becomes a 400 ms colour change. Acceptance: Playwright run with reduced motion records no element whose bounding box changes during any transition.

09-MOTN-006 Haptics (mobile): light impact on card flip and Got it; selection tick on keypad keys; none on Again, on Marks or on any tutor error — the product never punishes.

09.6Iconography

09-ICON-001 One outline family (Lucide), 24 px grid, 2 px stroke, 1 px optical padding; 16 and 20 px optical variants for dense rows; icon colour = the text colour of its row; never two families on one surface; no filled variants except the Send button glyph and the active mode segment.

09-ICON-002 Marking glyphs are typographic, never emoji: ✓ (credited), × (uncredited), Ø (nothing creditable), BOD, ECF, NC, CON, RE, GA, I rendered as 16 px --font-mono 600 margin badges; ✓ uses --success, × --danger, the rest --text-muted. Every glyph has a tooltip and aria-label with the full phrase ("Error carried forward").

09-ICON-003 Trust badges are text badges (Syllabus · Endorsed textbook · Mark scheme · Examiner report · Revision notes · Your notes) at --text-xs 500 caps, --bg-el fill, radius 4, never coloured by rank. Provenance chips (OWN · LICENSED · USER) appear only in Library and teacher views.

09-ICON-004 Emoji are banned from system copy, icons and model output (lint, 09-COPY-006). The only permitted symbols are typographic (· — → ✓ × ▸ ↓ ¼ ¾ ∑).

09.7Component inventory and states

09-COMP-001 Build the components below as one package (@margin/ui) on shadcn primitives under the token skin [founder default, E13/E15 — §15.G]. Every component ships with every state listed, a Storybook story per state, and an axe test. States use the shared vocabulary: default · hover · focus-visible · active · disabled · loading · streaming · error · offline · gated · empty · selected.

09.8The streaming contract

Every streamed surface (Turn, Mark, debrief, generated Item) obeys this contract; it is tested in CI against 20 recorded golden streams with synthetic TTFT of 0.3, 1.5, 3 and 8 s.

IDRequirementAcceptance
09-STRM-001Optimistic echo: the user message appears, composer clears, scroll pins, and a three-dot indicator occupies the assistant slot within 50 ms of Send.Performance trace: paint ≤50 ms after keydown.
09-STRM-002At 800 ms without a first token the dots become one 13 px muted status line drawn from the route ("Reading the 9609 P2 mark scheme…", "Checking the working with SymPy…"); text, never a spinner or pulsing background.Synthetic 1.5 s TTFT shows the line at 800±50 ms.
09-STRM-003At 6 s: "Taking longer than usual" plus Stop; at 20 s the InlineError offers "Retry with Think" and "Copy my message".Synthetic 8 s and 25 s traces.
09-STRM-004Tokens are buffered and painted per frame at ≤90 characters per 16 ms; bursts are paced.No frame paints >90 new characters.
09-STRM-005DOM above the stream cursor is immutable: earlier paragraphs, lists and tables are never re-laid out; markdown is committed block by block.CLS measured above the cursor = 0 on all golden streams.
09-STRM-006Unclosed $$…, `` fences, tables and AOCards hold a skeleton of the expected height until closed; inline $…$` renders only when closed.No visible raw LaTeX or fence markers at any frame.
09-STRM-007Auto-scroll stops after 120 px of user scroll; a "↓ New" pill (32 h, --bg-el, hairline) appears bottom-centre; tapping it re-pins.Scroll up 150 px during a stream: no yank; pill visible.
09-STRM-008Stop replaces Send in place (same position, same 36 px); the partial Turn stays, tagged "Stopped" and carrying the Continue control of 09-STRM-014; no animation on the swap.Screenshot diff of the button box before/after.
09-STRM-009Thinking renders as a collapsed non-animated "Thought for 6 s ▸" row; expanding shows a summary, never a live token stream by default.Story state.
09-STRM-010The lint (§04) runs before paint; a rejected draft regenerates without any visible artefact; the template fallback paints as a normal Turn.Golden stream with an injected "Great question!" shows no flash of the rejected text.
09-STRM-011Mark streaming order: MarkHeader → one AOCard each within 8 s → BandTotal + CalibrationBadge → next-mark advice; spans light in the answer as their card commits.Recorded Mark stream: header ≤2 s p95, each AO card ≤8 s p95, full ≤45 s p95. These three are the only stream budgets for a Mark; the 90 s landing→Mark figure of 10.1 is a funnel median, not a stream budget, and no section states either as a p50.
09-STRM-012Screen readers: the completed Turn is announced once via role="log" aria-live="polite"; never per token. Status lines are announced once each.NVDA/VoiceOver script.
09-STRM-013Resumable: on reconnect the client resumes the SSE stream from the last part id; the partial Turn is never duplicated.Kill the network at 40% of a golden stream; final DOM equals the uninterrupted golden.
09-STRM-014A stopped Turn is not terminal. Beside its "Stopped" tag it renders a Continue text button for 10 minutes; Continue resumes from the last committed part with the partial re-sent as the prefix (cache-friendly, §08.3) and appends to the same Turn, while Retry (⌘⇧R) discards the partial and re-runs. Continue and Retry each count as one metered Turn; the partial alone counts as none.Continue-after-stop on a golden stream produces a DOM equal to the uninterrupted golden, and the continuation call reports cache_read_input_tokens > 0.
09-STRM-015Interrupt-and-add (03-PAR-004): sending a new message during a stream cancels the current part, keeps the partial Turn with interrupted: true, and re-injects it to the model as a <partial> block so the next Turn continues rather than restarting the explanation. Interrupted partials are excluded from the praise-audit and leak-audit denominators.Interrupt at 40% of a golden stream: the partial persists tagged, the next Turn contains no repeated opening sentence, and the audit job's denominator is unchanged.
09-STRM-016Cross-device resume: a Session's active stream resumes on any of the user's signed-in devices from the last committed part id, so a Mark started on a laptop continues on the phone that took over via the QR hand-off (10.8).Start a Mark on client A, open the Session on client B at 50%: B paints the committed parts and receives the remainder; A shows the same final DOM with no duplication.

09.9Reading-comfort settings

09-READ-001 One preference object, stored per user (synced) and applied by CSS custom properties on :root, honoured by chat, Mark view, reader, Cards, artifacts and print:

{ "family": "inter|hyperlegible|opendyslexic|serif|system",
  "size_px": 17, "leading": "1.4|1.55|1.7", "tracking_em": "0|0.05|0.12",
  "measure": "narrow|medium|wide", "warm_bg": false,
  "preset": "none|comfort|dyslexia", "align_start_only": false,
  "theme": "system|light|dark", "contrast_plus": false, "reduce_motion": "system|on",
  "reduce_transparency": false, "read_aloud_rate": 1.0 }

09-READ-002 Controls (Settings › Reading comfort, also reachable from the reader header and ⌘K "Reading comfort"): family radio with live specimen in each face; size stepper 14–24 px (chat and reader scale together; UI text does not scale below 14); leading and tracking three-segment controls; measure narrow 56 ch / medium 68 ch / wide 75 ch. Two one-tap presets under one control, because they serve different readers and each is asserted by its own fixture:

Preset keyFamilySize / leading / tracking / measureAlso sets
preset.comfortunchanged18 px / 1.7 / +0.05 em / 60 chwarm background oklch(96% .012 85)
preset.dyslexia--font-dys (the radio offers --font-hyper as the alternate)18 px / 1.6 / +0.12 em / 66 chwarm background, reduce_motion: on, align_start_only: true (enforces text-align: start; justified text never renders)

Selecting a preset writes preset and the fields it implies; changing any single control afterwards sets preset: "none" and keeps the values. Every control has a one-line consequence beneath it.

09-READ-003 Read aloud: every Turn, Card and reader page has a Read-aloud action (system TTS; 0.8–1.5× rate); math is spoken via MathML + lazily loaded SRE ("x squared plus 3 x"); code is read with punctuation. Acceptance: read-aloud of a Turn with an inline fraction produces the SRE string, not "dollar frac".

09-READ-004 Size and family changes apply without reload and without layout shift outside the text itself; measure is enforced by max-width: var(--measure) on the text column, not by the pane width. Why: dyslexic and ADHD students name busy screens and dual-column text as the reason they cover half the browser (student-voice §9); a switcher beats a single "dyslexia font" (Wallace et al. 2022).

Tab (Mark view)Move through spansAlt+←Back (route stack)

Bare 1/2/3 are bound only where focus is not in a text field: the ConfidenceSlider (10.6) and card grading (10.12). A chord may be route-scoped (⌘⇧O exists only on /ask, ⌘. only on the Mark view); a route-scoped chord resolves to no handler elsewhere and is asserted absent there, which is not the same as being bound twice. No double-press chord exists anywhere: Esc has exactly the cascade above and nothing is triggered by pressing a key twice. Acceptance: the shortcut-registry unit test fails when any chord appears twice in the map, when a §03 parity row has no entry here, or when a bare single-letter binding is declared outside the two contexts named.

09-KEYS-002 Focus rules: :focus-visible only; ring = 0 0 0 2px var(--bg-app), 0 0 0 4px var(--border-strong) (3:1 against both neighbours); scroll-padding-bottom ≥ composer height so the sticky composer never hides a focused element (WCAG 2.4.11); Esc always restores focus to the element that opened the layer; after a Turn completes, focus moves to the composer (the hand-back) unless the user is typing elsewhere.

09-KEYS-003 Command palette (⌘K, <150 ms to first results, zero animation). Verb-first fuzzy index across Sessions, Cards, syllabus points, Papers, files, Settings and Sources. Canonical verbs and argument types:

Ask <anything>                Learn <syllabus point>          Practise <point|paper|"5 more like this">
Mark <clipboard|photo>        Quiz me on <point>              Open paper <code> <series> <component>
Open <source> page <n>        Explain simpler | deeper        Show me in the book
Save as card                  Start timed section <paper>     Plan this week | Move block
Readiness review              Reading comfort                 Switch Course <name>
New Session                   Find in this Session <text>     Memory: forget <fact>
Export <receipt|cards|session>  Challenge this Mark           End session
Teacher: open class <code>    Go to <screen>                  Toggle dark mode
Sign out

Rows show verb, argument, a 12 px context line ("3.2 Motivation · ¾ · due Thu") and a keycap. Recent verbs first; > prefix forces verb mode; ? prefix searches help. Acceptance: each verb has a unit test that it resolves to the right route with the right payload.

09.11Microcopy voice and the copy lint

09-COPY-001 Voice: an examiner who is on your side. Short, specific, declarative; examiner vocabulary explained in plain words on first use; the mark scheme's own terms ("developed", "application", "judgement") used exactly. No exclamation marks, no emoji, no "Great question", no therapy-speak, no guilt, no urgency framing. Numbers carry their basis. The system never speaks about its own feelings and never apologises more than once.

09-COPY-002 Canonical strings (do / don't). §15.E is the string catalogue of record: every row below exists there under the key given here, and the renderer reads §15.E, never this table. This table is the lint-fixture corpus — the "Do" column is the shipped string and the "Don't" column is the counter-example the copy lint must reject. A row whose key is missing from §15.E, or whose §15.E text differs byte-for-byte from the "Do" column, fails the catalogue test.

#keySituationDoDon't

Row 4 supersedes SYNTHESIS §10 canonical string 4 ("…so AO4 is capped at Level 2"): the command word sets which AOs are on offer and therefore an AO's ceiling, it does not set a level inside an AO that is on offer (§05.4), and three of the launch Packs have no AO4 at all. Row 10 supersedes SYNTHESIS §10 canonical string 9 for the same reason — SYNTHESIS §12's own free-tier rule is 6 levels Marks a day in grace, so "limits are off" is a limit claim the product does not honour.

09-COPY-003 Copy lint runs on the string catalogue (CI) and on model output before paint (§04/§08). Rules, each a regex or classifier with a fixture: (a) exclamation marks: 0 allowed; (b) emoji and pictographic symbols: 0; (c) person-praise lexicon ("great", "amazing", "brilliant", "well done", "good job", "you're a natural", "genius") outside a quoted span: block; (d) guilt/loss lexicon ("don't lose", "streak", "missed", "you failed to", "falling behind", "last chance"): block; (e) urgency ("now!", "hurry", "only today"): block; (f) therapy-speak ("take a breath", "it's okay to feel", "I hear you"): block in tutor and system copy, allowed once in the distress script; (g) "Great question", "Absolutely", "Certainly", "As an AI": block; (h) hedged marks ("might be", "roughly") in BandTotal: block — the band is the hedge; (i) unlabelled estimates: any grade or mark string must carry a basis token (series, n, or "practice estimate"); (j) vendor names in headlines: block (chip only); (k) price literals: no currency amount or plan price may appear in any in-product notice, banner, tooltip or model output — prices render only in Settings › Usage › Plan and on the pricing page, so a limit notice names the plan, never the number; (l) literal AO numbers in catalogue strings: block — an AO is always a slot filled from the Pack ({ceiling_ao}), because 9708, 0455 and 9702 Packs have three AOs. Thresholds: praise rate on the weekly 1% Turn audit <5%; catalogue violations = 0.

09-COPY-004 Placeholders name the action: after a Turn the composer placeholder is the hand-back ("Try the next line", "Name the stakeholder first", "Paste your rewrite"); default placeholder "Ask, paste an answer, or /practise".

09-COPY-005 Errors state cause and remedy in ≤2 sentences with no apology theatre: "The marker timed out. Retry with Think, or copy your answer." Never "Oops".

09-COPY-006 Localised strings follow the same lint per language; Russian and Kazakh catalogues are reviewed by a native examiner-teacher for register (formal "вы", no diminutives).

09.12Accessibility gates

WCAG 2.2 AA is a set of numbers, and every number below is a CI gate (09-PRIN-013). The table is the contract; the prose after it covers the four flows that automated tools cannot judge (streaming, Mark view, math, timers). Tooling: axe-core runs on every Storybook story and every route in the Playwright suite; custom checks live in @margin/a11y-checks; Lighthouse accessibility score ≥98 on every route; a manual audit (NVDA + Firefox, VoiceOver + Safari macOS and iOS, TalkBack + Chrome) runs on the 12 flows of 09-A11Y-014 before every release and monthly in between. A failing CI row blocks merge; a failing manual row blocks release.

IDCriterionRequirementAcceptanceGate
09-A11Y-001Target size (2.5.8)Every pointer target ≥24×24 CSS px (--target-min); ≥44×44 on pointer: coarse (--touch-min). Inline exception (WCAG 2.5.8 "inline"): targets that sit inside a line of running text — text links and CitationChips — are exempt from the 44 px box on coarse pointers and are asserted against a 24 px spacing circle instead; a CitationChip carries that 24 px hit area via padding, never via a transparent overlay, and gets the coarse-pointer behaviour of 09-COMP-001 so a phone still reaches the source. Nothing outside a text line may claim the exception.Custom check walks every button, a, [role=button], input, [tabindex], asserts the bounding box, and applies the spacing-circle rule only to elements whose computed display is inline inside a text block; run on every story at 1280 and on the touch profile at 390.CI
09-A11Y-002Focus appearance (2.4.13, treated as AA)Ring per 09-KEYS-002; outer 2 px band must measure ≥3:1 against both the element surface and the page surface in light, dark and Contrast+. Where --border-strong fails on a given surface, the ring outer colour for that surface is --accent (the token matrix decides at build time; no per-component overrides).Contrast matrix computes ring-vs-surface for every surface token; Playwright screenshots a focused control on every surface and measures the ring width ≥2 px on all four sides.CI
09-A11Y-003Focus not obscured (2.4.11)scroll-padding-bottom ≥ composer height + 16 px on every scroll container; sticky top bar and tab strip declare scroll-padding-top.Tab through 40 controls in a Session with the composer at 8 lines; every focused element's box intersects the viewport by ≥100%.CI
09-A11Y-004Reflow (1.4.10)No horizontal page scroll at 320 px CSS width and at 400% zoom on a 1280 px window; only data tables, code blocks and PDF pages scroll internally, each inside its own overflow-x: auto container with a visible scrollbar.Playwright at 320×568 and at 1280 with deviceScaleFactor 4 / zoom 400%: document.scrollingElement.scrollWidth ≤ clientWidth on every route.CI
09-A11Y-005Contrast (1.4.3, 1.4.11)Body and UI text ≥4.5:1; text ≥24 px or ≥19 px bold ≥3:1; the gated boundary token is --border-control, which every input, select, text field, checkbox, radio and unfilled button outline must use, at ≥3:1 against adjacent colours — as must icons carrying meaning, focus rings, span underlines (--warning-line, --accent) and the Shaky pip outline; placeholder text ≥4.5:1 (it is copy, 09-COPY-004). Purely decorative hairlines (--border-subtle, --border: table rows, list dividers, card edges) are the stated exemption under 1.4.11 and are confined to that role by 09-COLR-006.09-COLR-006 matrix plus a rendered-DOM pass (axe color-contrast) on every story in three themes.CI
09-A11Y-006Use of colour (1.4.1)No state conveyed by colour alone: mastery pips by shape (09-COLR-002); span states by underline style and wash and glyph — credited = solid underline + wash, partial = dotted, uncredited = dotted + trailing 12 px × glyph (09-ICON-002); heatmap cells carry a tooltip count; band modal mark by weight; timer overtime by the "+" prefix; offline by the banner text.Greyscale screenshot suite: every state pair remains distinguishable (perceptual diff ≥ 5 ΔE between states after desaturation).CI
09-A11Y-007Text spacing and resize (1.4.12, 1.4.4)Per 09-TYPE-007; plus 200% browser zoom and iOS Dynamic Type "AX3" without clipping, overlap or loss of function; UI text never below 14 px after scaling.Text-spacing injection + 200% zoom on every route; iOS snapshot at AX3 for composer, Cards and Mark view.CI
09-A11Y-008Dragging (2.5.7)Every drag has a single-pointer alternative: PlanBlock ⋯ › Move; sheets tap-to-close and a "Expand" button; crop handles have "Full page · Top half · Bottom half" buttons; sidebar/panel resize has Settings › Layout width fields; flashcard swipe has the two buttons.Story audit: every component with draggable or pointer-move handlers has a documented alternative that a keyboard script completes.CI
09-A11Y-009Reduced motion (2.3.3)Per 09-MOTN-005; prefers-reduced-transparency removes backdrop blur and raises scrim alpha to .70.Playwright reduced-motion run: zero bounding-box change during any transition.CI
09-A11Y-010Language of parts (3.1.2)lang on the root follows the UI locale; every quoted passage in another language (Kazakh syllabus wording, a Russian student answer inside an English UI) carries its own lang; model output segments detected in another script are wrapped by the renderer.Unit test on the renderer with mixed-script fixtures; axe valid-lang.CI
09-A11Y-011Name, role, value (4.1.2)Every icon-only control has an aria-label from the string catalogue; marking glyphs carry the full phrase (09-ICON-002); the ModeChip is role="radiogroup"; the ConfidenceSlider is role="radiogroup" with three radios (never a range input); HelpLadder rungs are a role="listbox" with the current rung aria-selected; the EffortDial is a role="radiogroup".axe + a snapshot of the accessibility tree per story compared against a committed baseline.CI
09-A11Y-012Status messages (4.1.3)Non-focus-moving updates use live regions: stream status lines role="status"; InlineError role="alert"; toasts role="status"; the "↓ New" pill aria-live="polite" text "New content below"; pip state changes are not announced (they are visible on hover/focus with a reason).Story-level assertion that each component renders the required role.CI
09-A11Y-013Timing (2.2.1, 2.2.2)Auth idle timeout ≥30 days sliding, never mid-Turn; toasts hold 4 s but every toast action is also available for 30 s via ⌘Z or the ⋯ menu; the Effort-Gate 90 s time-box can be extended by 90 s once per Item without conditions; timed papers: extra time 0 / 25% / 50% / custom 1–100% and rest breaks are Course settings set before start and inherited by every Timer (§05.9), the rest-break button pauses the clock, and a paused paper survives reload; no auto-advance on timer end — the paper locks input and shows the debrief button.Playwright: set 25% on a 90-minute paper → timer starts at 112:30; pause 3 min, reload, resume: elapsed preserved ±1 s; ⌘Z 20 s after an Undo toast reverts.CI
09-A11Y-014Keyboard (2.1.1, 2.1.2, 2.4.3)Twelve flows complete with keyboard only, visible focus at every step, no trap, logical order: (1) Landing → First Mark; (2) Setup sheets; (3) Today → Session; (4) a Learn Turn with a ladder climb and intent chip; (5) Practise Item with confidence + submit; (6) Mark view span traversal → Rewrite → re-mark; (7) Cards review 10 cards; (8) Paper runner 3 parts with the keypad; (9) Plan: move a block; (10) Settings › Reading comfort change; (11) ⌘K verb → route; (12) Challenge a Mark.One Playwright script per flow using only keyboard.press; a screenshot per step with the focus ring visible is attached to the run.CI + manual (SR)
09-A11Y-015Captions and transcripts (1.2.x)Voice input (v1) shows a live transcript before send; Read-aloud never removes the text; any audio or video content in Library carries captions or a transcript, enforced at ingestion (§06).Ingestion rejects media without transcript_id.CI

Screen-reader flow for streaming Turns

09-A11Y-016 The Session transcript is one role="log" aria-live="polite" aria-relevant="additions" region. Each Turn is a role="article" with aria-label "Tutor, turn 7" / "You, turn 6"; the article is inserted into the log only when its done part arrives (09-STRM-012), so a screen reader hears the finished Turn once, never token by token. While streaming, the pending article lives outside the live region with aria-busy="true". Status lines (800 ms, 6 s) are one role="status" element whose text is replaced, so each is announced once. Stop is a normal button labelled "Stop response"; on Stop the partial article enters the log with the suffix "— stopped". The composer regains focus at done unless focus is inside another text field (09-KEYS-002); the placeholder is exposed via aria-description, so the hand-back is heard. Intent chips are a role="group" "Reply options" of three buttons with aria-keyshortcuts="Alt+1"/"Alt+2"/"Alt+3" matching 09-KEYS-001; the disabled Just-the-answer chip is aria-disabled with its tooltip as aria-description ("After one attempt."). A MemoryChip written by the Turn is inside the Turn's article, so it is read as part of the finished Turn and never announced separately. The HelpLadder announces "Help level 2 of 5, Which principle?" and "More help" carries aria-keyshortcuts="Shift+ArrowDown". Acceptance: NVDA script on a golden stream produces exactly three utterances — the status line, the finished Turn, the composer placeholder — and with focus in the composer, ⌥2 selects "Check my steps" while a bare 2 types the character.

Screen-reader flow for Mark view and spans

09-A11Y-017 Reading order is header → command-word line → BandTotal with CalibrationBadge → AO cards → the answer. Before the answer a visually hidden summary reads "Your answer with 3 credited, 1 partial and 2 uncredited passages. Press Tab to move between them." Each SpanHighlight is a <mark> with tabindex="0", role="mark" (fallback aria-roledescription="marked passage"), an accessible name "Credited, AO3 Level 2, marking point 3b-2" and aria-describedby pointing at the reason text; Enter on a span moves focus to its AOCard, Enter on the card's "Show in answer" moves it back. Two skip links at the top: "Jump to AO cards" · "Jump to answer". The band is read as "11 to 13 out of 20, most likely 12", never as three bare numbers. ER quotes are <blockquote> with cite. Acceptance: VoiceOver rotor lists every span under Landmarks › marks; a blind tester (manual audit) can state the band, the capped AO and the first uncredited reason within 90 s on a 20-mark fixture.

Math read-aloud

09-A11Y-018 KaTeX renders with output: "htmlAndMathml"; the HTML layer is aria-hidden, the MathML layer is exposed. Speech Rule Engine loads lazily (first Read-aloud, first ⌘⇧M, or when Settings › Accessibility › "Describe maths for screen readers" is on) and generates ClearSpeak strings into aria-label on the <math> element ("x squared plus 3 x over 2"); the expression explorer (step into numerator/denominator with arrow keys) is available on focused display math. Every keypad key has an aria-label from the catalogue ("fraction", "square root", "raise to power"). Locale: SRE English for en; ru speech rules in v1, kk falls back to Russian with the fallback stated in Settings. Acceptance: the 200-formula suite (09-PRIN-017) produces a non-empty, non-LaTeX label for every formula; "dollar", "frac" and "backslash" never appear in a label.

Split of responsibility

09-A11Y-019 CI owns 09-A11Y-001…015 as automated rows. The manual audit owns: screen-reader comprehension of Turn, Mark view and Cards; switch-access completion of flows 1, 5, 7; a five-person reading panel (two dyslexic, two ADHD, one low-vision) per quarter rating comfort on a 1–5 scale with target ≥4 and no item ≤2; and a cognitive walkthrough of every new empty/error state. Findings are filed with a severity: blocker (a flow cannot be completed), major (completed with workaround), minor; a release ships with zero blockers and zero majors on flows 1–7.

Why: students with extra-time entitlements say the timer and rest breaks are the difference between a usable and an unusable mock (student-voice §"Accessibility across the year"); dyslexic users cover half the browser to cope with dense layouts (student-voice §9) — reflow and reading comfort are the same requirement viewed twice.

09.13Dark-mode rules

Dark mode is a second, complete palette that remaps the semantic roles of 09-COLR-001, not a filter. Every rule here is checked by the token test and the visual-regression suite in dark and Contrast+ dark.

09-DARK-001 Mode selection. Three states in Settings › Appearance and in ⌘K "Toggle dark mode": system (default; follows prefers-color-scheme, switches live without reload), light, dark. The choice is stored in the reading-preference object (theme, 09-READ-001) and mirrored to <html data-theme> before first paint from a cookie/localStorage read in a blocking inline script ≤300 bytes, so no flash of the wrong theme. Contrast+ is an orthogonal boolean that applies to whichever theme is active. Acceptance: reload 20 times in dark; zero frames with --bg-app light captured by the Playwright video.

09-DARK-002 Ladder and no pure black. The five dark surfaces are the ladder of 09-COLR-001 (16% → 19% → 23% → 26% → 29% L, chroma .006–.008, hue 260). No dark token has L <14%; #000, black and oklch(0% …) are forbidden outside --scrim. Elevation is expressed by stepping up the ladder, not by shadow strength: a floating layer sits on the surface one step above its parent (popover on --bg-el, sheet on --bg-subtle+1 relative to the page), and --shadow-2…4 keep their geometry but alpha is halved in dark (they exist to separate, not to lift). Hairline in dark is oklch(100% 0 0 / .08). Acceptance: token test asserts min L and no forbidden literals; screenshot of a stacked popover-over-sheet-over-page shows three distinct surface luminances measured ≥2% L apart.

09-DARK-003 Text and accent remaps. Text 94% (never 100%: pure white on dark grey halos), muted 70% (≥4.5:1 on all five surfaces — CI matrix), accent lifted and desaturated to 72% .13 250 with 16% text on it, --accent-subtle 26% .04 250. Semantic hues drop 2–3 points of chroma in dark (success 72% .12 150, --warning-fill 80% .13 80, --warning-line 78% .13 80, danger 70% .16 25) — bright saturated colour on grey vibrates. Credited underline stays --accent; the credited wash uses --accent-subtle at full opacity, not a light-mode alpha over dark. Acceptance: matrix passes; no dark token has chroma >.16.

09-DARK-004 Highlight and selection alphas. --highlight-source 85% .14 95 / .40 (light .35), --highlight-select 70% .10 250 / .35 (light .30); both are applied as a layer above the text with mix-blend-mode: normal, so highlighted text keeps ≥4.5:1 (the matrix tests text-on-highlight-on-surface as a composite). Heatmap dark ramp 24% .03 250 → 72% .13 250 (09-COLR-003).

09-DARK-005 Images, diagrams and PDF pages. PDF pages stay paper-coloured (rendered as-is) on a --bg-subtle surround with a 24 px gutter and a hairline — inverting a mark scheme is a defect. Product diagrams shipped as SVG use currentColor and semantic tokens and re-theme automatically; raster diagrams and student photos are shown unaltered with a 1 px hairline frame; user-uploaded images never receive filter: invert(). An optional per-document "Dim page" toggle in the reader header applies filter: brightness(.85) to the page canvas only (persisted per user). Charts (Progress, calibration curve) draw from tokens and are snapshot-tested in both themes. Acceptance: reader screenshot in dark shows a light page on a dark surround; no filter: invert in the stylesheet.

09-DARK-006 Code blocks and math. Code uses one syntax theme per mode from tokens (background --bg-subtle, hairline, text --text, keywords --accent, strings --success, comments --text-muted), never a third-party theme with its own background; inline code inherits the surrounding surface +1 step. KaTeX inherits currentColor; fraction rules and radicals are drawn in --text, never in a hardcoded black. Acceptance: grep the bundle for #282c34, #1e1e1e, #000 and other theme literals → 0.

09-DARK-007 Print from dark. Print (09.14) always uses the light palette regardless of screen theme: @media print resets data-theme tokens to light values; highlights print as underline styles plus wash at 15% grey; the scrim, banners, rail and composer are removed. Acceptance: print preview from a dark Session is visually identical to print preview from light (pixel diff <0.5%).

09-DARK-008 Focus, borders and states. Focus ring in dark: inner --bg-app 16%, outer --border-strong 42% or --accent per 09-A11Y-002; decorative borders 27/32%, --border-control 52% on every input and unfilled control, --border-strong 42%; disabled = --text-muted at .6 opacity plus a hairline, never a darker fill (it disappears); skeleton shimmer runs from --bg-el to --bg-el-hover. Selected sidebar row --bg-el + --text (not accent fill).

09-DARK-009 Tests. (a) Token test: every light role has a dark role; L and chroma bounds; no literals. (b) Contrast matrix in dark and Contrast+ dark (09-COLR-006). (c) Visual regression of every Storybook state in dark at 320/768/1280/1600. (d) Live-switch test: toggle system theme during a stream — no reflow, no re-render of committed Turns (09-STRM-005), the stream continues. (e) A 10-person night-use panel at 30% screen brightness rates legibility ≥4/5 on the Mark view and reader.

Why: pure black with saturated accents is the most-cited dark-mode failure (ux-design §19); students study late (student-voice §"21:40 on a school night", J3), so dark mode is a primary theme, not a bonus.

09.14Print and export

Print is a first-class surface: teachers file Marks, students revise from paper, and the Learning Receipt (§12) exists to be handed over. Four print templates ship at MVP; each has a Playwright print-to-PDF test on A4 and Letter in both orientations where relevant.

09-PRNT-001 Common print stylesheet. @media print and the PDF export share one stylesheet: light palette forced (09-DARK-007); body --font-serif at 11 pt / 1.4 unless the user's reading-comfort family is Hyperlegible or OpenDyslexic, which are honoured (09-PRIN-018); 2 cm margins; measure = full column; page numbers "3 / 7" bottom-right and the document title bottom-left in 9 pt; links printed as underlined text with the URL in 8 pt after them only in the Receipt; math via KaTeX SSR with fonts embedded; images at ≤300 dpi source, never upscaled; orphans: 3; widows: 3; break-inside: avoid on AOCards, Cards, ER quotes, tables ≤12 rows and code blocks ≤40 lines; a table >12 rows repeats its <thead> on each page. Colours: credited = solid underline + 15% grey wash; partial = dotted; uncredited = dotted + ×; the CalibrationBadge prints in full. Acceptance: printing a 20-mark Mark to A4 yields ≤3 pages with no AOCard split across a page.

09-PRNT-002 What is stripped. Composer, sidebar, rail, tab strip, banners, toasts, hover cards, IntentRow, HelpLadder, MessageActions, skeletons, scrim, the "↓ New" pill, usage meter, any aria-hidden decoration, and the celebrate ring animation frame. Citation chips print as superscript numerals with a numbered "Sources" list at the end (title · page · trust badge · deep link text). Turn branches print the active branch only. Acceptance: DOM audit in print emulation finds no element with data-print="strip" rendered.

09-PRNT-003 Templates.

TemplateTriggerContents and layoutPage rules

Teacher override state prints both marks and the reason.Portrait; answer never split mid-paragraph from its first span; AO cards break-inside: avoid.
Learning ReceiptSettings › Export; Receipt screen (§10.23)Cover block: student (display name only), assignment, Course, date range, signed hash (SHA-256, first 16 hex + QR to the verification URL); timeline table (timestamp · event · rung · Mark · seen-solution flag); appendix of drafts with diff bars (added = solid left rule, removed = struck).
