09-PRNT-004 PDF export fidelity. Server-side rendering (headless Chromium with the same stylesheet) so the PDF equals print preview: text is selectable and searchable, MathML is embedded as tagged structure (PDF/UA tagging for headings, lists, tables, alt text on images = the accessible name used on screen), fonts embedded and subset, file ≤2 MB for a Mark and ≤10 MB for a Receipt with images. Exports carry document metadata (title, author = student display name, subject = Course, creation date, margin:export_version). Anki .apkg export of Cards keeps LaTeX and images and writes provenance into a source field. ICS export of the Plan (§10.15) and Markdown/DOCX of artifacts (§10.17) follow the same strip rules. Acceptance: pixel diff between browser print preview and server PDF <1% per page on the four fixture documents; pdfinfo shows tagged = yes; VoiceOver reads the PDF headings.

09-PRNT-005 Watermarks. Handwritten-answer images print with a 9 pt "Original image — kept for teacher review" caption, not a diagonal watermark. Below-gate Marks (uncalibrated) print "Practice estimate — not yet calibrated for this paper" as the band position and print no number; provisional prints the badge. A Mark exported by a student for a teacher carries no watermark; a public Receipt link prints "Public copy — learner state removed". Nothing is ever watermarked "DRAFT" or "CONFIDENTIAL" in a way that fails 3:1 with body text beneath it.

09-PRNT-006 Non-affiliation notice. Every printed or exported page footer includes, in 8 pt: "Margin is not affiliated with or endorsed by Cambridge International Education or any examination board. Marks are practice estimates, not board marks. Syllabus and mark-scheme references are to the board's published documents." The board name is substituted from the Pack; the string is in the catalogue and localised. Acceptance: string present in every fixture footer; copy lint passes on it.

09-PRNT-007 Print from mobile. Mobile routes expose "Export PDF" (server render), not window.print(), since mobile print dialogs drop the stylesheet; the PDF opens in the system share sheet. Acceptance: iOS Safari export of a Mark produces the same PDF hash as desktop for the same fixture.

09.15Internationalisation

Margin launches with an English UI and English, Russian and Kazakh explanation languages; the Russian and Kazakh UI ship in v2 (SYNTHESIS §13). Internationalisation is built in from the first commit, so v2 is a catalogue and a font check, not a refactor.

09-I18N-001 Locale model. Three independent settings in one object, stored per user and overridable per Course:

{ "ui_locale": "en-GB",
  "explain_lang": "en|ru|kk",
  "exam_variety": "en-GB",
  "number_locale": "en-GB|ru-RU|kk-KZ",
  "decimal_comma": false,
  "timezone": "Asia/Almaty",
  "calendar": "gregory", "first_day": "monday",
  "units": "metric" }

ui_locale drives the catalogue; explain_lang is passed to the tutor route as a system-prompt variable (the syllabus terms stay in the exam's language and are glossed, e.g. "маржинальная прибыль (contribution)"); exam_variety fixes spelling and vocabulary in anything the student will write in an exam; number_locale and decimal_comma drive Intl and the keypad. Default detection: browser navigator.languages for ui_locale, Course board for exam_variety, explain_lang asked once in setup (10.2). Acceptance: a kk-KZ browser user on a Cambridge Course sees an English UI at MVP with Russian/Kazakh available for explanations, exam_variety en-GB, decimal comma on.

09-I18N-002 Glyph coverage. CI renders the fixture "Ә Ғ Қ Ң Ө Ұ Ү Һ І — Қазақстан, Өскемен; ёж, щука, ъ; Ў ў Ғ ғ Ҳ ҳ" plus "∑ ∫ ≤ ≥ ≠ → ⇌ ° µ ½ ¾ ‰ £ ₸ ₽" in every family of 09-TYPE-001 (Inter, Atkinson Hyperlegible Next, OpenDyslexic, Literata → PT Serif, Geist Mono → JetBrains Mono) at 400/500/600 and fails on any glyph drawn by a fallback font (detected by document.fonts + canvas glyph-bounds comparison against the fallback face). Where a family lacks a glyph (OpenDyslexic lacks parts of extended Cyrillic; Geist Mono's Cyrillic is unverified), the family declares a per-script fallback in @font-face unicode-range so the fallback is chosen per glyph and looks intentional: OpenDyslexic → Atkinson Hyperlegible Next for U+0400–04FF; Geist Mono → JetBrains Mono for Cyrillic. Subsets shipped: latin, latin-ext, cyrillic, cyrillic-ext, greek, math; total font payload ≤380 KB woff2 for the default UI path. Acceptance: zero fallback glyphs in the test; the Settings specimen line renders each Kazakh letter in the chosen family or its declared fallback.

09-I18N-003 String catalogue rules. Every user-visible string lives in catalogue/<locale>.json keyed by a stable id (mark.band.aria, gate.chip.label); no string literals in components (ESLint no-literal-jsx-text + a runtime check in dev that throws on unkeyed text). ICU MessageFormat for every plural, select and number: "{n, plural, one {# card due} other {# cards due}}"; Russian and Kazakh use one/few/many/other and CLDR handles Kazakh's one/other. Placeholders are named, never positional; no sentence is assembled from fragments; no string is reused across contexts with different grammar (a button "Mark" and a noun "Mark" are two keys). Each key carries description and max_length for the translator; keys over their length fail the catalogue test. Copy lint (09-COPY-003) runs per locale with a per-language lexicon; formal "вы" and no diminutives (09-COPY-006). Acceptance: catalogue test finds 0 missing keys per shipped locale, 0 unused keys, 0 plurals without all CLDR categories.

09-I18N-004 Typography per script. Serif reading face must have true Cyrillic italics (Literata does; PT Serif as fallback) — a synthesised oblique in a Russian textbook quote is a defect. Cyrillic body runs ≈8–10% wider than English: measures are in ch of the active family, so 68 ch holds; the UI must survive +35% string length (Russian and Kazakh averages) and +50% in buttons without truncation or overflow — labels wrap to two lines inside --control-h-lg, never ellipsise. Caps labels at +0.06 em tracking are permitted in Cyrillic; small caps are not (poor Cyrillic support). Acceptance: pseudo-locale run (09-I18N-008) at +35%/+50% shows no clipped text and no horizontal overflow on any route.

09-I18N-005 Numbers, dates, units and math input. All formatting through Intl.NumberFormat / Intl.DateTimeFormat / Intl.RelativeTimeFormat with number_locale; marks and bands keep the exam's convention ("11–13 / 20" with an en dash, never a hyphen); percentages follow locale ("12,5 %" in ru-RU with a narrow no-break space); currency in Business questions stays as printed in the Item ("$", "£", "₸") — never converted; dates default to "Thu 18 Sep" (short weekday + day + short month), 24-hour clock in ru/kk, 12-hour only if the OS says so; countdowns "243 days" via plural rules. Math input accepts both . and , as decimal separators and normalises to LaTeX . on submit while the preview line shows the locale form; thousands separators (space in ru-RU) are stripped on parse; the keypad's decimal key shows the locale glyph. SI units per the Pack's convention (Cambridge sciences: "m s⁻¹" in print, m/s accepted). Acceptance: 40-case formatter fixture per locale; entering 3,5 in the keypad yields 3.5 in the Attempt and "3,5" in the preview under ru-RU.

09-I18N-006 Exam-board spelling and vocabulary. exam_variety selects a spelling dictionary and glossary used by the tutor, the generator and the copy lint on model output: Cambridge/AQA/OCR/Pearson/IB(UK English) → en-GB ("organisation", "programme", "labour", "maths"); College Board/AP → en-US; a future Australian board → en-AU. The tutor never "corrects" a student's spelling toward another variety. Board term maps travel with the Pack (Pack.glossary: "trade payables" vs "creditors", "revenue" vs "sales turnover", "mark scheme" vs "scoring guidelines"). Acceptance: the model-output lint flags en-US spellings in a 9609 Course at ≥95% recall on a 200-word fixture; 0 corrections of student spelling in the Turn eval.

09-I18N-007 RTL readiness. Logical properties only (margin-inline-start, inset-inline-end, text-align: start); stylelint bans physical left/right in layout properties except inside [dir]-scoped math and code containers. Icons with direction (chevrons, back arrow, send, "↓ New" is vertical and exempt) are mirrored via [dir=rtl] { transform: scaleX(-1) } on a data-mirror allowlist; math, code, PDFs, timers, marks ("11–13 / 20") and citation numerals are never mirrored (dir="ltr" + unicode-bidi: isolate). Tab order follows visual order in RTL. No RTL locale ships before v2, but the smoke test runs from MVP. Acceptance: dir="rtl" pseudo-locale screenshot suite on every route shows mirrored chrome and un-mirrored math; 0 physical-side properties reported by stylelint.

09-I18N-008 Pseudo-locales in CI. Three built-in pseudo-locales run on every Storybook story and route: en-XA (accented, +35% length, brackets to expose concatenation: "[Ḿâŕķ ţĥîš âñšŵéŕ one two]"), en-XL (+50%, buttons and chips only), ar-XB (RTL mirrored, Latin text reversed). Failures: any string not wrapped in brackets (a literal), any overflow, any clipped ring or chip, any mirrored math. Acceptance: pseudo-locale job green on every PR.

09-I18N-009 Russian and Kazakh UI (v2 scope, prepared now). Catalogue keys, plural categories, per-script fallbacks and the +35% layout tolerance are in place at MVP; v2 adds the two catalogues, native examiner-teacher review (09-COPY-006), Kazakh SRE speech (09-A11Y-018), Kazakh Intl data checks (Kazakh month names, kk-KZ decimal comma), and the Latin-script Kazakh alphabet as a display option when the state transition is stable (founder-owned; default: Cyrillic only). Every date and number surface is already locale-driven, so the v2 change is data, not code. Acceptance (v2): the 12 keyboard flows of 09-A11Y-014 pass in ru-RU and kk-KZ with no English fallback strings visible.

09.16Pixel-level QA checklist (release gate)

This checklist is the release gate: every row runs on the release candidate, every row has a pass criterion and a named tool, and the release ships only when all rows are green or a founder-signed waiver names the row and the fix date. Rows marked CI run on every PR as well; rows marked manual are executed by a reviewer on the RC build and recorded in the release note. Tools: axe = axe-core in Playwright; LH = Lighthouse; PW-diff = Playwright screenshot diff against committed goldens (threshold 0.1% pixels unless stated); PW-script = Playwright assertion; stylelint/eslint = the lint rules of §09; lint-copy = the copy lint of 09-COPY-003; manual = human on the RC.

§10Screen-by-screen specification

10.0Conventions used in this section

§10 specifies the 25 canonical screens of SYNTHESIS §6 one by one, in the order of that list, each against the tokens and components of §09, followed by two surfaces the rest of the document depends on and that list does not name: 10.26 Ask (the Course-less conversation referenced by §00, §03 and 10.3) and 10.27 Public paper finder (the free-forever finder that SYNTHESIS §12 makes distribution channel 3 and §14.4 gives an engineering owner). Screens are numbered 10.1–10.27; requirement IDs are 10-<SCR>-NNN where <SCR> is the four-letter screen tag in the table below. Nothing in a screen spec redefines a token or a component; it names the component from 09.7 and the state it is in.

10-CONV-001 Per-screen template. Every screen subsection contains these blocks in this order; a missing block is a spec defect.

BlockContent
PurposeOne sentence: the learning outcome the screen exists to produce.
StageMVP or v1, and where a screen splits, which regions belong to which. Required on every screen: an unstaged screen is built at MVP by default, which is a spec defect if that was not intended. A docs-lint asserts one **Stage.** line per §10 subsection.
Jobs servedRow ids from §02.2 (J1–J12) and, where relevant, the exam-year moment (02-MOM-*).
RoutePath pattern, params, and what deep-linking to it requires.

Interactions and shortcutsPointer, keyboard (from 09.10), touch gestures, and the drag alternatives. A screen whose interaction model has genuinely distinct modes may split this block into named sub-blocks (10.10's Timer / Submit, 10.12's Review interaction), provided the screen's keyboard shortcuts appear in one of them; the block may not simply be absent.

10-CONV-002 Right-pane rail behaviour (applies to 10.5, 10.6, 10.7, 10.16, 10.17). Default state on every fresh Session is the 48 px rail: a vertical strip with the four tab icons (Source · Scratchpad · Artifact · Cards, 20 px optical) and a citation-count badge (--text-xs tabular) under Source. It opens to --panel-w on: the first citation-chip click, the first artifact card, any Mark (Mark view opens it to the cited scheme line), the Reader, ⌘J, or a tab-icon click. It collapses on ⌘J, the rail toggle, or Esc when focus is inside it and no layer is open. Opening does not change the centre measure (the centre column is fixed at 68 ch and centred in 1fr); the transition is --dur-drawer on transform only. On tablet portrait the same content is a bottom sheet at the 50% detent; on mobile it is a full-height sheet at 92%. The open/closed state persists per Course. Acceptance: fresh Session screenshot shows exactly two panes and a 48 px rail; a chip click opens the pane within one --dur-drawer with the centre paragraph width unchanged.

10-CONV-005a Syllabus numbers in wireframes and fixtures. Every syllabus point number and title shown in a §10 wireframe, example string or test fixture ("3.2.1 Motivation theories") is read from one fixture constants file, fixtures/syllabus_points.ts, generated from the Pack at build time — never typed into a wireframe or a test. The file is the reason a number can be corrected in one place when 15-OPEN-010 resolves the 2026–28 numbering from the syllabus PDF. Acceptance: a docs-lint matching \b\d\.\d(\.\d)?\s+[A-Z] in §04, §07 and §10 resolves every hit against the constants file and fails on an unknown point; the §07.5 and §10.6 examples resolve to the same title for the same number.

10-CONV-006 Shared acceptance for every screen (not repeated below): all rows of 09.16 pass on the screen; the screen has an empty and an error story; the primary action is the only filled button; no string outside the catalogue; Web Vitals per 09-QA-056 where the screen is a landing target; the screen's keyboard flow (09-A11Y-014) is scripted when it owns one.

10.1Landing / First Mark

Purpose. Give an anonymous visitor an examiner-grade Mark on their own answer inside 90 seconds, before any account exists, so the first thing Margin does is the thing nobody else does (SYNTHESIS §3.3, §5 bet 2).

Stage. MVP, in full. This is the acquisition surface: nothing on it is deferred, including /m/:markToken sharing of an anonymous Mark, which is the link a student sends a friend.

Jobs served. J1 (know what an examiner would give it and why); 02-MOM-001 (September start). Secondary: J4 for the "just mark it" visitor.

Route. / (anonymous). A sample chip appends ?q=<sample_id>. Once a Mark starts streaming the URL becomes /m/:markToken (24-hour token, shareable read-only) without a page load.

Layout. Desktop: no sidebar, no rail; one centred column, composer 640 px wide with its top edge at 40% viewport height; below it the four sample chips; footer with the non-affiliation line (09-PRNT-006). When the Mark streams, the page becomes the Mark view layout (10.7) in place: answer left, Mark right, right pane open at the cited scheme line. Tablet: same, composer 560 px. Mobile: composer full width above the keyboard-safe area, chips wrap to two rows, Mark view stacks (answer on top).

Regions and elements.

RegionElements
Top bar (48)wordmark (text, 14 px 600) · "Sign in" text button · theme toggle. No nav, no pricing link above the fold.
Line--text-h2 24/1.25 · 500: "Paste an answer, or photograph one. We'll mark it like an examiner." (key landing.line)
ComposerComposer in text state, placeholder "Paste your answer here — question text first if you have it" · + (file: PDF/DOCX/image) · ModeChip locked to Mark with Learn/Practise present but disabled (tooltip "After your first Mark") · camera (→ 10.8 anonymous path) · Send.
Sample chipsfour outline chips 32 h: "9609 12-mark evaluation" · "0580 vectors" · "9701 mechanism" · "Photograph your own". A sample chip fills the composer with a real OWN Item question and a stored exemplar answer (Tier 0, mid-band) and skips the board/subject sheet.
Two-field sheetSheet (desktop: 480 px centred panel, --shadow-3; mobile: 50% detent) with Board typeahead (MVP: Cambridge International live; AQA/OCR/Pearson/IB listed as "coming" and disabled) and Subject typeahead by code or name ("9609 Business"). Two fields, one primary button "Mark it".
Footernon-affiliation line · Privacy · Terms · "For teachers" text link.

States. empty is the default; there is no other landing content. loading: after "Mark it" the composer collapses upward over --dur-base and the Mark view skeleton (MarkHeader, three AOCard skeletons, BandTotal skeleton) appears; status line at 800 ms. streaming: per 09-STRM-011. error: InlineError in the Mark column ("The marker timed out. Retry, or copy your answer."); the pasted text is preserved in the composer. offline: composer stays editable; Send shows "Marks need a connection"; nothing is queued anonymously. gated: the anonymous allowance is the anonymous: block of limits.yaml (03-LIM-001) — 2 levels Marks per device per 24 h by a cookie + IP heuristic, 0 Deep Turns, Learn and Practise unavailable, nothing queued offline — and this screen renders that number rather than declaring one; the third attempt shows a one-line card above the composer "Two free Marks used today. Save a Course to keep marking — it takes a minute." with Save this Course; Learn/Practise stay disabled anonymously. No paywall copy appears before the first Mark.

Interactions and shortcuts. Paste (⌘V) into the composer; Enter sends; a paste longer than 4,000 words shows "Paste one question's answer at a time" inline and marks the first 4,000 words. Drag-and-drop of an image or PDF onto the composer opens the capture/confirm flow. The sample chip swaps the composer content and shows a 13 px muted line "Sample answer — edit it or paste your own". After the first Mark and the first re-mark, an inline card below the delta (not a modal) reads "Save this Course to keep this Mark, your rewrite and your Cards." with Email · Apple · Google; dismissing it leaves a text link in the Mark header. On token expiry (24 h) the /m/:markToken route shows the Mark read-only with the same card. ? in the empty composer opens the palette help.

Data. Writes an anonymous Attempt {anon_device_id, item_id | user_question_text, response, transcript_confirmed, timestamp} and its Mark; no Learner Graph, no memory, no Cards until Save (Cards are generated but held on the Attempt). An unclaimed anonymous Attempt and its Mark are deleted 30 days after creation and the device id is not retained beyond that (§11.13); the /m/:markToken link stops resolving at 24 h regardless. On Save the Attempts migrate to the account and the Course setup (10.2) starts pre-filled with the board and subject. Reads the Pack for the chosen syllabus (scheme items for the sample Items; command-word table for user questions). Telemetry: landing_view, paste, sheet_complete, mark_done (with ttfm_ms), remark_done, save_click.

Acceptance.

  1. Time from Send to MarkHeader ≤2 s p95 and to done ≤45 s p95 on the four sample Items (staging soak).
  2. No account, cookie banner, email field or pricing appears before mark_done; the only blocking UI before the Mark is the two-field sheet (skipped for samples).
  3. Web Vitals per the §11.14 route budget for / (this screen states no budget of its own); initial JS ≤220 KB gz, fonts ≤380 KB; Lighthouse performance ≥90 on the mid-tier Android profile.
  4. /m/:markToken renders the full Mark with spans and band for 24 h to anyone with the link, then the expiry card; no learner state is exposed (there is none).
  5. Funnel targets instrumented: paste→full Mark ≥55%, Mark→rewrite ≥70%, Mark→Save ≥35% within the session (SYNTHESIS §5 bet 2).
  6. Keyboard flow 1 of 09-A11Y-014 completes; the sample chips are reachable by Tab and announce their subject.

10.2Course setup sheets (onboarding as a flow)

Purpose. Turn the anonymous visitor's first Mark into a Course — the home object every Attempt hangs on — with the fewest fields that let the scheduler, the Examiner Twin and the Plan work on day one.

Stage. MVP for the six required sheets and the class-code path. Within import (optional at every stage): mock photos, Anki/Quizlet and class code are MVP; notes PDF, timetable and another assistant's export are v1 — the flow already treats every import as skippable and background, so a v1 row adds a picker option and nothing else.

Jobs served. J3 (highest-value 20 minutes needs a Plan, which needs a date), J8 (an honest estimate needs papers and target), J6 (mock import), 02-MOM-001.

Route. /start → /start/:step, steps in order: save · course · papers · date · level · consent · import. Each step is a route so the back arrow and browser Back work and a refresh resumes; progress is held in the session store (server-side once save completes, local before). Entry points: the "Save this Course" card (10.1), a class code (/join/:code, which pre-fills board, syllabus, papers and exam series from the Class and skips to level), the app-store first launch (which runs course → papers → date first and then routes to a marked Item before save, per SYNTHESIS §3.3 last sentence), and "Add a Course" from Home.

Layout. Not modals: a flow of sheets. Desktop: a 480 px panel centred in the viewport on --bg-app, --shadow-3, with a 12 px caps step line ("Step 2 of 6") and a hairline progress track (2 px, --accent) at the top; the previous sheet slides out left and the next in from the right over --dur-page on transform (reduced motion: crossfade). Mobile: each sheet is a full-screen route with the 44 pt top bar (back · step · skip when allowed). Every sheet has ≤2 fields, one primary button 44 h, and a text-button secondary ("Back" or "Skip"). The account step is one sheet; three Course sheets are required; consent is required by policy; import is optional. Anonymous pre-account onboarding (the two-field sheet of 10.1) is the only sheet shown before the Mark — SYNTHESIS §6's "≤3 sheets" bound applies to that pre-Mark path.

Sheets.

StepFields (≤2)Rules and copy
saveAge band (Under 13 · 13–15 · 16–17 · 18+), first field · then Email, or Apple / Google buttonsThe age band is asked before any identifier is collected, because collecting an email from an under-13 and gating afterwards is the COPPA/AADC failure the gate exists to prevent. Selecting Under 13 routes immediately to the school-only page and no email field is rendered, no user row is written, and the anonymous Attempt is discarded within 24 h. Otherwise: magic link; no password at MVP. Line: "Save this Course to keep this Mark, your rewrite and your Cards."

States. empty: each sheet's primary button is disabled until its required field is valid; no red until blur. loading: Pack fetch for the syllabus shows a 32 px row skeleton in the typeahead; the primary button shows a 16 px spinner ≤1 s. error: inline under the field ("That code isn't a class we know. Check with your teacher."), never a modal; magic-link send failure offers "Try Google instead". offline: the flow cannot start; a Banner explains and the pending anonymous Mark stays cached for 24 h. gated: a Class whose teacher locked syllabus/papers renders those sheets read-only with "Set by your teacher"; a board without a live Pack shows "Coming — we'll email you when 9700 Biology is ready" and still creates the Course in waiting state with Cards and Library working.

Interactions and shortcuts. Enter = Continue when valid; Esc = Back; ⌘. = Skip where allowed; segmented controls are radiogroups with arrow keys; typeahead accepts code or name and shows the Pack version on the row; the 7-day row toggles with Space. Changing board on course after papers resets papers and says so in one line. The whole flow completes in ≤90 s at the median (telemetry setup_ms).

Data. Writes the Course {board, syllabus_code, syllabus_version, level, exam_session, papers[] with dates, target_grade, study_days[], explain_lang, age_band, consent{parent_email, verified_at}, class_id?}; the anonymous Attempt(s) re-parent to course_id; probe answers create Attempts with confidence and seed the Learner Graph; imports create Library Sources (with provenance USER), Cards (with imported_from), Plan busy blocks or a mock run. Reads Pack metadata (papers, series, timetable), Class (for codes), policy object (age gates).

Acceptance.

  1. The required path is exactly six sheets (save · course · papers · date · level · consent) and the step counter says so ("Step 3 of 6"); import carries the word "Optional" instead of a step number; no sheet has more than two fields; a reviewer counts them in Storybook.
  2. Refresh on any step resumes at that step with entered values; browser Back moves one step, never exits the flow silently.
  3. A class-code entry pre-fills and locks teacher-set fields and lands on level in one step.
  4. An Under-13 selection on save collects no email, writes no user row, and discards the anonymous Attempt within 24 h. Under-16 with a pending (unverified) parent email reaches Today with memory visible and notifications off; the state is shown in Settings › Memory.
  5. Import of a 200-card .apkg with LaTeX and images completes in the background and produces Cards with provenance lines; the flow never waits on it.
  6. Keyboard flow 2 of 09-A11Y-014 completes; every segmented control announces its options and current value.

10.3Home / Today

Purpose. Answer "what is the highest-value thing to do right now" in one glance and start it in one tap: the scheduler's session mix rendered as three cards, with the week visible and nothing that shames.

Stage. MVP. Multi-Course merging is MVP because a student sits several papers; the exam chip and the 7-day strip are MVP.

Jobs served. J3 (21:40 on a school night), J12 (review what is due), J8 indirectly (the exam chip), 02-MOM-002…004 (calendar-position behaviour).

Route. /home. Default after sign-in. Multi-Course users see one Today merged across Courses by mark-yield, each card tagged with its Course; the Course switcher is in the top bar.

Layout. Desktop: sidebar shows Courses (not a syllabus tree — Home is above Courses), then a single Ask row directly under the Courses group, then Recent and Due; centre column 68 ch; no right pane (no rail either — nothing here cites). Tablet: same without sidebar (overlay). Mobile: single column; the 7-day strip is horizontally scrollable with today centred; the three cards stack; the composer is absent (Home is not a chat — a conversation without a Course is an Ask, 10.26, reached in one keystroke from the sidebar row, ⌘K → Ask <anything>, or /ask).

States. empty (new Course, nothing due, no Session): the three cards still show work — Continue: "Start with a probe on 3.2 Motivation" · Due: "No cards yet — they come from your Marks" · Next: "Practise one 4-mark Explain · 8 min"; never a greeting or an illustration. loading: three card skeletons with final geometry; the week strip renders from cache immediately. error (scheduler unavailable): cards fall back to the last computed queue with a 13 px line "Showing yesterday's plan — refreshing"; never blank. offline: Due card is live (local FSRS); Continue/Next show "Needs a connection" as their line with the action disabled; the Banner shows the offline string (09-COPY-002 #16). gated/quota: if today's levels-Mark quota is exhausted, Next never proposes a levels Mark; it proposes points Items or Cards and says why in the mix line ("levels Marks resume at 00:00"). Between-papers mode: Next is restricted to the next paper only.

Interactions and shortcuts. Tapping "Why" opens a popover with the phase rule and the mark-yield list behind Next (top 3 syllabus points with yield_s). Long-press/⋯ on Next offers "Something else" → the next two candidates; a decline is logged, not argued. The widget (iOS/Android) mirrors Due and Next with the same strings and deep links.

Data. Reads: Learner Graph (due queue with counts and minutes, phase, mark-yield ranking, last open Session/Item), Plan (blocks for the strip, rest days, Quiet Hours, weekly goal), Course (exam dates, papers, between-papers flag), policy object (quotas, teen defaults). Writes: session_started {source: continue|due|next}, next_declined {item_id, reason?}, home_view telemetry. Nothing on Home mutates mastery.

Acceptance.

  1. Copy corpus test on Home: zero matches for the streak/shame lexicon; no % in any mastery string; the mix line's percentages are the only percentages.
  2. Every state shows three actionable cards; the empty state has been reviewed in Storybook for a Course with 0 Attempts.
  3. TTI ≤1.5 s from cache; cards paint from the last queue before the network responds (stale-while-revalidate).
  4. Quiet Hours banner appears exactly inside the configured window across DST changes (unit test with Asia/Almaty and Europe/London).
  5. Exam-week collapse triggers at T−7 days 00:00 local for the nearest paper and reverts after the paper's end time.
  6. A moderated test of five students: each names what to do next within 3 s and starts it in one tap.

Purpose. Orient the student in the exam's own structure — the official syllabus tree with honest mastery on every point — and make the Course's facts (Pack version, dates, memory, files, class) visible and editable in one place.

Stage. MVP.

Route. /c/:courseId (the tree is the Learn tab's default state without a Session). Tabs /learn · /papers · /cards · /plan · /progress share the Course header.

Tablet: tree in the overlay sidebar, detail in centre. Mobile: the tree is the screen (route stack: Course → Unit → Point → detail), the header collapses to two rows.

States. empty (Course just created): every pip is Unseen (empty ring); the centre shows "Start with a 3-question probe on what school is teaching now" with Start probe and a "Pick a point" hint; rings show "—" with "No timed practice yet". loading: tree rows skeleton at final row height; header from cache. error: tree from cache with a 13 px line "Mastery may be out of date"; if the Pack fails to load, "Syllabus unavailable — retry" inline. offline: tree and pips from the local Learner Graph snapshot; Learn/Practise actions disabled with the reason; Cards enabled. gated: a Pack in waiting state (board not live) shows the official tree with pips disabled and the line "Marking for {code} arrives when its Pack is live — {roadmap_date}. A Class-locked Course shows a lock glyph on teacher-set facts.

Interactions and shortcuts. Click/Enter on a row selects (no animation, 09-MOTN-003); →/← expand/collapse; typing filters; ⌘K "Learn <point>" jumps here then into a Session; hovering/focusing a pip shows the reason tooltip; the Pack chip opens a changelog sheet ("v14: 3.2 wording updated to the 2026 syllabus; 2 Items withdrawn"); "Show in book" opens the right pane at the syllabus page (≤400 ms p95); memory rows edit inline with Enter/Esc and "Forget" removes with an Undo toast; the decay reason names the date and the fix ("practise unaided before 20 Sep").

Data. Reads: Pack (tree, wording, Items per node, misconceptions, version, changelog), Learner Graph (mastery state and M_s, retrievability, decay date, mark-yield yield_s, seen-solution expiry, last Attempts), Course (dates, target, papers, extra time), memory rows, Library files, Class. Writes: memory edits (memory_update), filter/sort/collapse state (per user), tree_node_selected, extra-time and rest-break settings (Course.extra_time_pct, Course.rest_breaks).

Acceptance.

  1. Pips are distinguishable in a greyscale screenshot and every pip's tooltip contains a count, a last-seen date and a decay date (or "—" with the reason).
  2. Node numbering and wording match the Pack byte-for-byte; the Pack version chip matches Course.pack_version; a changed Pack shows the new chip within one session start.
  3. No percentage appears anywhere in the tree or node detail; rings show a whole number with a reason line, hidden inside T−7.
  4. Filter "High yield" sorts by yield_s descending and the badge value equals the scheduler's number for the same node (same query).
  5. Memory rows are editable and forgettable with Undo; a forgotten row never re-appears from inference (unit test on the memory writer).
  6. Tree of 220 nodes renders in ≤120 ms after data and scrolls at 60 fps (virtualised).

10.5Session (Course › Learn workspace)

Purpose. The Session is the workspace where tutoring happens: one Course-scoped thread of Turns and Attempts in which the Effort Gate, the Help Ladder, intent chips, citation chips and the source pane are all one gesture apart, and the hand-back returns the work to the student after every Turn.

Stage. MVP, in full, including branching, edit-and-regenerate, the Scratchpad tab and incognito. This is the screen §03.2 parity is measured on, so a deferred row here is a parity failure.

Jobs served. J2 (I got it wrong and don't know why), J4 (explain this so it sticks), J5 (teach me the point school is on), J11 ("just the answer" without losing the learning); 02-MOM-002 (mid-course), 02-MOM-005 (the 21:40 school night).

Route. /c/:courseId/learn/:sessionId. ?turn=<turnId> scrolls to and focuses a Turn; ?item=<itemId> opens a Session with that Item already posed. ⌘⇧N mints a new sessionId in the same Course. A Session is a container, not a memory boundary: the Learner Graph (§07.3) is read on every Turn regardless of which Session it is in.

Layout. Desktop ≥1280: sidebar = CourseTree (280) with Recent and Due beneath; centre = Turn stream at 68 ch centred in 1fr with the Composer sticky at the bottom edge (56 px rest, grows to 8 lines); right pane = 48 px rail by default, opening to 480 per 10-CONV-002. Tablet 900–1279: 1fr 420px, sidebar as overlay, right pane a 50 % bottom sheet in portrait. Mobile <900: single column; the tree, the source pane, the math keypad and the mode menu are sheets; the composer sits above the keyboard-safe area and the HelpLadder moves from the message margin to a single "More help" button under the Turn.

States. empty (new Session): no greeting; the centre shows the Course's next Item proposal as a card ("Start where school is: 3.2.1 Motivation theories · one 8-mark Analyse") with Start and a 13 px line "or ask anything about 9609". loading: composer live immediately; history pages in as skeletons of the final geometry. streaming: 09-STRM-001…013 in full — optimistic echo ≤50 ms, status line at 800 ms drawn from the route, Stop in place, ↓ New pill after 120 px of user scroll. error: InlineError in the assistant slot with cause and "Retry with Think"; the user message is never lost. offline: composer stays editable, Send becomes "Will send", messages queue with a queued tag, Cards and downloaded sources remain usable, citation chips for uncached pages show "Available when you're back". gated/quota: past the Deep-Turn cap the Turn streams on the next route down with a one-line banner naming the change (03-LIM-003); the gate and ladder are never metered (03-LIM-005).

Interactions and shortcuts. Enter send, ⇧Enter newline, Esc stop-then-close-then-focus-composer; ⌘1/2/3 mode; ⌥1/⌥2/⌥3 fire the IntentRow while it is visible, from anywhere including the focused composer (bare digits type characters — 09-KEYS-001); ⇧↓ next help rung; ⌘E effort dial; ⌘J pane, ⌘⇧J pane tabs; ⌘F find in this Session; [ ] previous/next citation; ⌘↑ edit the last user message and ⌘⇧B branch this Turn (both create a branch pill "2/3 ◂ ▸"); ⌘⇧C copy Turn, ⌘⇧R retry, ⌘⇧S save selection as Card, ⌘⇧K Scratchpad, ⌘⇧M math keypad, ⌘⇧P photograph. Editing an earlier message is not keyboard-only: on desktop, hover or focus on any UserMessage reveals a 16 px pencil in a 24 px target; on touch, a 400 ms long-press or the ⋯ affordance opens a sheet with Edit · Copy · Branch. Hover or focus on an assistant Turn reveals MessageActions (copy · retry · explain simpler · quiz me · show in book); on touch they collapse to the same one ⋯, so every hover-reachable action has a touch path (09-A11Y-008). Selecting text in a Turn or in the source pane opens the SelectionPopover. Clicking a citation chip opens the right pane at the page in ≤400 ms p95 and returns focus to the chip on Esc. Long-press on the ladder margin (or the "More help" button on mobile) climbs exactly one rung.

Data. Reads: Learner Graph (mastery and state_reason for the Item's point, FSRS due, misconception priors, prefs.intent_by_item_type, memories, debt level), Pack (Item, scheme, syllabus wording, misconceptions, command-word table), Session history (last N Turns per §07.3), Course (papers, dates, phase, extra time), policy object (quotas, teen defaults). Writes: turns {role, text, rung, citations[], lint_result, route, latency_ms}, attempts {gate_state, gate_reason, gate_latency_ms, entry_rung, rung_reached, intent, seen_solution, confidence?}, mastery recomputation on Attempt close, FSRS scheduling for seen-solution retests, cards from Save-as-card, sessions {title, ended_at, end_card}, telemetry turn_sent, rung_climbed, chip_used, citation_opened.

10.6Practise runner

Purpose. Deliver one exam-shaped Item at a time — real tariff, real command word, real AO split — with the Effort Gate in front of it, a confidence rating on every submission, and a Mark at the end, so that practice produces evidence rather than a feeling of having practised.

Stage. MVP.

Jobs served. J5 (practise the point school is on), J7 (exam-style questions that behave like the real ones), J12 (retest what I got wrong); 02-MOM-002, 02-MOM-003.

Route. /c/:courseId/practise/:runId, ?item=<n> for the current position. A run is created by: Home › Next, the CourseTree node action Practise, ⌘K → Practise <point>, "5 more like this" from a Mark, a Wrong-question retest (10.13), or a teacher assignment (10.20). The run's composition is the scheduler's (§04.13): after first exposure no blocked run exceeds five same-type Items and interleaving pulls from the last three topics.

Layout. Desktop: 280px | 1fr | 480px with the sidebar showing the run strip (one row per Item: index, tariff pill, state) instead of the full tree; centre holds one Item at 68 ch; right pane is a rail and opens only after submission (never during the attempt — the source pane would be a leak). Tablet: 1fr 420px, run strip in the overlay. Mobile: one Item per screen, run strip as a 50 % sheet from the top-bar counter ("3 of 8"), answer area above the keyboard, actions pinned in the bottom 40 %.

RegionElements

A raw word count remains available but is unlabelled and carries no target, because the marker is instructed that length is not evidence and a words-per-mark constant coaches the behaviour it is built to ignore. States. empty: a run with zero Items cannot exist — the creator falls back to a generated Item and says so ("No past-paper Item left on 3.2.1 at this tariff — this one is a Margin original in P2 format"). loading: header and tariff paint first; the question body skeletons at final height; the timer starts only after the body paints. streaming: applies to the Mark after Submit (09-STRM-011) and to generated Items ("Writing an 8-mark Analyse on 3.2.1…" as a status line, ≤6 s p95). error: generation or scheme fetch failure shows an InlineError with "Try another Item" and preserves any typed text; a Mark failure keeps the Attempt and offers "Mark it again". offline: Items already in the run are answerable and answers are queued with the queued tag; Marks stream on reconnect; the Effort Gate and the ladder work from the cached Item (rungs 1–3 only; rungs 4–5 need the pre-solved key). gated/quota: when the levels-Mark quota is spent, the run continues and the submission returns evidence-only feedback with the copy of 09-COPY-002 #15 plus "Full Mark at 00:00"; points Items are never gated.

Interactions and shortcuts. Enter submits when the answer area is not focused, ⌘Enter submits from inside it; s skip, f flag, n next, p previous, ⇧↓ next rung, 1/2/3 set confidence when the slider has focus, ⌘⇧M keypad, ⌘⇧P camera. Skip records skipped_reason ∈ {too_hard, seen_it, no_time, other} from a two-tap row and reschedules the Item rather than deleting it. Flag adds the Item to the run's review list and to the Wrong-question bank if the subsequent Mark loses marks. "5 more like this" holds tariff and cognitive-demand tag fixed (§05.10) and appends to the current run. Leaving mid-run keeps the run open on Home › Continue for 7 days.

Data. Reads: Pack (Item, scheme, tariff, command word, AO split, minutes-per-mark, diagram checklist), Learner Graph (mastery, entry rung, misconception priors, interleaving pool, prefs), Course (extra time — applied to the soft timer's guide only), policy object. Writes: attempts {item_id, response, input_mode, confidence, confidence_default, gate_state, gate_latency_ms, entry_rung, rung_reached, latency_s, skipped_reason?, flagged}, the Mark, runs {composition, position, source}, mastery and FSRS updates on Mark commit, Cards generated from uncredited marking points (10.12), calibration.predict_postdict rows from confidence vs outcome.

Brier and the reliability diagram (10.14) are computed from touched values only; defaulted rows are counted separately and shown as "not rated" rather than as a guess. 10.7Mark view

Purpose. Render the Mark object (§05.2) as evidence on the student's own page: every credited, partial and uncredited span highlighted in their words, one card per AO with the descriptor it relied on, the command-word and cover-the-name checks, the band with its calibration basis, and exactly one thing to do next.

Stage. MVP. ?compare=<markId> re-mark deltas and the teacher-flag line are MVP; the wide ≥1600 side-by-side layout is MVP-optional (it degrades to the two-tab pane, which is the specified behaviour at every other width).

Jobs served. J1 (what would an examiner give this and why), J2 (why did I lose the mark), J10 (how do I turn a Level 2 into a Level 3); 02-MOM-003, 02-MOM-006 (post-mock).

Route. /c/:courseId/marks/:markId; anonymous first Mark at /m/:markToken (24 h, 10.1). Deep links: #ao=AO4, #span=<id>, ?compare=<markId> for a re-mark delta. A superseded Mark opens read-only with a banner "Superseded by a re-mark · Open the current Mark".

Layout. Desktop 1280–1599: sidebar auto-collapses to its 48 px rail on this route; centre = the answer at 56–68 ch; right 480 px carries two tabs ⟨Mark⟩ ⟨Source⟩ with Mark active — a citation chip switches to Source and [ ] walk citations, Esc returns to Mark. Desktop ≥1600: the wide grid variant of 09-SPCE-005 shows both side by side (Mark --panel-w-2 440, Source --panel-w 480) and the tab strip disappears. Tablet: answer above, Mark column below as a 92 % sheet reachable from a sticky "Mark" bar. Mobile, in this order: MarkHeader → command-word check line → BandTotal + CalibrationBadge → AO cards, each collapsed to its first credited span → "Show my answer" disclosure that expands the spanned answer inline, with a sticky "Jump to answer" chip. The student's own 400-word essay never sits above their result. Tapping a span scrolls to its card and tapping the card's quote scrolls back with a 400 ms highlight (no colour change beyond --highlight-source).

States. loading: the answer paints immediately (it is local); the Mark column shows MarkHeader then one AOCard skeleton per AO at fixed height. streaming: 09-STRM-011 — header ≤2 s, each AOCard ≤8 s, spans light in the answer as their card commits, BandTotal and badge last; the primary action button appears only when next_mark_advice has streamed. error: InlineError in the Mark column ("The marker timed out. Retry with Think, or copy your answer."); the answer and any confirmed transcript are untouched. offline: an already-received Mark is fully readable from cache including spans; new Marks queue. gated/quota: uncalibrated renders the evidence-only Mark with 09-COPY-002 #8; quota exhaustion renders the same evidence-only card with "Full Mark at 00:00". superseded: read-only banner. teacher-flagged (show_teacher_flag = true from a valid alternative or low AO confidence): a 13 px line "Flagged for your teacher: a valid point outside the indicative content" — never presented as an error.

Interactions and shortcuts. Tab walks spans in reading order; each span announces "credited / partially credited / not credited" plus its reason; Enter on a span scrolls its AOCard into view and back. ⌘. runs the primary action; ⌘⇧L "Another like this"; [ ] citations; ⌘E expands every AOCard. Hovering a span shows the reason and, for points papers, the marking_point_id. Selecting text in the answer offers "Ask about this line" (opens a Session Turn scoped to the span). Challenge this Mark is one tap → 10.22 with the AO preselected if an AOCard had focus. Show teacher copies a read-only link scoped to the Class. Nothing on this screen edits the student's text — the answer column is not an editor (10.17 owns rewriting).

Data. Reads: the Mark object in full (§05.2), the Attempt (transcript, image, input mode, confidence, gate_state), Pack (grid paraphrase, command-word definition, ER insights), calibration state for the paper, Class (for Show teacher and override), policy object (visibility). Writes: mark_views {mark_id, spans_focused[], dwell_s}, rewrite_started, challenge_created, cards on "Turn into Cards", calibration.predict_postdict postdict row when the student rated confidence before submitting, receipt_export. The Mark itself is immutable (05-MARK-012); re-marks, challenges and overrides create linked rows.

10.8Handwriting capture → confirm

Purpose. Turn a photograph of handwritten work into a transcript the student has confirmed, so that marking quotes the student's own words with no invented text and no silent OCR error.

Stage. MVP. Phone capture, QR hand-off and the confirm step are all MVP; batch mock import (10.2) rides the same flow.

Jobs served. J1 and J6 (mark what is in my exercise book / my mock script), J2 (why did this working lose the mark); 02-MOM-006. This screen is the entry point for §05.11 and for the mock import of 10.2.

Route. /capture/:token. The token is minted by the desktop client (QR + 6-character code), by the composer camera button, by the Paper runner's photo tab (confirmation deferred to after Submit, 10-RUNR-004) or by the mock-import step; it is single-use, bound to a Session, run or Attempt, and expires in 30 minutes. Opening the token on the phone requires no sign-in beyond the bound session's device claim; a re-used or expired token shows "This code has been used — scan a new one on your computer."

Layout. Phone (the primary surface, <900): full-bleed camera with a 44 pt top bar (close · flash · page counter "2 of 3") and a bottom action area in the lowest 30 % (shutter 72 px, gallery, Done); confirm is a full-screen route with the image on top (pinch-zoom, double-tap to fit) and the editable transcript beneath, split 45/55 with a draggable divider that also has a "Swap" button (09-A11Y-008). Desktop ≥1280: capture is a 480 px sheet showing the QR, the code, a drop zone and a "Use this computer's camera" link; confirm is side-by-side — image left in the centre column, transcript right in the 480 px pane, both scroll-synced by page. Tablet: side-by-side in landscape, stacked in portrait.

Regions and elements.

RegionElements
Capturelive edge detection (a 2 px --accent quad over the detected page, no animation) · auto-shutter when the quad is stable for 400 ms and blur passes (Laplacian variance ≥ threshold) · manual shutter always available · per-shot chips: Retake · Crop · Rotate · Add page
Crop / deskewfour corner handles plus the button alternatives Full page · Top half · Bottom half · Auto; deskew preview applied live; longest side normalised to ≤2,000 px
Quality gateone line under the thumbnail, never a modal: "Too blurry to mark — retake" (blur), "Part of the page is cut off" (edge), "Very dark — try more light"; the shot is kept and can still be used with a "Use it anyway" text button that sets quality_override = true on the Attempt

Transcriptlayout-preserving text: line breaks, ~~crossings-out~~ shown struck and never dropped, insertions, arrows, tables, units, superscripts, maths as rendered KaTeX with a "edit as LaTeX" toggle; low-confidence tokens (<0.7) underlined with a dotted 2 px rule and a 24 px tap target; [illegible] chips are red-free, labelled, and tappable to type the word

States. empty: no shot yet — the camera is the empty state; the desktop sheet shows the QR with "Scan with your phone · or drop a photo here". loading: transcription shows a per-page progress line "Reading page 2…" with the page thumbnail dimmed; target <20 s p95 per page (05-HAND-002). streaming: transcript text commits page by page, never token by token, so the editable field is never rewritten under the cursor. error: transcription failure gives an InlineError per page with "Retake" and "Type it instead" (a plain textarea that sets input_mode = typed); an expired token shows the re-scan line. offline: shots are stored locally with their crop, the page strip works, transcription queues and the confirm step opens when connectivity returns; the student is told which pages are waiting. gated/quota: camera Marks count against the levels-Mark quota only at Submit, never at capture, so a student is never blocked from photographing work.

Interactions and shortcuts. Volume keys fire the shutter; long-press the shutter takes a burst and keeps the sharpest frame. On the transcript, Tab jumps to the next low-confidence token (desktop), swipe-down on mobile does the same via a "Next to check" chip; editing a flagged token clears its underline; every edit is diffed into transcript_edits. Desktop ⌘⇧P opens the capture sheet; scanning the QR moves capture to the phone while the desktop shows a live "Page 2 received" list and takes over the confirm step when Done is pressed on the phone. Pinch-zoom inside the image disables sheet drag (09.7 Sheet).

Data. Reads: the bound Session/run/Attempt, Course subject (routes maths pages to Mathpix per 05-HAND-002), tenant retention policy. Writes: attempt_images {page_index, storage_key, crop, deskew_deg, blur_score, quality_override}, attempt.transcript, attempt.transcript_confidence[], attempt.transcript_confirmed, transcript_edits {token_index, from, to} (the OCR eval corpus, 05-HAND-009), input_mode = handwritten, illegible_tokens[]. Originals are kept encrypted per tenant policy (default 12 months), visible to the teacher of record for override review, never used for training (05-HAND-008).

Purpose. Course › Papers is the index of every past paper and original paper-format Item set for the Course, with the student's own status on each. 10.10Paper runner / Timed mock

Purpose. The Paper runner turns a past paper (or a 30-minute section, or an OWN paper-format set) into a timed, question-by-question sitting with real tariff, real minutes and no help. It produces one Attempt per question part; the debrief (10.11) consumes them.

Stage. MVP.

Jobs served. J7 (exam-style questions under exam conditions), J3 (the highest-value block tonight), J6 (photograph my handwritten answers at the end); 02-MOM-002, 02-MOM-006.

Route. /paper/:runId, ?part=<n> for the current position; /paper/:runId/debrief after Submit. A run is bound to one paper_instance and one student; the route refuses a second concurrent run of the same instance and resumes the existing one.

Layout. Desktop: the three-pane grid collapses to 72px 1fr 0 — the sidebar becomes a question nav rail (72 px, tariff pills), the right pane is closed and cannot open, the centre holds one part at a time at 68 ch. Tablet identical. Mobile: one part per screen, timer in the 44 pt top bar, nav via a bottom sheet (50%) listing parts.

Predict-before-start. Before the timer starts, one card: "Your predicted total for this paper" (a band slider 0–60 in 3-mark steps) + ConfidenceSlider, plus a fourth option Not sure that stores predict = null, predict_skipped = true and starts the paper. One tap before a 90-minute commitment is a fair ask; a wall is not. Stored as attempt_set.predict. Why: predict–postdict–compare is the calibration loop (§04.14).

No-help rule. While the runner is open: no tutor Turn can be sent; the ModeChip, IntentRow, HelpLadder, CitationChips, Library and Cards are not rendered; ⌘K exposes only Go to part, Flag, Rest, Submit, Reading comfort; pasting text from outside the app is permitted but tagged paste_events[] on the Attempt (shown to teachers on assignments). Leaving the route shows a sheet "Leave the mock? The timer keeps running for 2 minutes, then the paper submits" — tap alternative to drag.

Timer. minutes × (1 + extra_time_pct); ticks without animation; at 0 the label becomes "+00:01" in the same colour and the paper continues (overtime is recorded per part as overtime_s); no sound, no red, no modal (09.7 Timer). Rest pauses the timer and greys the answer area; rests beyond the Course allowance are allowed but logged rest_over_allowance=true.

Autosave and resume. Every 5 s and on blur, per part, local-first (IndexedDB) then server; a crash or tab close resumes at the same part with the timer advanced by wall-clock time; offline continues locally and syncs on Submit.

Submit. Sheet lists unanswered and flagged parts, photo parts awaiting confirmation, and the quota line ("Marking this paper uses 3 levels Marks"). Confirm → Attempts close (timed=true, minutes_used, per-part latency) → photo parts go through 10.8 confirm → Marks stream in the debrief. Mobile keeps Submit in the bottom 40%.

10.11Mock debrief

Purpose. The Mock debrief is the Principal-Examiner report on one sitting: what each part earned, where the time went, which AO leaked marks, the three things to fix, and when to retest. It is generated only from the sitting's Marks and the ER corpus (§05.9) — never from a model's impression of the paper.

Stage. MVP.

Jobs served. J1 (what would an examiner give this), J8 (how do I stand against real thresholds), J10 (what turns a Level 2 into a Level 3), J12 (schedule the retests); 02-MOM-003, 02-MOM-006.

Route. /paper/:runId/debrief, #part=<id> opens a part's Mark in the right pane; reachable from Papers (10.9), Home › Continue and ⌘K → Go to debrief.

Layout. Desktop: sidebar shows the question nav (same rail as the runner, now with band chips); centre is the debrief at 68 ch; right pane opens on the Mark of the selected part (10.7 content) and defaults to the first lost-mark cluster. Tablet 1fr 420px. Mobile: single scroll; parts table collapses to a card list; Mark opens as a full route.

Regions and elements.

RegionElements and rules
Postdict cardrendered first, before any mark is visible; band slider + ConfidenceSlider; stores attempt_set.postdict. The rest of the screen stays skeletoned while it is open, but it is not a wall: a plain secondary Show me the marks appears after 10 s and stores postdict = null, postdict_skipped = true, and the card is auto-skipped when affect_tag ∈ {distress, crisis} in the last 24 h or in between-papers mode. Skipped rows are dropped from the Brier computation and the postdict is re-offered once after the marks have been read (10-DBRF-009).
Component headerBandTotal for the whole paper (sum of modal marks with combined low/high) + CalibrationBadge (worst status among parts governs: any uncalibrated part → whole-paper total not shown, per-part feedback still shown); predict vs postdict vs actual line in plain words; last-three-series thresholds labelled "historical" with the series named; "marks to next grade" per series line
Grade band slotshows "B–A (s24–w23 thresholds) · spread ±4 marks · practice estimate, not a board mark" only when §05.8 unlock is met (paper gated, ≥3 series thresholds loaded, ≥3 marked Attempts on this paper by this student). Otherwise a three-row checklist with ✓/○ per condition ("2 of 3 marked attempts on P2"). Hidden entirely in exam week for that component.
Parts tablepart · command word · tariff · Mark band · time vs tariff time (tariff × minutes_per_mark from Pack, e.g. 1.5 min/mark on P2) with over/under stated as minutes, never coloured red · AO ceiling · one-line reason from the Mark's next_mark_advice
AO profileone bar per AO: marks gained / marks available in this paper, where the denominator is computed as pack.papers[p].ao_weights[ao] × paper.marks and never hard-coded (10-DBRF-008). For 9609 P2 that is AO1 18 · AO2 18 · AO3 12 · AO4 12 of 60; a Pack with three AOs renders three bars. Label + numbers, single hue
Time chartper-part bars, actual vs tariff time, tabular labels; overtime parts get "+m:ss" text
Three prioritiesranked by marks lost × recurrence across the student's last five Marks; each = AO, marks lost, ER phrase (≤40 words, attributed, deep link) and one action; at most three
ActionsSchedule 3 retests (proposes Plan blocks at 24–72 h / 7 d / pre-exam; opens Plan in proposed state), Turn lost marks into Cards (one Card per uncredited marking point, provenance "From your mock · s24 P2 Q3(b)"), Challenge a Mark (10.22), Share receipt (10.23)

Streaming. Order: postdict gate → per-part Marks stream one at a time in paper order (each obeys 09-STRM-011) → AO profile and time chart compute client-side from committed Marks → the narrative (priorities) streams last and only after all Marks commit. A part whose Mark fails shows an InlineError in its row; the debrief still renders from the remaining parts and states "2 parts not yet marked".

States.

StateRendering
loadingpostdict card live; everything below skeletoned to final geometry
partial quotaparts beyond quota show "Practice estimate — Mark at 00:00 or on Student" in the band column; component total shows "n of m parts marked"
offlineif the sitting was submitted offline: "Marks will stream when you're back"; postdict still collectable
exam weekgrade slot, thresholds line and any ring hidden; priorities and retests kept
challenge pendingaffected part shows "Re-mark in progress"; totals recompute on outcome

Data. Read: attempt_set, attempts[], marks[], pack.thresholds{series, component, grade→mark}, pack.minutes_per_mark, ER corpus citations from each Mark. Written: attempt_set.postdict, plan_proposals[], cards[], challenge rows.

Requirements.

IDRequirementAcceptance
10-DBRF-001No mark, band or threshold is visible while the postdict card is open, and the card offers Show me the marks from 10 s onward.DOM before the postdict is answered or skipped: 0 numerals in the header region; the escape appears at 10 s and the marks render on click.
10-DBRF-002The grade band renders only when all three §05.8 conditions are true; otherwise the checklist renders with live counts.Fixtures: (gated, 3 series, 2 attempts) → checklist "2 of 3"; (gated, 3, 3) → band.
10-DBRF-003Every priority carries an attributed ER extract ≤40 words with a deep link, or no ER line at all; the priority is never invented prose.Copy audit: each ER line matches an examiner_insights row id.
10-DBRF-004Thresholds are labelled with the series used and the word "historical"; no threshold for a future series is ever shown.String test on the header.
10-DBRF-005Time vs tariff uses Pack minutes_per_mark; deviations are stated in minutes, no colour semantics.Visual regression in greyscale identical to colour.
10-DBRF-006"Schedule 3 retests" creates proposed Plan blocks, never accepted ones.Plan state after click: 3 blocks proposed.
10-DBRF-007Whole-paper streaming completes ≤45 s × parts p95 with per-part InlineError isolation.Inject one failing part in a 6-part fixture: 5 Marks render, 1 error card, totals say "5 of 6".
10-DBRF-008AO denominators are computed from pack.papers[p].ao_weights × paper.marks; a hard-coded denominator anywhere in the debrief fails the render test, and a Pack with three AOs renders three bars.Render the 9609 P2 fixture: denominators 18/18/12/12 of 60; render a 9708 fixture: three bars, no AO4. Grep the component for numeric denominators returns 0. PROVISIONAL until 15-OPEN-010 confirms the P2 structure from the syllabus PDF; the weights, not the fixture, are the source.
10-DBRF-009The postdict is requested, skippable and re-offered once — never a gate between a frightened student and their marks. The escape stores postdict_skipped with its reason (user_skipped · distress · between_papers), the card auto-skips when a distress or crisis affect tag was set in the last 24 h, and Brier simply uses fewer points.Fixture with affect_tag = distress at T−2 h: marks render immediately, no postdict card, skip_reason = distress; a normal fixture re-offers the postdict once after the marks are read.

Why: post-mock is where students burn out or quit (student-voice §8); the debrief must be evidence, thresholds and three moves, not a grade headline.

10.12Cards / Review

Purpose. Course › Cards is the retrieval engine: FSRS-6 decks fed automatically by Marks, wrong questions and reader highlights, reviewed with two buttons, tuned to the paper date.

Stage. MVP (calc_regen cards are v1 and marked so in the card-type table).

Jobs served. J12 (review what is due), J4 (make it stick), J2 (retest what I got wrong); 02-MOM-002, 02-MOM-005.

Route. /c/:courseId/cards (deck list) · /review/:deckId (full-screen review) · /c/:courseId/cards/wrong (10.13). ?new=1 opens the editor.

Layout. Deck list: sidebar tree (280) · centre deck table · right pane rail. Review: full-screen route on every breakpoint (no sidebar, no pane); mobile buttons in the bottom 20 %. Editor: right-pane Cards tab (desktop) or a 92 % sheet (mobile).

│ From wrong questions         │  6  │  0  │  31   │ 0.90             │ yesterday          │
│ From highlights · Hodder ch.3│  3  │  4  │  22   │ 0.85             │ 3 d ago            │
│ Imported · "Business defs"   │  2  │  0  │ 180   │ 0.85             │ 6 d ago            │
└──────────────────────────────┴─────┴─────┴───────┴──────────────────┴────────────────────┘
Review (full-screen):  ▬▬▬▬▬▬▬░░░ 12 of 30
  [ face: "Define *working capital*." ]  (Space to flip)
  From your Mark · 9609 P2 Q1(a) · s24        [Again  ·  <1 d]   [Got it  ·  9 d]

Scheduling rules (FSRS-6, §04.12). Desired retention by phase: 0.85 (>8 weeks to the paper), 0.90 (3–8), 0.95 (<3); intervals capped at the paper date of the card's mapped component; Cepeda prior for new material inside 8 weeks; overconfident-wrong Items (probe said "Sure", answer wrong) get interval ×0.5; a rung-5 "seen solution" card cannot count toward Secure. Exam-anchored caps per Course per day: review_cap = max(20, planned_review_minutes × 3.5) (median 17 s per card); new_cap = 20 in Phase A, 10 in Phase B, 0 in Phase C unless the student overrides in Settings ("I know — show new cards anyway"); caps are shown as plain numbers on the deck list, never as a lock.

Card types.

TypeFace / backGenerated from
basicprompt / answer (KaTeX, images ≤60 % height)highlights, editor
definitionterm / syllabus-verbatim definition + citation chipsyllabus glossary, Marks with AO1 loss
clozetext with {{c1::…}} (multiple clozes → sibling cards, buried same day)editor, Turns via "Save as card"
worked_stepprevious steps shown, one step blank / the step + whypoints Marks (uncredited M/A step), Help Ladder rung 4
marking_pointquestion stem + "what earns the next mark here?" / marking point in our wording + ER phraselevels Marks (uncredited attempt), wrong-question bank
misconceptioncontrast pair (two cases differing in one feature) / which is which and why§04.6 misconception diagnosis
calc_regen (v1)numeric item with regenerated values / SymPy-checked answerpoints Items

Every card carries provenance {kind, mark_id | attempt_id | source_id+page, created_by ∈ {system, student, teacher, import}} rendered as the 12 px provenance line.

Review interaction. Space/tap flips (200 ms; 150 ms crossfade reduced); 1 Again · 3 Got it; Hard/Easy appear only when Settings › Cards › "Four buttons" is on (2/4); interval hints under each button (hideable); e edit in place; s suspend; ⌘Z undo last grade (one step); Esc ends the session with the three-line end card ("30 reviewed · estimated retention 0.91 · next review tomorrow"). No haptic on Again (09-MOTN-006). Provenance line click opens the source Mark or page in the right pane after the session, not during.

Generation. On Mark commit: one marking_point card per uncredited attempt with a marking_point_id, one definition card per AO1 term missed; deduplicated by (item_id, marking_point_id); new cards enter as proposed in the "From your Marks" deck and a Toast offers "3 cards added · Undo". Wrong-question entries (10.13) generate misconception or worked_step cards when the diagnosis is misconception or prerequisite.

Import / export. Import .apkg (Anki 2.1 schema: notes, cards, revlog → FSRS state seeded from revlog), Quizlet/CSV (term,definition), plain text pairs; imported decks are USER provenance, private, never pooled; mapping to syllabus points is offered per deck via the Pack's embedding match with a confirm step. Export: .apkg, CSV, JSON (with FSRS state); export never strips provenance lines.

States. empty: "Cards appear here from your Marks and highlights." + Make one; loading: deck rows skeletoned; offline: full review with local FSRS-6, grades queued, sync on reconnect with per-card log replay (server wins only on identical timestamps); error (sync conflict): silent merge, toast "2 reviews merged"; quota: none — Cards are never metered (SYNTHESIS §12 free-tier rule).

Data. Read: cards, card_state{stability, difficulty, due, reps, lapses, last_review}, Course paper dates, phase. Written: reviews {card_id, rating ∈ {again, hard, good, easy}, elapsed_s, at}, cards (create/edit/suspend), card_state.

Requirements.

IDRequirementAcceptance
10-CARD-001Two-button grading by default; Hard/Easy only behind the setting.Fresh account: exactly two buttons in the review DOM.
10-CARD-002No interval ever exceeds the mapped paper date; after the paper, the deck archives silently (§03.4).Unit test: card due > paper date is clamped; post-paper deck archived=true.
10-CARD-003Desired retention follows the phase table and is displayed per deck.Move the exam date across the 8-week boundary: deck target flips 0.85→0.90.
10-CARD-004Full offline review: 50 cards reviewed in airplane mode sync with zero loss and identical FSRS state to an online run.Deterministic replay test.
10-CARD-005Every generated card has a resolvable provenance target; a card without provenance fails creation.0 rows with provenance = null.
10-CARD-006Anki import seeds FSRS from revlog; 1,000-note deck imports ≤20 s with a progress line.Fixture deck; timing in CI.
10-CARD-007Overconfident-wrong halving is applied and visible in the interval hint.Probe "Sure" + wrong → next hint half of the baseline fixture.
10-CARD-008Median grading time ≤3 s per card; no card face exceeds 60 words without a "long" tag surfaced in the editor.Telemetry; editor lint.

Why: students say card-making is procrastination bait and pre-made decks are boring but Anki "is the best thing in the world" (student-voice §4); the fix is cards that arrive from their own lost marks, scheduled to the exam, and never paywalled.

10.13Wrong-question bank

Purpose. The Wrong-question bank is the automatic ledger of every lost mark — the thing students build by hand with screenshots — re-attemptable with its marking point, tagged by misconception, scheduled by FSRS, linked to mastery.

Stage. MVP.

Jobs served. J2 (why did I lose the mark), J12 (retest what I got wrong), J10 (stop losing the same AO), J8 (which solutions have I only seen); 02-MOM-002, 02-MOM-006.

Route. /c/:courseId/cards/wrong, surfaced as Course › Progress › Wrong questions, ⌘K → Open wrong questions, and the "Wrong" chip on Course home; ?point=3.2 and ?status=open are filter params so a link carries a view.

Layout. Desktop: sidebar tree acts as the syllabus-point filter; centre list at max 960 px; right pane opens the original Mark (10.7) on row focus, with the lost span pre-scrolled. Mobile: list route; row → Mark route; filters as a sheet.

│ Point  │ Question              │ Tariff│ Lost       │ Tag                 │ Retest  │ Status │

│ 5.1    │ OWN P2-like Q2(a)     │ 8     │ AO2 −3     │ misconception: name-as-application  │ Thu   │ seen solution │

Entry creation (automatic). On every Mark commit, one entry per lost unit: for levels papers, per AO where marks < max (grouped, with uncredited_attempts[] and the descriptor gap); for points papers, per marking point not credited (M1, A1…). Fields:

{ "id": "wq_…", "attempt_id": "…", "mark_id": "…", "item_id": "…",
  "syllabus_points": ["3.2"], "paper_ref": "9609/22 s24 Q3(b)", "tariff": 12,
  "lost": {"ao": "AO4", "marks": 4, "marking_point_id": null, "descriptor_gap": "L1→L2: judgement weighed against context"},
  "diagnosis": {"class": "slip|misconception|prerequisite|unclassified", "label": "judgement-as-summary", "prereq_point": null},
  "seen_solution": false, "retest_due": "2026-09-08", "retests": [{"at": "...", "unaided": true, "correct": false}],
  "status": "open|retested_wrong|retested_correct|mastered|dismissed", "card_ids": [] }

diagnosis comes from the §04.6 classification when the student gave a reasoning trace; otherwise unclassified with a Diagnose action (opens a two-Turn Learn exchange that asks for the trace, then classifies). seen_solution=true when rung 5 or "Just the answer" was used on the Item; such entries retest on a near-transfer variant (same tariff and cognitive-demand tag, §05.10 generator), never the same Item.

Filters and sort. Syllabus point (tree), paper/series, tariff band, AO, diagnosis class and label, status, seen-solution only, date range, Course (cross-Course view on Home shows counts only). Default sort: retest due asc, then marks lost desc. Persisted per Course.

Actions. Row: Retest (opens the Practise runner 10.6 with the Item or its variant, Effort Gate on, entry rung from mastery), Show Mark, Show in book (citation of the descriptor/marking point), Make card (10.12 marking_point/worked_step), Dismiss (reason chips: "Teacher overrode", "Off-syllabus", "Duplicate"; kept in history). Header: Retest 5 due (an interleaved set, no more than 5 same-type in a row, §04.13) and Diagnose 3 unclassified.

Status machine and mastery link. open → retest unaided correct → retested_correct (1 of 2) → second unaided correct on a different day → mastered (feeds M_s via the correctness posterior; a seen-solution first attempt contributes 0, §07.2). Retest wrong → retested_wrong, FSRS shortens the next due, diagnosis re-asked once. Entries never delete; mastered and dismissed move to the History tab. A point's pip tooltip cites the bank: "¼ — 3 open wrong questions on 3.2".

States. empty (new Course): "Lost marks collect here after your first Mark." + Mark an answer; empty (all mastered): "Nothing open. 14 mastered this month." (no celebration animation); loading: rows skeletoned; offline: list from cache, Retest disabled for gradable Items with tooltip, Make card works; error: inline row card; quota: retests of points Items are unmetered; retests of levels Items follow the levels-Mark meter with the plain-number line before start.

Data. Read: wrong_questions, marks, items, card_state, mastery. Written: wrong_questions (status, diagnosis, retests[]), attempts (via runner), cards.

Requirements.

IDRequirementAcceptance
10-WRNG-001Every lost mark in a committed Mark produces exactly one entry within 2 s; no manual step.Mark fixture with 3 lost units → 3 rows; idempotent on re-mark (updated, not duplicated).
10-WRNG-002Seen-solution entries retest on a variant, never the original Item text.Retest of a seen_solution=true row: item_id ≠ original, variant_of = original.
10-WRNG-003mastered requires two unaided correct retests on ≥2 distinct days.State-machine unit test; same-day double correct stays retested_correct.
10-WRNG-004Diagnosis labels come from the Pack's misconception list (≥3 per point) or unclassified; no free-text labels from the model.Every label ∈ pack.misconceptions[point].
10-WRNG-005Retest sets interleave: ≤5 consecutive same-type Items.Set builder unit test.
10-WRNG-006Filters return in ≤200 ms p95 for a bank of 2,000 entries (client-side index).Perf test.
10-WRNG-007No shame copy: the header shows counts and due dates only; the lint lexicon (09-COPY-003 d) applies.Copy catalogue test.

Why: "screenshot the questions that u get wrong with their model answer then redo them a few days later" is the ritual students already run by hand (student-voice §4); automating it, with the marking point attached, is the product's clearest delta over a chat.

10.14Progress / Calibration

Purpose. Course › Progress is the evidence view of the Learner Graph: mastery by syllabus point, readiness per paper, calibration, activity. It is the only surface (with the mock debrief) where a predicted grade band may appear, and only on the Paper tab under §05.8 rules.

Stage. MVP.

Jobs served. J8 (where do I stand and how ready is Paper 2), J12 (what changed this week), J10 (am I over-confident); 02-MOM-002, 02-MOM-004.

Route. /c/:courseId/progress with tabs ?tab=overview|paper|calibration|activity, /c/:courseId/progress/paper/:paperId, and /c/:courseId/cards/wrong for the fifth tab (10.13).

Layout. Tabs (40 px strip): Overview · Paper · Calibration · Activity · Wrong questions (10.13). Desktop: sidebar tree (clicking a point filters every tab) · centre at max 960 px · right pane opens the point's evidence (Attempts list, last Mark) on pip focus. Mobile: tabs as a segmented control under the 44 pt bar; heatmaps scroll horizontally inside their own container.

Regions and elements.

TabElements and rules
OverviewMastery heatmap = the syllabus tree laid out as rows of MasteryPips (shape-coded per 09-COLR-002, official numbering, unit totals as counts "Secure 3 · Shaky 2"); no percentage anywhere. "This week" list of state changes with the reason string from the graph. Three trend lines as numbers with n: unaided delta (marks per tariff on unseen Items of gated papers, the UMG numerator), median ladder rung, mastery velocity.
Paperone card per component: ReadinessRing (arc = Σ tariff_exposure_s × M_s / Σ tariff_exposure_s, reason text = the largest decaying contributors), last three mock bands, AO profile from marks gained/available, Predicted grade band slot (rules below), Start timed mock, Debrief links.
CalibrationBrier score overall and per unit, weekly, as a line chart with n per point; reliability diagram with the three confidence buckets: "Sure: 40 said · 26 right (0.65)", "Think so: 31 · 19 (0.61)", "Guessing: 12 · 5 (0.42)" and the ideal line; predict–postdict view per mock: three bands on one axis (predicted · postdict · actual) with the gap in marks and one sentence generated from the gap sign ("You under-predict on P2: actual above predicted in 4 of 5 sittings").
Activity12 px heatmap, five tones (09-COLR-003), tooltip minutes + topics; weekly sessions vs goal with rest days neutral; no streak count, no "longest run".

Predicted grade band rules (§05.8, SYNTHESIS §8.7). Render only when all hold: (1) the paper's calibration status is gated; (2) ≥3 series of thresholds for that component are loaded in the Pack; (3) this student has ≥3 marked Attempts on that paper at full tariff. Content: option or component grade range from component raw → last-three-series thresholds → PUM; the series used; spread in marks; "marks to next grade" per series line; the fixed label "practice estimate, not a board mark". A* only at option level. When locked, render the three-condition checklist with live counts, never a greyed grade. Never render: on Home, in a notification, in the parent digest unless student-enabled (10.21), in a share card, or in exam week for that component.

States. empty (no Attempts): the tree with all pips Unseen and one line "Probes on this week's topics seed this map." + Start probe; loading: pips render immediately from cache, trends skeleton; offline: last synced state with a 13 px "as of 09:12" line; exam week: Paper tab hides ring, deltas and grade band for the component in its T−7 window, keeps AO profile and mock bands; error: per-tab inline card.

Data. Read: mastery{point, M, state, retrievability, reason, changed_at}, attempts, marks, attempt_sets (predict/postdict), pack.thresholds, pack.tariff_exposure, calibration status per paper. Written: none (view only); the sidebar filter persists.

Requirements.

IDRequirementAcceptance
10-PROG-001A predicted grade band string appears in the DOM only on Progress › Paper and the debrief, only with the three conditions true.Route crawl with a fixture meeting the conditions: string present on exactly those two routes; with any condition false: 0 occurrences app-wide.
10-PROG-002Every rendered band carries series, spread and the "practice estimate, not a board mark" label.Regex on the band component.
10-PROG-003No % character and no numeric mastery appears in Overview; states are the four shapes with reasons.Copy corpus test + DOM scan.
10-PROG-004Ring arc equals the tariff-weighted mastery formula to ±0.01; reason names the largest decaying contributors.Unit test on a 10-point fixture.
10-PROG-005Reliability diagram shows counts, not only rates; buckets with n<5 render "too few to say".Fixture with Guessing n=3.
10-PROG-006Exam-week hiding is per component and time-boxed to T−7 → paper sat.Clock test at T−8, T−7, T+1.
10-PROG-007Pip hover/focus reason resolves in ≤100 ms from local state.Perf test.

Why: a predicted grade on Home is an anxiety device in an exam year already full of them (vision-craft §8 dissent on A24; student-voice §8); calibration — "you said Sure 40 times, 26 were right" — is the number that changes behaviour (§04.14).

10.15Plan

Purpose. Course › Plan (and the cross-Course Plan on Home) is the calendar from today to each exam: weekly blocks proposed by the scheduler from the phase mix (§04.13), Mark-Yield priorities (§07.5) and decay, edited by the student, never silently applied.

Stage. MVP.

Jobs served. J3 (what is the highest-value thing this week), J12 (fit the retests in), J9 (fit my teacher's assignment); 02-MOM-001, 02-MOM-002, 02-MOM-005.

Route. /c/:courseId/plan, ?week=YYYY-Www for a specific week and ?day=YYYY-MM-DD from the Home week strip; the cross-Course plan is /home/plan.

Layout. Desktop: sidebar shows the exam spine (all papers of all Courses, dated) · centre week view (7 columns × hours, 44 pt day headers) at max 1040 px · right pane opens "Why this block" on block focus. Tablet: week view + 420 px card. Mobile: day strip (7 × 44 pt) + a single day's block list; week switch by swipe with a button alternative.
