Regions and elements.

RegionElements and rules
Headerweek label · phase chip ("Phase B · 5 weeks to P2") · weekly goal with rest days ("4 sessions · rest Tue, Fri") — hidden in exam weeks · Accept week · ICS · Why this plan
Exam spineevery component as a chip with tabular countdown; between-papers windows (T−7 per component) shaded; clicking a chip filters blocks to that paper
Block25 or 45 min; label = type (Review · Practise · Paper · Debrief · Retest · Assignment · Readiness review) + syllabus point or paper ref + one 12 px reason line; states per 09.7 PlanBlock: proposed (dashed) · accepted · done · declined-late · missed (neutral, rolls forward) · locked (assignment)
Why this blockthe yield line in words and numbers: "3.2 Motivation: 8 marks of exposure on P2 · mastery ¼ · retrievability 0.55 by 11 Jun · est. 1.5 h → yield 2.7 marks/h, rank 1 of 14"; the pip it came from; Swap for rank 2
Sleep line and quiet hoursbedtime from Settings (default 22:30) greys the hours below; Quiet Hours block notifications, not study; in exam weeks no block ends after 22:00 and the planner declines with one sentence ("Late blocks cost more than they give in exam week — moved to 16:00 tomorrow.")
Teacher assignmentsappear as locked blocks with the lock window ("opens Wed 08:00 · locks Fri 18:00") and allowed-help level; the student can move them inside the window, not outside

Scheduling rules. Session mix by phase enforced when the week is generated (Phase A ≥60 % due retrieval / ≥25 % interleaved / ≤15 % new; B ≥50/≥35 incl. one timed section/≤15; C ≥50 % timed + debrief retrieval, ≤40 % exam-critical due, 0 % new) — the header shows the achieved mix as three numbers on hover of the phase chip. The "new" and "interleaved" slots are filled by Mark-Yield rank; cohort medians until ≥30 Attempts, then the student's own numbers (the reason line says which). Debrief-scheduled retests (10.11) and seen-solution retests (24–72 h) are pinned first. Timetable import (ICS/photo, onboarding) marks busy hours; blocks never overlap them. Weekly session length: 12–25 min weekdays, 25–45 weekends; one Readiness review block on the chosen day (default Sunday).

Rescheduling. Drag with ⋯ › Move as the tap alternative; moving a block keeps its content; a moved timed section must land ≥45 min before the sleep line; Decline asks nothing but records declined_reason optionally; a missed block rolls forward once, then dissolves into the next generation (no "you missed" copy). Regeneration ("Re-plan from today") keeps accepted blocks and re-proposes the rest. Accept week accepts all proposed blocks; individual accept on block focus (a).

States. empty (no exam date): "Add the exam date to get a plan." + Set date — the week still shows due cards; loading: week grid skeleton; offline: read-only view with "as of" line, edits queued; error: inline card at the top of the week; exam week: goal hidden, only the next paper's blocks, 25-min defaults; quota: none.

Data. Read: courses.papers[].date, phase, mastery, card_state due counts, yield_rank[], assignments, busy_hours, Settings {bedtime, quiet_hours, review_day}. Written: plan_blocks {id, type, ref, start, minutes, state, reason, source ∈ {scheduler, debrief, assignment, student}}, plan_events {moved, declined, missed}; ICS export contains accepted blocks only, no learner state.

Requirements.

IDRequirementAcceptance
10-PLAN-001Scheduler output enters as proposed; nothing becomes accepted without a student action.DB assertion after generation: 0 accepted rows without a plan_events.accept.
10-PLAN-002Generated weeks satisfy the phase mix within ±5 pp of each floor/ceiling.Property test over 200 synthetic learners × 3 phases.
10-PLAN-003No block ends after the sleep line; in exam weeks none after 22:00; the decline copy is the single canonical sentence.Clock fixtures; copy test.
10-PLAN-004Every proposed block has a "Why" that names its source (yield rank, decay, debrief, assignment) with numbers.0 blocks with empty reason.
10-PLAN-005Assignment blocks cannot be moved outside their lock window.Drag past window → snap back + inline line.
10-PLAN-006Missed blocks produce no notification and no loss-framed string.Notification scheduler test; lint.
10-PLAN-007Drag has a keyboard/tap equivalent for every operation (move, resize between 25/45, decline).Keyboard traversal script.
10-PLAN-008ICS export validates (RFC 5545) and contains no mastery, band or grade strings.Validator + grep.

Why: month-before sleep explains roughly a quarter of grade variance (SYNTHESIS §3.2, A60); a plan that schedules 23:30 blocks is a worse tutor, not a keener one.

10.16Library / Reader / Source pane

Purpose. Library is the Course's sources by trust rank; the Reader is the page-accurate viewer; the Source pane is the same viewer docked in the right pane, opened by citation chips. Together they make "the source is one gesture away" (09-PRIN-002) true: every syllabus, scheme, ER or textbook claim resolves to a page and span.

Stage. MVP.

Jobs served. J4 (show me in the book), J2 (find the source behind the lost mark), J5 (read what school is on), J9 (upload my teacher's notes); 02-MOM-001, 02-MOM-002.

Route. /library (Course-scoped by the switcher) · /read/:docId?page=n&span=id · the Source pane is the ⟨Source⟩ tab of 10-CONV-002 and has no route of its own.

Layout. Library: sidebar Course tree · centre source table · right pane rail. Reader: full route — centre page at 66 ch text (Focus 60 ch/20 px), --bg-subtle surround, PDF pages paper-coloured in dark mode (09.13). Source pane: 480 px (360–640) right pane, tab strip Source · Scratchpad · Artifact · Cards, page header with page number and [ ] citation arrows. Tablet: pane as a bottom sheet in portrait (50/92 %). Mobile: Reader as a full route pushed from the chip.

Regions and elements.

RegionElements and rules
Source tablegrouped by trust badge (09-ICON-003 order); columns: title, provenance chip OWN · LICENSED · USER (visible here and in teacher views only), pages, ingestion confidence (per-source mean with "n pages to check" link to the per-page list), last used. Rows for deep-link-only sources (board PDFs) show ↗ and "opens the official page".
UploadLibrary ingestion accepts PDF only (§06): a PDF is the only form the two-pass parser can page-address, and page addresses are what citation chips resolve to. The composer accepts every type in 03-PAR-013; a non-PDF document attached there is either converted to PDF before ingestion or attached to the Turn without entering retrieval, and the composer says which. Per-file and per-message ceilings are rendered from limits.yaml (03-LIM-001), never restated here. Photos route through 10.8 into a PDF; Anki/Quizlet files route to Cards import (10.12). Uploads are USER: private to the user (or tenant when a teacher uploads to a class), never pooled, deletable. Status chips: queued · parsing · audited (n % conf) · ready · failed (reason).
Files managementthe Course's file count against its ceiling as a plain number ("38 of 200 files"), per-row Delete with a 30 s Undo and a line naming what goes with it ("3 citations in past Turns will show 'source removed'"), and at the ceiling an inline line "This Course holds 200 files. Delete one to add another." — never a modal, never a silent failed upload.
Paste a mark schemetextarea → structured mark_scheme_items preview (§05.3 schema: marking points, levels, accept/reject) with confidence per row → Use for my Marks (USER scope). Verbatim official wording stays USER-scoped and is never displayed to other users.
Reader headertitle · page · trust badge · citation arrows (prev/next citation in this Session) · reading-comfort quick control · ⌘F find · Focus · ↗ Open original (deep link where the source is an official PDF)
PagePDF at device DPR with selectable text layer, or structured text for parsed sources; cited span in --highlight-source; selection popover (Ask · Explain · Define · Save as card · Quote); per-page confidence <0.9 shows the "Verify against the PDF" badge
Conflict cardwhen a USER note contradicts canon on the same syllabus point: both citations, canon shown by default, Keep mine records the choice on the memory object with a reason; conflicts listed in the Library row

Citation resolution. A chip carries {source_id, page, span:{start,end}, sha256, confidence, fallback}. Resolution: local cache (last 20 pages) → page image + text layer → scroll and highlight ≤400 ms p95 (09-PRIN-002). When display rights are absent (fallback = extract), the pane shows the ≤40-word attributed extract, the page number and Open the official page ↗; extract count per Session is capped and audit-logged (§06). Show me in the book (MessageAction, palette verb) takes the current Turn's top citation, or — with none — runs retrieval on the Turn's syllabus point restricted to trust ranks 1–2 and opens the best page with the badge "Best match, not a citation".

States. Library empty: "The syllabus and our marking points are here. Add your notes or a textbook PDF." + Upload; loading: rows and page skeletons at final geometry; low-confidence page: badge; licence-unavailable: extract card; offline: downloaded units readable (per-unit download toggle on the source row, size shown), others show "Download when online"; error (parse failed): row chip with reason and Retry / Delete; quota: free tier ≥20 uploads/day with the plain-number meter line at 15.

Data. Read: sources {trust_rank, provenance, licence_basis, source_url, sha256, pages[], page_confidence[]}, citations, memory conflicts. Written: sources (USER uploads), ingest_jobs, highlights, cards (from popover), memory.conflict_choices, per-unit offline downloads (device-local).

Requirements.

IDRequirementAcceptance
10-LIBR-001Chip → highlighted page ≤400 ms p95 from cache, ≤1.5 s p95 cold.Perf trace on 50 chips.
10-LIBR-002Every citation resolves to page+span or to an attributed extract with a deep link; a chip that resolves to neither is a defect.Fixture crawl: 0 dead chips.
10-LIBR-003USER uploads never appear in another user's or tenant's retrieval or Library.RLS + retrieval isolation test across two tenants.
10-LIBR-004Canon wins conflicts by default; Keep mine is explicit, reasoned and reversible.Conflict fixture: default render shows canon; choice stored with reason.
10-LIBR-005Board PDFs are deep-linked, never rendered from Margin storage.Storage audit: 0 objects with a board source_url host.

Why: hosting or displaying scheme wording without a licence is the takedown risk (§06, SYNTHESIS §9); extract + deep link keeps the trust gesture without the exposure. [founder default] No licensed textbook is assumed at launch; the Endorsed-textbook row appears only when a LICENSED source exists.

10.17Scratchpad / Artifact

Purpose. Give the student a versioned place to write the thing being marked — an essay through plan → draft → Mark → rewrite, or working-out through steps → check — inside the Session, where the tutor can annotate and mark but can never alter the student's text.

Stage. MVP for the Scratchpad (it is where the rewrite happens, and the rewrite is bet 2). Artifact export to .docx and the standalone /c/:courseId/artifact/:artifactId route are MVP; collaborative or versioned Artifacts are not in scope at either stage.

Jobs served. J1, J10 (turn a Level 2 into a Level 3), J6 (draft coursework feedback without a ghost-writer), J4 (work the maths out somewhere that checks it); 02-MOM-003, 02-MOM-006.

Route. Right-pane tabs ⟨Scratchpad⟩ and ⟨Artifact⟩ inside a Session (10-CONV-002), plus the full route /c/:courseId/artifact/:artifactId for writing at full width and for sharing into a Receipt (10.23). A Mark's primary action "Rewrite the weakest paragraph" opens the Artifact tab with that paragraph loaded and the rest of the answer present but collapsed.

Distinction. Scratchpad is ephemeral thinking: one document per Session, plain text plus maths, never marked, never cited, kept for 30 days. Artifact is a named, versioned document that can be marked: essay, working, plan, notes. Artifacts belong to the Course and appear in Course facts and the Receipt.

Layout. Desktop: as a right-pane tab at 480 px (min 360, max 640) with the Session visible beside it; the full route gives a 68 ch centre with the Session collapsed to a 48 px rail on the left and the version list as a 240 px right column. Tablet: full route only. Mobile: a 92 % sheet with a segmented header (Write · Versions · Marks) and the toolbar docked above the keyboard.

Regions and elements.

RegionElements
Headertitle (auto from the Item: "9609 P4 Q1 · Evaluate · 20 marks", editable) · type chip · word count, unlabelled and with no target ("214 words") — the marker is instructed that length is not evidence, so no surface in the product prints a words-per-mark goal (10.6 answer area, same rule) · autosave dot ("Saved 12:04") · ⋯ (Duplicate · Export .docx/.md/PDF · Delete)
Toolbarone row, 32 px: Plan · Draft · headings, bold, italic, list, quote · ∑ math (MathLive inline, ⌘⇧M) · Insert citation (from the Session's chips) · Mark this (the only filled button)
Plan modea structured outline for levels items — Define · Chain 1 · Chain 2 · Counter · Judgement — each row a one-line field with a tariff hint ("two developed chains = AO3 L3"); Plan converts to Draft with the outline as headings the student can delete
Draft modethe editor: 17/1.55, measure from reading comfort, line numbers matching the Mark's line_ref, paragraph anchors so a Mark's span survives editing elsewhere
Working padfor numeric Courses: line-per-step entry with a = ? checker per line (SymPy, §11.5) that marks a line ✓ or flags "this line does not follow from the one above" — a check, never a correction
Margin commentstutor annotations anchored to a paragraph, collapsed to a 12 px dot; opening shows the note, its rung and, after a Mark, the AO it belongs to; a comment can never edit the paragraph
Versionsa list of v1 … vn with timestamp, word delta, and any Mark attached ("v3 · 14 Feb · +180 words · 11–13/20"); Compare shows a two-column diff; Restore creates a new version, never overwrites
Mark stripafter "Mark this": the compact Mark (10.7) docked beneath the editor with spans mapped onto the live text; a re-mark shows the delta chip "+3 · AO4 L1→L2" (09-COPY-002 #14)

States. empty: "Write here. Plan first if it is an essay — the plan becomes your headings." with Plan and Draft; the working pad's empty state is one blank step line. loading: editor is interactive before versions load. streaming: only the Mark strip and margin comments stream; the editor's text is never touched while a stream runs, and the caret never moves. error: "Not saved since 12:01 — retry" inline with local content preserved in IndexedDB; a failed Mark leaves the version intact. offline: full editing, local versions, "Mark this" queues with the queued tag. gated/quota: "Mark this" respects the levels-Mark quota with the standard line and offers points-style checks (working pad) and a self-check rubric meanwhile. coursework: when the Course or the title matches an NEA/IA/EE pattern, a persistent Banner (--banner-h) reads "Coursework mode: I mark your draft against the criteria and log what we did. I won't write it." (09-COPY-002 #18) and every Mark writes a Receipt entry.

Interactions and shortcuts. ⌘S names a version explicitly (autosave every 5 s and on blur creates unnamed versions, coalesced to one per 10 minutes); ⌘. runs the Mark's primary action on the current paragraph; ⌘⇧M maths; ⌘⇧D compare with previous version; ⌘⇧E export. Selecting a paragraph and pressing ⌘⇧A asks the tutor about it in the Session without leaving the editor. The tutor's suggestions arrive as margin comments and Insert buttons that the student must press; a paragraph the student did not type carries a pasted_from_tutor flag on the Attempt and appears in the Receipt.

Data. Reads: the Item, the Mark's spans and line_ref map, the Session's citations, reading-comfort object, Course type patterns (coursework), quota state. Writes: artifacts {course_id, type, title, current_version}, artifact_versions {n, body, word_count, created_at, named?, hash}, attempts (a "Mark this" creates or updates the Attempt bound to the artifact version), annotations {paragraph_id, rung, ao?, text}, pasted_from_tutor events, Receipt entries (§12.2), scratchpads {session_id, body, expires_at}.

IDRequirementAcceptance
10-SCRA-001No model output ever mutates the student's text. Every suggestion is a margin comment with an explicit Insert control; there is no code path from a model response to an editor mutation.Static check: the editor's mutation API is unreachable from the streaming handler; adversarial prompt ("rewrite my essay in place") produces a comment, not an edit.
10-SCRA-002Every "Mark this" is bound to a specific artifact_version; the version is immutable once marked.Edit after marking creates v+1; the marked version's hash is unchanged.
10-SCRA-003Restore never destroys: restoring vN creates vN+1 with the same body.Version count increases; no row deleted.
10-SCRA-004Spans from a Mark re-anchor to paragraphs, not character offsets, so edits elsewhere do not corrupt the highlight; an unresolvable span is hidden with "This paragraph changed since the Mark".Edit fixture: 20 spans, 0 mis-anchored.
10-SCRA-005The working pad's line checker verifies, never corrects: it may mark a step ✓ or flag a non-sequitur, and may not print the next step while gate_state = open.SymPy fixture set; adversarial run asserts no solution tokens.
10-SCRA-006Rung 4 on a levels Item inserts at most one model paragraph with a blanked sentence, never a model essay (04-LADR-004).Lint: no inserted block >220 words of continuous answer prose.

10-SCRA-008Autosave loses ≤5 s of typing on hard crash; offline editing survives a reload with no version loss.Kill the tab mid-sentence; reload restores to the last tick.

10.18Search / Command palette

Purpose. One input that reaches every verb, every syllabus point, every Session, Card, paper, source and setting across all of a student's Courses, in under 150 ms, with no animation and no mouse.

Stage. MVP. The palette is how every verb in 09-KEYS-003 is reachable without a mouse; a deferred palette would strand them.

Jobs served. J5 (get to the point school is on), J2 (find the thing I got wrong), J12; and the expert path for every other screen — the palette is the keyboard interface to §10 as a whole.

Route. A layer, not a route: ⌘K from anywhere (including inside a Session while streaming, which does not stop the stream), / in a non-text context, and the search field in the sidebar header on mobile. ? opens help search. > forces verb mode. The Paper runner restricts the verb set to five (10-RUNR-001).

Layout. Desktop: a 640 px panel pinned 96 px from the top on a 40 % scrim; input 36 px, rows 32 px, radius 6, hairline border, --shadow-3, no entrance animation (09-MOTN-003). Tablet: 560 px. Mobile: a full-height sheet with the input under the 44 pt top bar and the keyboard open on mount; rows 44 px.

Regions and elements.

RegionElements
Inputplaceholder "Type a verb, a topic, or a question number"; a scope chip on the left when the palette was opened from a Course ("9609 ▾", ⌫ on an empty input clears it to All Courses)
Result groupsin fixed order: Verbs · Syllabus points · Sessions & Marks · Cards · Papers & Items · Sources · Settings & Help. Each group shows ≤4 rows with a "Show all (17)" row; group headers are 12 px caps
Rowicon (16) · primary label · argument slot in --text-muted · a 12 px context line ("3.2 Motivation · ◔ Shaky · due Thu · 9609") · keycap on the right for the first 9 rows (⌘1…⌘9 is not used; the keycap shows ↵ on the focused row only)
Verb argument stepchoosing a verb with a required argument keeps the panel open and swaps the list to argument candidates ("Practise →" then a point list), with ⌫ returning to the verb
Recentswith an empty input: Recent (last 5 verbs with their arguments) then Jump back in (last 3 Sessions with their syllabus point) then Due today as a single row
Previewon the focused row, a right-hand 240 px preview at ≥1280 only: for a syllabus point the pip with its reason; for a Mark the band and AO levels; for a Card the face; for a source the page thumbnail

                │ (9609 ▾) practise 3.2                                    │
                │──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────│
                │ VERBS                                                    │
                │ ▸ Practise  3.2 Motivation            8-mark Analyse   ↵ │
                │ ▸ Learn     3.2 Motivation            ◔ Shaky            │
                │ ▸ Quiz me on 3.2.1                    3 items            │
                │ SYLLABUS POINTS                                          │

                │ PAPERS & ITEMS                                           │
                │ ▸ Open paper 9609 22 s24                Show all (17)    │
                └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

Verbs. The canonical list is 09-KEYS-003; the palette is its only complete surface. Each verb declares {verb, arg_type ∈ {syllabus_point, paper_ref, source_ref, course, screen, free_text, none}, route, payload, scope ∈ {course, global}, guard}. guard hides a verb where it cannot act (no "Challenge this Mark" without a Mark in context; no "Teacher: open class" without a teacher role; no "Start timed section" inside a running paper). Adding a screen to §10 without registering its Go to <screen> row is a spec defect.

Ranking. Score = 0.45 × prefix/fuzzy match on label and aliases + 0.25 × recency of the same verb+argument + 0.20 × context (current Course, current syllabus point, open Item) + 0.10 × scheduler priority (yield_s, due count). Exact syllabus numbering (3.2.1, 9609/22, Q3b) short-circuits to that row at rank 1. Aliases are indexed: "evaluate" → the command-word help row; "essay" → Practise levels Items; "mark scheme" → the paste tool; "dark" → Toggle dark mode.

States. empty (no query): Recents, Jump back in, Due today; never a blank panel. loading: local index answers immediately; remote groups (Sources, Papers) append with a 12 px "searching sources…" line and never reorder rows already shown. error: the remote group shows "Sources unavailable — local results shown"; the palette never fails closed. offline: verbs that need the network are shown with a muted "needs a connection" note and are not selectable; Cards, syllabus points, downloaded sources and Settings all work. gated: a verb whose action is quota-limited still runs and the destination screen carries the banner — the palette never explains a quota.

Interactions and shortcuts. ↑ ↓ move, ↵ run, ⌘↵ run in a new tab where the target is a route, ⇥ completes the highlighted verb into the input, ⌫ steps back through the argument stack then clears the scope, Esc closes and returns focus to the element that opened it (09-KEYS-002). Type-ahead is never destructive: the palette never runs a verb without an explicit ↵. ⌘/ opens the shortcut sheet, which is the same layer with a different list. Search results are keyboard-only reachable; no result requires hover.

Data. Reads: a client-side index (verbs, the Course's syllabus tree, Session titles, Card faces, Settings rows — rebuilt on Course switch and Pack version change, ≤400 KB per Course) and a server index for full-text over Turns, Marks, sources and the item bank, scoped by tenant and by the user's Courses. Writes: palette_used {verb, arg_type, rank_selected, latency_ms} and the recents list (per user, synced, last 20). No search query is retained beyond 30 days, and queries are excluded from model-training exports (§11.13).

10.19Settings / Memory / Usage

Purpose. Put every control that changes how Margin reads, remembers, interrupts, charges and stores — in one scrolling page where each control states its consequence in one line and nothing about the account is hidden from its owner.

Stage. MVP for account · appearance · reading · language · memory · usage · data; notifications ships MVP with in-app and email channels only and gains push at v1 with the Expo builds; shortcuts is MVP (it renders 09-KEYS-001, it does not re-specify it).

Jobs served. J9 (make it readable for me), J12 (stop it pinging me at night), plus the trust obligations of §12: see what it remembers, see what it costs, take the data out, delete it.

Route. /settings/:section with the nine sections of 10-CONV-003 — account · appearance · reading · language · memory · notifications · usage · shortcuts · data. Plan and billing live at the foot of usage so that price and limits are read together; there is no separate billing route. ⌘, opens the last section used; ⌘K → Reading comfort deep-links to the control, focuses it and outlines it once for 400 ms.

Layout. Desktop: one continuous scroll at 68 ch with a sticky 240 px left nav listing the nine sections (current section marked by weight and a 2 px --accent left rule, updated by an IntersectionObserver, never by animation); no tabs, no accordions, no modal dialogs anywhere in Settings. Tablet: the nav becomes a sticky horizontal strip. Mobile: the same single scroll with a sticky section chip row; destructive flows (delete account, delete a Course) are full-screen routes, not sheets.

Regions and elements.

SectionControls (each with a one-line consequence beneath it)

First section in the scroll, because an account the owner cannot leave is not their account.
AppearanceTheme (System · Light · Dark) · Contrast+ toggle · Reduce motion (System · On) · Reduce transparency. There is no density control: the product has one row height and one measure by design, and a second density doubles the visual-regression matrix for no named student job.

LanguageUI language (English · Русский · Қазақша) · Explanation language (independent of UI — the tutor may explain in Russian while the exam terms stay English) · Decimal comma · Date format · "Keep exam vocabulary in English" toggle, on by default

Grace state shows the plan-conditional exam-week line (09-COPY-002 #10) and names the number, never "off". A What each limit means table rendered verbatim from limits.yaml (03-LIM-001). Then Plan: current plan, price, renewal date, "Until exams · expires 5 July 2027", change/cancel (cancel is two taps and never routed through a retention interstitial), invoices, regional-price note.

States. empty: Memory with no rows reads "Margin hasn't stored anything about your learning yet. It will, and you'll see it here." loading: controls render from local preferences immediately; usage counters show their last value with a 12 px "updating" line. error: a failed save reverts the control and shows an inline line "Not saved — retry"; never a toast for a setting. offline: appearance, reading, language, shortcuts and notification preferences all apply locally and sync later; memory edits, exports and plan changes queue and say so. gated: teen accounts show notification and memory rows their guardian controls with "Set by your parent or guardian" and a link to ask for a change; school tenants show tenant-locked rows the same way. deleting: the account-delete route shows what will go, what is kept and for how long, requires typing the word delete, and offers Export first as the adjacent action.

Interactions and shortcuts. Every change applies immediately — there is no Save button anywhere in Settings, and no change is destructive without Undo except the two delete routes. Reading changes apply without reload and without layout shift outside the text (09-READ-004). ⌘, opens Settings; ⌘F searches the page (native find works because Settings is one document); ⌘K → Memory: forget <fact> reaches a row directly. Rebinding a shortcut listens for one chord, shows conflicts inline, and refuses only chords the browser owns.

Data. Reads: prefs (reading comfort, language, decimal comma, intent defaults), memories[] with provenance, notification config, Quiet Hours, limits.yaml and server counters, subscription state, tenant and guardian policy object. Writes: prefs.*, memories (edit/forget/pin with tombstones), memory_paused, sensitive_exclusions, notification_prefs, quiet_hours, shortcut_overrides, export_jobs, deletion_requests, subscription_changes. Every write to memory or deletion is audit-logged with actor and timestamp (§11.13).

10.20Teacher console (calibrator scope)

Purpose. Give the teacher the two powers that make Margin trustworthy and that only a teacher has — setting the conditions of an assignment, and overruling a Mark — while feeding every override back into calibration. At MVP the console is calibrator scope: class, assignments, Mark audit, override, calibration queue, disagreement trends. Everything else is labelled v1.

Stage. MVP at calibrator scope only (SYNTHESIS §6 row 20): classes by code, locked assignments with an allowed-help level, aggregate attempts and hint depth, Mark audit with override, mock import, calibration tasks. Heatmap, SSO/roster sync and evidence export are v1 and are marked in the regions table below.

Jobs served. J9 (teacher: is this thing marking my class the way I would), plus the human-oversight posture of SYNTHESIS §8.11: nothing reaches a school-recorded grade without teacher confirmation. Teacher mode is free forever (SYNTHESIS §12).

Route. /t/:classId with tabs roster · assignments · marks · calibration · settings. /t lists classes. Students join at /join/:code (10.2). A teacher's own student Courses live at /c/... as normal; the console never mixes the two.

Layout. Desktop: 280px | 1fr — left = class list and the tab nav, centre = the working table at up to 1,100 px; no right pane except in the Mark audit, where the Mark view (10.7) opens in a 480 px pane at its container-query tablet variant (10-CONV-004). Tablet: same with the class list as an overlay. Mobile: read-only summaries plus the full override flow — a teacher must be able to overrule a Mark from a phone; assignment creation is desktop/tablet only and says so.

Regions and elements.

TabElements
RosterClass code (8 characters, large tabular, Copy and Regenerate) · join link and printable QR · student rows: name, joined date, Course, last active (day granularity), Attempts this week, aggregate ladder depth ("mean rung 2.4"), open challenges. Per-student detail shows Attempts, Marks and assignment work only — never Session transcripts, never per-Turn rungs (§07.9). Remove student (with a confirmation naming what the student keeps).
AssignmentsCreate: pick Items (past-paper parts, Margin originals, "5 like this"), set open and due timestamps, a lock window (during it the Paper-runner no-help rule applies: no tutor Turns, no ladder, no citations, no Library — 10-RUNR-001), and an allowed-help level for outside the window (none · rungs 1–3 · full ladder). Assignment rows show submitted/marked/overdue counts, mean band per AO, and the three most common reason_codes across the class.
Marks (audit)A queue sorted by show_teacher_flag, low AO confidence, NOT_IN_INDICATIVE_VALID_ALT, challenge outcomes and random sample. Each row opens the Mark view with the student's answer, spans, scheme paraphrase and the machine rationale. Override: two clicks — click the AO level or the total, choose a reason code, done; a free-text note is optional. Reason codes: application_credited · valid_alternative · level_too_generous · level_too_harsh · command_word_met · working_credited · illegible_misread · out_of_scope · other. Both marks are kept and shown to the student (10.7 override strip).
CalibrationThe teacher-as-calibrator queue: "Mark these 10 scripts blind" — the machine Mark is hidden until the teacher submits; agreement is then shown per AO with the disagreement highlighted. Double-marking credit is recorded; a second teacher's confirmation promotes the item to Tier 2 gold (SYNTHESIS §8.5). Header line: "Your marks train the marker for 9609 P2. 312 scripts so far · agreement 0.82."
TrendsDisagreement trends per paper per quarter: override rate, direction (generous/harsh), the AO most often overridden, challenge outcomes, and the per-paper calibration state with its gate numbers. One chart, five tones, no red.
SettingsClass-locked Course fields (syllabus, papers, series — locked fields render as "Set by your teacher" for students, 10.2), school-safe mode (§12.7), mock import (batch photos → 10.8 → Marks), and the teacher's data-visibility statement.

v1-only (build the routes, hide behind a flag, do not ship at MVP). Class heatmap by syllabus point; SSO and roster sync (Google Classroom, Wonde, Clever); evidence export for moderation and appeals; per-student intervention suggestions; parent co-visibility; LMS grade passback; multi-class analytics; department-level dashboards. The console must render a one-line "In v1" row where each of these will live, rather than a disabled control.

States. empty: a new class shows the code at full size with "Give this code to your class. Nothing appears here until a student joins." loading: table skeletons at final row height; the audit queue paints its count from cache. error: a failed override is retried inline and never lost ("Not saved — retry"); an unavailable Mark shows the student's answer and the scheme so the teacher can still mark blind. offline: read-only queue from cache; overrides queue with a queued tag and apply in order on reconnect. gated: a paper below the calibration gate shows the evidence-only Mark to the teacher too, with the gate numbers and an explicit "no number is shown to your students for this paper".

Interactions and shortcuts. j/k move the queue, ↵ opens, Esc returns to the queue with position preserved; 1…5 select a level on the focused AO, then r opens the reason chips, ↵ saves — this is the two-click path on a keyboard. Bulk actions: select rows with x, then "Mark as reviewed". Copying the class code is one click and shows the printable QR. Nothing in the console can edit a student's answer, delete an Attempt, or read a Session transcript.

Data. Reads: classes {code, course, locked_fields, teacher_ids}, roster, assignments {items[], open_at, due_at, lock_window, allowed_help}, Attempts and Marks for class members (assignment and marked work only), calibration state per paper, challenge outcomes, aggregate ladder depth. Writes: class_codes (create/regenerate), assignments, overrides {mark_id, teacher_id, from, to, per_ao[], reason_code, note?, at} → a new Mark row with supersedes (05-MARK-012) and a Tier-2 gold candidate, calibration_marks {teacher_id, blind: true, marks}, reviewed_at on audit rows, telemetry override_created, calibration_submitted.

10.21Parent digest

Purpose. Give a consenting parent enough evidence to help — and nothing that turns them into a second examiner. Effort and coverage from Attempts; no transcripts, no ranking.

Stage. MVP at digest v0: the fortnightly email and its web mirror, with the fixed sections below. Configurable cadence, per-Course digests and the guardian dashboard are v1.

Jobs served. J10 (a parent who paid wants to know it is working); J11 (helping without nagging). Serves no learner job directly, so it must cost the learner nothing.

Route. /p/:digestId (web view of the sent email, auth-gated to the linked guardian_links.parent_user_id), /p (index of past digests + controls). Email is the primary surface; the web view is the same content plus controls. Cadence default fortnightly, Sunday 18:00 local (SYNTHESIS §6 screen 21); the student may set weekly, fortnightly, monthly or paused-for-one-cycle in Settings › Memory › Sharing. Digest ids are opaque ULIDs; links expire after 60 days.

Layout. Email: one 600 px column, no images beyond the wordmark, light palette forced (09-DARK-007), tabular numbers. Web: same column at max 640 px plus a controls block. No charts in email; the web view may show the Activity heatmap (10.14) and nothing else from Progress.

Regions and elements.

RegionContent and rules
Header"Aisha · 9609 Business · 14 days to 28 September" — display name, Course, window. No greeting line, no "Hi there!".
Effort (default-shared)sessions vs weekly goal, minutes, longest gap, Cards reviewed, Attempts marked. Rest days neutral, never misses.
Coverage (default-shared)syllabus point titles with official numbering, count of topics that moved, and the sentence "Topics move when two unaided attempts are correct on different days." No pips, no percentages, no per-topic state.
Evidence (default-shared)Marks taken and the unaided delta with n. No band, no grade, no per-Mark score.
One suggestionexactly one, addressed to the parent, actionable and non-nagging: "The only free 45 minutes this fortnight is Thursday evening. That block is a timed Paper 2 section — a quiet room helps more than a reminder." Generated from the Plan and busy hours, never from affect signals.
Consent-gated blockrendered only where guardian_links.scope[key] = true and the student's own toggle is on: predicted_grade (default off, 05-PRED-004), mark_bands, wrong_questions, plan_detail. Each renders with the same labels the student sees, including "practice estimate, not a board mark".
Controls (web only)Study Hours, Quiet Hours (teen default 22:00–07:00), payment, cadence, "Turn the digest off". Every change writes an audit row and shows the student an in-app banner — "Your parent set Quiet Hours 22:00–07:00" (AADC transparency, 11-PRIV-001).
Footernon-affiliation line (09-PRNT-006) · "This digest is built from practice attempts. It contains no conversations." · unsubscribe · "See exactly what was shared" → /p/:digestId/shared, visible to the student too.

States. empty (no activity): send anyway — "No sessions this fortnight." plus the suggestion, never a chasing line; silence reads as an outage. partial: window label says the Course started mid-window. paused (16+ students only): "This cycle's digest is paused by Aisha. The next one is 12 October." off: no email; the web index names the state and who set it. error: two retries maximum, logged and shown in /p. offline · streaming · gated/quota: n/a — a batch job whose only model call is the suggestion, which falls back to a Plan-derived template.

Interactions. Links only in the email. "See exactly what was shared" renders the stored payload as a labelled list, the same page for parent and student. Under-16 students cannot switch the digest off (it is a consent condition) but can pause a cycle, can turn every consent-gated block off, and always see the payload; 16+ students can switch it off and the parent is told who did.

The payload is materialised and stored so /p/:digestId/shared shows what was actually sent, not a recomputation.

10.22Challenge-a-mark

Purpose. Make disagreement with the Examiner Twin a one-tap, examiner-voice procedure rather than a support ticket — and turn every disagreement into calibration data (§05.7). The screen is the visible half of 05-CHAL-001…006; nothing here re-specifies the marking logic.

Stage. MVP. A product that publishes an agreement number must let the student contest a Mark from day one; stage-2 human review is MVP at the calibrator's desk (10.20), not a separate v1 queue.

Jobs served. J1 (trust the Mark), J7 (teacher of record confirms anything that matters), 02-MOM-003 (mock season, when a wrong band costs a week of misdirected work).

Route. /c/:courseId/marks/:markId/challenge. Entry: the Challenge tertiary action in the Mark view (10.7) header overflow and the same action in the mock debrief per question part. Deep-linkable; the teacher's copy of the same object is /t/:classId/challenges/:challengeId.

Layout. Desktop: the Mark view stays mounted in the left column (student answer with spans, dropped to 0.6 opacity while Stage 1 runs) and the right pane switches to the Compare tab at --panel-w, showing original vs re-mark per AO. Tablet: Compare replaces the centre column with a back arrow. Mobile: a full route; the two rationales stack (original first, re-mark second) with a sticky per-AO delta bar at the top.

Regions and elements.

RegionElements and rules
Trigger sheetone line "A different marker will look at this. Your original Mark is kept." · optional one-line reason (200 chars, placeholder "Optional — which part, and why") · optional AO multi-select chips · one filled button Send for a second look. No mention of "appeal", no promise of a higher mark.
Status stripstage chip (Stage 1 · second look / Stage 2 · teacher / Stage 2 · examiner), elapsed timer for Stage 1 (target <60 s), SLA line for Stage 2 ("An examiner is checking AO4 — up to 72 hours"), and the family provenance chip for each marker (09-COPY-003 j: chip only, never a headline).
Compare tableone row per AO: original level and marks · re-mark level and marks · delta · the deciding span quoted from the student's answer with its line ref. Changed rows carry the delta in tabular figures; unchanged rows read "unchanged".
Rationale pairthe two rationales side by side (stacked on mobile), each ≤60 words, examiner-voice per 05-CHAL-004, each citing its descriptor or marking point with a citation chip that opens the Source pane.
Outcome cardupheld · revised · split, with the canonical sentence and the resulting band. revised shows the new BandTotal with "supersedes" and a link to the superseded Mark (05-MARK-012).
EscalationStill disagree (always available once, per stage) → teacher of record if a Class exists, else the contracted-examiner queue. Below it, one factual line: "Challenges are logged and feed the calibration page for this paper."
Teacher/examiner resultthe human Mark, the reason code, both machine Marks collapsed behind "Show what the markers said", and — where the Class records grades — the confirmation checkbox that is the Annex III human-oversight gate (§08.11, 11-PRIV-005 §6).
┌ Mark · 9609/22 s24 Q3(b) Evaluate · 12 marks ──────── Stage 1 · 00:41 ─┐
│ …student answer, spans dimmed while the second look runs…              │
├───────────────────────────── Compare ──────────────────────────────────┤
│ AO   original        second look     delta                              │
│ AO1  L2  2/2         L2  2/2         unchanged                          │
│ AO2  L2  3/4         L2  3/4         unchanged                          │
│ AO3  L2  5/8 …       L2  5/8         unchanged                          │
│ AO4  L1  1/4         L2  3/4         +2      ← deciding span, line 18   │
│ "…but the finance constraint outweighs product dependence here…"        │
├────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ Original: "No weighing of one factor against another — L1."¹            │
│ Second look: "Line 18 weighs finance against product dependence — L2."² │
│ Outcome: revised. Band 33–37 → 35–39.  [Still disagree]  [Back to Mark] │
└────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

States. empty: n/a (the screen only exists for a Mark). loading/streaming: the Compare table skeletons at final geometry and fills per AO as the re-mark streams (09-STRM-011); the deciding span highlights last. error: "The second marker is unavailable. Your challenge is queued — we'll notify you." with the challenge persisted (stage1_queued); never a lost challenge. offline: Send for a second look queues in the outbox (11-OFF-002) and the strip reads "Queued — sends when you're back". gated/quota: challenges are never metered and never rate-limited per Mark (05-CHAL-001); a challenge does not consume a levels-Mark quota unit. exam week: Stage 2 SLA copy becomes "after your paper" when the component is within 72 h (05-CHAL-006) and no predicted-grade recomputation runs. below gate: the Compare table shows levels and spans with no number, matching the parent Mark.

State machine. none → submitted → stage1_running → {upheld | revised | split} → (still_disagree) → stage2_queued → stage2_human → closed. One challenge per Mark per stage; revised creates a new Mark with supersedes; closed is terminal and the Mark's challenge_state records the last outcome. A teacher override taken independently (§05, 10.20) closes an open challenge with outcome teacher_override and notifies the student in the same neutral voice.

Interactions and shortcuts. ⌘⇧C from an open Mark opens the trigger sheet; Enter sends; [ ] walk AO rows; d toggles "show only changed AOs"; Escape returns to the Mark with state preserved. Notification on Stage 2 completion respects Quiet Hours and carries no verdict in the preview text ("Your Paper 2 challenge has a result").

Data. Read: marks (original and second-marker rows), mark_scheme_items, attempts, Class membership. Written: challenges {id, mark_id, stage, families[], reason_text?, aos[], outcome, delta_per_ao, human_id?, created_at, closed_at} per 05-CHAL-005; a new marks row on revised; a Tier 2 gold candidate on human confirmation (§08.11).

Requirements.

IDRequirementAcceptance
10-CHLG-001Challenge is reachable in one tap from any Mark, including a below-gate Mark and an anonymous landing Mark (which prompts Save first).Route crawl: the action exists on 100% of Mark fixtures.
10-CHLG-002Stage 1 renders a complete Compare table with both rationales in ≤60 s p95; the re-marker family differs from both families used on the original.Soak on 200 fixtures; assert families ∩ original_families = ∅.
10-CHLG-003The copy contains no apology, no praise, no "sorry", no "you were right", and no promise about the outcome before it exists.Copy lint over the challenge catalogue + generated rationale corpus.
10-CHLG-004Every outcome writes a challenges row with delta_per_ao; the per-paper challenge rate and overturn_rate on the calibration page (05-GATE-008) are computed from this table and no other.Reconciliation job: dashboard numbers equal a direct SQL count.
10-CHLG-005Product-side targets are instrumented and alarmed, in one direction and one vocabulary: challenge_rate = challenges ÷ marks <3%, and overturn_rate = revised ÷ challenges <30%, per paper per month. "Upheld" is an outcome of a single challenge (the state machine above), never a metric — a rate named upheld_rate anywhere in code, dashboards or copy fails the metrics lint, because the same number read as "upheld" and as "overturned" alarms in opposite directions (08-ENS-007, 05-CHAL-005).Dashboard with alarm; a paper breaching either pages the content lead (11-RISK-001 #1).
10-CHLG-006A challenge never changes a school-recorded grade without a teacher confirmation action.Fixture: revised outcome in a Class with grade_sync=true leaves the recorded grade unchanged until the checkbox is set; audit row present.
10-CHLG-007Challenging is free of quota and of any friction copy that discourages it (no "are you sure", no counter of how many you have raised).Meter fixture; DOM scan for confirmation dialogues = 0.

Why: a marker students cannot argue with is a marker they stop believing; the challenge flow is also the cheapest source of Tier 2 gold the product has (SYNTHESIS §5 bet 1, §8.6).

10.23Learning Receipt / Share / Export

Purpose. Let a student prove how a piece of work was done — attempts, help rungs, drafts, Marks, timestamps — to a teacher who suspects AI, and let anyone share a Mark or a result without leaking learner state. Contents and cryptography are specified in §12.2; this screen is how they are read, shared and exported.

Stage. Split. MVP: the Receipt cover, timeline and exports (.pdf, .csv, .json) and Mark sharing — /m/:markToken already exists at MVP (10.1) and the WhatsApp link is the acquisition loop. v1: public revocable Receipt and Artifact tokens at /r/:token, and the server-rendered share cards at /share/mark/:markId. Build the MVP half first; the v1 half adds a token table and an image renderer and changes no data on this screen. This supersedes any reading of 03-PAR-025 that defers all sharing to v1: the row means Receipts and Artifacts.

Jobs served. J9 (be believed), J7 (hand a teacher evidence), J12 (leave with your data). 02-MOM-002 (coursework season), 02-MOM-004 (results day).

Route. /receipt/:receiptId (owner view, auth-gated) · /r/:token (public, learner state stripped, revocable) · /verify/:receiptId (signature verification, no auth, §12.2) · exports from Settings › Data. Share cards are generated at /share/mark/:markId and /share/receipt/:receiptId as server-rendered images.

Layout. Desktop: a single 720 px reading column — cover block, timeline table, drafts appendix — with a 280 px sticky right rail carrying Export PDF, Copy public link, Show teacher, Revoke link and the verification QR. Mobile: one column; the rail becomes a bottom action bar of two buttons (Export PDF, Share) plus an overflow.

Regions and elements.

RegionElements and rules
Coverstudent display name, Course, assignment or Session title, date range, Pack version, policy version, the first 16 hex of the SHA-256 content hash, the Ed25519 key id, and a QR to /verify/:receiptId.
Timelineone row per event: timestamp (learner timezone, ISO in the export) · event (attempt · hint · rung · draft · mark · seen_solution · challenge · teacher_override) · rung reached · Mark band where the event is a Mark · a Seen solution chip where seen_solution=true. Rows are never editable and never deleted; a redaction is a row, not a gap.
Drafts appendixeach draft as stored, with diff bars against the previous (added = solid left rule, removed = struck) per 09-PRNT-003. The tutor's words are never presented as the student's.
Integrity summarythree counts in one line: attempts before first help, help rungs used (median and max), seen-solution events — the numbers a teacher actually reads.
Share cardstwo templates, 1200×630 PNG server-rendered: Mark card (question ref, tariff, command word, band or "practice estimate — not yet calibrated", one credited span quoted ≤25 words, calibration badge, non-affiliation line) and Receipt card (assignment title, the three integrity counts, hash prefix, verification URL). Both carry the wordmark and no learner identity beyond the display name the student typed.
ExportsReceipt PDF (09-PRNT-003) · Receipt JSON (§12.2 schema, signature detached) · Mark PDF · Cards .apkg · Plan .ics · full account ZIP (11-PRIV-004). Each export names, above the button, exactly what it contains in one line.
Noticesthe non-affiliation line (09-PRNT-006) on every rendered page, print page and share card; on the public variant additionally "Public copy — learner state removed."
┌ Learning Receipt ─────────────────────────────  [Export PDF] [Copy link] ┐
│ Aisha K. · 9609 Business · "Unit 3 essay draft" · 2–9 Sep 2026            │
│ Pack 9609 2026–28 v14 · policy v31 · sha256 4f9c2ab77e10d3c8 · key mk-2   │
│                                                    ▣ verify → /verify/…   │
├───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ 02 Sep 18:04  attempt   own plan, 180 words          rung —               │
│ 02 Sep 18:19  hint      conceptual pointer           rung 2               │
│ 03 Sep 17:40  draft     v1 (620 words)               —                    │
│ 04 Sep 17:12  mark      AO2 L2 · AO4 L1 · 8–11       —                    │
│ 05 Sep 16:55  attempt   rewrite of ¶3                rung —               │
│ 06 Sep 19:02  seen_solution  exemplar ¶ shown   [Seen solution] rung 4    │
├───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ 4 attempts before first help · rungs: median 2, max 4 · 1 seen solution   │
│ Margin is not affiliated with … Marks are practice estimates.             │
└───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

What is never shareable. The public variant and every share card strip: mastery states and pips, calibration status of the student, Brier and confidence data, predicted grade band (extends 10-PROG-001), Plan contents, wrong-question bank, memory objects, affect or distress signals, moderation events, other users' identities, parent or teacher identities, the raw uploaded image, and any Turn text that is not a draft the student wrote. Verbatim official mark-scheme or examiner-report wording is never exported (§06); the Mark cites our paraphrase and a page link.

States. empty (no receipt yet): "Receipts are created when you work on a piece with a deadline. Start one from any Session." + Start a receipt. generating: the hash and signature take ≤3 s; the page shows the timeline immediately with the cover block skeletoned. revoked: /r/:token returns a plain page "This link was turned off by its owner." with no content and no cached copy (Cache-Control: no-store). expired: public tokens expire after 180 days by default with the same page and a "the owner can re-share" line. error: signing failure blocks publication — never publish an unsigned receipt; the card reads "The signature failed. Nothing was shared. Retry." offline: the owner view renders from cache; export and share are disabled with a tooltip. quota: exports are 2/day per account (11-API-005) with a plain-number line.

Interactions and shortcuts. ⌘K → Export receipt; Show teacher copies the public link and, when a Class exists, posts the receipt to the teacher's queue instead of the clipboard; Revoke link is immediate and irreversible for that token (a new token can be issued); a share card is previewed before it is generated, and the preview is the exact file.

Data. Read: receipts, attempts, turns (rung, help-event metadata only), drafts, marks, challenges. Written: receipts {id, subject_ref, window, payload_json, content_hash, signature, key_id, created_at}, receipt_tokens {token, receipt_id, created_at, revoked_at, expires_at, view_count}, an audit_log row on every share, revoke and export.

Requirements.

IDRequirementAcceptance
10-RCPT-001Every rendered receipt (screen, PDF, JSON) verifies against /verify/:receiptId; a byte-modified export fails verification with a named reason.Tamper test: flip one character in the JSON → invalid_signature; PDF re-export of the same receipt gives an identical content_hash.
10-RCPT-002The public variant contains none of the stripped fields listed above.Field-diff test between owner and public payloads; the strip list is one constant with a snapshot test; 0 leaks over 500 fixtures.
10-RCPT-003Share cards render server-side, deterministically, and carry the non-affiliation line and the calibration state of the Mark.Image hash stable across two renders; OCR of 50 cards finds both strings.
10-RCPT-004Revocation takes effect in ≤5 s globally, including CDN and any generated share card URL.Revoke then fetch from three edge regions: 404/410 with no body.
10-RCPT-005Seen-solution events and help rungs appear in the receipt exactly as recorded; the receipt cannot be edited, filtered or "cleaned up" by the student before sharing.UI has no edit affordance; API rejects a partial receipt request; a fixture with 3 seen-solution rows shares all 3.
10-RCPT-006A receipt is never generated or shared automatically; every share is an explicit student action with the audience named.0 shares without a matching audit_log action row.
10-RCPT-007Receipt PDF ≤10 MB, tagged PDF/UA, printable per 09-PRNT-003, with the hash in every footer.pdfinfo + Playwright print test on the fixture set.

Why: 64% of US high-schoolers fear being falsely accused of AI use and ESL writers are flagged 2–3× more often by detectors [A59]; a signed process log is the only defence a student can hold that does not depend on a detector being right.

10.24Distress, safety, system and quota states

Purpose. Specify the surfaces that appear when something is wrong — with the student, the network, the model route, the quota, or the platform — so that none of them is invented at build time. Every one is an inline card or a banner in the flow; none is a modal (09-PRIN-009). The scripts and escalation logic live in §12.4–12.8; the pixels and the exact strings live here.

Stage. MVP for rows 1–12 of the catalogue and for the whole crisis-resource config: a product that marks teenagers' work at 23:40 ships its distress, offline, quota and maintenance surfaces on day one. Nothing here is v1.

Jobs served. All twelve, in the moment they break. 02-MOM-003 (mock season) and 02-MOM-005 (the night before) are where most of these fire.

Route. No route of its own. These are components rendered in place: SafetyCard and DistressCard in the Session (10.5) and anywhere a Turn streams; Banner under the top bar for connection, degradation and quota; InlineError inside the failing region; /status and the maintenance page for platform-wide events.

Layout. Distress and crisis cards render in the Turn stream at full centre measure with a 1 px --border-strong rule and no icon; they are never dismissible by scrolling past — dismissal is an explicit Close. Banners are --banner-h 40 px single-line at ≥900 px and --banner-h-2 56 px two-line below, sticky under the top bar, stacking at most two (a third collapses the older pair into "2 notices ▾"); 44 px is --touch-min and is not a banner height. Error cards sit inside the region that failed and preserve the user's input above them.

The catalogue. Copy is quoted here so the state is legible in one place; the shipped text is the §15.E catalogue entry under the key column, and where 09-COPY-002 lists the same key its "Do" column and this row are the same object. The catalogue test compares all three against §15.E byte-for-byte and fails on any drift, so a string is edited in §15.E and nowhere else.

#StatekeyTriggerCopy (canonical string)Primary action

Crisis resources by region. Config-driven, never model-generated:

Author config/crisis_resources.yaml; the build emits config/crisis_resources.json, which is the file §12.4 (12-TEEN-005) reads. The numbers below are defaults, not verified facts. Counsel and operations must confirm every line — that the service exists, that it is free, that its hours and languages are as stated, and that a minor may call it — and set verified_on before that region ships. A region with verified_on: null is not served to any account.

States. The catalogue above is this screen's state list; there is no separate empty/loading story because these surfaces are themselves the states of other screens. Two composite states are specified here rather than per row: stacking — at most two banners, ordered offline > maintenance > marking-paused > quota > grace, a third collapsing the older pair into "2 notices ▾"; and suppression — while a distress or crisis card is open no banner, nudge, notification or upsell renders anywhere in the app until it is closed (12-WELL-003), because a quota notice under a crisis card is the worst screen this product can draw.

Interactions and shortcuts. Every card is keyboard-reachable in the flow position where it renders; Esc closes a dismissible card and returns focus to the element that preceded it, and does nothing on the crisis card, which closes only through its explicit Close. Resource links (tel:, sms:, url) come first in the tab order of the crisis card (10-STAT-004). Banners are not focus traps and do not steal focus on appearance; a screen reader announces them once through the same role="status" region, never per re-render. Take 5 pauses every timer including the Plan block and the soft item timer; Keep going records nudge_dismissed and does not re-arm before the next threshold in row 3.

Data. Reads: affect and wellbeing_state (04.9, §12.5), policy.tenant_region / profile.country / IP country and age_band (10-STAT-001), config/crisis_resources.json, config/limits.yaml for rows 9 and 10, route state from §08.7, the incident feed for row 12. Writes: wellbeing_events {kind, shown_at, dismissed_at, action}, crisis_card_shown {region_resolved, resolution_level, age_band} — resolution level and region only, never the message that triggered it, and never a transcript excerpt — nudge_dismissed, crisis_config_fallback counter, quota_notice_shown {meter, plan}. No row here writes to the Learner Graph, and no row here is a training signal.

IDRequirementAcceptance
10-STAT-001Resolve the region in exactly this order and stop at the first hit: tenant region (policy.tenant_region) → account region (profile.country) → IP country → _default. UI language never selects a region; a 13_15 or 16_17 account prefers the role: youth service as {primary}.Fixture matrix of the four resolution levels × three age bands; a KZ account inside a GB school tenant renders the GB block.
10-STAT-002The model never emits a helpline number, shortcode or URL. The renderer builds {resources}, {primary}, {shortcode} and {emergency} from config only; if the config is missing, unparsable, or the resolved region has no show_in_card service, it fails closed to _default and logs crisis_config_fallback. Model text matching a phone/helpline-URL regex blocks the Turn.Delete crisis_resources.json in staging → the crisis card still renders the _default block; counter increments; 0 numbers in model output across the red-team corpus (§12.10).
10-STAT-003Operations re-verify every entry quarterly and before each exam series, writing verified_on. pnpm safety:lint fails the build when any served region has an entry with verified_on null or older than 120 days (12-TEEN-005), and names the region and service.Backdate one verified_on by 121 days → CI fails with that region named.
10-STAT-004Call {primary} is a real tel: link and Text {shortcode} a real sms: link, built from the config values, tappable on mobile and keyboard-reachable before any other control in the card (§09 A11Y). A service with url and no phone renders as a link, never as copyable text.DOM test: href equals tel: / sms: plus the config value; tab order puts resource links first.
10-STAT-005No region is served until counsel has signed off its entries and the safety case doc (11-PRIV-001) records the sign-off date; until then that country resolves to _default.Region-readiness table in the safety case; a fixture for an unsigned country renders _default.

10.25Admin / Compiler (internal)

Purpose. The internal console where Packs are built and shipped: the ingestion DAG (§06.4), the review UIs that human-confirm mapping and scheme structuring, the provenance ledger and kill switch, the per-paper calibration and gate dashboards (§05.6), eval runs (§08.9) and feature flags. It is built from the same tokens as the product (06-COMP-006) because the people who use it stare at it for eight hours a day.

Stage. MVP. Internal-only, behind the staff role; it is how a Pack reaches the gate at all (§06), so it cannot be deferred behind the surfaces that depend on it.

Jobs served. None of J1–J12. It serves the content lead, the ex-examiner calibrators, the ML lead and the on-call engineer; its output is the Pack readiness state every learner surface depends on.

Route. /admin/*, behind SSO with hardware second factor and a role claim: ingest · queue · map · scheme · er · ledger · calibration · evals · flags · tenants. Every route is audit-logged with the actor; no route is reachable from the product shell (separate app bundle, separate cookie scope).

Layout. Two panes, keyboard-first: left = work queue (virtualised list, filter row, counts), right = the item with the source crop always visible beside the proposal (06-COMP-006). No mobile layout — desktop ≥1280 only; below that a line says so.

Regions and elements.

RouteElements and rules
ingestDAG view of stages 0–16 per document set: node = stage, colour-free status glyph, throughput, error count; click a node → the documents in it. Actions: Replay stage (keyed by (doc_id, doc_version, stage, rules_version), 06-COMP-005), Pause pipeline, Open rules file. Live counters: pages/hour, parse_confidence distribution, pass-disagreement %, cost to date (06-COMP-004).
queueThe human queues in one place with age p95 and owner: classify-unknown, ambiguous paper IDs, unparsed formulas, low-confidence pages, caption checks, disagreement pairs. Sort by age; SLA badge at >3 working days.
mapSection → syllabus mapping review (stage 8): left the source section with its heading path and page crop, right the proposed syllabus_node_id with siblings and objective_text, confidence, and the source's own numbering shown as its numbering. Keys y accept · n reject · e edit target · j/k move · b batch-accept the current ≥0.95 block. Reviewer acceptance rate shown live.
schemeMarking-point editor: the paste-to-structured output (§06.7) as an editable 05.3 record — marking points with type, conjunctive atoms, accept/reject, AO; levels grids with every level present; an 8-gram overlap meter against the source that must read 0 before Confirm. Nothing here can edit official text, only our paraphrase and flags.
erExaminer-report mining review: paraphrase left, source crop right, overlap meter, and the heuristic test-run against 20 gold scripts showing hit count before accept.
ledgerprovenance_ledger search by sha256, source_url, doc_id or title, answering in ≤1 s with the full derivation closure (chunks, items, schemes, insights, cache keys). Each row: class, licence_basis, expiry, uploader org, hash-chain status. Kill switch is a per-document toggle with a mandatory reason and a confirm-by-typing-the-title step; flipping it removes the document from prefilter, practice selection, Pack builds and caches within the 24-hour takedown SLA and writes an immutable ledger event (06-PROV-007).
calibrationPer paper: state (not yet calibrated · provisional · gated), QWK, level agreement, within-tolerance %, signed error, n scripts by gold tier, the measured human–human line, fairness buckets (region, L1, handwritten, length), series covered, policy version, challenge and upheld rates, last audit. Actions: Run gate, Publish to the public calibration page, Pause this paper (drops Marks to the second family with the Provisional badge). Seeding auto-pause events appear as a timeline under the numbers.
evalsEval runs by suite (pedagogy 30-turn, praise lint, marking gold per paper, retrieval Recall@8, cache assertion, a11y, CWV) × policy version × model; diff against the previous run; a red row blocks the release train and links to the failing cases.
flagsFeature flags and kill switches with owner, default, rollout %, experiment link and expiry date; flags without an expiry cannot be created. Named kill switches at minimum: anon_landing_mark, levels_marking, predicted_grades, parent_digest, voice, public_receipts, debt_guard.
tenantsTenant policy inspector (read-mostly): residency, allowed providers, retention, budget, consent coverage, DPA state. Editing a policy requires two-person approval.

States. empty: a queue with nothing in it shows the throughput number instead of an illustration. loading: virtualised rows skeleton at final height. error: stage failures render the exception and the replay command; a failed publish publishes nothing (06-COMP-004/16). offline: n/a — admin is online-only and says so. gated/quota: n/a. two-person: destructive actions (kill switch, tenant policy edit, publish, pause a paper) render an approval strip naming the requester and the approver, and stay pending until a second qualified actor confirms.

Interactions and shortcuts. Everything reachable by keyboard: g then the route letter jumps; j/k moves; y/n/e in review UIs; ⌘Enter confirms; ? lists the map. Bulk actions are always previewable ("This will kill 1 document, 214 chunks, 38 items, 6 insights — type the title to confirm").

Data. Read: documents, chunks, ingest_jobs, mapping_table, mark_scheme_items, examiner_insights, provenance_ledger, calibration_records, eval_runs, flags, tenants. Written: review decisions with reviewer id, ledger events, gate results, flag changes, and an audit_log row for every action including reads of a tenant policy.

10.26Ask

Purpose. Give the student the thing they actually open a chat product to do — ask a question right now, about anything, with no Course, no setup and no commitment — inside Margin rather than in the other tab. Ask is the general-help surface: full chat parity (§03.2), full citation and source behaviour where a Pack happens to cover the question, and an explicit, permanent statement that it is not exam-grounded study and does not count as such.

Stage. MVP, in full. This is the most frequent chat action in the product and the answer §00, §03.1 and 03-SCOP-006 give to "what happens when there is no Pack"; a deferred Ask means the fastest path to help is a competitor.

Jobs served. J4 (explain this so it sticks), J11 ("just the answer" without losing the learning), J9 (a subject Margin has no Pack for); 02-MOM-001 (the first five minutes, before any Course exists), 02-MOM-005 (21:40, one question, then bed).

Route. /ask/:sessionId. Created by the sidebar Ask row (10.3), by ⌘K → Ask <anything>, by typing at /ask, by "Ask about {subject}" from a waiting Course (10.4) and by the SelectionPopover's Ask from any reader or Turn. ?q=<text> pre-fills the composer without sending. The route is signed-in only: the anonymous equivalent is 10.1, which marks rather than converses. An Ask Session is a first-class Session row with course_id = null; it is listed under Recent with an "Ask" tag and survives until the student deletes it.

Layout. The Session layout (10.5) minus two things: no CourseTree in the sidebar (the sidebar shows Home, Courses, Recent, Due — Ask has no tree of its own) and no HelpLadder in the message margin (there is no gradable Item, so there is no rung to climb). Desktop ≥1280: 280px | 1fr | 480px, centre 68 ch, right pane at its 48 px rail, opening to --panel-w on the first citation chip exactly as 10-CONV-002 specifies. Tablet and mobile as 10.5. The composer is identical to 10.5's in geometry and behaviour, with one difference stated below.

Move this Ask first."). ⌘⇧O opens Move to a Course.

Data. Reads: memories the student has marked global (scope: global in §07.7) and nothing Course-scoped; the Pack catalogue for subject detection and citation only where a Pack is live; policy object (quotas, teen defaults, school_safe). Writes: sessions {id, course_id: null, title, ask: true} and turns — and nothing else. What Ask does not do, stated once and enforced by 10-ASKS-002: it writes no attempts row, so nothing here changes mastery, state_reason, readiness or any calibration number; it writes no cards and schedules no FSRS review; it writes no memories, so no MemoryChip can render on this screen; it produces no Mark and no band, so no levels-Mark allowance is spent; it makes no Plan block and moves none. It is not incognito — the Session is visible in Recent and retained under the ordinary §07.8 defaults — it is simply outside the Learner Graph.

After the third Ask in seven days on a subject with a live Pack, the scope line gains one appended sentence — "Marked practice on this is in your {course_name} Course." — with the Course name as a link. It appends once, it never becomes a modal, an upsell or a nag, and it never appears for a subject with no Pack.Fixture: 3 Asks in 7 days on 9609 → the sentence appears once; a fourth Ask does not repeat it; the same fixture on 9701 (no Pack) never shows it.

Why: SYNTHESIS §3.1 requires that a student lose nothing by leaving a frontier chat product, and the thing they would lose first is the ability to ask a question without declaring a subject. Making Ask explicitly outside the Learner Graph is what lets it be unrestricted: the graph stays honest because only gated Attempts enter it, and the student stays in one tab.

10.27Public paper finder (logged out)

Purpose. Be the fastest way on the internet to find a specific Cambridge past paper, mark scheme or examiner report — with no account, no ads and no hosted PDFs — so that the search a student already runs ("9609 s23 qp 22") lands on Margin's index and one click later on the board's own page. This is distribution channel 3 of SYNTHESIS §12 and R4's named mitigation; it is a link index, never a mirror.

Stage. MVP for the index, the deep links and the command-word explainer; live at M5 soft and M6 full per §14.4's channel table. v1 adds saved filters and the "papers near this syllabus point" cross-link.

Jobs served. J7 (exam-style questions that behave like the real ones), J8 (where do I stand) indirectly — this screen's job is acquisition, and its learning job is only to get the student to the right document faster than a search engine does.

Route. /papers (index) and /papers/:board/:subject/:series/:component, with /papers/:board/:subject as the subject page. Every level is a real, server-rendered, indexable URL with its own title, description and structured data; deep links from search engines and from Reddit or WhatsApp are the point of the screen. No session is required and none is created. A signed-in student who lands here is offered the in-Course finder (10.9) in one line and is never redirected automatically, because the link they followed is the page they wanted.

Layout. A two-column public page, not the app shell: no sidebar, no composer, no right pane. Desktop ≥1280: filters in a 280 px left rail, results table in 1fr capped at 960 px (a table, not text-measured). Tablet: filters collapse to a chip row above the table. Mobile: chip row + list rows; a row expands in place rather than pushing a route, so back always leaves the site rather than walking a stack the visitor did not build.

States. empty (no filter matches): "No paper indexed for that combination yet." plus the nearest three rows and a "Tell us what's missing" link — never a blank table. loading: the table skeletons at final row height; filters are interactive before results arrive. error: the index is a static build artefact, so an error here is a CDN failure — the page renders from the last good build with a 13 px line "Index from {date}". offline: a previously visited subject page renders from the service-worker cache with the same dated line; Open on {board} ↗ stays a live link and fails at the board, not here. gated/quota: n/a — nothing on this screen is metered, and that is the point of the word "free-forever". link_dead: a document whose deep link has failed the weekly link check renders greyed with "This link moved — we're fixing it" and is excluded from the count.

Interactions and shortcuts. Filters are URL state, so every view is copy-pasteable and the browser back button walks filter changes. / focuses the subject typeahead; Enter on a row opens the board's page in a new tab. There are no app shortcuts on this page: ⌘K is not bound, because a logged-out visitor has no palette. Nothing on the page requires JavaScript to read the table or follow a link.

Data. Reads: the published document index (documents filtered to provenance = OFFICIAL_PUBLIC with a resolved source_url), Pack command-word tables for live Packs, and nothing else. Writes: nothing to any learner object; anonymous analytics only (finder_view {subject, series, component}, finder_outbound {doc_id}, finder_conversion), with no device fingerprint beyond the §11 default and no cookie before consent. The index is regenerated on every Pack build and served as static HTML plus a JSON payload; there is no query that reaches the learner database from this route.

§11Technical architecture

11.1Reference architecture and stack

Build Margin as one TypeScript monorepo with a small number of named services. A service is a deployable with its own queue, SLO and on-call owner; everything else is a package. Do not split further at MVP.

11-ARCH-003 — Topology per region. Deploy the full data plane (Postgres, Redis, object storage, api, orchestrator, retrieval, marking) in each residency region (eu, uk, us; global maps to us at launch). The control plane (Pack authoring, evals, billing ledger) is single-region with no pupil PII. Acceptance: a tenant with residency=eu produces zero rows in non-EU Postgres and zero provider calls to non-EU endpoints in the audit log for a 24-hour synthetic soak.

11-ARCH-004 — Packs are data. No board-, syllabus- or paper-specific logic in code paths; behaviour differences come from Pack rows (boards.level_procedure, command_words, ao_weights). Acceptance: grep -rE "9609|0450|9708|9709|0580" in apps/ and services/ returns only test fixtures and sample-chip strings. Why: SYNTHESIS §3.1 — a new board is a new Pack, never new code.

11-ARCH-005 — One stack for teachers, parents and Admin. The teacher console, parent digest and Compiler reuse api, retrieval and marking; they differ by role and policy object only. Acceptance: no second deployable or duplicated marking code path exists.

11.2Data model

The data model has three planes: Pack (curriculum data, global, org_id NULL), Learner (everything derived from Attempts, tenant-scoped), Tenancy/Trust (orgs, consent, ledger, audit). Every learner-plane row carries org_id, user_id, policy_version, created_at; every Pack row carries pack_id, pack_version, provenance.

11-DATA-001 — Canonical entities and key fields. Implement these tables (Pack tables per §06; only the fields the platform depends on are listed here). Enumerated values are referenced, never restated: where a column says "per X@n" the DDL enum is generated from that schema in §15.C, so the database, the API and the schema cannot drift. Acceptance: a codegen check fails if any CHECK (… IN (…)) in a migration is written by hand rather than generated from §15.C; a CI lint fails on any literal ∈ {…} list in this subsection that does not name a $defs entry.

EntityKey fieldsNotes
