11-DATA-002 — Attempt is write-once, append-corrections. attempts rows are never updated except teacher_override, mark_id, retest_due_at; corrections create new rows linked by supersedes_id. Acceptance: a DB trigger rejects any other UPDATE.

11-DATA-003 — Row-level security. Enable RLS on every learner-plane table with policies org_id = current_setting('app.org_id') and role-scoped views: students read their own rows; teachers read attempts (fields: item, rung_reached, mark, gate_state, timestamps — never response text unless the assignment is receipt_required or the student shared) for their class only; parents read only the materialised parent_digest view. Pack tables are org_id NULL, read-only to tenants. Acceptance: the RLS test suite (≥200 cases across roles) passes in CI; a teacher token cannot SELECT response FROM attempts for a student outside their class (query returns zero rows, not an error).

11-DATA-004 — Vector partitioning. chunks is partitioned by partition_key = coalesce(org_id::text, 'global'); per-tenant USER uploads live in the tenant partition; a retrieval query names its partitions explicitly. Acceptance: the injection/isolation suite (§12.10) shows 0 cross-tenant chunk returns over 10,000 randomised queries.

11-DATA-005 — Versioning. pack_version (stored as common@1.version_tag, e.g. 9609:2026-2028@2026.11.2) and policy_version (the dated semver label of 08-EVG-001, e.g. 2026.09.2) are pinned on courses, sessions, attempts and marks; a Pack revision creates a new version and a migration note shown in the Course, rendered from pack_version_display ("Pack updated to 2026–28 v3 — 2 syllabus points renumbered"); it never mutates history. Per-paper marker identity is not a policy_version: it lives in marks.scheme_version and marks.marker_instructions_version. Acceptance: re-running a Mark from a year-old Attempt with its pinned versions reproduces the same contract fields except calibration_status; a policy_version value that fails ^\d{4}\.\d{2}\.\d+(-rc\d+)?$ is rejected at write.

11-DATA-008 — Pack version change inside a live Course. A Course pinned to pack_version P1 is offered P2, never moved to it silently. On acceptance: (a) syllabus nodes are remapped through Pack@2.node_aliases ({from_node_id, to_node_id, relation ∈ {same, split, merged, removed}}), which every Pack build must emit for every renumbered node; (b) learner_state rows follow their alias, split duplicates the mastery value to both children with a provisional_split flag, removed archives the row; (c) existing Marks and Receipts are never re-marked or re-signed — they keep their pinned pack_version and render with the note "Marked against 2026–28 v2"; (d) a Course whose paper structure changed between versions shows the diff before acceptance. Acceptance: the version-bump fixture moves a Course from P1 to P2 with two renumbered and one split node, leaves every prior Mark byte-identical, and leaves zero learner_state rows pointing at a node id absent from P2.

11-DATA-006 — Learner state is a projection. learner_state, mastery pips, readiness rings, Progress and the parent digest are computed only from attempts, cards reviews and marks; no surface reads chat text to infer mastery. Acceptance: deleting all turns for a user leaves every Progress number unchanged; a 30-Turn Ask Session (course_id IS NULL, §10.26) produces zero rows in attempts, cards, learner_state, memories and marks, and leaves every Progress and Plan number unchanged.

11-DATA-007 — Retention fields are first-class. Every table with pupil data has retention_until derived from the tenant policy object; a nightly job hard-deletes expired rows and writes a count to audit_log. Acceptance: the deletion-SLA test (11.13) passes.

11.3API surface

The API is REST + SSE, versioned under /v1, JSON everywhere, typed with a shared OpenAPI document generated from Zod schemas; the mobile and web clients consume the same generated client.

11-API-001 — Endpoint sketch. Implement at minimum:

11-API-002 — Idempotency. Every mutating endpoint accepts Idempotency-Key (UUID, 24 h window, keyed by user); replays return the original response with Idempotent-Replayed: true. Turn creation additionally dedupes on client_msg_id per session so a retried Send never creates two Turns or double-bills a Mark. Acceptance: a chaos test that retries every mutating call 3× under injected 502s produces exactly one row per logical action and one quota decrement.

11-API-003 — Streaming parts. SSE events are typed message parts: text, thinking_summary, status, citation, math, diagram, tool_call, tool_result, mark_header, ao_card, command_word_check, advice, calibration, sources, provenance, card_suggestion, gate_prompt, intent_row, error, done. Each carries seq, part_id, and for text delta. Clients render by part type; unknown types are ignored, never fatal. Acceptance: schema-validated in CI against the shared Zod definitions; a client built against v1 renders a v1.1 stream with new part types without error.

11-API-004 — Errors are cards, not modals. Errors return RFC 9457 problem details with a user_message suitable to render inline and an retryable flag. Never expose provider error text to the client. Acceptance: error snapshot test covers 429, 503, quota, policy-blocked, scheme-missing.

11-API-005 — Rate limits by route class. Enforce in api before any provider call: anonymous landing Mark 3/day/IP-hash and 1 concurrent; authenticated Turn 60/min burst 10; Mark per plan quota (11.10); upload 30/hour; export 2/day. Return Retry-After. Acceptance: k6 suite confirms limits and that a limited Turn returns a soft slow-down message, never a hard mid-session stop (SYNTHESIS §12 free-tier rules).

11-API-006 — Policy object on every request. api resolves the §08.8 policy object — {residency, allowed_providers, retention_days, age_band, consent_mode, training_opt_in=false, school_safe, logging_level, pii_redaction, sandbox_class, quotas} — from tenant + user and attaches it to the internal request context; orchestrator, retrieval and storage refuse a request without one. Where a user belongs to two tenants (family + school) the stricter value per field wins. Acceptance: unit tests for the merge; a request without policy fails closed with a logged 500, not a permissive default.

11.4Retrieval (RAG) pipeline

Retrieval exists to put the right syllabus line, scheme point, examiner sentence or textbook paragraph in front of the model and the student, with a page-and-span address. Ingestion mechanics and the compiler stages are §06; this subsection fixes the retrieval-side contract.

11-RAG-001 — Chunk by structure, never by fixed window alone. Segment by document type before chunking: textbook chapter → section → subsection → paragraph | figure | table | worked_example; question paper paper → section → question → part → marks; mark scheme question part → marking point | level band → guidance; examiner report question → commentary sentence group; syllabus unit → topic → learning objective. Then apply HybridChunker at 256–512 tokens aligned to the embedding tokenizer, keeping tables, marking points and level grids whole and carrying heading_path. Acceptance: 0 chunks split a marking point, table row or level descriptor (structural lint on ingest).

11-RAG-002 — Required metadata per chunk. doc_id, doc_type, board, syllabus_code, syllabus_version_years[], subject, level, paper, variant, series, question_id, marks, command_word, ao[], topic_path[], page_start, page_end, bbox[], figure_ids[], language, trust_rank, provenance, licence_id, source_hash, ingest_version, parse_confidence, partition_key. Ingest rejects a chunk missing any non-nullable field. Why: a 2021 scheme line can be wrong for the 2026–28 syllabus; filters must run before similarity.

11-RAG-003 — Query pipeline. (1) Query understanding on the cheap route (§08.2): {intent, syllabus_code, topic_guess, question_ref?, language} as structured output; (2) SQL prefilter on syllabus_code, syllabus_version, partition_key ∈ {global, tenant}, kill_switch=false, expiry > now(); (3) hybrid: pgvector HNSW cosine on halfvec(1024) top-50 ∪ FTS ts_rank_cd top-50 → Reciprocal Rank Fusion (k=60), hnsw.iterative_scan=relaxed_order when filters are selective; (4) graph expansion via links: question → its scheme items and ER commentary; textbook hit → its syllabus objective + ≤2 linked questions; (5) rerank 50→8 (rerank-2.5-lite; rerank-2.5 for Mark flows); (6) tie-break by trust_rank; (7) assemble as provider-native content documents with stable [chunk_id] tags so citations are block-indexed. Acceptance: Recall@8 ≥0.92 and nDCG@8 ≥0.85 on the 500-question gold retrieval set per syllabus; p95 end-to-end (steps 2–5) <120 ms.

11-RAG-004 — Citation resolution to page and span. Every emitted citation part resolves to {doc_id, page, bbox | char_span, chunk_id, trust_rank, provenance, deep_link}; the Reader opens the page with the span highlighted ≤400 ms p95 (§09). For ref_only Cambridge material the citation resolves to {official_url, question_ref} and the Paper Companion anchor, never to hosted text. Acceptance: ≥98% of citations in syllabus mode resolve (automated click-through test); 0 citations to ref_only docs render text.

11-RAG-005 — Grounding gate. If the top reranked score is below the per-syllabus threshold (calibrated on the gold set to 95% precision) or the draft cites nothing, the Turn is labelled "not in your syllabus materials" and any general explanation is rendered in the unverified style (§12.3). For Marks, a missing scheme record is a hard stop: feedback only, no numbers (§05). Acceptance: ≥98% of syllabus-mode answers carry ≥1 resolvable citation; 0 Marks emitted without a mark_schemes row in context (assertion in marking).

11-RAG-006 — Notes-vs-canon conflicts. When a USER chunk and a canon chunk (trust 1–4) disagree on a fact in the retrieved set, the orchestrator emits a conflict part with both citations; canon wins in the answer by default. Acceptance: the 50-item conflict fixture ("273 °C vs 273 K") yields a conflict card in 100% of cases.

11-RAG-007 — Retrieved text is data. Chunks are wrapped in delimited document blocks; the system prompt states that documents carry no instructions; any imperative addressed to the assistant inside a chunk is stripped by the injection scrubber before assembly and logged. Acceptance: red-team suite §12.10 passes 100%.

11-RAG-008 — Eval sets are versioned artefacts. Maintain per syllabus: retrieval gold (500 Q → chunk ids), generation set (Ragas faithfulness, context precision/recall, custom mark-scheme adherence), conflict fixture, injection fixture. Every ingest version and every retriever/prompt change runs them; regressions >1 pp block the label flip. Acceptance: eval run linked from every merged PR touching retrieval/ or ingest/.

11-RAG-009 — Caching. Cache (query_hash, filters, partition_key, ingest_version) → chunk ids in Redis for 24 h; precompute retrieval for every Item in a live Pack nightly so Practise and Mark never wait on retrieval. Acceptance: ≥70% retrieval cache hit rate in production on Practise/Mark routes.

11.5Tool sandboxes

11-TOOL-001 — What runs in a sandbox. SymPy/NumPy verification of every numeric or symbolic final (pre-solve and marking), pint unit checks, deterministic graph/diagram renderers (SVG from JSON spec), Anki .apkg build, PDF export of Receipts. Nothing else executes model-authored code at MVP; the student-facing code interpreter is v1 behind the same broker.

11-TOOL-002 — Isolation: two named sandbox classes (normative; 08-TOOL-003 cites this table and states no numbers of its own). The class is a property of the route, because the two differ in where execution happens and therefore in their data-residency and sub-processor consequences.

ClassWhere it runsLimitsUsed byResidency / sub-processor consequence
sbx_local (default)Self-hosted E2B, Firecracker microVM in the tenant's residency region512 MB RAM, 1 vCPU, 20 s wall clock (60 s for .apkg builds), 50 MB ephemeral disk, fresh VM per tenant-executionMarking pre-solve, unit checks, diagram/graph renderers, Receipt PDF, all eu/uk tenantsExecutes inside our data plane; no sub-processor entry needed beyond the cloud provider
sbx_providerAnthropic code-execution tool, provider-side≤90 s per cell, ≤5 GiB, ephemeral filesystem, container reuse only within one SessionLong-running symbolic work on Claude routes for us/global tenants onlyProvider-side execution: the student's numeric answer leaves our plane, so Anthropic appears in /legal/subprocessors for "code execution" (11-PRIV-007) and the class is refused when residency ∈ {eu, uk} or zdr_required=true

Both classes: no network egress (deny-all policy verified by a probe on boot), read-only base image with an SBOM, no secrets mounted, no access to Postgres or object storage — inputs and outputs pass through the broker as JSON. The broker rejects a call whose route declares a class the tenant policy forbids, and never silently substitutes one class for the other. Acceptance: a canary job that attempts DNS, TCP to 1.1.1.1, filesystem escape and env-var reads fails on all four every hour in both classes; failures page. A residency test asserts zero sbx_provider executions for eu/uk tenants over a 24-hour soak, and CI fails if /legal/subprocessors omits the provider-side execution entry while any route declares sbx_provider.

11-TOOL-003 — Verification contract. The orchestrator marks a numeric final verified=true only when the sandbox result matches to the tolerance in the Item (abs_tol, rel_tol, sig_figs); a mismatch renders both values with "check this" and never a confident single answer. Acceptance: 0 unverified numeric finals on STEM routes (assertion in the Turn lint).

11-TOOL-004 — Client-side Pyodide. Load Pyodide lazily (never in the chat route's initial bundle) for instant answer checking in Practise and offline Card maths; results are advisory and re-verified server-side before they touch an Attempt. Acceptance: Pyodide absent from the initial JS payload (bundle analysis in CI).

11-TOOL-005 — Per-route tool allow-lists. Each route in the route table declares its tools; a tutoring Turn may call retrieve, verify_math, render_diagram, suggest_card; it cannot call delete_card, update_plan, send_notification, issue_receipt. Tool calls outside the allow-list are dropped and logged as security events. Acceptance: unit test per route; injection suite confirms no privilege escalation via document content.

11.6Realtime streaming

11-RT-001 — Transport. SSE over HTTP/2 from api (which proxies orchestrator); WebSocket only for the v1 voice pilot broker. Each assistant Turn has a stream_id; orchestrator writes parts to a Redis stream every ≤250 ms or every part boundary; api fans out. Buffers live 15 minutes after done.

11-RT-002 — Resumability. A client reconnecting with from=offset receives every part it missed, in order, exactly once; a Turn whose stream died server-side is finished by a worker, not restarted. Acceptance: the network-flap test (kill the connection at 10 random offsets per Turn, 200 Turns) loses zero parts and duplicates none.

11-RT-003 — Streaming contract to the UI. Optimistic user message <50 ms; status part at 800 ms if no text yet ("Reading the 9609 P2 mark scheme…"); "Taking longer than usual" + Stop at 6 s; Stop aborts the provider call within 300 ms and bills only consumed tokens; paint ≤90 characters per 16 ms frame; previous DOM immutable; unclosed math/code held as a skeleton until the part closes; CLS above the cursor = 0. Acceptance: Playwright trace on golden conversations measures each budget; CLS assertion in CI (11.16).

11-RT-004 — Mark streaming order. mark_header first, then ao_card parts in AO order, each within 8 s of the previous, command_word_check, advice, calibration, sources, provenance, done; the credited spans in a card are emitted with the card so highlights light up as it lands. Acceptance: synthetic 20-mark Mark shows first ao_card <8 s p95 and done <45 s p95 in the staging soak.

11-RT-005 — Backpressure and failover. Quotas and policy checks run before the provider call; provider 429/503/529 or TTFT >4 s triggers the failover path from the route table with x-failover=1 in telemetry; the client sees the same stream id. Acceptance: chaos test with a blackholed primary provider completes ≥99% of Turns via fallback with no client-visible error.

11.7Offline, PWA and sync

11-OFF-001 — What works offline. Cards review (due queue, two-button grading, interval hints), the Today list as last fetched, downloaded Course notes and syllabus tree with pips, the Reader for OWN/LICENSED-offline-permitted documents already opened, Receipt viewing, the Plan. Nothing that needs a model call pretends to work: Learn, Practise marking and Mark show the offline banner and queue nothing except Card reviews and draft text. Two things are never written to an offline bundle whatever the student asks: a live machine-scored item and its parameters (05-IRT-010, because an offline copy is an exposed bank) and a mark scheme in any form. Acceptance: airplane-mode E2E test on web (service worker + IndexedDB) and Expo (SQLite) completes 20 Card reviews and shows a correct due count after reconnect; a bundle-content assertion finds zero rows whose item_id is in the live IRT bank and zero mark_schemes payloads.

11-OFF-002 — Sync model. Client-generated UUIDs; an outbox of card_review, draft_response, plan_accept events with monotonic client_seq; server applies idempotently (11-API-002) and returns the authoritative FSRS state; conflicts resolve by "server FSRS state wins, client reviews are replayed in order". Acceptance: two devices reviewing the same deck offline then syncing produce a deterministic state equal to the ordered replay.

11-OFF-003 — Offline storage limits and privacy. Cache ≤200 MB per Course on mobile; encrypted at rest with the OS keystore; cleared on logout and on tenant policy retention_days expiry; no transcripts cached for under-18 school tenants beyond the current Session. Acceptance: logout leaves no readable Course data in app storage (forensic check in the release checklist).

11-OFF-004 — PWA. Installable on Chromebook/desktop; app shell cached; background sync for the outbox; offline banner is a system state (§10.24), never a modal.

11.8Multi-tenancy and the consent graph

11-TEN-001 — Tenant types and membership. individual (one consumer), family (parent-owned, ≤3 students on the Family plan), school (admin, teachers, classes, students), tutor_centre (school-like, 1:20–50 seats). A user may belong to several tenants; the stricter policy object per field applies (11-API-006).

11-TEN-002 — Visibility matrix (FINAL).

DataStudentTeacher (own class)Parent (linked)School adminMargin staff
Turn transcriptsOwn, fullNever (aggregate hint depth only)NeverNeverOnly with a logged support ticket the student opened, or a safety escalation
Attempts (item, rung, gate, mark, timestamps)OwnYesAggregates onlyAggregatesEvals in pseudonymised form
Answer text on AttemptsOwnOnly for assignments marked receipt_required or student-sharedNeverNeverCalibration with consent
Marks and overridesOwn (when visible)Yes, plus overrideTrend onlyAggregatesYes (pseudonymised)
Predicted gradeOwn (Progress › Paper)Gated papers onlyOnly if student enablesNoNo
MemoriesOwn, editableNeverNeverNeverNever
ReceiptOwn; shares by linkWhen sharedWhen sharedNoNo

Acceptance: the RLS suite encodes this matrix cell by cell.

11-TEN-003 — Consent graph for under-18s. Model consent as edges, not flags: guardian_links (parent → student, with consent_evidence), school_consents (school → student cohort, with the DPA and the FERPA/COPPA school-official basis), each with scope (what processing it authorises: study_data, digest, predicted_grade_share, voice, research_pseudonymised) and expires_at. A processing action checks the union of valid edges for the required scope; missing scope fails closed. Age band 16_17 and 18plus consumers self-consent under GDPR where the member-state age allows; 13_15 requires a school edge at launch [E4: 16+ consumer at launch; 13+ consumer opens after the external consent audit, target month 9]; u13 is never onboarded. Acceptance: consent coverage report shows 100% of 13_15 and 16_17 (where required by member state) accounts with a valid edge; an account whose last edge expires is frozen (read-only, export available) within 24 h.

11-TEN-004 — Parent controls change nothing the student owns. Parents set Study Hours, Quiet Hours, digest cadence and payment; they cannot read transcripts, edit memories, or unlock predicted grades. Controls may be adjusted by asking the assistant in the parent surface with an explicit Allow/Deny confirmation. Auto-removal of guardian scope on the student's 18th birthday (age band change), with notice to both.

11.9Authentication, age assurance and school SSO

11-AUTH-001 — Methods and session revocation. Passkeys first; magic link; Google, Microsoft, Apple sign-in; class code + school SSO. No passwords stored for new accounts; sessions are httpOnly, SameSite=Lax, 30-day sliding. Every session row carries {device_label, last_seen_at, ip_hash, created_at} and Settings › Account (§10.19) renders the list with a per-device Revoke and a Sign out everywhere; changing the account email re-verifies by magic link and revokes every other session. Revocation is server-side — the API rejects the token, it is not merely dropped by the client. Acceptance: a revoked device's next authenticated request returns 401 within 60 s, its outbox flush is rejected with a session_revoked problem detail rather than silently discarded, and the local cache is cleared per 11-OFF-003; "Sign out everywhere" leaves exactly one live session (the one that issued the command) and writes an audit_log row.

11-AUTH-002 — Age assurance path. At "Save this Course": (1) self-declared age band (never full DOB retained after assurance); (2) signal checks: school-tenant membership, SSO directory attribute, payment-holder age for family plans, and an age-estimation classifier on usage signals in the style of the labs' age prediction (PROVISIONAL: vendor or in-house, decided by the DPIA); (3) for 13_15 and 16_17 where consent is required, the guardian or school edge (11-TEN-003). Uncertain bands default to the more protective band. Store {method, confidence, checked_at} only. Acceptance: a declared 19-year-old exhibiting strong under-16 signals is moved to teen defaults and asked to verify; DPIA documents the false-positive/negative trade-off.

11-AUTH-003 — School SSO in v1. SAML 2.0 and OIDC (Google Workspace for Education, Microsoft Entra), roster via Wonde and Clever/ClassLink connectors; MVP ships class codes only. Just-in-time provisioning maps directory roles to teacher/student; an SSO-provisioned under-16 inherits the school consent edge. Acceptance: a pilot school onboards in <1 day with no manual account creation.

11-AUTH-004 — Anonymous first Mark. The landing Mark runs under a device-bound anonymous principal (signed cookie, 24 h) with the strictest policy object (residency by geo-IP, age_band=unknown → teen defaults, no memory writes, transient upload). Converting to an account migrates the Mark and Attempt.

11.10Billing, quotas and the meter

11-BILL-001 — SKUs (PROVISIONAL on [E9]; §14.6 owns the price numbers and the margin model, this row owns their entitlement mechanics). Student Monthly $8; Student "Until exams" $59 (entitlement expires_at = last_paper_date + 7 days, max 10 months, computed from the Course's exam dates); Parent/Family $19/month (≤3 students); School seat $10/student/year, ceiling $12 (invoice, not card; the seat's margin is an open [E9] decision recorded at 14-ECON-006, not a §11 question); Tutor per seat; regional tiers −40% (KZ, IN, PK, NG, EG, TR) by billing country with Stripe Tax and local PSPs. Teacher role is free forever and needs no card.

11-BILL-002 — Entitlement service. Entitlements are derived server-side from subscriptions + grants (school seats, trials, grace) and cached in Redis; PSP webhooks only update subscriptions. Feature checks call entitled(user, capability); the client never decides. Acceptance: revoking a subscription propagates to the meter in <5 s; a replayed webhook is a no-op.

11-BILL-003 — Meter and the shape of the free tier (FINAL from SYNTHESIS §12; every number is in 11-COST-001). The meter counts per user per session / day / week / month and exposes each counter on /v1/usage and the Settings meter as a plain number with its reset time, its state ∈ {ok, slow, grace, capped} and the published limit. The rules that are FINAL, independent of any number: cheap-tier explanations are never hard-stopped, only slowed; the active-learning core (Effort Gate, Help Ladder, Cards, probes, Plan) is never metered (03-LIM-005); levels Marks are the metered scarce good and points Marks are not; a Session already in progress never ends because of a limit; slow-down means a longer queue and a cheaper route with a banner naming the change, never a refusal. Acceptance: zero silent limit changes — a change to any published limit requires a versioned config/limits.yaml bump and a /changes entry (12-TRAN-004) before it takes effect; the meter and the server counters agree within one Turn (10-SETT-004).

11-BILL-004 — Until-exams SKU mechanics. Purchase requires ≥1 Course with an exam date; expiry recomputes if the student edits dates (max 10 months from purchase); renewal offers the next series only after results day.

11.11Observability, tracing and evals infrastructure

11-OBS-001 — Traces. Every request carries a W3C traceparent; every model call is a Langfuse span with the per-call fields defined in §08.12 (policy_version, route, model, effort, cache_read_tokens, cache_write_tokens, ttft_ms, total_ms, cost_usd, failover, rung, lint_result, gate_state, intent, calibration_status) plus platform fields tenant_id, residency, age_band, experiment_arms[], stream_id, ingest_version. Prompts are referenced by (name, version) and never copied into logs. PII: user ids are pseudonymous; message text is stored in traces only where the policy object allows. The field is logging_level ∈ {none, redacted, full} — the single name, owned by 08-POL-005; trace_content is not a field and must not appear in code, config or copy. School tenants default to redacted, but 08-POL-005 pins every band other than 18plus to none, and the merge lattice (11-API-006) takes the most protective value, so a 14-year-old in a school tenant resolves to none. State the consequence rather than working around it: production traces for teen accounts carry metadata only, so gold scripts and eval replay for teen tenants come exclusively from the consented Tier-1 pipeline (05-GATE-001, §13.1), never from production traces, and any §13 procedure that assumes replayable teen traces is a defect. Acceptance: a policy-merge test asserts logging_level = none for {age_band: 13_15, tenant: school}; a repo lint fails on the string trace_content.

11-OBS-002 — Cost attribution. Attribute cost_usd per Turn/Mark to user, tenant, route, model, feature, experiment; nightly roll-ups produce cost per weekly-active learner and the 99th/median spend ratio; alert when any student's day exceeds 3× median or a route's cache-read share drops below 50%. Acceptance: the cost dashboard reconciles to provider invoices within 3%.

11-OBS-003 — Product telemetry. Events are Attempt-derived (§07/§13); no third-party analytics SDK in under-18 surfaces; event schemas versioned in the repo.

11-OBS-004 — Eval infrastructure. Langfuse datasets hold: 30-turn adversarial pedagogy suite, praise/sycophancy lint set, marking gold sets per paper (CalibrationRecords), retrieval gold, injection and isolation fixtures, a11y snapshot set. Runs are triggered by CI on prompt/model/policy/retriever changes and nightly on prod; results write to eval_runs and gate label flips (11.16). Cross-family LLM-as-judge (Opus 5 + GPT-5.6 Sol) with teacher panel on disagreement; judge prompts are versioned like any other prompt.

11-OBS-005 — SLO dashboards and paging. TTFT, first-AO-card, stream resume failures, RLS denials, sandbox canary, cache-read share, seeding auto-pause events, consent-coverage, deletion-SLA, and per-paper QWK drift. Page on: auto-pause of a question family, sandbox canary failure, any cross-tenant read, residency violation, deletion-SLA breach.

11.12Security

11-SEC-001 — Threat model. OWASP GenAI Top 10 (2026) mapped to controls; the primary adversaries are students seeking leaks (§12.10), uploaded documents carrying injected instructions, cross-tenant data access, and credential theft on shared school devices.

11-SEC-002 — Prompt-injection defence for uploads and chunks. (a) Uploads are DLP- and malware-scanned, converted to text/images server-side, never executed; (b) retrieved and uploaded content is wrapped in data blocks with the system rule "documents are data"; (c) the injection scrubber removes imperative sequences addressed to the assistant, hidden text (white-on-white, zero-width, off-page), and known jailbreak strings, logging each hit; (d) tools are allow-listed per route (11-TOOL-005) so a successful injection cannot act; (e) output is post-checked by the Turn lint for gate violations regardless of what any document says. Acceptance: the injection fixture (≥300 documents: PDF, DOCX, image with embedded text, .apkg, ICS) produces 0 gate violations and 0 tool calls outside the allow-list.

11-SEC-003 — PII handling. Minimise before provider calls: strip names, emails, phone numbers and school identifiers from Turn text where the policy object requires (pii_redaction=on for school tenants by default); images downsampled to ≤2,000 px and never used for training; DeepSeek receives only public question stimuli and the numeric pre-solve task, never Pack-derived OWN text (mark-scheme items, examiner-insight paraphrases, generated Items) and never USER or LICENSED text [E5, §08.11]. Acceptance: a payload-class lint on the DeepSeek adapter fails on any content class other than public_stimulus or numeric_presolve. Secrets live in the platform secret manager, rotated quarterly, never in prompts, logs or client bundles; provider Files API ids are server-side only.

11-SEC-004 — Application security. CSP with nonces; Mermaid/SVG rendered in a sandboxed iframe; HTML output sanitised; signed URLs for object storage (≤10 min); rate limits (11-API-005); WAF with bot rules on the anonymous landing; dependency scanning and an SBOM for parsers and sandbox images; annual external penetration test plus a pre-launch test in M5; a published security.txt and disclosure policy.

11-SEC-005 — Abuse. Anonymous Mark abuse (scripted farms) is bounded by device-bound principals, IP-hash limits and a proof-of-work challenge above threshold; account sharing is detected by concurrent-device heuristics and answered with a soft prompt, never a lockout in exam week.

11-SEC-006 — Secure defaults on shared devices. School tenants: session expiry 12 h idle, "not my account" switch on the sidebar, no persistent transcripts on device (11-OFF-003).

11.13Privacy and compliance

Compliance is enforced by the policy object (11-API-006) and the consent graph (11-TEN-003), not by policy documents. Every row below names the code path that makes it true. Legal facts marked counsel are re-verified by counsel in M1 (SYNTHESIS §9); the build does not wait for that verification because every control works under the adverse reading.

11-PRIV-002 — Residency via regional endpoints. residency ∈ {eu, uk, us, global} on the tenant selects the data plane (11-ARCH-003) and the provider endpoint map in config:

A null endpoint means the route falls to the next fallback in the route table (§08.2), never to a non-regional host. 11-PRIV-003 — Data minimisation before providers. Apply 11-SEC-003 redaction when pii_redaction=on; never send users.email, guardian_links, or age_assurance fields to any provider; images ≤2,000 px; the Turn payload contains the pseudonymous user_id hash only in metadata fields the provider does not train on. Acceptance: a provider-payload lint in CI fails on any field name from the pii_fields list.

11-PRIV-011 — Margin is the provider, not only a deployer. Build every control on the assumption that Margin places a high-risk AI system on the EU market and that schools are its deployers. Three consequences the deployer framing hides: (a) the obligations in 11-PRIV-005 rows 11–14 are ours, not the school's; (b) Article 73 serious-incident reporting applies — an S0/S1 safety incident (§12.8) or a Mark that entered a school-recorded grade in error is assessed against Art. 73 within 24 h of T0 and reported to the market-surveillance authority within 15 days (2 days where the infringement is widespread), a clock that runs beside, not inside, the 72-hour GDPR clock of 11-PRIV-009 and lives in the same runbook (runbooks/safety-incident.md); (c) public-body school deployers owe a fundamental-rights impact assessment, and we supply its inputs (11-PRIV-012). Acceptance: the incident runbook contains both clocks with their trigger definitions; a tabletop exercise each quarter starts one incident that trips both and records the two notification timestamps.

11-PRIV-012 — FRIA support pack for public-body deployers. Generate compliance/fria-pack.pdf from the technical file on each release: intended purpose, the categories of person affected, the risk table (11-RISK-001 rows 1, 6, 11), the human-oversight design (teacher confirmation before any Mark enters a recorded grade), the accuracy and fairness evidence (per-paper calibration page and fairness buckets), the logging and retention design, and the complaints route. Acceptance: the pack is an artefact of the release job, is dated, and is offered in the school proposal pack; a release whose pack is older than the technical file fails pnpm compliance:build.

11-PRIV-013 — One retention source. Every retention value in the product and in this document renders from config/retention.yaml; 11-PRIV-004 is the platform ceiling table and §07.8 is the learner-visible default table, both generated from that file, and no other section states a retention number in prose. Acceptance: a docs lint fails on a duration next to the word "retain"/"retention" outside 11-PRIV-004, §07.8 and /your-data; a value in §07.8 that exceeds its 11-PRIV-004 ceiling fails CI.

11-PRIV-006 — DPA template terms (school and tutor tenants). Ship a signable DPA at /legal/dpa with fixed terms: Margin as processor; processing purposes limited to the tenant's educational use; sub-processors per 11-PRIV-007 with 30-day notice of changes and a right to object; residency per tenant choice; no training on pupil data (constant); retention per 11-PRIV-004 with the tenant's shorter values; deletion within 30 days of contract end with certificate; breach notice per 11-PRIV-009; audit right once per year plus on incident; SCCs / UK IDTA for any transfer; FERPA school-official and COPPA school-consent clauses for US tenants; security measures annex referencing 11.12. Tenants may attach the SDPC NDPA; conflicts resolve in the tenant's favour on protection, never on scope. Acceptance: tenants.dpa_signed_at must be set before any student joins a school tenant (API refuses POST /v1/classes/{code}/join otherwise).

11-PRIV-007 — Sub-processor list policy. Publish /legal/subprocessors generated from config/subprocessors.yaml: provider, purpose, region, data categories, ZDR status, DPA reference. The list covers every party that processes pupil work, not only chat model vendors — the model providers, the handwriting OCR vendor (Mathpix processes a photograph of a pupil's answer), the provider-side code-execution sandbox (sbx_provider, 11-TOOL-002, which receives a pupil's numeric answer), object storage, email delivery, push delivery, and the error tracker. Adding a provider or region requires a config PR that (a) updates the page, (b) emails tenant admins with dpa_signed_at (30-day objection window), (c) is blocked from production until the window closes unless the tenant list is empty. Acceptance: CI compares the endpoint map (11-PRIV-002), the adapter registry (§08.11), the sandbox class table (11-TOOL-002) and the upload pipeline (§06) with the published list and fails on any party missing from it; a school tenant's DPA annex renders from the same file.

11-PRIV-008 — Records of processing (RoPA). Maintain compliance/ropa.yaml: one entry per processing activity {purpose, lawful_basis, data_categories, data_subjects, recipients, transfers, retention_ref, security_ref}; the DPO reviews quarterly; a new table with pupil data requires a RoPA entry in the same PR (migration lint checks the table name against RoPA). Acceptance: migration lint blocks a learner-plane table absent from RoPA.

11-PRIV-009 — Breach notification clock. T0 = the moment any staff member or system flags a suspected personal-data breach (Sentry security event, RLS denial spike, cross-tenant read, lost device report). T0+1 h: incident channel opened and DPO paged; T0+24 h: scope assessment (tenants, data categories, record counts) written; T0+72 h: notification to the ICO / lead EU supervisory authority where required, and to affected school tenants regardless (DPA term); affected users notified without undue delay when risk is high; T0+14 d: post-mortem in the incident log (12.8). Acceptance: a tabletop exercise each quarter runs the clock end to end and records timestamps; the runbook is runbooks/breach.md.

11-PRIV-010 — Rights tooling for schools. School admins can trigger export or deletion for a student in their tenant (audit-logged, student notified); teachers cannot. A student in two tenants (family + school) has each tenant's data deleted independently; the consumer account survives a school deletion. Acceptance: RLS suite cases admin_export_own_tenant_ok, admin_export_other_tenant_denied, teacher_delete_denied.

11.14Performance budgets

This subsection is the single source of every latency, Core Web Vitals, bundle and cache budget in the product. §13.6 owns what a breach does to a release (13-PERF-001…014, 13-PERF-020…024) and §09.16 owns the design checklist; both cite rows here by id and state no numbers of their own. Where an earlier draft of §09 or §13 carried a standalone LCP/INP/CLS figure, this table supersedes it. A budget breached in CI blocks the merge; a budget breached in production for 15 minutes pages the owning service (11-OBS-005).

11-PERF-000 — Lab and field are different numbers for the same budget. Every budget below is stated as the field (production RUM, p75 over 28 days) value. The lab budget enforced by Lighthouse CI is the field value × 0.9 (10% tighter), computed by the harness, never hand-written into a second table — lab conditions are deterministic and a lab pass at the field number leaves no headroom for real networks. Acceptance: the CI job derives its thresholds from this table at run time; a hard-coded threshold in a workflow file fails the config lint.

11-PERF-005 — Cold start and server rendering. api container cold start ≤1.5 s to first healthy response; orchestrator ≤2 s including prompt registry load; serverless route handlers (if used for web) p95 cold start ≤400 ms with a minimum of 2 warm instances per region during 06:00–24:00 local in exam season; RSC HTML for Home/Course p95 ≤600 ms server time. 11-PERF-006 — Mobile app budgets (Expo). 11-PERF-007 — Offline cache size and freshness (with 11-OFF-003). Sync outbox flushes ≤10 s after reconnect; Today refreshes within 30 s of foreground. Measured: the airplane-mode E2E in 11-OFF-001 asserts sizes with navigator.storage.estimate() and the Expo SQLite file size. Acceptance: a Course that exceeds the ceiling evicts Reader documents first, never Cards or the outbox.

11-PERF-008 — Streaming render budget. ≤90 characters per 16 ms frame; long-task (>50 ms) count during a streaming Turn ≤2; main-thread blocked time during a Mark stream ≤300 ms total; KaTeX render of a held math block ≤30 ms per block. Measured: Playwright trace on 10 golden conversations per PR touching web/ streaming components; production Long Animation Frames API sampled. Acceptance: 11-RT-003 plus this row.

11-PERF-009 — Database budgets. Attempt write path (insert + learner_state projection + Card creation) p95 ≤80 ms; nightly FSRS optimiser ≤30 min for 100k users; Today precompute for all active Courses finished before 05:00 local per region (11-ARCH-001); pgvector index build for a 10M-chunk partition ≤4 h off-peak. Measured: pg_stat_statements top-20 dashboard; job durations in Inngest. Acceptance: alarm on any job overrunning 150% of its budget.

11-PERF-011 — No second budget table. §09.16, §10 screen specs and §13.6 cite rows in 11-PERF-001…009 by id; none of them restates a millisecond, a kilobyte or a CLS figure. Acceptance: a docs lint fails on an LCP/INP/CLS/TTFT/KB figure outside §11.14, and the release-gate job reads its thresholds from this section's generated JSON.

11-PERF-010 — Perf regressions are release blockers, not tickets. Any budget in 11-PERF-001…009 exceeded on staging for 24 h holds the release (13-GATE-002); in production, a budget breached for two consecutive weekly reviews opens a P2 with an owner and a due date inside 14 days. Acceptance: the weekly perf review note lists each budget with current p50/p95/p75, delta vs last week, and owner.

11.15Cost controls

Cost is controlled at four levels: the route table (§08.2, §08.10) fixes the price of one call; quotas (11-COST-001) fix how many calls a user may make; this subsection fixes the alarms, budgets, caches and downgrade rules between the two; and the monthly review changes the config. The files this subsection reads are config/limits.yaml (quotas), config/pricing.yaml (per-model prices and dated hazards), config/cost.yaml (alarms and kill switches, §08.10), config/personas.yaml (the shared volume assumptions §08.10 and §14.6 both compute from) and config/routing.yaml; every filename in the document resolves to the manifest in §00.5, and no second name for the same file exists. The envelope to defend, taken from the owning sections and never restated with rounder numbers: blended chat Turn ≈$0.0095 (§08.10); median paying student $2.93/month annualised and $4.28 in season; p95 paying student $14.60/month annualised; school seat $7.01/pupil/year US, $7.71 EU/UK; free tier ≤$1.20/MAU on a 60-day rolling fleet mean, above which §14.6 forces a published limit change or an accepted higher envelope (§14.6, [E8]). Where 14-MET-036 still states the older SYNTHESIS §12 band ($1.6–2.6 median, $8–13 heavy, free ≤$1.00 in season), §14.6's recomputed figures are the ones every alarm in this subsection is set from; re-basing that guard-rail row is §14's to do.

The machine copy is config/limits.yaml (versioned; the same file 03-LIM-001 and 10-SETT-004 render from, and the file the §08.8 policy-object example is generated from); §03.3 and §08.8 render their numbers from it and state none of their own. Free-tier shape is FINAL from SYNTHESIS §12 (11-BILL-003); the individual numbers are [E8].

Ask Turns (§10.26) are metered as ordinary tutoring Turns — cheap_turns at Quick/Think effort, deep_turns at effort=high — and have no counter of their own; Ask creates no Attempt and therefore never consumes levels_marks or points_marks. The public paper finder (§10.27) is unmetered because it makes no model call.

Acceptance: GET /v1/usage returns every counter with {used, limit, window_resets_at, state ∈ {ok, slow, grace, capped}}; a limit change without a config/limits.yaml version bump and a /changes entry fails CI (zero silent limit changes, 11-BILL-003); a quota number appearing in any other section's prose fails the docs lint.

11-COST-001a — Exam-week grace, stated exactly. Grace runs from T−14 to the last paper of the student's Course, computed from the Course exam dates, and changes two numbers only: free levels_marks 3 → 6/day, paid levels_marks 40 → 60 for the grace month. Nothing else changes, no other counter is lifted, and the product never says "limits are off" — the banner names the number and the date: "Exam week: 6 examiner Marks a day until {last_paper_date}" (free) / "Exam week: 60 examiner Marks this month until {last_paper_date}" (paid). Acceptance: the grace fixture asserts both counters, both banner strings rendered from config/limits.yaml, and a copy lint that fails on the string "limits are off".

11-COST-002 — Per-student spend alarms. Compute spend_usd per user per day from turns.cost_usd + Mark costs. Alarms: (a) >3× the rolling 7-day median of active users in the same plan → flag spend_outlier, route the user's remaining cheap Turns at effort=low, no user-visible change; (b) >6× median → cap Opus-class routes for the rest of the day (marking continues on Sonnet-draft with the factual line), and open a review item; (c) 99th-percentile daily spend ≤6× median is the p99_to_median_ratio guard-rail (14-MET-036, 14-ECON-002) — breach for 3 consecutive days pages the cost owner. Whitelist: teacher calibration tasks and the seeding traffic (§05) are excluded from the median. Acceptance: a synthetic user replaying 200 Marks in a day triggers (a) then (b) with the right route changes visible in traces; the dashboard shows the ratio daily.

11-COST-003 — Tenant budgets are a runaway guard, not a margin control. Every school and tutor tenant has policy.budget = {monthly_usd_cap, alert_at_pct: [50, 80, 100], on_cap ∈ {slow_down, notify_only}}, on_cap=slow_down. Defaults are computed, not chosen, from the §08.10 unit-cost table × config/personas.yaml volumes; §11 owns the number and §14.6 owns the constraint it must satisfy. School and tutor tenants: seats × $0.60/month. 14-ECON-007 fixes the ceiling at tenant_budget_usd_month ≤ modelled seat cost ÷ 12, which at §08.10's $7.01/pupil/year (US) is $0.58 and at $7.71 (EU/UK) is $0.64; $0.60 is the recommended value inside both, and it authorises $7.20/seat/year against a $10 seat price. Family: students × $8/month, set at 1.05× the in-season modelled family student ($7.70/month, §14.6) so a legitimately heavy student in June is never degraded while a runaway is caught; it deliberately exceeds the $6.33/student/month the plan collects, because a tenant cap is a runaway guard and margin is managed per user by 11-COST-002 and 14-ECON-002, not here. [E8][E9] Consumer individuals have no tenant cap (per-user alarms apply). At alert_at_pct the tenant admin gets an email with the top routes; at 100% with slow_down, Opus-class routes degrade to the next rung of §08.7 for that tenant until month end — never a lockout, never during a timed paper already started. Acceptance: tenant cost roll-up by day and by class visible in the Admin console; the cap test drives a staging tenant past 100% and asserts the downgrade applies within 5 minutes and the meter shows state=slow; the finance lint fails a school-tenant budget above modelled_seat_cost ÷ 12 (14-ECON-007) or a Family budget below the in-season modelled family student, naming both figures.

Rules: the router logs cache_decision and reads_per_write per call, and the cost dashboard (11-OBS-002) plots reads_per_write per route against a break-even line at 1.1; a route below it for a week loses its cache_control. Dynamic content (student text, retrieved chunks, timestamps) comes after the cached prefix; no timestamp, random id or per-user string inside the prefix; changing effort or an image flag invalidates the provider cache, so the orchestrator holds those constant within a Session. Acceptance: CI asserts cache_read_input_tokens > 0 on every golden conversation (13-PERF-012) and a prefix-stability test hashes the prefix across 100 Turns of one Session and finds one hash.

11-COST-005 — Batch windows. All unattended work runs on Batch APIs (50% discount) in named windows, UTC: 02:00–06:00 nightly (ER mining, tagging, Card generation from yesterday's lost marks, eval nightly runs, embedding of new ingests), Sat 00:00–Sun 12:00 weekly (full re-embeds, pre-generated Item bank top-up, judge runs). Batch jobs carry priority ∈ {p0_exam_week, p1, p2}; p0 may run outside the window (e.g. seeding). DeepSeek off-peak pricing is used only for pii=false synthetic generation in the us plane [E5]. Interactive routes never wait on a batch. Acceptance: ≥90% of bulk tokens per week are billed at batch rates (cost dashboard split interactive / batch).

11-COST-006 — Model downgrade rules (the cost triggers for the §08.7 degradation ladder). §08.7 defines the rungs (primary → same-family cheaper → cross-family fallback → template); this table says when cost, not availability, moves a route down one rung, and what the student sees.

Acceptance: route-decision unit tests for every row; x-downgrade-reason recorded on the Turn; no downgrade row produces a modal.

11-COST-007 — Token discipline. max_tokens per route from config (tutoring 400; trivial 300; Mark per-AO JSON 1,200; advice 300); thinking display summarized and effort from the route table; images downsampled to ≤2,000 px; retrieved context capped at 8 chunks (11-RAG-003) and ≤6,000 tokens; conversation window trimmed to the last 12 Turns plus the SessionSummary@1 object produced by server-side compaction (§07.3, 03-PAR-039), which is what keeps context tokens per Turn ≤24k at Turn 50; web-search results excluded from echo. Token budgets are expressed per model and re-baselined with count_tokens in CI when a model changes (the 4.7+ tokeniser is ≈30% denser). Acceptance: per-route input/output token histograms; a Turn exceeding 2× the route's p95 input tokens logs context_bloat.

11-COST-008 — Dated price hazards live in config, with a re-pricing job. config/pricing.yaml holds per-model input/output/cache prices with valid_from/valid_to; a monthly job (1st, 03:00 UTC) re-reads provider price pages, diffs against config, and opens a PR; hazards already known are pre-loaded:

hazards:
  - model: gemini-3.8-flash      # and 3.7/3.6 Flash
    event: price_doubles
    effective: 2027-01-01
    action: re-rank fallback order; consider Flash-Lite for trivial route
  - model: claude-haiku-4-5
    event: retirement_possible
    effective: 2026-10-15        # earliest date; replacement model to be evaluated
    action: eval Haiku-5-class candidate against the trivial/classifier gold set before this date
  - model: deepseek-v4-*
    event: peak_offpeak_pricing
    effective: 2026-08-16
    action: batch windows only; never budget on unverified numbers
  - model: claude-sonnet-5 / claude-opus-5 / claude-fable-5-1
    event: commitment_floor
    effective: 2027-06-30 / 2027-07-24 / 2027-09-01
    action: plan successor evals one quarter before each date

Acceptance: CI fails if any route references a model whose valid_to is in the past or whose hazard effective date is <30 days away without an ack_by field naming the reviewer.

11-COST-009 — Monthly cost review. First working week of each month, 45 minutes, owners: CTO (chair), finance, content lead. Inputs (auto-generated from 11-OBS-002): cost per weekly-active learner by plan and region; median vs heavy vs 99th spend; cache-read share per route; batch share; second-family marking share per paper; top 20 users by spend with anonymised route mix; provider invoice reconciliation (≤3% variance); forecast for the next exam-season peak at 3× (13-PERF-020); hazards due in 90 days. Outputs: a PR to config/limits.yaml/pricing.yaml/route table if anything changes, each with a changelog line; a one-paragraph note in the release notes if any student-visible limit moved. Acceptance: review notes exist for every month since M3; every config change links to a review note or an incident.

11-COST-010 — Exam-season grace is budgeted, not absorbed. Before each Cambridge series (March, June, November) finance signs the grace budget, computed from §08.10's unit costs — never from a rounded memory of them:

grace_usd = (free_users × (6 − 3) × 14 days × levels_mark_cost) + (paid_users × (60 − 40) × levels_mark_cost)

levels_mark_cost is taken per paper from §08.10 at the $0.175 figure (primary + 100% cross-family second mark) for any paper inside its first two exam series under 08-ENS-001, and $0.139 (primary + 20% second) only for papers past that window; the per-paper crossover date is a column on the cost dashboard. Budgeting the whole fleet at $0.139 understates FY1 by ≈26% on exactly the papers the launch depends on. The platform alarm at 120% of forecast (11-COST-006) refers to this signed number. Acceptance: 13-PERF-024 sign-off record per series; the grace-budget job fails if any paper in the forecast is priced at $0.139 while its series counter is below 2.

11.16CI/CD gates, environments and release process

§13.7 defines what must pass per environment (13-GATE-001…005); this subsection defines the pipeline that runs those checks, the environments themselves, flags, migrations, rollback and how a release becomes visible to users. AI coding agents and humans go through the same pipeline; there is no bypass label.

11-CICD-001 — Pipeline stages (GitHub Actions or equivalent; every stage is a required check on main).

11-CICD-002 — Environments.

EnvDataProvidersWhoPurpose
dev (local + ephemeral preview per PR)Seeded synthetic tenants (one per type), 9609 sample Pack, no real pupil data everRecord/replay fixtures by default; live providers behind LIVE_PROVIDERS=1 with a $20/day cap per developerEngineers, agentsFast loop

Rules: no production pupil data leaves prod (pseudonymised eval extracts go through the §13.1 consent path); every environment has its own secrets, provider keys and Langfuse project; staging is destroyed and recreated from migrations monthly to prove reproducibility. Acceptance: an engineer can stand up dev with one command in ≤10 minutes; the monthly staging rebuild is logged.

11-CICD-003 — Feature flags. Flags live in Postgres (flags table) with a 5-second cache, evaluated server-side and passed to clients in the policy context; three kinds: release (dark-launch, removed within 30 days of 100%), experiment (user-level randomised, registered in the §13 experiment registry with primary outcome and kill criterion, e.g. the debt guard 04-DEBT-003), ops (kill switches: marks_visible_{paper}, second_family_on, voice_pilot, provider_{name}_enabled, anon_landing_mark). Every flag has an owner, an expiry, and a default that is safe when the flag service is unreachable (fail closed for anything that shows numbers or unlocks help). Flags never change pedagogy rules that §00 lists as non-negotiable. Acceptance: a flag past expiry fails CI; the flag audit lists every flag with owner, age, exposure; killing provider_anthropic_enabled in staging reroutes 100% of Turns within 10 s.

11-CICD-004 — Release trains. Web and api: continuous, canary → prod at least daily on weekdays outside freeze; Mobile: EAS Update for JS changes daily, store builds fortnightly. Freeze windows: from T−3 days before the first paper of a Cambridge series to the day after the last paper (per series calendar in config), only P0/P1 fixes ship, each with the CTO's approval, canary ≥6 h. Prompt and model changes are releases (they pass stage 5 and 13-GATE-003) and are pinned per Session by policy_version so a live Session finishes on the version it started with (13-GATE-004). Acceptance: the release log shows the freeze windows honoured; no prompt version changes mid-Session in traces.

11-CICD-005 — Migration policy. Expand–migrate–contract only: (1) additive migration (new column/table, nullable or defaulted) deployed with code that writes both; (2) backfill as a resumable job with progress in audit_log; (3) contract (drop/rename) in a later release after one full canary cycle. Forbidden in one release: renaming a column, changing a type in place, dropping anything with rows. Every migration has a tested down for the additive step and a written fallback for backfills; migrations run before the new code takes traffic; long locks (>2 s) are rejected by a lint (lock_timeout=2s). RLS policies are part of the migration and covered by the RLS suite in the same PR. Pack data migrations follow 11-DATA-005 (new pack_version, never mutation). Acceptance: the nightly staging rebuild replays all migrations from zero; a migration touching a learner-plane table without an RLS test fails CI.

11-CICD-006 — Rollback. Web/api: previous image is kept warm; rollback is one command and ≤5 minutes to 100%; automatic on any 13-GATE-003 breach (5xx >0.5%, TTFT p95 >1.5 s for 10 min, seeded-QA out of tolerance, leak sample ≥5%, challenge rate +1 pp). Prompts/models: rollback is a policy_version pointer change (≤60 s). Mobile: EAS Update rollback to the previous bundle; store binaries carry a minimum-supported-API version so an old client keeps working against new api for ≥90 days (11-API-003 tolerance). Data: a release that ran a contract migration cannot be rolled back past it — the release notes state this and the release owner accepts it explicitly. Acceptance: a rollback drill each month in staging and each quarter in production canary, timed and logged.

11-CICD-007 — Release notes visible in-product. Every production release writes a release_notes row {version, date, user_facing[], limits_changed[], packs_updated[], calibration_changed[], suites {leak, praise, qwk_by_paper, cwv, ttft}, design_checklist_signed_by}. Students see the user-facing subset in Settings › "What changed" (§10.19) and, when a limit or a Pack pinned to their Course changed, a one-line notice in the Course ("Pack updated to 2026–28 v3 — 2 syllabus points renumbered", 11-DATA-005; "Free examiner Marks: 3/day → 4/day"). Teachers see calibration changes per paper in the console. Nothing about limits changes silently (11-BILL-003). Acceptance: a release that changes config/limits.yaml without a limits_changed entry fails the promote step; the notes page renders the last 20 releases.

11-CICD-008 — Definition of a shippable PR (for humans and agents alike). Title states the requirement IDs it satisfies; description names the eval suites it ran and links the Langfuse run; screenshots for any UI change in light and dark; no new TODO without an issue link; no new provider call outside the adapter interface (§08.11); no new table without RoPA entry; a changed copy string passes the copy lint. Acceptance: PR template enforced by a check that parses these fields.

11.17Top 15 technical risks and mitigations

Likelihood and impact are scored 1–5 (5 = near-certain / company-ending). "Early signal" names the dashboard or test that must exist before launch so the risk is seen while it is still cheap. Owners are roles; the register is reviewed monthly alongside the cost review (11-COST-009) and each row links to its controls by requirement ID. Register file: compliance/risk-register.yaml, which also feeds the Annex III technical file (11-PRIV-005 §2).

11-RISK-002 — Register hygiene. Each row carries last_reviewed, trend ∈ {up, flat, down}, open_actions[]; a row whose early signal has fired in the last month must have an open action with a date; new risks enter through the incident post-mortem (12.8) or the monthly review. Acceptance: pnpm risk:lint fails on a stale row (>45 days) or a fired signal without an action.

11-RISK-003 — Risks accepted, not mitigated (recorded so nobody re-litigates them). (a) No efficacy claims until the pre-registered study reports (SYNTHESIS §12) — marketing carries the calibration number only. (b) English Literature and Psychology essays are out of MVP scope (SYNTHESIS §8.12). (c) Below-gate papers show feedback with no number even if a competitor shows one. (d) The +10% Vertex regional uplift is paid for every EU/UK tenant call [E14]. Why: the alternative to each is a trust cost that the moat analysis rates higher than the revenue at stake (business-moat Part C).

§12Safety, integrity and wellbeing

12.1The academic-integrity stance

Integrity is a product decision, not a disclaimer. Margin's position is that a student who used it should be better off in an integrity investigation than one who did not, because the evidence exists (§12.2) and because the tool refused to produce the thing that would have got them into trouble. "No submittable coursework" is a non-negotiable (SYNTHESIS §0, [A59]); this subsection makes it executable.

12-INTG-001 — The two lists, published verbatim at /legal/integrity and in Settings › About.

Margin willMargin will not
Mark a draft against published criteria and name what is missingWrite, rewrite or "improve" prose that will be submitted for assessment
Ask questions about a draft, quote the student's own sentences back, and say which criterion each meetsProduce a paragraph, section, conclusion or bibliography entry for a submitted artefact
Teach the underlying content with the Help Ladder and the Effort GateGenerate text in the student's voice, or "sound more like a student"
Deliver full solutions to exam-style practice Items on request (§04.5) with the seen-solution tag and a retestDeliver solutions to an artefact tagged submittable
Produce a signed Learning Receipt on requestDetect AI writing, score "AI likelihood", or certify that work is human-written
Say plainly, when asked, what it did and did not doDeny that it withheld anything, or hide the reason (04-INTN-003)

Margin ships no AI-detection feature and no originality score, for students, teachers or schools. Why: detectors flag ESL writers 2–3× more often and 64% of US high-schoolers already fear false accusation [A59]; selling a detector would make the product the cause of the harm the Receipt exists to prevent.

12-INTG-002 — The submittable tag is the switch. Every Item, artifact and Session carries submittable ∈ {false, suspected, true}. true puts the Session into draft-feedback-only mode for that artefact. Set true when any of: (a) the student selects an assignment type in the composer or Scratchpad; (b) a teacher-set assignment in a Class is marked as coursework; (c) the classifier below fires at high confidence; (d) the student says so. suspected prompts one question, never a refusal: "Is this for a piece you'll hand in? I'll switch to draft feedback if so." — one tap Yes, it's coursework / No, it's practice. The answer is stored on the artefact, is revisable, and is recorded in the Receipt.

12-INTG-003 — Coursework detection heuristics (recall-first, precision-second, because the failure mode of a false positive is a question and the failure mode of a false negative is ghostwriting). A Haiku-class classifier over the Turn plus artefact metadata, plus deterministic rules:

SignalRuleWeight
Named assessmentLexicon match on NEA, non-exam assessment, coursework, IA, internal assessment, EE, extended essay, TOK, EPQ, portfolio, controlled assessment, dissertation, ISA, PIP, SBA, moderation, candidate record sheet, JCQ (localised)high, single-signal sufficient
Assignment brief uploadedUpload contains a criteria grid, word count, deadline, candidate/centre number fieldshigh
Class assignment flagassignments.type = coursework in a Classconclusive
Continuous-prose requestRequest for ≥250 words of first-person continuous prose that is not an exam answer to a tariff-bearing Itemmedium
Artefact shapeTitle page, contents, referencing style, word-count target, appendices in the Scratchpadmedium
Subject × artefact9609 "research project", IB "IA on my dataset", EPQ "5,000 words"medium
Deadline language"due Friday", "hand in", "submit", "my teacher marks it" combined with a draft in the Scratchpadmedium (with any other medium → true)

Two medium signals or one high signal ⇒ true. Acceptance: on a 400-case labelled corpus (200 coursework, 200 exam practice) recall ≥0.97 on coursework, false-positive rate ≤0.10; every false positive costs one question, not a refusal, and the student's override is honoured for the artefact's lifetime.

12-INTG-004 — Draft-feedback-only mode: exactly what it does. The tutor may (1) mark the draft against the published criteria for that qualification with per-criterion evidence quoted from the student's own text; (2) name gaps as questions ("Which of your two sources actually supports the claim in ¶4?"); (3) explain the underlying subject content at any Help Ladder rung; (4) critique structure at the level of a plan the student then writes; (5) check citations exist and are consistent. The tutor may not (6) emit more than 40 consecutive words of candidate-voice prose; (7) rewrite a sentence into an improved version; (8) supply a thesis, conclusion, evaluation sentence or source summary in submittable form; (9) produce a full plan for a coursework artefact (an exam-answer plan at rung 5 is allowed only on non-submittable Items, §04.5). Rung 4 in this mode is the student's own paragraph annotated, never a model paragraph. Enforcement is in the Orchestrator lint (04-ORCH-001, check 2): a draft exceeding the 40-word candidate-voice budget on a submittable=true artefact is rejected and regenerated as feedback. Acceptance: the coursework red-team set (12.10) yields 0 submittable paragraphs across 200 adversarial attempts, including "pretend it's practice", "translate my plan into full sentences", and role-play framings.

12-INTG-005 — How "Just the answer" coexists with this. The intent chip (§04.5) is scoped to gradable, tariff-bearing Items from the Pack or the generator — never to an artefact with submittable=true, where the chip renders disabled with the tooltip "Not for work you'll hand in." Nothing else changes: the chip is never removed, never rate-limited, never lectured about (04-INTN-002). A student under deadline pressure on coursework gets the same speed of help in a legitimate form: the criteria gap named in one Turn, and the writing left to them.

12-INTG-006 — Policy strings. These keys are entries in the one string catalogue whose rules §15.E fixes (15-STR-001…004: the key is exact, slots are typed, a locale missing a key falls back to English and logs). §15.E does not restate them and no other section carries a second copy; the rows below are their definition site.

KeyString
integrity.refuse"I can't write this for you — it would be submitted. I can mark your draft against the criteria and log what we did."
integrity.confirm"Is this for a piece you'll hand in? I'll switch to draft feedback if so."
integrity.mode_on"Draft feedback for {artefact}. I'll mark it against the criteria and ask questions; the writing stays yours."
integrity.chip_disabled"Not for work you'll hand in."
integrity.receipt_offer"Want a signed record of how you did this? It takes one tap."
integrity.no_detector"Margin doesn't detect AI writing and never scores work for it. A Receipt shows what you actually did."

12-INTG-007 — Teacher and school posture. A Class may set allowed_help_level per assignment (§10.20); Margin enforces it and shows the student the level before they start ("Your teacher allows hints up to rung 2 on this task"). Margin reports what help was used to the teacher in aggregate and, with the student's share action, per receipt — never a judgement about whether a student cheated. Where a teacher turns on receipt_required, the setting's own description states its limit in the teacher's words — "A Receipt shows what happened in Margin. It cannot show work done elsewhere" (12-RCPT-006) — so the affordance never implies coverage it does not have. School-safe mode (§12.7) may set submittable_default=true for a tenant so every artefact starts in draft-feedback mode. Acceptance: a Class fixture with allowed_help_level=2 blocks rungs 3–5 in the product and in the API, and the student sees the limit before the first Turn, not after a refusal.

12.2The Learning Receipt

The Learning Receipt is the artefact a student hands to a teacher who asks "did you write this?" It is a signed, verifiable log of process — Attempts, Help Ladder rungs, seen-solution flags, drafts, Marks, time — and it is the product's answer to detection, which Margin does not sell (12-INTG-001). §10.23 specifies the screen; §04.16 the pedagogy hooks; this subsection fixes the payload, the cryptography and the rules of use.

12-RCPT-001 — Scope of a Receipt, and the rule that automatic creation is never covert. One Receipt covers one subject: an artefact (a coursework draft, an essay in the Scratchpad), a Session, an assignment in a Class, or a date range within a Course. Receipts are created on explicit student action, or automatically when submittable=true — and automatic creation is announced, never silent: the artefact carries a persistent one-line notice, "Draft feedback mode — Margin is keeping a private process log of this piece. You can open, export or delete it," linking to the Receipt. Consumer accounts get a Settings toggle that turns automatic creation off (the artefact then keeps its draft-feedback restrictions and no log); school tenants with receipt_required=true cannot turn it off, and the notice says who required it. An automatic Receipt is private to the student until they share it. A covert process log of a minor needs a stated basis, so automatic creation has its own RoPA entry (11-PRIV-008) and its own row on /your-data (12-TRAN-005). A Receipt is append-only until sealed_at; after sealing it is immutable and any later work produces a new Receipt with supersedes. Acceptance: a fixture that switches an artefact to submittable=true renders the notice in the same paint as the mode change; a consumer account with the toggle off produces zero receipts rows; the deletion test removes an unshared automatic Receipt in one tap.

12-RCPT-002 — Payload schema (Receipt@1). The schema lives at schemas/Receipt@1.json and its $id is the only legal schema_id for a Receipt anywhere in config, prompts, telemetry or an export; the Name@n form is the document's one schema-naming grammar (§15.C), and receipt.v1 is not a spelling of it.

{ "schema_id": "Receipt@1", "receipt_id": "rcp_01JXQ…",
  "subject": {"type": "artefact|session|assignment|course_window",
              "ref": "art_01J…", "title": "Unit 3 essay draft",
              "course": {"board": "Cambridge International", "syllabus_code": "9609",
                         "pack_version": "9609:2026-2028@2026.11.2",
