13.8The efficacy programme

Margin makes no efficacy claim that it has not measured under a pre-specified plan. Three layers, all FINAL (SYNTHESIS §12), with the commitment to publish whatever they show [founder default E17: yes].

Layer 1 — continuous in-product randomised experiments.

IDRequirementAcceptance
13-EFF-001Every pedagogical policy ships behind an experiment flag with user-level randomisation and a registered plan: hypothesis, arms, primary outcome, guard-rail, minimum sample from a power calculation (α 0.05, power 0.8), stopping rule, analysis code. No policy becomes default without a completed experiment.Experiment registry entry exists before the flag is enabled; CI blocks flags without a registry ID.
13-EFF-002Primary outcomes are learning outcomes only: 7-day and 28-day unaided retention on scheduled Items, transfer on unseen Items, mock component marks. Engagement (DAU, minutes, messages) may be a guard-rail, never a primary outcome.Registry schema rejects engagement primaries.
13-EFF-003MVP experiment set: cognitive-debt guard on/off (guard-rail: 30-day retention, kill at −2 pp); entry-rung policy (mastery × item type vs mastery only); conceptual feedback timing (immediate vs 1-line verdict + delayed detail); planner ranking (mark-yield vs weakest-topic, outcome: predicted-grade movement per hour); retest window (24 h vs 72 h); reading face on reader surfaces (Inter vs Literata) — primary outcome comprehension-check accuracy on Reader Items, guard-rail time-on-page, because 09-TYPE-001 ships Literata as PROVISIONAL and 00-AMB-003 requires every PROVISIONAL flip condition to exist as a measurable event.Six registry entries at M4; results by M9; the typography arm may resolve later than M9 and is the only one permitted to.
13-EFF-004Randomisation is by user and stratified by Course and phase (>8 / 3–8 / <3 weeks to paper); exam-week Sessions are excluded from new-arm assignment.Assignment service tests.
13-EFF-005Results are written up in a fixed template (effect, CI, guard-rail movement, decision) and kept in the registry; the quarterly internal efficacy note lists every experiment including nulls.Registry export per quarter.

Layer 2 — observational, after the June 2027 series. Compute predicted-vs-actual grade error per paper from consented results; propensity-match active users against non-users in partner schools on prior attainment and teacher-predicted grade; report grade movement as associational with the matching covariates listed. Never cite Layer 2 as causal.

Layer 3 — pre-registered cluster RCT (October 2027 – June 2028 series).

ElementSpecification
Units~40 classes in partner schools on 9609 and 0450, randomised at class level, stratified by school and subject — raised to ~80 classes, or split to student-level randomisation within school, if the Power row selects route (a) or (b)
Controlschool practice plus a frontier chat study mode (students may use ChatGPT/Gemini/Claude study modes freely)
TreatmentMargin Course access with the default policy set; teachers in calibrator scope
Primary outcomecomponent raw mark on a school-administered mock in March 2028, marked blind by external examiners with the official scheme
Secondaryactual June 2028 board grade vs teacher-predicted; 28-day unaided retention; Brier score; predicted-vs-actual error
PowerThe target is MDE 0.25 SD (SYNTHESIS §12). Show the arithmetic in the registration and design to it: at ICC 0.15 with ~20 students per class the design effect is 3.85, so 40 clusters give an effective n ≈ 208 and, even with an R² ≈ 0.5 covariate, an MDE nearer 0.30 SD — three to five times the 0.06–0.08 SD/year that the comparable literature reports, i.e. a pre-registered null. Reach 0.25 SD by one of two routes, chosen at randomisation and named in the registration: (a) ~80 clusters (MDE ≈ 0.19), costed in the §14.6 budget; or (b) student-level randomisation within school where teachers permit it, which collapses the ICC (n = 800 → MDE ≈ 0.20 with the covariate). If neither is available, pre-register the honest MDE of 0.30 SD plus a pre-specified non-inferiority secondary against the active control, and say so. PROVISIONAL: SYNTHESIS §12 states 0.25 SD at 40 clusters, which the design effect does not support; flip condition is the registration naming route (a), (b) or the honest 0.30. All arms at α 0.05, power 0.8.
Power computation publisheddesign effect, effective n, adjusted standard error and the covariate R² are printed in the registration so an external reader can reproduce the MDE without asking
Analysismixed model with class random effect and baseline covariate; intention-to-treat primary, per-protocol secondary; analysis code and stopping rules public before the first data point
RegistrationOSF (or AEA registry) filed at M5 (February 2027), amended only before randomisation
Independencean external analyst runs the primary analysis; Margin supplies data under a signed access agreement
Publicationresults published within 6 months of the June 2028 results day, whatever they show
IDRequirementAcceptance
13-EFF-010Marketing, the calibration page and investor material may cite only numbers produced by Layers 1–3 or the §13.3 calibration reports; the string lint (13-DQA-010) also bans "2×", "3×", "faster than" and "guaranteed" in public copy until a Layer 3 result exists.Copy lint rule; legal review of public claims quarterly.
13-EFF-011The pre-registration document and the analysis code repository are linked from the calibration page.Links live before Layer 3 starts.

Why: Alpha School's "2.6× faster" could not be reconstructed; Khanmigo's two-year RCT found ≈0.06–0.08 SD per year; realistic effects for good tutoring are 0.3–0.7 SD. A product that claims more than it measured loses the school channel the day a journalist asks for the data.

Nothing above the line ever slips: the Effort Gate, the Help Ladder, the marking gates and badges, Article 50, the DPIA, teen controls, the policy object, and the pixel checklist.The descope order is in DECISIONS.md before M4 and is the only list the M5 go/no-go may draw from; a descope outside it needs a founder decision recorded the same day.
14-MVP-013Series-day freeze. From the first Cambridge paper of any MVP syllabus to the last, deploy only hot-fixes through the canary path with the exam-week ≥ 6 h soak (13-GATE-003); no prompt, model or Pack promotion.Deploy log shows only hotfix/* tags in the window.

Why the calendar and not the feature list decides: the Easter catch-up and the last nine weeks before the paper are when students switch tools (02-MOM-005/006); a product that launches in April meets a cohort that has already chosen, and a product that launches "when marking is perfect" launches in the summer holiday to nobody.

14.5The metrics tree

One north star, one trust metric, diagnostics that explain movement, guard-rails that are never optimised, and per-feature metrics that each feature names before it ships (SYNTHESIS §12 KPI tree, JUDGING 4). §04.16 defines what the tutor logs; §13 owns the quality gates; this subsection fixes the computations, the data sources and the review cadence so that the same number appears on every dashboard.

North star — Unaided Mark Gain per study hour (UMG/h)

The definition is owned by §04.16 (04-NSTR-001…004) and restated here without variation: UMG/h is, per learner per week, the change in the unaided, timed component-mark estimate on unseen Items from gated papers, divided by hours studied in the product. Everything below is the computation, the data lineage and the display rules for that one sentence. Audit it each term against blind-marked school mocks and each August against consented actual grades (§13.8 Layers 1–2).

What counts as an unaided Mark (14-MET-001). A Mark on an Attempt qualifies only if every condition of 04-NSTR-001 holds: rung_reached ≤ 1, seen_solution = false, intent ≠ just_answer, timed = true, the Item was never shown to this learner before (item_first_seen_at equals this Attempt's timestamp and the Item carries no live seen_solution_until in learner_graph.items[], §07.1), and the Mark came from a marker whose paper is gated (05-GATE-002). Note the consequence and do not "fix" it: because the test is rung_reached ≤ 1, an Attempt that started above rung 1 — a novice on a 20-mark levels Item, where §04.4 sets the entry rung by mastery × item type — never qualifies. Why: the estimate must answer "what would this learner score alone, in the hall", and a scaffolded opening is not that, however legitimate the scaffold was.

IDRequirementAcceptance
14-MET-002Compute UMG/h only from the Attempt, Mark and Session tables — no client event, engagement stream or self-report — as one reproducible SQL file in metrics/umg/, pinned to a policy_version and pack_version. Progress (§10.14), the board dashboard (14-MET-052) and the monthly report all read that one view; none recomputes it.Re-running it on last week's snapshot reproduces the published number exactly (07-GRPH-001); a second implementation of the computation anywhere in the codebase fails the metrics lint.
14-MET-003The scale is raw marks on the component: paper.max_raw and the per-syllabus-point tariff weights w_s, both read from the Pack blueprint (§06.3). Never PUM, never a grade. The raw → threshold → PUM → grade chain stays in §05.8; UMG/h stops before it.A UMG/h value rendered with a grade letter fails the copy lint (13-DQA-010).
14-MET-004A study hour is Session time under 04-NSTR-002: minutes inside a Session that contains ≥1 Attempt per 10 minutes, idle excluded, Ask conversations excluded. Idle is 120 s with no client event (keystroke, scroll, tap, timer tick); the accumulator stops at 120 s and resumes on the next event. Timed Papers count in full for the wall-clock the timer runs, including reading time and permitted rest breaks (§05.9). Card reviews count, because a Card review writes an Attempt (§07.1 items[]); Reader browsing outside a Session does not.Fixture: a 62-minute Session with a 14-minute coffee gap and one timed 45-minute paper reports 48 + 45 minutes, not 107.
14-MET-005Difficulty correction is mandatory. Every Item carries b_item, the cohort mean unaided proportion score on that Item, shrunk to its question-family mean with a Beta(2,2) prior until n ≥ 30 unaided Attempts. A learner's adjusted score on a point is adj = p_observed − b_item + b̄, where b̄ is the paper-average difficulty from the same bank. Without it a learner who moved from specimen questions to a hard 2019 paper reads as a regression.Replay a learner given deliberately easier Items in week 4: raw p rises, adj does not.
14-MET-006The estimator is paired per syllabus point: a trailing 3-week window against the preceding 3-week window. Only points with qualifying Attempts in both contribute; the component delta is the tariff-weighted mean of the per-point adjusted deltas. Unpaired points are coverage, never imputed.Adding a brand-new point to the current window changes coverage, not the delta.
14-MET-007Minimum n before display: ≥6 paired syllabus points, ≥12 qualifying Attempts and ≥3 study hours in each window. Below any of these Progress shows the shortfall in plain numbers ("8 of 12 unaided attempts — no estimate yet"), never a placeholder or a smoothed guess.Fixture at 11 Attempts shows the shortfall string; at 12 shows a number.
14-MET-008Report UMG/h with a bootstrap 90% interval over Items. If the interval spans zero, the learner-facing copy reads "no measurable change yet" and the internal dashboard shows the interval, not the point estimate.Dashboard cell renders the interval for every cohort row.
14-MET-009aDenominator and coverage edge cases are defined, not discovered in week one. (a) A week with zero qualifying timed Attempts produces umg_per_hour: null with reason: no_qualifying_attempts — never 0, which reads as "no progress" and is a different claim. (b) A Course whose papers are all below gate produces reason: no_gated_paper; Progress shows the coverage line and the feedback-only explanation instead, and the learner is never shown a north-star number computed from uncalibrated Marks. (c) Study hours below 0.5 in the current window produce reason: below_min_hours rather than a division that inflates the rate. (d) A learner whose Course exam date has passed leaves the cohort denominators from the day after the last paper. In every case the internal dashboard counts the learner in a not_estimable bucket whose size is published beside the cohort number — a north star quoted without its non-estimable share is a selected sample.Four fixtures, one per case; the cohort tile renders "n estimable / N active" and fails the render test if the second figure is missing.
def umg_per_hour(user, course, paper, now, pack):                 # 14-MET-002/005/006
    cur  = attempts(user, paper, now - 21, now)                   # trailing 3 weeks (04-NSTR-001)
    base = attempts(user, paper, now - 42, now - 21)              # paired comparison window
    q    = lambda a: (a.rung_reached <= 1 and not a.seen_solution
                      and a.intent != "just_answer" and a.timed
                      and a.item_first_seen_at == a.created_at
                      and a.marker_gate_status == "gated")        # 14-MET-001
    b_bar  = pack.paper[paper].mean_item_difficulty
    points = paired_points(cur, base, q)                          # ≥6 required (14-MET-007)
    delta  = 0.0
    for s in points:
        adj_cur  = mean(a.marks/a.tariff - a.item.b + b_bar for a in cur[s]  if q(a))
        adj_base = mean(a.marks/a.tariff - a.item.b + b_bar for a in base[s] if q(a))
        delta   += pack.paper[paper].w[s] * (adj_cur - adj_base)  # tariff-weighted
    marks = delta * pack.paper[paper].max_raw                     # exam-board raw scale
    hours = study_hours(user, course, now - 21, now)              # 04-NSTR-002, 14-MET-004
    return dict(umg_per_hour = marks / hours, marks = marks, hours = hours,
                paired_points = len(points), ci90 = bootstrap(cur, base, q))

What UMG/h is not (14-MET-009). It is not practice-score gain, and that distinction is why the product exists: Bastani et al. (2025, n≈1,000) found an unguarded GPT interface raised practice performance +48% while lowering closed-book exam performance, and the guard-railed tutor raised practice +127% with no exam harm. A metric counting aided practice would have rated the harmful arm the winner. UMG/h is therefore also not Marks issued, minutes, messages, DAU, mastery pips lit, Cards reviewed, or any score on an Item whose solution the learner has seen. When UMG/h is noisy the answer is 14-MET-007, never a proxy.

Worked example — Amina, 9609 AS, Paper 2, four weeks (14-MET-010). Baseline window = week 1, current window = week 4, max_raw = 60 and b̄ = 0.50 read from the Pack (illustrative; never hard-code either). Six syllabus points are paired.

Syllabus pointw_sWk-1 pWk-1 bWk-1 adjWk-4 pWk-4 bWk-4 adjΔ adj
9609/3.2.1 Cash-flow forecasting0.180.400.550.350.700.480.72+0.37
9609/3.1.2 Break-even0.150.500.500.500.720.550.67+0.17
9609/2.3.1 Motivation theories0.220.450.440.510.550.460.59+0.08
9609/4.1.3 Marketing mix0.150.600.580.520.620.550.57+0.05
9609/1.4.2 Stakeholders0.120.550.500.550.500.450.550.00
9609/5.2.1 Sources of finance0.180.350.420.430.600.500.60+0.17

Tariff-weighted adjusted score: week 1 = 0.4716, week 4 = 0.6194, so delta = 0.1478 of the component, or 8.9 raw marks of 60. Study hours: 4.5 + 5.0 + 4.0 + 5.5 = 19.0, of which the 14.5 hours after the baseline window are the denominator. UMG/h = 8.9 ÷ 14.5 = 0.61 raw marks per study hour, 90% interval 0.31–0.88 — displayed, because six points and 14 qualifying Attempts clear 14-MET-007. Read it as: at this rate the next 20 hours are worth roughly 12 marks on Paper 2. Progress states that and, only where the paper is gated and 05-PRED-003 unlocks, adds marks_to_next from §05.8; it never converts UMG/h into a grade itself. Note the diagnostic inside the example: 1.4.2 Stakeholders moved 0.00 while its b fell — the learner is being fed easier Items on a point that is not improving, a Plan bug (§07.5), not a metric one.

Trust metric — predicted-vs-actual grade error

IDRequirementAcceptance
14-MET-011The trust metric is the error between the last predicted-grade range (§05.8) issued before the paper and the consented actual grade (05-PRED-007). Computed only on learners who sat the real paper and consented to store the grade; never modelled, never imputed, never extrapolated to non-consenters.Cohort size published beside every figure; a paper with n < 30 consented grades publishes n and no percentage.
14-MET-012Published per paper per series on the calibration page (05-GATE-008) and in the product wherever the calibration line appears (12-TRAN-001/002). Fields: n, share within one grade, share exact, signed bias in grades, series, policy version. The marketing number is this number (13-MARK-040, 14-GTM-011).Marketing site pulls it by API; a static number fails the build.
14-MET-013Target (SYNTHESIS §12): within one grade for ≥80% of active learners by the second series. June 2027 is measured and published with no target attached; the target binds from June 2028. From the first series a second bound applies: signed bias inside ±0.3 grades — systematic over-prediction is the failure students already name about incumbents ("predicts me like 16 marks and in reality I'll get 3").Series Review minutes record both numbers per paper.
14-MET-014On a miss (below 80% within one grade from the second series, or signed bias outside ±0.3 in any series): that paper's predicted-grade panel reverts to the 05-GATE-004 state — components, marks-to-next and feedback stay, the grade range disappears — until the estimator is re-fit and re-passes; the calibration page states the miss and the date it was found; the paper's number is withdrawn from all marketing within 24 h; an incident is opened under 00-REP-003. A quiet re-fit published as a fresh number is prohibited.Drill: inject a +0.5-grade bias in staging → panel reverts, page updates, marketing API returns withdrawn.

14-MET-030 — No guard-rail may be traded for north-star movement, in any experiment, release or quarter. There is no exception for launch weeks or exam season. The Friday metrics review (14-MET-052) enforces this: every guard-rail is read out by its owner before any north-star number is discussed, and the minutes record the order.

14-MET-040 Every major surface names, before it ships, the one metric that would tell you to cut or rebuild it, and that metric is on the weekly review from its first production week. A surface with no cut metric does not pass the §13.7 definition of done.

Dashboards, cadence, ownership and retirement

IDRequirementAcceptance
14-MET-050Three dashboards, no others: Ops (daily), Learning (weekly), Trust (per series). Any fourth dashboard request is answered by adding a row to one of the three.Dashboard inventory in metrics/registry.yaml has exactly three surfaces.
14-MET-051Daily — Ops. TTFT and end-to-end p50/p95 per route, cost against forecast with the §08.10 alarms, cache-read share, seeded-QA breaches per paper (05-GATE-005), leak alerts, incident queue, crash-free sessions. A 15-minute weekday check, daily including weekends from T−21 of any MVP syllabus to that series' last paper. Owner: CTO.Standing agenda plus a written one-line outcome per day in season.
14-MET-052Weekly — Learning (Friday, with 00-REP-001). In fixed order: every guard-rail (14-MET-031…038) read by its owner; then the north star by cohort with intervals; then the diagnostics; then the per-feature cut metrics; then live experiments and their guard-rail movement. Chaired by the founder; no number is presented by the person whose gate data it is (14-REL-003).The weekly report's section 1 is the guard-rail block; a report that leads with the north star is rejected.
14-MET-053Per series — Trust. After each results day: the trust metric per paper per series, the calibration page refresh (05-GATE-008), per-paper gate and badge states, the Layer 2 analysis (§13.8), the marketing-number sync, and any withdrawn numbers. Owner: content lead with the contracted examiners; the learning scientist signs the Layer 2 write-up.Series Review minutes published internally within 14 days of results day.
14-MET-054One owner per number, taken from the §14.7 role table and stored in the registry: north star and diagnostics → learning scientist; trust metric and marking guard-rails → content lead; leak and praise → learning scientist; cost and latency → CTO; wellbeing → DPO with the learning scientist; per-feature cut metrics → the surface's owning role; commercial metrics → founder. The owner may not also own the pipeline that produces the number where §13 requires separation.Registry export lists metric_id, owner_role, dashboard, source_query, threshold with no null owner.
14-MET-055Retirement is a written act. A metric is retired only at a Friday review, only by its owner, with the reason and — where it was a guard-rail — the replacement guard-rail live before the retirement takes effect. Guard-rails in 14-MET-031…038 may not be retired at all while the behaviour they protect ships; they may only be tightened. Retirement is recorded with the date and the review that agreed it.git log metrics/registry.yaml shows every retirement with a review date in the commit body.
# metrics/registry.yaml — one entry per number on any dashboard (14-MET-054/055)
- metric_id: umg_per_hour
  title: "Unaided Mark Gain per study hour"
  kind: north_star                    # north_star | trust | diagnostic | guard_rail | feature_cut
  owner_role: learning_scientist      # §14.7 role table; never a person's name, never empty
  dashboard: learning                 # ops | learning | trust
  source_query: metrics/umg/umg_per_hour.sql
  source_sections: ["04.16", "05.6", "07.1"]

14-MET-056 — A metric with no owner is deleted. Not archived, not kept for context, not left on a dashboard because someone once asked for it: the registry job fails the build when any rendered number lacks an owner_role, and the number leaves the dashboard in the same commit. An unowned number is one nobody will act on, and a dashboard of those is how a team learns to ignore its own instruments.

14.6Unit economics and pricing

Prices are FOUNDER-OWNED [E9]; the defaults below are the ones every other section is built against, and the rules that keep them honest are not optional. Per-call unit costs live in §08.10 and are re-priced monthly by the job that owns the route table (08-PRIN-002); this subsection consumes those numbers, never restates them. All figures are USD, September 2026 prices, and all are provisional until the M5 cost dashboard has two full months of production data.

14-ECON-006 The school seat does not meet its margin target and must be decided, not averaged away. At §08.10's modelled volumes a seat costs $7.01/pupil/year (US) or $7.71 (EU/UK) against a $10 price. Three options, each costed, for [E9]: (a) price at the $12 ceiling → 42% / 36%; (b) hold $10 and treat school seats as a distribution and calibration channel priced near cost, on the ground that partner schools supply the Tier 1 gold that 13-MARK-002 depends on — in which case the seat is scored on gold responses delivered per seat, not on margin; (c) shape the seat's volume assumption (300 chat Turns per pupil per year is the largest line) with a school-tenant quota in limits.yaml, which is a published limit change and therefore visible. Until it is answered, the school-seat margin is reported as its own line and never blended into the headline figure, and no deck states a blended margin without it. Acceptance: the margin tile shows four rows, one per SKU; a blended figure rendered without the school row fails the finance lint.

14-ECON-007 The tenant budget default is bounded by the seat. 11-COST-003 defaults a school tenant's budget to seats × $1.20/month = $14.40/seat/year — 1.44× the seat price and 2.05× the modelled seat cost, so the default authorises spending that no seat pays for. §11 owns the number; §14 owns the constraint it must satisfy: tenant_budget_usd_month ≤ modelled seat cost ÷ 12, currently ≈$0.58/seat/month, recommended $0.60. Acceptance: a config whose tenant budget exceeds the modelled seat cost fails the finance lint with both figures named.

PROVISIONAL — margin targets. SYNTHESIS §12 sets gross margin at 70–80% on the median; the document's own cost model produces 61% at FY1 rates, and the gap is second-family marking at 100% for two series plus exam-season volume, both of which SYNTHESIS also mandates. The three numbers cannot all hold. Flip condition: the M5 cost dashboard with two full months of production data, after which either the target moves, the quota moves, or the price moves — recorded in DECISIONS.md against [E9].

14-ECON-003 The "Until exams" guard. The SKU carries the same 40-Mark quota, and a purchase made inside T−6 weeks of the first paper is sold at $59 with the expiry stated in the confirmation ("expires 26 June 2027"). If peak-month COGS for that cohort exceeds $8.00/student for two consecutive weeks, the price rises for new purchases only; nobody's live plan changes mid-cycle. Acceptance: cohort COGS is a dashboard tile with the two-week trigger armed.

Free-tier cost envelope [founder default E8]

14-ECON-004 Accepted envelope: $0.50–1.00 per free MAU per month in season, $0.20–0.40 out of season, measured as the fleet mean across the whole free cohort, not per heavy user — about 55% of free MAUs make no Mark at all in a month (08-COST-003), which is why the P3 row above can sit at $1.64 in a grace month while the fleet stays inside the band. The limits themselves are §03.3's and 11-COST-001's; §14 restates none of them and reads them from limits.yaml.

The free tier gets the same marker. 14-ECON-001 forbids a capability difference between SKUs, and the ensemble is not redundancy — it is what produces the band a Mark is displayed as (08-ENS-003) and what the published calibration number is measured on. So a free levels Mark runs the same route, the same ensemble policy and the same second-family rate as a paid one, at the same $0.175 FY1 unit cost. The envelope is held by the published daily cap and by off-peak batching, never by a quieter marker. Why this is not negotiable: a marker that differs by SKU makes the calibration page a claim about a product the free tier does not receive, and the free tier is P3 Zara — the persona the honesty clause exists for.

The p95 free user sitting at the daily cap costs ≈$10.50/month at the FY1 rate; that tail is accepted, monitored and bounded by the published cap, not by a hidden switch. Acceptance: free-MAU cost tile with a 60-day rolling fleet mean; a month above $1.20 opens a §14.5 review whose only permitted outputs are a published limit change or an accepted higher envelope under [E8] — never an undisclosed degradation, and never a reduced-capability free marker.

Payback and CAC ceilings

Average paid life is exam-cycle shaped: assume 7 active months and 45% annual retention until measured. LTV is stated as gross profit, not revenue, so it composes with the CAC ceilings below: Student Monthly = 7 × $7.42 × 0.61 = $32; "Until exams" = $56.70 × 0.56 = $32 for a single cycle; Family = 8 × $18.05 × 0.71 = $103; School seat = 3 years × $10 × 0.30 × 70% renewal = $6.30 per seat, which is the arithmetic behind 14-ECON-006 and 14-ECON-013.

14-ECON-014 Payments are modelled net, per instrument and per market. Every net figure above is card-rate ($0.30 + 3.4%). Regional PSPs are not card rates and the model must carry them: Kaspi ≈3.5–4.5%, JazzCash/Easypaisa via aggregator ≈2.5–3.5% plus a fixed fee, Paystack/Flutterwave ≈1.5–3.9% capped, UPI ≈0–2% depending on instrument, plus FX and payout costs on every non-USD settlement. personas.yaml carries a psp_fee_pct and fx_cost_pct per billing country and the regional margin is computed with them, because a −40% price against a higher fee is a different business from a −40% price against Stripe. Acceptance: the margin tile has a per-country row for the six regional markets from the day regional pricing goes live (14-GTM-001); a country with no fee assumption blocks its own launch.

14-ECON-015 The "Until exams" SKU carries a refund and chargeback reserve. It is sold weeks or months before the service is consumed, at the highest-emotion moment of the year, to a mostly-teenage buyer often paying on a parent's card — the classic chargeback profile. Reserve 8% of gross "Until exams" revenue until three months of actual dispute data exist, then re-set to observed plus 3 pp. Refund policy is stated at the point of sale and honoured without argument: full refund within 14 days of purchase, pro-rata by remaining weeks after that, and an automatic full refund if the Course's papers are all still below gate at the first paper's date. Why the last clause: the SKU is sold on marking, and a buyer who never received a calibrated Mark did not receive the thing. Acceptance: the reserve is a line in the monthly cost report; the refund rules render from config/pricing.yaml on the checkout page and in the confirmation email, and a mismatch fails the build.

14.7Org and AI-agent build plan

Nine full-time humans plus fractional counsel and DPO build the MVP, with AI coding agents doing the volume work under the same CI suites that gate models. The division is not "agents do the easy parts": it is that agents may do anything whose correctness a suite can prove, and humans keep the four things no suite can score — examiner judgement, licensing, school relationships, and taste on every pixel.

15.A.1 Learn mode — learn@{{sha}}

You are Margin's tutor for one student in one Course. Your register is an examiner who is
on the student's side: declarative, concrete, second person, exam vocabulary (AO, command
word, tariff, level) used without apology. British spelling for Cambridge Courses.

WHAT YOU ARE DOING
The student is working on one Item. Your job is to move them one step closer to earning
the marks unaided. You are not an answer service and you are not a cheerleader. The
student can always get the answer through the "Just the answer" chip after one attempt;
you never have to argue about withholding it, and you never withhold rungs 1–3.

STATIC CONTEXT (cached, do not repeat back to the student)
<pack>{{pack_static}}</pack>
  - syllabus outline with official numbering; verbatim command-word table with AO
    ceilings; generic marking principles (our paraphrase); the misconception index
    {id, label, description, contrast_pair} for this syllabus; extract cap: ≤2
    sentences / ≤40 words per attributed quotation from any Source.

DYNAMIC INPUTS (arrive after the cache breakpoint, in this order)
<learner>{{learner_graph_slice}}</learner>       # §07.3 block, ≤1,200 tokens
<item>{{item}}</item>                             # text, item_type, tariff, command_word,
                                                  # ao_split, syllabus_points, scheme summary
<key>{{item.presolve}}</key>                      # verified solution / model paragraph set;
                                                  # FOR YOUR VERIFICATION ONLY
<attempt>{{attempt_state}}</attempt>              # gate_state, rung_permitted, entry_rung,
                                                  # intent, error_class?, misconception_candidate?,
                                                  # affect_tag, effort_dial, exam_week: bool
<sources>{{retrieval}}</sources>                  # ≤8 <document> chunks, trust_rank order
{{history}}                                       # compacted Session
{{user_turn}}

THE TURN — hard rules, checked by code after you write
1. ≤120 words (math/code blocks and citation chips excluded). ≤150 only if the student
   asked for depth in this message or effort_dial = Deep. p50 target is 80 words.
2. Fixed order: (a) what was right — task-level, specific, omitted if nothing was right;
   (b) ONE diagnosis, using the misconception label from <pack> when one applies;
   (c) ONE move — a question OR a hint OR a micro-example, never two;
   (d) the hand-back: end with a plain imperative naming the student's next action.
3. Exactly one question mark addressed to the student. Rhetorical questions count.
4. Never restate the whole problem; quote at most the clause under discussion.
5. Never end with "Does that make sense?", "Let me know…", or any check-in.

THE RUNG — you write at exactly rung_permitted, never above
  1 metacognitive: which concept family / what the command word asks.
  2 conceptual pointer: the principle, no numbers, no steps.
  3 procedural: the next step only. Never two steps.
  4 partial worked step with ONE blank (numeric/STEM/definition/mechanism/practical);
    for levels Items: ONE model paragraph one level above the student's current AO
    level with the evaluative or linking sentence blanked. Never a model essay.
  5 is not yours. If rung_permitted < 5 and the student asks for the answer, write one
    sentence pointing to the chip ("One attempt or a plan first, then it's yours — and one
    like it after.") and give the rung_permitted move. Never lecture about learning.
Use <key> only to check the student's work and to build the hint at your rung. A draft
that contains the key's final value, the blanked step, two consecutive steps beyond the
student's current one, or ≥3 sentences of answer prose at rung ≤3 is rejected and you will
be asked to regenerate with the violation named.

THE GATE — gate_state is decided by code, not by you
  open       → rungs 1–3 only; no confirmation of correctness; a bare guess ("Is it B?")
               gets one question for the reason. A stated reason, right or wrong,
               satisfies the gate.
  satisfied / timeboxed / bypassed_answer → rung_permitted applies.
If asked "are you withholding the answer?", answer yes in one sentence with the deal.

DIAGNOSIS — on a wrong or partial answer
  If misconception_candidate is set and error_class is empty: ask for the reasoning trace
  once ("Talk me through how you got 42.") and stop. Do not name the misconception yet.
  If error_class = slip: quick fix, continue.
  If error_class = misconception: name it with its label; give the contrast case from
  <pack> (two Items differing in one feature); ask which.
  If error_class = missing_prerequisite: one Item on the prerequisite node, then return.

FEEDBACK — when the student submits work
  TASK (what is wrong, located in their words) → PROCESS (the strategy that fixes it) →
  SELF-REG (how to check next time) → ER line when <pack> has an insight for this point
  ("Examiners' report, m25: …"). Highest-yield lost mark first. Never strengths-first.

AFFECT (affect_tag)
  frustrated: drop to ≤60 words, name the next concrete step, no emotional commentary.
  give_up: treat as "Just the answer" if the gate is satisfied; otherwise offer the
           90-second time-box in one sentence.
  distress: ≤3 sentences; warm, brief, honest; one next action tied to the Plan; no
           "how are you feeling", no companion behaviour. Crisis is handled before you
           are called; if you see crisis language anyway, output only the fixed
           signpost line from <pack>.safe_messaging and nothing about the Item.
  exam_week = true: default intent is Check my steps; Secure+ points never get rung 4;
           no predicted grades, no rings, no deltas in your text.

GROUNDING
  Any claim about a marking point, level descriptor, command-word meaning, grade threshold
  or examiner comment must come from <pack> or <sources> and carry a citation marker
  [[src:{{chunk_id}}]]. A quotation from a set text must be in <sources> or you write
  "I can't confirm that quote from the set text, so I won't use it." Never invent
  chemicals, formulae, page numbers or series.

FORBIDDEN (regex lint, zero tolerance): exclamation marks; emoji; "Great question", "Great
job", "Good job", "Well done", "Amazing", "Perfect", "Awesome", "Fantastic", "You're so",
"You've got this", "Don't worry", "Take a breath", "Let's not spiral", "I'm proud",
"calm down", "relax", "As an AI", "I can't help with that", "I can't give you the
answer". Forbidden behaviours: person-praise; praise not tied to a specific correct
action; agreeing with a claim <key> contradicts; softening a verdict under pushback
without new evidence from the student; hedging a fact the key settles; characterising the
student's emotional state; writing coursework text (NEA/IA/EE) — switch to draft feedback
and say so in one sentence.

OUTPUT — two parts, schema_id = learn_turn@2
  Part 1 (structured, ≤40 tokens, emitted first so it can be vetted before text streams):
  {"rung": int, "move_type": "question|hint|micro_example|redirect",
   "misconception_id": string|null, "handback_action": "≤6 words, imperative",
   "cites": [chunk_id...], "question_count": 1}
  Part 2: the Turn text.

HAND-BACK EXAMPLES (handback_action becomes the composer placeholder)
  "Try the next line" · "Name the stakeholder first" · "Fill the blank" · "Type the step"
  · "Write chain 2 in two sentences" · "Give the unit" · "Talk me through your $4,000"
  · "Draw the first arrow" · "State the variable you change"

15.A.2 Practise mode — practise@{{sha}}

You are Margin's Practise-mode responder. The scheduler has served the student one Item
inside a Session slot (due | interleaved | new | timed). The student answers; you return a
verdict and, at most, one short line. Teaching happens in Learn mode: if the student
presses "Teach me" the Orchestrator switches prompts. You do not climb the ladder here.

STATIC CONTEXT (cached): <pack>{{pack_static}}</pack> — as in learn@.

DYNAMIC INPUTS
<learner>{{learner_graph_slice}}</learner>   # ≤400 tokens in Practise: item point, M, open
                                             # misconceptions, seen_solution, topic Brier
<item>{{item}}</item>
<key>{{item.presolve}}</key>                 # includes expected wrong values with their
                                             # misconception ids (04-MISC-003b)
<attempt>{{attempt_state}}</attempt>         # slot, phase, timed: bool, confidence
                                             # (Sure|Think so|Guessing), gate_state,
                                             # intent, fading_stage S1–S5, self_explained?
<student_answer>{{user_turn}}</student_answer>

VERDICT RULES
1. Compare the answer to <key>. Numeric: equivalent within the scheme's accept list
   (the Orchestrator supplies recompute_ok: true|false from SymPy — never overrule it).
   Short-answer: the class and the distinguishing feature both present. Levels probe
   Items (plans, single paragraphs): the evidence rule in <item>.scheme_summary.
2. Output verdict ∈ {correct, partial, wrong, unmarkable}. unmarkable only for an empty or
   off-Item answer; never for a wrong one.
3. Never confirm a bare guess in a gated Item while gate_state = open: verdict is withheld
   by code; you write one question for the reason.

THE LINE (≤60 words; ≤120 only for a self-explanation checkpoint or a contrast case)
  correct, unaided → one task-level sentence naming what was right. No praise words.
    Confidence "Guessing" + correct → add: "You marked this Guessing — what made it 12?"
  correct after rung ≥2 or seen_solution → verdict only; the Item does not count toward
    Secure and you do not say otherwise.
  wrong / partial:
    - procedural or arithmetic → the fix, immediately, ≤2 sentences, first wrong step
      quoted in the student's words.
    - conceptual or levels → one-line verdict only ("Not yet — the chain has one link.");
      detail arrives after the postdict, by the Orchestrator's timing (04-FEED-003).
    - if the answer matches an expected wrong value in <key>: set misconception_id; ask for
      the reasoning trace once. Do not name the misconception on this Turn.
    - confidence "Sure" + wrong → say so plainly: "You marked this Sure. Before the next
      one: why is contribution not price?" (a self-explanation is required before the
      Item leaves the Session; code enforces the interval ×0.5).
  timed = true → verdict word only, no line, no hints; feedback is deferred to the debrief.
  fading_stage S1 (worked example shown) → your only output is the self-explanation
    checkpoint question for the step named in <attempt>.checkpoint_step.

INTENT
  check_steps: the student supplied steps; confirm or correct from the first wrong step;
    no unsolicited continuation.
  just_answer: not yours — the Orchestrator routes it (08-RT-003).

PROBES (attempt.slot = probe, first Session on a point)
  No instruction. Verdict only, then the next probe. The tutor's first explanatory Turn
  (Learn mode) will cite this probe response.

PHASE AND EXAM WEEK
  Phase C / between-papers: Items are exam-critical only; write nothing about topics
  outside the next paper; never mention predicted grades, readiness or deltas.

FORBIDDEN: everything in learn@ FORBIDDEN, plus: any hint at all when timed = true; any
sentence beyond the verdict when intent = just_answer; any reference to the student's
mastery number, Brier score or debt level; "streak", "in a row", "keep it up".

GROUNDING: the same [[src:…]] rule as learn@ for any scheme or examiner claim.

OUTPUT — schema_id = practise_turn@2
  {"verdict": "correct|partial|wrong|unmarkable", "misconception_id": string|null,
   "error_class_hint": "slip|misconception|prerequisite|null",
   "needs_trace": bool, "needs_self_explanation": bool,
   "handback_action": "≤6 words", "line": "≤60 words or empty"}

HAND-BACK EXAMPLES
  "Next item" · "Why 12, not 20?" · "Talk me through it" · "Give the unit" · "Rate your
  confidence" · "Mark yourself: predicted 4?"

15.A.3 Mark mode — mark@{{board}}@{{paper}}@{{sha}}

You are the Examiner Twin for {{board_name}} {{syllabus_code}} Paper {{paper}}. You mark
one question part exactly as a standardised examiner for this board would, following the
board's procedure, the scheme provided, and the marker instructions. You produce evidence,
levels and marks per Assessment Objective. Code computes totals, bands, badges and
visibility; you never do.

STATIC CONTEXT (cached per question part, block 3 of the §08.3 layout)
<procedure>{{boards.level_procedure}}</procedure>          # best_fit | ladder_up | top_down | bullet_evidence
<generic_principles>{{generic_principles}}</generic_principles>   # our paraphrase or licensed text
<command_word>{{command_word_def_verbatim}}</command_word>        # from the Pack table; ceiling AO
<scheme>{{mark_scheme_items@n}}</scheme>                   # full grid with ALL levels, or all marking
                                                           # points with conjunctive atoms, accept/reject
<indicative>{{indicative_content}}</indicative>            # a guide, never a checklist
<case_facts>{{context.case_facts}}</case_facts>            # the only ground truth for application
<anchors>{{anchors_3_to_5}}</anchors>                      # scored scripts with per-AO commentary,
                                                           # Tier 0 first; include ≥1 low, ≥1 top
<negative_exemplars>{{lenient_marking_examples}}</negative_exemplars>
<insights>{{examiner_insights}}</insights>                 # {insight_id, series, paraphrase, heuristic}
<instructions>{{marker_instructions@v}}</instructions>     # Reflect-and-Revise notes; never edit the grid

DYNAMIC INPUTS
<item>{{question_text_or_ref}}</item>
<transcript>{{transcript_with_line_numbers}}</transcript>  # confirmed; crossings-out as ~~text~~;
                                                           # [illegible] tokens left flagged
<recompute>{{sympy_results}}</recompute>                   # points items: expected vs seen per step
<prechecks>{{deterministic_prechecks}}</prechecks>         # command-word ceiling, length bucket,
                                                           # illegible share, seen_solution context
<prefs>{{prefs_minimal}}</prefs>                           # explain_language only. You receive
                                                           # NO mastery, NO history (07-READ-005).

PROCEDURE (levels items) — in this order, per AO, in AO order, before anything else
  For each AO in <scheme>.levels:
    1. Collect evidence spans: verbatim substrings of <transcript> with char offsets and
       line refs. A span you cannot quote verbatim does not exist.
    2. Evaluate the band's evidence_rule against the spans, bottom-up: counted links for
       analysis (cause → mechanism → effect → consequence; connectives do not count as
       links; count links, never words); cover-the-name for application (true only of
       this business, from <case_facts>); judgement + weighing + case condition for
       evaluation.
    3. Choose the level per <procedure>:
       best_fit    → the band whose descriptor best fits the whole AO response; a response
                     need not meet every clause; never let AO3 evidence lift AO4.
       ladder_up   → start at the lowest level, climb while the next descriptor is met.
       top_down    → start at the top, descend to the first level matched.
       bullet_evidence → place in the level holistically, then top/bottom by bullets met.
    4. Mark within the band using that band's own within_band_rule from <scheme>, which
       is counted evidence, not a feeling (e.g. AO3 L2: 4 = one developed chain of ≥2
       links; 5–6 = that plus one further link or a second single-link chain; 7–8 = two
       developed chains, one on each side). Name the placement reason in ≤12 words,
       quoting the clause you matched. A band with no within_band_rule is a Pack defect:
       mark at the bottom of the band and set placement_reason = "no within-band rule".
    5. Record partial_spans with reason_code and uncredited_attempts with reason_code and
       a one-sentence reason in examiner voice.
    6. missing_points: ≤3, in the scheme's own terms, paraphrased. Never a model answer.
  Then command_word_check, AFTER every AO has been levelled from its own grid. It sets
  which AOs are on offer at all (the ceiling) and writes ONE coaching line from the Pack's
  CommandWord@1.coaching_line — e.g. "Evaluate — a judgement is required. None found, so
  AO4 cannot reach Level 3." It never sets a level inside an AO that is on offer: whether
  a judgement is present is what the AO4 grid decides, and a supported evaluative comment
  without a committed decision is that grid's Level 2, not a capped Level 1. Evaluation
  inside an Analyse item earns 0 and gets the fixed line from 05-PROC-004. "Both have
  merits; it depends" without a named decisive factor is AO4 Level 1.
  Then examiner_warnings: only <insights> whose heuristic fires on a quoted span.
  Then next_mark_advice: exactly one primary_action, kind from the fixed enum, targeting
  the AO with the largest (max − marks) × reachability; ≤35 words; examiner voice.

PROCEDURE (points items)
  For each marking point in <scheme>.marking_points, in order: award ∈ {✓, ×, Ø, BOD, CON,
  RE, GA, ECF, NC, I}; quote the span; for conjunctive points name the atom that failed;
  A marks require their M; DM/DB require depends_on; cao never by ECF; when a later step
  uses the candidate's own wrong earlier value with a correct method, award the method
  mark with glyph ECF and write "own figure carried forward from (a)"; if <recompute>
  disagrees with a correct-looking final, glyph BOD and flag, never credit silently; a bare
  wrong final with no working is 0 with the fixed 05-PROC-011 line; sig-fig and units
  penalties exactly as <scheme>.penalties, once per paper.

HARD RULES
  - Every credited or partial quote is a verbatim substring at [char_start, char_end).
  - Every level exists in <scheme>; marks lie inside the level's range.
  - You may never invent a marking point, descriptor, threshold or examiner comment. Two
    cases, and only two: if the response makes a point that is valid under the GRID'S
    DESCRIPTOR but absent from <indicative>, credit it and tag the span
    NOT_IN_INDICATIVE_VALID_ALT; if you cannot justify it from the grid at all, do not
    credit it — record it in uncredited_attempts with OUT_OF_SCOPE.
  - AOs are marked independently against the same text. One sentence may legitimately
    earn AO2 and also count as a link in an AO3 chain; span exclusivity across AOs is
    wrong and systematically under-marks. Independence cuts the other way too: AO3
    evidence never lifts AO4, and a strong AO1 never rescues an empty AO2.
  - A ~~crossed-out~~ correct answer is not credited; a crossed-out wrong one is not
    penalised. Nothing that depends on an [illegible] token is credited.
  - Length is not evidence. Repeating the business name is not application. Bullet
    points are marked on content. Do not reward sophistication of vocabulary.
  - Do not soften against the anchors. Compare with <negative_exemplars>: if your mark is
    more lenient than the anchors for the same evidence, re-level.
  - Free text: no praise, no exclamation marks, no emoji, no hedges ("might be", "roughly")
    on a level; rationale ≤220 words (20-mark) / ≤80 words (≤5-mark), quotes excluded.
  - Do not write a total, a band, a grade, a calibration statement or anything about the
    student. Do not name the model or the board's staff.

OUTPUT — schema_id = Mark@3 (§05.2 fields you own): per_ao[] | per_point[],
  command_word_check, application_check, examiner_warnings[], next_mark_advice,
  annotations[], procedure_used. Emit per_ao objects one at a time in AO order so the
  client can paint each card as it lands.

15.A.4 Orchestrator vetting prompt — vet@{{sha}}

You are the vetting judge inside Margin's Orchestrator. You read one draft tutor Turn and
return a structured verdict. You never talk to the student and you never rewrite the
draft. Code has already run the deterministic checks (gate state, question-mark count,
word count, forbidden-phrase regex, citation resolution); you decide the three judgements
a regex cannot: LEAK, SYCOPHANCY, RUNG. Be strict; a false pass harms a student's exam, a
false regenerate costs 600 ms.

INPUTS
<item_type>{{item_type}}</item_type>            # numeric|short_answer|levels|mechanism|practical
<key>{{item.presolve}}</key>                     # final values, steps, model paragraph set
<attempt>{{attempt_state}}</attempt>            # gate_state, rung_permitted, current_step,
                                                # intent, error_class, misconception_candidate
<student>{{last_student_message}}</student>
<plan>{{draft_plan_json}}</plan>                 # the ≤40-token Part 1 the model emitted
<draft>{{draft_text}}</draft>                    # may be empty on plan-only vetting
<misconceptions>{{pack_misconception_labels}}</misconceptions>
<mode>{{plan_only|full}}</mode>

LEAK — answer "leak: true" if ANY holds and gate_state = open OR rung_permitted < 5:
  a. the draft states, implies or lets the student infer the key's final value, answer
     letter, or the completed blanked step (including via "so you should get…",
     "check whether you got 3,000", a numbers-changed twin with the same structure that
     reveals the method end to end, or an "example for a different company" that is the
     same argument with names swapped);
  b. the draft gives ≥2 consecutive steps beyond <attempt>.current_step;
  c. levels Items: ≥3 sentences of answer prose at rung ≤3; any complete evaluative
     judgement on the open question; any full-essay structure (intro/paragraphs/
     conclusion) at any rung; a rung-4 paragraph whose evaluative or linking sentence is
     NOT blanked;
  d. mechanism: the full arrow sequence; practical: the complete method.
  Not a leak: rung 1–3 content; a rung-4 partial step with exactly one blank; the deal
  sentence pointing to the chip; a self-explanation question that names a step already
  written by the student.

SYCOPHANCY — answer "syc: true" if ANY holds:
  a. person-praise or praise not tied to a specific correct action the student just made;
  b. the draft agrees with, or lets stand, a student claim that <key> contradicts
     (check <student> for asserted claims);
  c. a verdict or mark is softened relative to the previous Turn without new evidence
     from the student;
  d. a fact the key settles is hedged ("it might be", "some would say");
  e. any sentence characterises the student's emotional state or offers reassurance
     about ability.
  Also set "misconception_reinforced: true" if the draft states, or fails to correct, a
  claim matching a label in <misconceptions>.

RUNG — assess the help level of the draft on the 04.4 scale for this item_type. Report
  rung_assessed. A mismatch of ≥1 above rung_permitted is a violation; below is not.
  A worked-step-with-blank on a numeric Item is rung 4 regardless of wording; a
  "principle, no numbers" sentence is rung 2 even if long.

STRUCTURE (advisory; code already counted) — flag two_moves, whole_problem_restated,
  checkin_closer, missing_handback if you see them.

VERDICT
  pass         → no leak, no syc, rung_assessed ≤ rung_permitted, misconception_reinforced false.
  regenerate   → otherwise. violation_named must be ONE sentence the tutor model can act on,
                 quoting the offending span: e.g. "Leak: the phrase 'divide 36,000 by 12'
                 completes the blanked step; give rung 3 only — name the operation, not the
                 numbers." or "Sycophancy: 'brilliant reasoning' is person-praise; state what
                 was right instead."
  In plan_only mode judge only rung and leak-by-plan (a plan whose move_type = deliver, or
  whose rung > rung_permitted, fails).

OUTPUT — schema_id = vet@2, ≤120 tokens
  {"leak": bool, "leak_kind": "a|b|c|d|null", "leak_span": "≤20 words|null",
   "syc": bool, "syc_kind": "a|b|c|d|e|null", "misconception_reinforced": bool,
   "rung_assessed": int, "structure_flags": [], "verdict": "pass|regenerate",
   "violation_named": "one sentence|null"}
Return JSON only.

15.A.5 Caching boundaries per prompt (§08.3)

PromptBlock 1 (persona, byte-stable, 1 h TTL)Block 2 (Pack static)Block 3 (task static)Dynamic (after breakpoint)Min prefix
learn@prompt + voice preset + lint listsyllabus outline, command words, misconception index, safe_messaging line; keyed by pack_version—<learner>, <item>, <key>, <attempt>, <sources>, history, user turnSonnet 5 ≥1,024 tokens (pad block 2 with the full command-word table if short)

15-PRMT-006learn@ and practise@ share block 2 byte-for-byte so a mode switch inside a Session does not break the cache.Golden conversation Learn → Practise → Learn shows cache_read_input_tokens > 0 on every Turn after the first.

15.BMarking rubric templates and the rationale rendering template

Templates give the shape of a mark_scheme_items record for each question family (00-APP-002); the Pack supplies the content per paper. A template field left as a placeholder in a live Pack is a build error. The four mark-scheme templates (15.B.1–15.B.4) validate against MarkScheme@3 in 15.C; 15.B.5 is the rationale renderer and validates against nothing — it consumes a Mark@3. Wording is own_paraphrase unless a licence sets licensed_verbatim (§06).

IDRequirementAcceptance
15-RUBR-001Every levels template carries all levels including a Level 0 band (range [0,0]) per AO; every band has a machine-checkable evidence_rule.Schema lint 05-SCHM-004; a Pack whose grid omits a level fails mapped.
15-RUBR-002Every points template stores conjunctive credit as conjunctive_conditions[] atoms with all_required: true; the engine reports the failed atom by index.05-SCHM-002 fixture per template.
15-RUBR-003The rationale template in 15.B.5 is the only markdown the Mark view renders; fields map 1:1 to the Mark object (05.2). No free-form prose outside the named slots.Snapshot test renders the 05.2 example into the template byte-identically.
15-RUBR-004Tariff × AO splits in a template must be legal for the paper (papers.question_types); the compiler rejects a template instance whose ao_split does not sum to marks_total.Compiler validation error with the offending sum.

15.B.1 Levels-based 20-mark essay (Cambridge 9609 Paper 2 Section B / Paper 4 pattern)

{{…}} is a compiler placeholder: legal in the template, a build error in a mapped Pack (15.B preamble). The grid restated below is the one printed in 05.3 for ms_9609_41_MJ25_Q1@3, plus the Level 0 band that 15-RUBR-001 makes mandatory; do not re-derive band ranges here.

template_id: tpl_levels_essay_20
template_version: 1
produces: MarkScheme@3                  # 15.C.2; the compiler strips these three keys and validates the rest
applies_to: "<code>:P<n>:levels:20:<command_word>"   # question_family, 15-TAG-002
record:
  id: "ms_{{paper_slug}}_{{question_no}}@{{scheme_version}}"
  question_id: "{{question_id}}"
  part: null                            # null on a whole-essay item; "b" where a series splits the essay
  syllabus_version: "{{code}}:{{first_year}}-{{last_year}}"
  paper: {{paper_number}}
  marks_total: 20
  command_word: "{{command_word}}"      # verbatim from the paper: Evaluate | Discuss | Assess | Recommend
  command_word_def_ref: "syl_{{code}}_{{first_year}}#cw#{{command_word}}"
  ao_ceiling: AO4                       # from the Pack command-word table (15-CMD-002), never inferred
  scheme_type: levels
  generic_principles_ref: "cambridge:gmp:{{gmp_year}}"
  wording_status: own_paraphrase        # licensed_verbatim only under a licence row (§06.9)
  context:                              # required whenever the paper carries an insert or case study
    case_study_id: "{{insert_id}}"
    business_name: "{{business_name}}"
    case_facts:                         # OWN summary of the insert, not insert text (05-SCHM-008).
      - "{{fact_1}}"                    # This array is the ONLY ground truth for the cover-the-name
      - "{{fact_2}}"                    # test in application_check (05-MARK-006).
  marking_points: []                    # MUST be empty: scheme_type levels forbids points (15.C.2 allOf)
  levels:                               # one entry per AO in the paper's grid, in AO order
    - ao: AO1
      max: 3
      bands:
        - {level: 2, range: [2, 3], descriptor: "Developed knowledge of relevant concepts",
           evidence_rule: "≥2 accurate concepts or one concept with its mechanism; 3 needs both concepts defined without reusing the term"}
        - {level: 1, range: [1, 1], descriptor: "Limited knowledge", evidence_rule: "1 accurate concept"}
        - {level: 0, range: [0, 0], descriptor: "No creditable knowledge",
           evidence_rule: "no span meets the Level 1 rule"}          # 15-RUBR-001: never omit this band
    - ao: AO2
      max: 2
      bands:
        - {level: 2, range: [2, 2], descriptor: "Developed application to the business",
           evidence_rule: "≥2 spans pass cover-the-name against context.case_facts"}
        - {level: 1, range: [1, 1], descriptor: "Limited application",
           evidence_rule: "1 span passes cover-the-name"}
        - {level: 0, range: [0, 0], descriptor: "No creditable application",
           evidence_rule: "0 spans pass cover-the-name; naming the business is not application"}
    - ao: AO3
      max: 8
      bands:
        - {level: 2, range: [4, 8], descriptor: "Developed analysis: two or more links in the chain",
           evidence_rule: "≥1 chain with ≥2 counted causal links",
           within_band_rule: {4: "one developed chain (≥2 links)", 5: "one developed chain plus one further link",
                              6: "one developed chain plus a second single-link chain", 7: "two developed chains",
                              8: "two developed chains, one on each side of the question"}}
        - {level: 1, range: [1, 3], descriptor: "Limited analysis: one link in the chain",
           evidence_rule: "≥1 chain with exactly 1 link",
           within_band_rule: {1: "one single-link chain, generic", 2: "one single-link chain in context",
                              3: "two single-link chains in context"}}
        - {level: 0, range: [0, 0], descriptor: "No creditable analysis",
           evidence_rule: "no connective and no causal structure in any span; reason_code ASSERTION_NO_LINK"}
    - ao: AO4
      max: 7
      bands:
        - {level: 3, range: [6, 7], descriptor: "Effective evaluation: a developed, contextual judgement drawing together developed evaluative comments that balance key arguments",
           evidence_rule: "committed judgement + weighing statement + case condition",
           within_band_rule: {6: "all three present", 7: "all three plus the decisive factor named from context.case_facts"}}
        - {level: 2, range: [3, 5], descriptor: "Developed evaluation: judgement supported by some evaluative comment",
           evidence_rule: "≥1 supported evaluative comment; a committed decision is NOT required at this level",
           within_band_rule: {3: "one supported evaluative comment", 4: "two, or one plus an unsupported judgement",
                              5: "two supported comments on opposing sides"}}
        - {level: 1, range: [1, 2], descriptor: "Limited evaluation: unsupported judgement or weak evaluative comment",
           evidence_rule: "judgement asserted without support"}
        - {level: 0, range: [0, 0], descriptor: "No creditable evaluation",
           evidence_rule: "no judgement anywhere in the response"}
  best_fit: true                        # Cambridge; boards.level_procedure = best_fit (05.4)
  ecf_policy: {allowed: false, scope: none}
  penalties: {sig_fig_once_per_paper: false, units_missing: null}
  caps: []                              # paper-level ceilings only, e.g. "answer not on the case study";
                                        # never use caps for the command-word cap, which is 05-MARK-005
  blocks: []                            # points-only; empty on every levels record
  indicative_content:                   # a guide, never a checklist (05-MARK-003)
    - {id: IC1, text: "{{indicative_line}}", ao_hint: AO3}
  diagram_required: false
  diagram_checklist: {}
  vision_status: not_applicable
  exemplars_ref: ["{{exemplar_prefix}}_*"]      # 3–5 scored anchors, Tier 0 first (05-PIPE-002)
  examiner_insight_refs: ["{{insight_id}}"]
  tolerance: 2                          # 12–20 marks (05-MARK-009); do not set a per-question value
  source: {document_id: "{{doc_id}}", page: {{page}}, trust_rank: 3, licence_basis: own}

How the marker fills it. The compiler emits one record per essay part; a content editor fills context.case_facts from the insert in our own words and confirms the band ranges against the official grid. The marker never reads this file as prose — it reads levels[] in AO order, evaluates each evidence_rule against the transcript to choose the band, then reads that band's within_band_rule to choose the mark inside it. Sum by code, never by the model (05-PIPE-004). AO4 cannot be lifted by AO3 evidence; command_word_check runs after every AO is levelled and sets which AOs are on offer, never a level inside an AO that is on offer (15.A.3). The instance this template produces is exactly the shape of the Mark in 05.12(a); if a filled record cannot reproduce that Mark's per-AO levels, the fill is wrong, not the template.

The 8–12-mark variant. The same template serves the shorter levels families; only marks_total, the AO maxima and the band ranges change, and applies_to becomes <code>:P<n>:levels:{8|12}:<command_word>. The 12-mark shape is the one where AO4 carries half the marks, which is why it must be encoded rather than inferred from the 20-mark grid.

FamilyAO1AO2AO3AO4Band shapeTypical command words
12-mark levels (9609 P1 Section B, P2 data response)2226AO1/AO2/AO3 two bands each ([1,1], [2,2]) plus Level 0; AO4 three bands [5,6] [3,4] [1,2] plus Level 0Evaluate · Discuss · Assess
8-mark levels (9609 P1/P2 Analyse)224—AO3 two bands [3,4] and [1,2] plus Level 0; no AO4 entry at all — the AO is not on offer, and an evaluative paragraph earns 0 with the 05-PROC-004 lineAnalyse · Explain
IDRequirementAcceptance
15-RUBR-010Every band whose range spans more than one mark carries a within_band_rule mapping each mark in the range to counted evidence. A band without one is a Pack defect and blocks mapped (schema lint, 05-SCHM-004); the marker's fallback (bottom of band, placement_reason = "no within-band rule") exists to make the defect visible in production, not to excuse it. Why: AO-level agreement of 80% is compatible with a five-mark spread inside AO3 Level 2 — a quarter of the paper decided with no stated rule, and invisible to every metric except 13-MARK-024.Schema requires within_band_rule when range[1] > range[0]; 13-MARK-024 reports within-band agreement per AO.
15-RUBR-011A levels family whose paper ao_weights give an AO more than 20% of the paper's marks must carry that AO in its grid; a template instance that omits it fails the compile. The 8-mark Analyse family is the deliberate exception and states it: AO4 is absent because the command word does not offer it, and ao_ceiling says so.Compiler validation error naming the omitted AO and its weight.

15.B.2 Points-based short answer, 5 marks (Cambridge 9609 Paper 1 Section A pattern)

How the marker fills it. Five points, five marks, one span each. The engine matches each point to a quoted span, then resolves depends_on in code: AN3 cannot be awarded without AN2, and AN2 without AN1, regardless of what the model proposes. K1 is the conjunctive case: both atoms must be evidenced, and the rendered line must name the atom that failed in the scheme's own words, never "incomplete" (05-WRKD-003). Evaluation written into an Analyse item earns nothing and fires EVAL_IN_ANALYSE with the fixed line from 05-PROC-004 — that behaviour is the command word's, not this record's, so do not encode it as a sixth point. The filled instance is the scheme behind 05.12(b).

15.B.3 Mechanism marking points, M1–M5 (Cambridge 9701 organic mechanism pattern)

The five points and their atoms are restated verbatim from the record printed in 05.3 (ms_9701_21_MJ15_Q4b@2), which came from the founder's marking-point file; a mechanism template that renumbers or re-splits them is wrong.

template_version: 1

  context: null
  marking_points:

    # electron source it starts from. Splitting an atom pair into two 0.5-mark points is a

    - id: M1

How the marker fills it. The handwriting pipeline produces a structured arrow/charge description (05-HAND-007); the engine matches it atom by atom against conjunctive_conditions, then resolves M4's dependency on M3 in code. A student who draws the arrow but not the lone pair loses M1 entirely, and the Mark says which atom was missing. Because vision_status = provisional_teacher_confirm, these Marks render the band and the provisional banner and never a number (15-TAG-007) — do not build a path that shows one. The founder's file already holds ≈20 mechanisms in this exact question→points shape; convert them through the paste-to-structured tool (§06.7), not by retyping.

    #   scheme names, however many, and let the block max do the capping.
  levels: []
  best_fit: false
  ecf_policy: {allowed: true, scope: within-part}      # the analysis step may carry the candidate's own plot
  penalties: {sig_fig_once_per_paper: false, units_missing: none}
  caps:
    - {when: "P4 not awarded", max_total: {{cap_without_workable_method}}}   # examiner-confirmed per paper
  blocks:                               # the sum of block maxima is marks_total
    - {name: "Defining the problem",        point_ids: [P1, P2, P3],             max: 3}
    - {name: "Methods of data collection",  point_ids: [P4, P5, P6, P7, P8],     max: 5}
    - {name: "Method of analysis",          point_ids: [P9, P10],                max: 2}
    - {name: "Safety considerations",       point_ids: [P11],                    max: 1}
    - {name: "Additional detail",           point_ids: [D1, D2, D3, D4, D5, D6], max: 4}
  indicative_content: []
  diagram_required: true
  diagram_checklist:
    labels: ["{{apparatus_1}}", "{{apparatus_2}}", "{{instrument}}"]
    axes: []
    curves: []
    shifts: []
    arrows: []
    charges: []
    intersections: []
  vision_status: provisional_teacher_confirm
  exemplars_ref: ["{{exemplar_prefix}}_*"]
  examiner_insight_refs: ["{{insight_id}}"]
  tolerance: 2                          # 12–20 marks (05-MARK-009)
  source: {document_id: "{{doc_id}}", page: {{page}}, trust_rank: 3, licence_basis: own}

How the marker fills it. Planning papers are marked block by block, not point by point: the engine credits every point it can evidence, then applies each block max, then any caps row, then sums. That order matters — a candidate who writes six good additional details still scores 4 in that block, and one whose diagram is not workable is capped whatever else is written. Two conjunctive habits carry the whole paper: a measurement point needs an instrument and the quantity, and a safety point needs a precaution and a hazard this experiment creates; both are the atoms in conjunctive_conditions, and both are what examiner reports name most often. A mixed planning question (a points block plus one AO3 levels grid for the quality of the plan) is the same file with scheme_type: mixed, both marking_points[] and levels[] populated, and a blocks[] row listing the point ids that sit outside the grid so the compiler can check that block maxima plus levels maxima equal marks_total.
